# S2 Requirements Reconciliation

Sprint: 39b7cc253f5d — active project sprint: S2

The Agentic_Framework phase-1 record is attached to the already active S2. It does not create a new product sprint or authorize starting S3. This document consolidates the existing S2 scope and acceptance state; it does not add product scope or reopen the accepted architecture.

## Context and goal

S2 delivers a bounded, authenticated path for dispatching work that has already been assigned by the existing Store, and establishes the evidence needed to qualify its runner boundary. The Store remains the sole task, assignment, and lease authority. The accepted coordinator path is the existing `DispatchOwnerService`, authenticated Supervisor/Store admission, Store-filtered Pub/Sub, and `StoreBackedDispatcher`. No external coordinator, second scheduler, or assignment authority is required. [S1: `core/STATE.md`, “Current S2 coordinator/runtime adjudication — 2026-10-29”; `core/BACKLOG.md`, “S2 — signed dispatch-instruction provenance and owner relay”.]

## Scope

**In scope:** source-level signed-instruction verification and owner relay for already-authorized work; fail-closed admission and outcome handling; bounded runtime configuration/evidence under the recorded authorization; truthful S2 acceptance and exact-head review.

**Out of scope:** granting production signing authority, provisioning production issuer/attestor keys, activating production dispatch or E5, migrating an existing Store, running restricted process-kill, crash/recovery, mutation, E8, or policy selectors, or starting S3 before S2 closes. Bounded source preparation for an explicitly machine-labelled delegation contract, pure validators, and read-only measurement collectors is authorized within S2 under the GPT-PM adjudication below. Preparation does not itself authorize signing, replace active E5 verification, or permit activation.

## Requirements

## Non-functional requirements and constraints

- **Security:** fail closed on invalid provenance and ambiguous admission; keep signer authority distinct from Store assignment authority. [REQ-001–REQ-004; sources above.]
- **Runtime isolation:** use the accepted authenticated identities, root-controlled configuration, and bounded runtime profile; do not claim isolation from mocked peer credentials or transient test units. [REQ-004–REQ-005; `core/STATE.md`, current S2 coordinator/runtime adjudication.]
- **Numeric service targets:** UNKNOWN. The active S2 records do not establish a numeric dispatch-latency, availability, throughput, or recovery-time target. No target is invented here.
- **Restricted verification:** process-kill, crash/recovery, mutation, E8, and policy selectors remain `NOT_RUN` under the recorded restrictions. A skipped or unrun selector is not a pass. [`core/STATE.md`, current S2 coordinator/runtime adjudication; `core/BACKLOG.md`, S2 closure boundary.]
- **Data safety:** fresh schema-v6 Store initialization is conditionally allowed by the recorded adjudication; migration of an existing Store requires a separate gate. [`core/STATE.md`, current S2 coordinator/runtime adjudication.]

## Facts, assumptions, and unknowns

## Evidence file: design.md (sha256 6febd304cda3079dbc21888ece272d5ae8e4942d769d2e4104f8830fbbf32959)
# S2 exact runtime bundle and revision transition

Sprint: `39b7cc253f5d` (active S2)
Design scope: source/config preparation and a reversible, bootstrap-only artifact transition from the observed runtime `d5001797cb94113efd9a8dc26e4a15f2dc130976` to source revision `9c1be0fbe42b48f7a9cd547be36af23413fcfc8e`. This transition is supported only while the host remains unconfigured; upgrades of configured hosts are refused and deferred to a separately reviewed design.

## Goal and non-goals

Prepare the smallest reproducible, non-secret deployment description and a safe way to select the exact initial runtime revision on the observed unconfigured host, while retaining the previous revision. Keep all S2 services inactive until their separately gated configuration and activation prerequisites pass verification.

This design does not create or impersonate an instruction issuer, sign E5, execute provisioning, migrate or initialize a Store, activate a service, dispatch work, or close S2. It does not add a scheduler, coordinator, or assignment authority: GPT-PM accepted the existing bounded `DispatchOwnerService` → authenticated Supervisor/Store → filtered Pub/Sub → `StoreBackedDispatcher` path; production M01 remains open pending real authorized runtime evidence (`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-coordinator-runtime-adjudication-20261029.md`). The machine issuer/attestor source design is accepted in principle only; production signing and attestation remain gated by the separate trust-contract review recorded by GPT-PM.

## Current behavior and evidence

The point-in-time WSL inventory records `/opt/vst-runtime` resolving to the immutable `d5001797…` directory, and Supervisor, Runner, and Signer units loaded but inactive. It found no Store database by immediate-entry metadata inspection, so Store disposition remains **UNKNOWN**, not “fresh” (`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-runtime-bundle-inventory-20261029.md`). The observed identity and UID/GID availability is not a reservation; repeat collision checks immediately before any authorized identity creation.

`tools/qa/install_wsl_runtime.ps1` packages the committed HEAD and writes a root-only source manifest containing schema, full HEAD, and archive SHA-256. `tools/qa/install_wsl_runner_runtime.sh` installs a versioned `/opt/vst-runtime-<HEAD>` tree with a matching manifest and checks systemd unit bytes. Both installers deliberately fail closed if `/opt/vst-runtime` already selects a different revision or an installed unit differs. They install immutable artifacts; they do not implement revision switching, rollback, or service activation. The old runtime and versioned worker helper are retained and must not be overwritten or deleted. `docs/sdlc/S2_VERSIONED_WORKER_HELPER_DESIGN.md` records the same no-overwrite rule for the helper. The inventory shows `/etc/vst-runner`, `/run/vst-supervisor`, and `/run/vst-runner` absent, and the observed relevant loaded units inactive. This supports only a first-deployment transition while those preconditions still hold; it is not evidence for a configured-host upgrade.

Service loaders are strict contracts, not config generators: Supervisor requires its exact field set (`tools/vst/supervisor_service.py`), Runner binds the full helper commit, source digest, binary digest, and exact versioned helper path (`tools/vst/runner_service.py`), Signer has a separate key/ledger contract (`tools/vst/signer.py`), Dispatcher has fixed Supervisor/Runner socket paths (`tools/vst/dispatcher_service.py`), and Dispatch Owner accepts only the fixed principal/OpenSSL contract plus a root-controlled trust registry (`tools/vst/dispatch_owner_service.py`). `tools/vst/systemd/README.md` documents the root-owned config paths, service identities, startup preflight, inactive-by-default operator peer, schema-v6 migration gate, and unit ordering.

## Design

Keep the deployment description separate from secrets and executable authority. Add one canonical, non-secret bundle manifest during source/config preparation. It binds:

- repository identity, full source HEAD, exact archive SHA-256, `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md` digest, source-manifest schema, and hashes of all six shipped systemd unit files;
- the exact runtime and worker-helper paths, full helper HEAD, helper source and binary digests, and the expected root/group/mode metadata;
- each service config's schema/field set and intended absolute path, owner, group, and mode; fixed service UID/GID and socket/cgroup relationships; and the required unit start order;
- Store disposition as `UNKNOWN`, `FRESH`, or `EXISTING`, with evidence reference. `UNKNOWN` blocks Store initialization, migration, and service activation. It does not block selecting inactive code artifacts because the bootstrap transition neither opens nor changes Store data. An existing Store is read-only inspected and any migration remains behind its separate gate;
- key purpose, custody owner, and expected key-file path only. Never include private key bytes, passwords, tokens, or signing material. Public trust entries may name a verified public-key path and key ID, but must not be fabricated to make validation pass;
- the prior selected runtime, prior unit digests, and rollback target so the transition is reviewable and recoverable.

Config examples produced at this stage are explicitly non-installable templates: values for runtime keys, issuer identity, signed probe, operator attestation, and unresolved Store disposition remain absent. Do not write placeholder JSON into privileged config paths. A schema validator should reject missing values and any unknown field before installation; the existing loaders remain the final runtime contract.

### Ordered operational stages

1. **Source and config preparation (non-privileged).** Finish source changes and their required test/review gates first. Rebuild the archive from the canonical checkout at the exact reviewed HEAD; record archive, sandbox-spec, helper, and unit digests. Prepare the manifest and non-installable schema templates. Reconcile it with the accepted conditional PM scope in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-coordinator-runtime-adjudication-20261029.md`. No WSL state changes.
2. **Artifact staging (conditional GO only).** Recheck host identity and exact old runtime, helper, and unit fingerprints. Require `/etc/vst-runner`, `/run/vst-supervisor`, and `/run/vst-runner` absent; require all six S2 service/socket units inactive, no systemd jobs for them, and no nonempty S2 service cgroups. Verify that the exact new versioned runtime and helper destinations are absent, then install them with no-replace semantics and verify owner, group, mode, manifests, and every digest. Do not create identities, configs, sockets, or Store data in this stage. Store remains UNKNOWN and unopened. Keep every old immutable artifact. Any failed precondition or destination collision aborts before selector or unit changes.
3. **Bootstrap artifact selection (new code required).** Add a separate explicit root transition operation limited to that unconfigured state. It rechecks every staging precondition immediately before mutation and verifies exact old selector/link and fixed-name unit bytes plus exact staged runtime/helper fingerprints against the reviewed manifest. It must refuse if any service config/runtime/socket directory exists, any relevant unit is active/has a job, an S2 cgroup is nonempty, any baseline fingerprint differs, or a destination is unexpected. Preserve old selector and unit bytes as a verified rollback snapshot. Replace the selector and each unit file through same-filesystem temporary files and atomic rename; each individual rename is atomic, while the multi-path set is not one atomic transaction. Record completed replacements in a root-owned transition journal before proceeding to the next path. Re-read and verify all selected paths and fingerprints. Never start, enable, or reload a service as part of selection. This design explicitly refuses configured-host upgrades; support for them needs a later independent cutover/rollback design.
4. **Configuration and Store classification (separately gated).** Only after artifact selection, recheck identities and inspect Store using the authorized procedure. Install exact root-owned configuration only when all values and trust references are known. Store UNKNOWN continues to block initialization, migration, and activation; an EXISTING Store remains read-only until its separate migration gate. Do not generate issuer authority or attestation keys as a side effect of artifact selection.
5. **Service activation (blocked).** Keep units disabled/inactive and production dispatch fail-closed until an authorized issuer policy/key and the applicable accepted machine or human E5 trust contract exist, plus authentic fresh run-bound host/probe evidence passes against the exact sandbox-spec and policy digests. A machine attestation must be explicitly machine-labelled, sourced from independent trusted measurements, and accepted under its own versioned trust domain; it must never masquerade as a human signature. Then, only within the accepted mapped scope and separate activation gate, execute the precise unit activation and runtime E2E sequence. Restricted process/crash/mutation/policy selectors remain `NOT_RUN`.

## State ownership and failure behavior

### Staging and journal implementation contract

Use two different manifests. The reviewed pre-stage source plan binds source HEAD, archive,
sandbox spec, helper source/build recipe, shipped unit bytes and fixed target paths. It does not
claim installed-runtime or compiler-result provenance. After stage-only finishes, a read-only
target-host `prepare` emits a second canonical manifest with the actual complete new tree and
helper binary digests plus the exact old selector/unit/runtime baseline. GPT-PM must review that
second manifest's digest before selector mutation; a locally calculated digest is not approval.

Add an explicit `--stage-only` argument to the distro runtime installer and a corresponding
`-StageOnly` argument to the Windows handoff. Launch the selector with Python `-B -I -S` and
load it from the fixed full-versioned runtime path so importing it cannot create `__pycache__`
inside the immutable measured tree. The repository wrapper must disable bytecode before import.
Default install behavior stays fail-closed and
unchanged. Stage-only validates the same source archive, host restrictions and immutable tree,
installs only the absent versioned runtime/helper, and must skip the fixed selector/unit
collision checks and ALL selector/unit writes. Report `selected=false`; the separate bootstrap
transition consumes the staged tree, never calls the default installer, and verifies its complete
tree against the source bundle plus helper identity before mutation. Stage-only is not selection
or authority to activate anything.

There are two distinct reviewable records. Before staging, a source/staging plan derived from
the committed archive binds HEAD, archive/spec/unit/helper-source hashes, compile flags and
requested fixed destinations; compiler identity and any missing prerequisites remain explicit,
not invented. This reviewed plan and source/test gate are prerequisites to artifact installation.
After staging, a separate read-only `prepare` operation binds the actual complete installed tree,
compiled helper digest/metadata and current old selector/unit baseline. Its exact manifest digest
must be reviewed before selection. A prepared selection manifest cannot retroactively authorize
earlier staging. Neither manifest is a GPT approval, authority delegation or activation permit.

Use a write-ahead journal under a root-owned, mode-0700, no-follow transition directory with
exclusive lock. Before any replacement, persist the exact old and new fingerprints, retained
old bytes/link target, ordered paths and manifest digest; fsync the journal and containing
directory. For each path persist/fsync `intent`, recheck current old fingerprint, rename the
prepared file/link, fsync its parent directory, verify new fingerprint, then persist/fsync
`complete`. A missing completion record never proves a rename did not happen. Recovery checks
EVERY path against old AND new fingerprints, regardless of progress flags: old means untouched
or already restored, new means eligible for exact old restoration, anything else means unresolved
and prohibits writes/start. Refuse an unfinished prior journal on normal apply; explicit recovery
requires its exact original manifest digest and the same inactive/unconfigured preconditions.
Persist/fsync restore intent and completion around each restoration too. Snapshots and journal
are retained, never deleted by successful apply/recovery. No process-crash test is authorized;
later source tests use deterministic injected exceptions only.

The Git source/archive owns revision identity; the root-owned manifest owns the deployment's immutable digest record; systemd owns active unit/process state; the root-controlled Store remains the sole assignment/lease authority; and each root config references purpose-separated key paths without transporting secret bytes in the bundle. No cross-service atomic transaction is assumed. During bootstrap selection, the selector and each fixed-name unit file are changed only while the host is unconfigured and all affected units are inactive. Atomicity applies per rename only. A root-owned journal records progress across the selector and unit replacements. A partial transition fails closed: keep services stopped, inspect which exact renames completed, and restore the prior selector and each old unit file from the verified snapshot before any start. If rollback cannot be proven, leave services inactive and stop for recovery; never claim a collectively atomic replacement. Never infer success from a command exit alone: re-read selector, files, ownership, digests, unit states, and Store/claim disposition.

If the host differs from its reviewed baseline, an unexpected config/key or Store mutation is observed, a key or required signature is unavailable, or any per-path replacement/rollback cannot be proven, stop before modifying that dependency. Store UNKNOWN alone does not block inactive artifact staging/selection, but it blocks any Store initialization, migration, or activation. Preserve all prior runtime/helper artifacts and evidence. No automatic retry may reinterpret an ambiguous dispatch result or reactivate production dispatch.

## Rollback

Before the selector/unit transition, rollback is simply to leave the old selector and units untouched; newly installed versioned artifacts remain retained and inactive. After transition starts but before any service start, use the journal to restore the old selector and each unit file through individual atomic renames, verify their hashes and inactive state, and retain the new immutable tree for diagnosis. These operations are recoverable as a sequence, not one atomic transaction. Once any service starts, do not use this bootstrap rollback as a live downgrade: first reconcile Supervisor/Store/Runner claims and outcomes under the existing recovery contract, then use a separately reviewed and authorized stop/rollback procedure. Never delete or overwrite the old runtime or helper.

## Acceptance and verification plan

The design is accepted when the bundle is deterministic for the exact reviewed HEAD and contains no secret material; schema templates map exactly to existing loaders; Store UNKNOWN/EXISTING states cannot trigger initialization or migration; artifact staging preserves prior artifacts; bootstrap selection refuses a configured host, active/job-bearing units, nonempty S2 cgroups, stale baseline, collision, digest mismatch, and incomplete rollback metadata; the journal recovers interrupted per-path replacements; and no unit is activated by preparation or selection. Configured-host upgrades remain unsupported and must be refused. After implementation is complete, assigned functional/e2e test owners should verify archive/hash binding, schema rejection, no-overwrite behavior, interrupted transition recovery, per-path selector/unit rollback, inactive-unit invariants, refusal on configured hosts, and permitted mapped runtime evidence. No tests, checks, provisioning, migration, or service activation were run for this design artifact.

## Ownership and remaining gate

Codex owns the manifest/schema-preparation and reversible transition implementation plus permitted evidence. GPT-PM owns architecture/source adjudication and the exact-head final gate. The operator is the sole human owner for any human attestation and for genuine key-custody actions. GPT-PM accepted bounded machine trust in principle, but the precise versioned issuer/attestor contracts, independent measurement provenance, key custody/revocation, and separate production authority gate remain incomplete. Until those contracts are reviewed and their applicable evidence is genuine and verified, activation and production dispatch remain blocked, and S2 remains open.

GPT-PM adjudicated the machine issuer/attestor architecture under request `a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55` (reply `0b0b8a4d-0816-4146-ba21-71857b5de49d`): bounded machine trust is accepted in principle, but production signing/attestation remain held pending corrected provenance, independent measurements, and separate authority review. This decision does not authorize production keys, replace the active E5 contract, or activate services. The design must be amended with the precise versioned trust contracts before those components are used.

If the scoped question is genuinely satisfied, say APPROVE even when out-of-scope work remains -- an unrelated open item is not a reason to withhold a verdict on this one.

Apply a devil's-advocate stance throughout: actively look for reasons this change is wrong, unsafe, incomplete, or will break something, rather than defaulting to approval. This does not license inventing problems that aren't real: every objection still needs the same real file/line evidence required above -- if after genuinely trying to find a problem there is none, say so plainly rather than manufacturing a NIT to seem thorough.

+## 2026-10-27 -- Latch the runner after unconfirmed cgroup cleanup

+Decisions: (1) use the hand-written worker only; no external candidate is authorized; (2) only `NOT_RUN`, `INCONCLUSIVE` and `BLOCKED` evidence may receive a named, scoped waiver; `FAIL`, `MODIFY` and `NO_GO` cannot be waived; (3) until a VST store is initialized for this repository, `docs/sdlc/STATE.md` records phase state, then becomes a generated read-only view of the store; (4) reviewer registry trust is rooted in the operator key, and its version/digest is bound by the manifest; (5) command execution, trusted runner and signer have separate OS/IPC boundaries; (6) anchor recovery may append only the single valid event immediately after the checkpoint and remains write-locked on every other mismatch; (7) mandatory parsers are selected from a trusted catalog by id/version/digest; (8) the positive sandbox probe uses only a sandbox-local loopback canary while external egress remains denied; (9) push/PR idempotency is supervisor-only and worker credentials do not permit those operations. Evidence: `docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md` sections 3-10 and `docs/sdlc/STATE.md`; no tests or code checks were run.

+## 2026-10-24 -- S2 anchor serialization and suffix recovery
+
+The database review on code HEAD `d779d55ea0cbb5f391a1f028cbab0345cab7e155` found that one transaction can commit multiple event rows while the external anchor accepted only one-count successors, and that concurrent Store processes/read snapshots could be mistaken for anchor tampering. Source inspection confirmed both paths. The store now serializes anchored writes and authoritative reads with a cross-process sidecar lock; it verifies the complete event chain and resumes a missing anchor suffix only when the existing signed checkpoint is an exact prefix. Anchor-ahead, missing-for-nonempty, forked or malformed state remains locked. No tests/checks were run for this fix; required test-agent scenarios are recorded in change 0043. This supersedes the earlier one-event-only recovery rule in the S2 plan. Source: `docs/changes/0043-s2-external-anchor-concurrency-and-recovery.md`.

+## 2026-10-24 -- S2 strict Windows process starts inside its Job Object
+
+Reliability review found the strict runner's Popen-then-assign ordering allowed command code to spawn a descendant before Job Object membership. Strict Windows launches now use documented `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assign the process to the configured kill-on-close Job Object, and resume the primary thread through documented Toolhelp/OpenThread/ResumeThread APIs. Any setup, assignment, discovery, or resume failure terminates/refuses the command; there is no unsuspended fallback in strict mode. Non-strict behavior remains compatible. Pinned Python 3.14 source inspection confirmed Popen accepts creation flags but closes its primary-thread handle, which is why the implementation uses documented OS APIs instead of CPython private handles. No tests/checks or Windows runtime proof were performed; change record 0046.
+
+## 2026-10-24 -- S2 supervisor state is derived from durable control events
+
+Reliability MAJORs on code HEAD `e67b9ac0c09b1c2dff334dd34d65d67d8c71bf3a`: Supervisor construction reset provider failure count and breaker state, and lifecycle callback intent/outcome existed only in memory. Decision: persist threshold/policy, stable-ID provider outcomes, override records, and lifecycle intent/completion/unknown/reconciliation as reserved typed payloads inside the existing hash-chained `NOTE` event stream; avoid a schema migration. Replay verified controls before any action. A duplicate outcome ID is idempotent; a different breaker policy fails closed. An intent without a confirmed terminal outcome blocks lifecycle work after callback failure or restart. An explicit reconciliation record must include an evidence reference; completion advances state without effect replay, and confirmed non-completion permits only same-ID continuation. Generic caller events cannot emit the reserved marker. Implemented in change record 0047. No tests, builds, CI, migrations or runtime probes were run. A prohibited `git diff --cached --check` was accidentally invoked; it returned empty output and no exit code was provided, so it is not treated as passing. Designated test agents must establish behavior on the exact final head.

+## 2026-10-24 -- S2 lifecycle intent admission is atomic
+
+Follow-up reliability review found that separate Supervisor instances could hold stale `READY` state and both run callbacks after appending distinct intents. Decision: Store derives the current lifecycle state and unresolved actions under its serialized write transaction, verifies the event chain and external checkpoint, validates the requested predecessor state, and appends the intent before releasing the transaction. The rule covers start, stop termination/cleanup, rollback effect/cleanup, and resume. Implemented in change record 0048. No tests/checks/builds/CI/migrations/runtime probes were run; the two-instance regression belongs to the E2E test agent.

+## 2026-10-24 -- S2 idempotent backend operation remediation

+- Root cause: the vendor-neutral worker API models a trusted supervisor call seam, while the repository slice does not define its caller authentication transport.
+- Rule: callers must authenticate before invoking STOP; never claim an actor label is proof. Add an authenticated boundary before exposing this API to an untrusted caller or candidate process.
+- Fix status: limitation explicitly recorded in change record 0088; current worker is local synthetic only, and production/external candidate execution is not authorized.

+# S2 E8 synthetic harness design — 2026-10-28
+
+## Goal
+
+Make the existing helper executable for a narrow, safe synthetic candidate and budget flow, while
+restricted process/crash, STOP/resume, out-of-scope mutation, and external-egress scenarios remain
+`NOT_RUN`. No result represents real sandbox or E8 acceptance. The active source is
+`tools/vst/slice.py` (`HandWrittenWorker` and
+`run_lifecycle_scenarios`); `tests/vst/test_s2_sandbox_probe.py` currently has six unconditional
+E8 skips because real sandbox evidence is absent.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Close VST-020/E8 or replace the real sandbox skip placeholders.
+- Create an E5 signature, real worker identity, external candidate, production coordinator,
+  service configuration or egress boundary.
+- Make an operator candidate choice or claim production isolation from a synthetic fixture.
+
+## Options and decision
+
+1. Leave the existing helper uncalled and E8 wholly untested. This avoids code risk but leaves
+   locally reproducible lifecycle behavior without evidence.
+2. Add a narrow safe synthetic candidate/report contract to the existing helper and test it with
+   temporary repositories and the existing test-owned worker. This yields local evidence while
+   retaining process/crash, STOP/resume, mutation, real E5/E6/S1, external egress, candidate
+   comparison and operator choice as separate gates.
+
+Choose option 2. It reuses the existing helper and avoids a second execution authority. The report
+must label its environment as synthetic and must never return an E8 acceptance PASS. Real E8
+acceptance remains blocked on the provisioned sandbox, valid current-run E5, actual worker path,
+egress evidence and operator decision required by the S2 plan.
+
+## Design
+
+- Extend only `run_lifecycle_scenarios` and its existing synthetic worker helpers.
+- Return a local synthetic candidate head, gate/receipt outcomes and budget rejection. Mark child
+  process exit, process kill, STOP, crash/restart/resume, out-of-scope write attempt and external
+  egress as `NOT_RUN`; do not invoke those scenarios.
+- Record the probe properties that the supplied signed probe actually asserts, but label the
+  provider as caller-supplied; synthetic probe fixtures are not host-boundary evidence.
+- Mark candidate comparison, real blocked-egress attempt and operator choice as unavailable in
+  the synthetic report. Do not infer these from “no remote configured” or a synthetic attestation.
+- Require a fresh, non-existing work directory under the caller-provided temporary parent. Keep all
+  repositories, databases and files beneath that new directory so an existing path cannot be
+  reinitialized or overwritten.
+
+## Failure modes and boundaries
+
+- A report consumer could mistake local results for real E8; prevent this with a stable
+  `environment_scope: synthetic` marker and explicit unavailable fields.
+- A fabricated probe callback could be mistaken for E5; label it caller-supplied and make no
+  environment assertion from it.
+- Do not invoke the child's `os._exit(97)` path, a process restart/recovery path, an out-of-scope
+  write attempt, STOP injection or resume during this focused run. Keep their outcomes `NOT_RUN`.
+- No real network probe, external candidate, persistent service, key or credential is used.
+
+## Verification plan
+
+`functional-test-reviewer` derives focused acceptance tests for the safe synthetic report.
+`e2e-runner` executes them against disposable local repositories and verifies
+cleanup. Relevant code reviewers inspect the final implementation diff. Keep the real E8
+placeholder selectors `NOT_RUN` until a genuine operator-provisioned sandbox and signed current-run
+E5 evidence exist. No production/system check or external candidate run is part of this design.
+
+## Rollout, rollback and ownership
+
+The helper is test-facing and is not activated by production. Revert the focused code/test commit

+# S2 POSIX cross-UID process cleanup design
+
+Status: persistent-service, lifecycle-fence, and fixed UID-drop helper source is implemented in the current working tree but has not been tested, reviewed against the exact final diff, provisioned, or runtime-proven. Earlier exact-head tests and bounded WSL lock/empty-scope observations describe earlier revisions only, 2026-10-27.
+Scope: VST-013 / S2 E4.1 and VST-017 bounded process cleanup in the existing Ubuntu-24.04 WSL sandbox.
+
+## Goal and constraints
+
+The runner must stop a worker and every descendant after timeout, normal root exit, output-reader failure, or runner cleanup, even when runner UID and worker UID differ. Keep the worker's effective/permitted/inheritable/ambient capability sets empty. Do not give the runner broad `CAP_KILL`, use a shell, or fall back to a best-effort success when containment is unavailable.
+
+## Options and decision
+
+1. **Grant `CAP_KILL` to the runner.** Small change, but the capability can signal unrelated processes in the runner's user/PID namespace. Rejected as broader authority than the worker process tree requires.
+2. **Use a systemd-delegated cgroup-v2 child per worker command.** The trusted runner can create and kill only a child cgroup under its own delegated service subtree. Chosen; the scoped destructive boundary matches the process tree.
+3. **Use a fixed narrow identity-drop helper together with systemd cgroup delegation.** The helper does not kill processes or manage cgroups; it accepts only the configured `vst-runner` to `vst-worker` transition, validates two pipe descriptors, clears supplementary groups and capability sets, sets `no_new_privs`, and irreversibly drops privileges. The systemd delegated cgroup remains the only process-tree cleanup authority. This narrow helper is authorized for the selected WSL boundary; its binary provenance and installation still require review and runtime evidence.
+
+## Design
+
+The runner service must have `Delegate=yes` and run on unified cgroup v2. For each POSIX launch using the fixed `vst-runner` (997:988) to `vst-worker` (999:989) identity boundary, the runner creates a unique child cgroup under its delegated cgroup and requires `cgroup.procs`, `cgroup.events`, and `cgroup.kill`. It starts the fixed root-owned `/usr/local/libexec/vst-s4-worker-exec` helper, which accepts only the exact runner identity, worker gate, and two pipe descriptors. The helper clears supplementary groups and capabilities, irreversibly drops to the worker identity, sets `no_new_privs`, closes every descriptor except standard streams and the two validated pipes, and runs the isolated (`python -I -S`) exec gate. No UID, GID, environment, shell, or executable path is accepted from the caller. The gate starts with a fixed environment containing no loader hooks or Python startup controls. The intended worker environment is sent as data through a separate inherited pipe, never as the helper/gate process environment. The gate waits on a second inherited pipe; the worker command has not executed yet. The runner moves the gated process PID into the child cgroup, starts output readers, then releases the gate to `execvpe` the manifest-pinned argv with the supplied worker environment. Descendants inherit the cgroup even if they change session or process group.
+
+On timeout, root-command exit, reader failure, or exceptional cleanup, the runner writes `1` only to that current run's `cgroup.kill`, waits for `cgroup.events` to report `populated 0`, reaps the root process, closes capture pipes, and removes the empty child cgroup. Each command owns a unique scope; concurrent commands in one process never share a kill target. A private `/run/vst-runner` directory is provisioned for the daemon with mode 0710 and the dispatcher group; the daemon-owned admission lock is mode 0600. The runner holds `cgroup-admission.lock` with an exclusive POSIX `flock` across stale-scope reconciliation, command admission, execution, and cleanup. Under that lock it inspects only strict `vst-command-<pid>-<uuid>` child scopes under its delegated cgroup. Empty scopes are removed only after bounded `populated 0` and empty `cgroup.procs` confirmation. Populated, unknown, inaccessible, or unremovable scopes refuse admission and are never killed or adopted. A root-only manager fence records BOOTSTRAP_EMPTY, RUNNING, STOPPED_EMPTY, or UNVERIFIED transitions, exact systemd invocation and cgroup identity, lock/cgroup inodes, and a hash-chained audit record. The runner accepts only a matching root-owned published RUNNING snapshot. Windows continues to use the existing Job Object path. The all-descendant guarantee applies to distinct-UID worker launches that use this cgroup path; same-UID compatibility calls retain the legacy process-group behavior and are outside this S2 acceptance guarantee.
+
+## Failure behavior
+
+- Missing unified cgroup v2, missing `Delegate=yes`, unwritable delegated parent, or absent cgroup control files: refuse to execute a distinct-UID worker and return a non-approving containment result.
+- Failure to attach the gated PID: close the gate without releasing the requested command, reap the no-op trampoline, and return non-approving. The trampoline runs only with the fixed sanitized environment until attached, so inherited dynamic-loader variables cannot execute code before containment.
+- Failure to kill/reap the cgroup or confirm `populated 0`: return `EXIT_CAPTURE_INCOMPLETE`, preserve diagnostics, never report PASS, and stop launching later commands from the same manifest run.
+- Distinct-UID launches are serialized both within one process and across processes by the private runtime lock. Waiting for the lock and reconciling abandoned scopes consume the same per-command/overall time budget. If the budget expires while queued or reconciling, the runner returns timeout without creating a cgroup or starting a process. If a scope's kill/removal remains unconfirmed, latch the failure and refuse subsequent launches from that process; a replacement runner must first acquire the same stable lock and reconcile every stale runner-owned scope. The service must use one stable delegated subtree and stop all pre-lock runner instances before rollout; a runner in a different subtree cannot prove or clean scopes in the old subtree.
+- The exec-gate environment handoff is nonblocking and shares the command deadline. If the gate cannot receive the environment before the deadline, close the gate and kill its cgroup without releasing worker code.
+- Do not add `CAP_KILL` as a fallback. The outer service timeout is only emergency cleanup, not acceptance evidence.
+
+## Rollout and rollback
+
+Provision the runner systemd service/scope with `Delegate=yes`, a stable delegated subtree, and `RuntimeDirectory=vst-runner` with mode `0710` (runner owner and dispatcher group); retain the existing memory, task, time, private-network and temp-filesystem limits. The service must ensure only the lock-aware runner version can start in that subtree. Validate delegation, private lock ownership, restart recovery, and stale-scope reconciliation before enabling worker commands. Rollback reverts the code/config contract and leaves cross-UID POSIX execution refused; it does not restore broad process-kill capability.
+
+## Verification plan and owners
+
+- `functional-test-reviewer`: maintain a temp-only acceptance test where UID 997 runner launches UID 999 worker, a bounded descendant writes a heartbeat, timeout cleanup stops it, and the descendant self-exits within six seconds if cleanup fails; also cover fail-closed gate handoff timeout and stopping later manifest commands after incomplete cleanup.
+- `e2e-runner`: execute that selector in the existing Ubuntu-24.04 WSL profile with `Delegate=yes`; record exact source/test head, cgroup path/properties, capabilities, command, result, and cleanup.
+- `functional-test-reviewer`: author deterministic helper tests for unavailable delegation and gated-launch failure; Codex implements least-privilege cleanup and reconciles the systemd sandbox specification and evidence.
+- Fresh reliability/security/architecture reviewers: inspect the exact post-test head; no real process result may be upgraded from the scoped WSL profile to general platform proof.
+- GPT-PM: exact final S2 gate only after remaining acceptance evidence is ready.
+
+## Unknowns
+
+The initial read-only systemd preflight established that this WSL host can run a transient `Delegate=yes` unit whose cgroup directory is writable by `vst-runner` and exposes `cgroup.kill`. Exact-head evidence at `a6ea0dc` subsequently established a runner-owned mode-0700 `/run/vst-runner`, real cross-process `flock` serialization, and removal of a synthetic stale scope only after confirming `populated=0` and empty `cgroup.procs`; see `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-restart-fence-exact-a6ea0dc-20261027.md`. A separate bounded read-only namespace observer found no Windows-drive or host-backed mount candidates in its 29-row view; details and limits are in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-current-namespace-snapshot-a6ea0dc-20261027.md`. These observations do not establish a persistent runner service, stable delegated-parent behavior across replacement, populated-scope cleanup, runner crash/restart recovery, Windows Job Object nesting, or a complete signed E5 preflight.
+
+Change 0470 proposes a dedicated persistent manifest-runner service; its first GPT-PM adjudication
+returned `MODIFY` with three MAJOR and one MINOR design findings. The revised proposal now records
+the required manager-mediated predecessor stop/fence, the Supervisor/Store grant issuer and
+fail-closed key lifecycle, and a daemon-only OS execution boundary with grant plus durable
+pre-dispatch claim. This remains a proposal: it is not approved, implemented, provisioned, or
+runtime-proven. See `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-persistent-runner-service-design-20261027.md` and the
+correlated decision IDs recorded there.
+
+## Attribution
+
+Executor: Codex. Change 0470 records the approved design only; the source implementation is
+tracked separately in change 0471 and does not establish acceptance without assigned evidence.
+
+## Persistent runner entry point follow-up
+
+Repository inspection at documentation HEAD `2da827b` found `run_manifest_commands` only as a
+library entry point; `Supervisor.start_worker` accepts a caller callback and does not host or
+dispatch manifest runs. The current working tree now adds a bounded foreground daemon and
+authenticated local Unix-socket contract, signed one-use run grants, atomic pre-dispatch `PENDING`
+claims, non-replayable `INDETERMINATE` recovery, signer-side peer-cgroup enforcement, and
+race-resistant peer PID binding with `SO_PEERPIDFD`. These source controls are implemented but

+# Operator guide: provision the S2 worker sandbox
+
+Status: dedicated Ubuntu-24.04 WSL2 provisioned and accepted for the recorded per-run E5 correlation; persistent production deployment is not claimed. The operator selected WSL2 and delegated autonomous execution to Codex. The final signed inventory and attestation passed for one fresh run, but this does not waive remaining E4/E8 limits or qualify other environments. See `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-e5-operator-attestation.json` and `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-e5-runmanifest-wsl-280e2d0.md`.
+
+## Recommended setup
+
+Use a dedicated WSL2 distribution only when its network, filesystem, and identity boundaries can be enforced and evidenced. Otherwise use a dedicated VM with equivalent or stronger isolation. Do not repurpose the interactive development distribution or mount the repository's parent directory.
+
+For this delegated run, the operator is the accountable task owner and Codex is the executor. The repository does not identify a named infrastructure service owner; that technical ownership remains unknown. Evidence records distinguish Codex's execution/signing from independent human approval; no independent human review is claimed.
+
+## Provisioning sequence
+
+1. Create a dedicated WSL2 distribution or VM for this project. Keep its image and mutable runtime state outside the repository. Record the environment name, image/version or VM identity, host platform, and provisioning date in the private operator handoff; do not put personal paths, secrets, or host identifiers in public repository files.
+2. Configure the network boundary before starting a worker. Deny outbound traffic including DNS and indirect routes by default. Do not add an external allowlist entry for S2. Permit only the probe's ephemeral sandbox-local `127.0.0.1` canary. Record the firewall/network policy and the control that enforces it. Prepare an operator-root-signed attestation bound to the run ID, spec SHA-256 and fresh nonce; include environment identity, policy SHA-256, private evidence SHA-256, `empty_external_allowlist=true`, `no_container_socket=true`, and `no_unapproved_host_paths=true`. The supervisor validates this signature independently. The reserved-address connection is only a smoke probe and cannot establish the policy.
+3. For WSL, set `/etc/wsl.conf` so Windows drive automount is disabled and Windows/Linux interoperability is disabled (`[automount] enabled=false`; `[interop] enabled=false`, `appendWindowsPath=false`). Restart the distribution after changing this file. Confirm that no Windows drive, host home directory, Windows executable path, or host credential store is visible. If these controls cannot be enforced, use a VM.
+4. Create distinct unprivileged identities for worker, runner, signer, supervisor, and read-only reviewer. Do not run the worker as root. Keep the worker out of the runner group and drop supplementary groups at launch. The reviewer must have read-only access to the worktree and no store write access.
+5. Keep all six S2 trust roots pairwise distinct: worker, supervisor, operator, event, reviewer, and runner-signer. The runner's OS identity is separate from the signer key root; only that runner identity may use signer IPC. Store keys outside the worker mount. The signer key must be readable only by the signer identity (POSIX mode `0600`). Place the Unix signer socket under a signer-owned directory with traversal restricted to the runner group (directory `0710`; socket group-owned by the runner group with mode `0660`). Do not copy signer or operator credentials into the worker environment.
+6. Ensure there is no Docker/Podman/container-engine socket, host socket, or host path exposed to the worker. Mount only a per-run workspace. Provide only short-lived, run-scoped credentials required by the fixture and remove them during cleanup.
+7. Set and record CPU quota, memory ceiling, process-count limit, disk quota, and wall-clock deadline before any worker run. Missing limits block launch. Verify the host's process containment behavior; unsupported Windows Job Object nesting must refuse execution.
+8. From the provisioned target, execute the repository's standard-library pre-flight probe using the actual sandbox configuration and a fresh run ID and nonce, supplying the signed network-policy attestation. Preserve its runner-signed inventory, operator-signed attestation, exact command, interpreter/version, probe output, spec SHA-256, run ID, nonce, environment identity, and code HEAD. Do not substitute a hand-written or synthetic inventory. If any socket inventory source cannot be enumerated, launch is refused.
+9. Confirm that the probe records all required properties in `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md`: mount table, interop state, user/group identity, container socket paths, denied external target, successful local loopback canary, and environment variable names. A reachable external endpoint, failed loopback, root UID, exposed host path/socket, missing field, invalid signature, or stale run binding is a failed pre-flight.
+10. Return the private provisioning evidence and signed inventory to the project coordinator. The coordinator records only non-sensitive identifiers and hashes in the repository, verifies the signature and binding, and leaves every unproven property `NOT_RUN`.
+
+## Acceptance record
+
+The handoff must contain:
+
+- Environment identity and type (dedicated WSL2 distribution or VM), image/version, and host platform.
+- Evidence that automount/interoperability are disabled when using WSL, or equivalent VM isolation evidence.
+- Network policy showing default-deny egress, DNS/indirect-route denial, and no external allowlist for S2.
+- User/group and key/socket permission evidence, with secret material withheld.
+- Resource limits and evidence of their enforcement.
+- Evidence that no host drive, host credential store, container socket, or unapproved path is mounted into the worker.
+- Fresh signed probe inventory bound to run ID, nonce, `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md` digest, and exact code HEAD.
+- Operator-root-signed network-policy attestation bound to the same run ID, nonce and spec digest; policy and evidence hashes are retained, while sensitive evidence remains private.
+- Explicit result for process containment and reviewer read-only enforcement.
+
+The recorded E5 per-run acceptance is documented above; this guide alone does not approve persistent deployment or all E5-E8 criteria. Windows Job Object nesting, process-kill/kill-table scenarios, and full E8 crash/resume remain `NOT_RUN` with their exact constraints in the S2 state and evidence records.

+- S7.2 Idempotency keys at the trusted supervisor/coordinator boundary for simulated push, pull request and receipt creation: a durable `PENDING` intent is committed before the local bare-Git callback runs outside the Store write transaction and anchor lock; a completion event records its canonical result. Store verifies the signature and episode inside atomic action admission before invoking the recorder, then rechecks the same episode atomically before appending the breaker-clearing event. A stale signed record cannot clear a later pause episode, and a completed action ID cannot be replayed with a different signed record. Provider outcomes and the threshold/policy are durable, stable-ID control NOTE events replayed at supervisor startup; duplicate outcome IDs cannot inflate counts, a changed policy fails closed, and worker start checks the durable breaker state atomically with lifecycle intent admission.
+- S7.4 Startup reconciliation after restart: leases, slots, in-flight attempts and anchors are reconciled before any new lease; orphaned attempts become `INCONCLUSIVE(WORKER_LOST)`. A callback exception or missing completion leaves an ambiguous action that blocks further lifecycle actions and restart; it is never assumed side-effect-free. Same-ID continuation is allowed only after an operator-key-signed resolution record binds the action, attempt, outcome, external evidence ID and evidence SHA-256; unsigned booleans or references cannot unblock retries. A resolution confirming completion advances the replayed state without calling the effect again; a confirmed STOP/rollback stage resumes the remaining cleanup after restart.

+- Denominator: every state-event pair in the table; every operation kind with an idempotency key; each breaker state; provider failure/success/override replay across restart and duplicate IDs; override signature invalid, tampered, replayed after a later pause episode, and valid signed-record cases; breaker threshold mismatch and stale-supervisor breaker check; lifecycle intent/completion/unknown/reconciliation, including STOP and rollback continuation after restart; concurrent starts from separate Supervisor/Store instances sharing one store; signed and unsigned reconciliation cases.
+- Must reject: a STOP event in a state where the table has no entry; a duplicate push key causing a second push; a worker start while the durable breaker is open; a stale provider success closing a paused breaker; a lease started before reconciliation completes; generic NOTE forgery of a reserved control event; duplicate outcome IDs with changed payload; callback retry with a different action ID while the prior outcome is ambiguous; reconciliation without a valid operator signature and evidence digest; a second lifecycle intent whose expected predecessor state or unresolved-action guard fails, before its callback executes.

+## 10. Decisions required before implementation
+
+The following contracts are binding for S2 implementation and test design:
+
+1. The operator key is the trust root for the signed reviewer registry; the manifest binds its exact registry version and content digest. Registry validation fails closed.
+2. The worker identity cannot read signing keys or reach signer IPC. After the UID/GID transition, it must not retain effective, permitted, inheritable, or ambient capabilities that could cross into the signer identity. Only the runner identity may submit a canonical signing request; the signer signs runner-derived evidence and rejects malformed or replayed requests.
+3. A cross-process coordinator lock serializes each anchored SQLite transaction with its external checkpoint synchronization and authoritative reads with their checkpoint comparison. After a crash, recovery may append a multi-event suffix only when the database's full HMAC chain verifies and the external checkpoint matches the exact event prefix; checkpoints are appended sequentially. An anchor ahead of the database, a fork, missing anchor for non-empty data, malformed checkpoint history, or any failed append stays write-locked and fail-closed pending operator recovery. The lock file is stored beside the external anchor and outside the worker mount.
+4. Mandatory result parsers are selected from a trusted catalog by manifest-pinned id, version, and digest; caller-supplied parser callables are removed from the acceptance path.
+5. Egress is deny-by-default. The positive pre-flight probe targets an ephemeral loopback canary inside the sandbox; it does not grant external network access.
+6. Idempotent push/PR simulation belongs to the supervisor/coordinator boundary. The worker has no credential or path that can push or open a PR.
+7. S2 does not authorize an external bake-off candidate. The hand-written worker is the only candidate unless separate operator authorization is recorded.
+8. Only `NOT_RUN`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, and `BLOCKED` can receive the separately recorded waiver verdict; failure or reviewer rejection cannot.
+9. Introduce an explicit manifest contract version 2. Add `reviewer_registry: {version, sha256}`, `mandatory_commands: [{slot, argv, parser_id, parser_version, parser_sha256}]`, and `change_scope: {allowed_paths}`. Include them in the canonical manifest hash. Unknown versions and unrecognized fields fail closed.
+10. A signed reviewer registry has `{version, entries:[{principal, key_id}], signature}`; its digest is calculated from canonical entries, excluding the signature. `IndependentReview` adds `reviewer_key_id`. The gate validates registry signature, version and digest against the manifest, principal/key mapping, reviewer/author separation, and receipt signature.
+11. Runner submits one exact-field signing request containing `{request_id, task_id, slot, attempt, epoch, manifest_sha256, candidate_head, commands:[{argv, exit_code}], parser_results, artifact_digests}`. The runner derives the head after execution. The signer authenticates the runner OS identity, accepts a request ID once, returns the original signature for an identical request, and rejects reuse with a different payload. Commands cannot access signer IPC.
+12. Parser selection uses a trusted built-in catalog keyed by `(parser_id, version, sha256)`. The manifest can select only a catalog entry; caller-supplied parser callables are not accepted by the runner or gate.
+13. External anchoring uses `read_latest()` and compare-and-append semantics. Every public compare-and-append call acquires the same cross-process sidecar coordinator lock used by the store; nested calls within an anchored Store transaction are reentrant. The JSONL checkpoint file is not separately byte-locked. The store serializes each SQLite commit and its external checkpoint synchronization with that coordinator lock. It appends each event checkpoint in order after commit. Startup verifies the full keyed chain, then may recover any contiguous committed suffix only if the stored external checkpoint matches the exact database prefix. Authoritative read snapshots share the coordinator lock, so concurrent writes cannot turn a valid checkpoint advance into an integrity lock. Any true mismatch or recovery failure remains locked pending operator recovery.
+14. A diff check returns `{diff_sha256, changed_paths, verdict, reason}` from manifest digest, base head, candidate head, and allowed paths. Normalize paths; reject traversal, out-of-scope paths, blocked file classes, unsafe renames, and symlink changes. Bind this evidence to the required v2 receipt.
+15. A probe receipt binds `{run_id, spec_sha256, nonce, checked_properties, result}` and is fresh for that run. It includes an operator-root-signed network policy attestation bound to the same run/spec/nonce and carrying environment identity, policy/evidence SHA-256 digests, an empty external allowlist, and explicit no-container-socket/no-unapproved-host-path evidence. Supervisor verifies this attestation independently; the one reserved-target connection is only a limited smoke probe and cannot prove egress policy. Socket enumeration covers known engine endpoints, every numeric per-user runtime directory, and `/proc/net/unix`, and fails closed if incomplete. The operator key is never exposed to the worker/analyzer; all six roots remain pairwise distinct. Supervisor reconciliation and anchor recovery complete before lease acquisition. Idempotency keys bind both operation and payload: identical retries return the prior result; key reuse with a different payload fails.
+16. Keep v1 signed bodies and hashes immutable. V2 validation is explicit; v1 evidence never passes a v2 gate. Any store migration preserves event/receipt bytes and chain hashes; failure leaves the store read-only and acceptance blocked. Do not reconstruct an external anchor from the database.
+17. Receipt authority is type-specific: only the signer key signs runner-produced `TestRun`; the registry-mapped reviewer key signs `IndependentReview`; worker or supervisor keys sign `StaticAnalysis` and `Documentation` according to slot; the operator key signs registry/waiver authority; the event key signs event checkpoints and never acts as a receipt signer. All six key roots are pairwise distinct.

+# Sprint S3 plan: vendor-neutral worker pilot
+
+Status: **PREPARED; NOT STARTED**. This document is a next-sprint plan only. It authorizes no candidate acquisition, installation, cloning, additional sandbox provisioning, production use, or S3 test execution.
+
+Baseline reference: S2 source head `dc95915018b80f498d5cf775363712fb915fe04e` on branch `s2-isolated-worker-sandbox`. The functional recovery-module rerun at source `dc959` recorded 4 passed / 0 skipped (record 0085). The focused Windows runner/store E2E run recorded 80 passed / 14 skipped and the POSIX flock test recorded 1 passed under `vst-runner` in the selected Ubuntu-24.04 WSL2 (record 0083). Earlier E2E results at `ed531` include 3 Windows snapshot-identity failures; the following source fix `dc959` passed the focused suite. Fresh security and reliability reviews found no source blocker; the database review likewise found no MAJOR, while confirming that abrupt-crash child cleanup and filesystem quotas remain unverified. Earlier S2 Windows/WSL evidence is recorded at source head `280e2d0a613a0b70252c13ce7afe85f22734f7d1`; it is evidence for that head only. The selected dedicated Ubuntu-24.04 WSL2 environment has per-run E5 evidence, not persistent deployment proof. S2 retains explicit `NOT_RUN` criteria for process-kill/kill-table, post-start overflow cleanup, Windows Job Object nesting, full POSIX containment, and complete E8 crash/resume. OS memory and per-run filesystem quotas, source-workspace binding, and external-writer exclusion are `NOT_VERIFIED`; production qualification requires those environmental limits. Reconcile the final S2 state before S3 worker execution; no S2 result is inherited as an S3 acceptance pass.
+
+Sources: `docs/sdlc/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION_PROMPT_S2_S5.md` section 1; `docs/UNIFIED_ENGINEERING_ORGANIZATION_MASTER_BLUEPRINT_2026-10-23.md` sections 6, 10, 13.2-13.4; `docs/DESIGN_BASELINE_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-10-24.md` section 4; S2 interfaces and prerequisites in `docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`; ADR-0001 (`docs/ADR_0001_TEST_AUTHORITY_MODELS_CI_NOT_RUN_2026-10-24.md`). Where the blueprint names an OpenHands/Aider comparison, this S3 plan follows the later explicit continuation: BMad Loop, a hand-written worker, and one durable engine (Temporal provisionally).
+
+## 1. Goal and scope
+
+Run one synthetic story through one isolated story adapter on the S2 sandbox. Compare three worker implementations on the same fixture and evidence contract:
+
+1. BMad Loop.
+2. A hand-written worker loop.
+3. Temporal as the provisional durable-engine candidate from the project's in-scope candidate set.
+
+The comparison is about recovery and safety behavior, not an overall product ranking. The adapter interface remains vendor-neutral, and the VST control plane remains the only phase, acceptance, and receipt authority. No candidate may approve its own work or write authoritative VST state.
+
+Out of scope: more than one story, concurrency/scale, live repositories or customer data, push/merge, unattended workers, candidate auto-fallback, public-network access, unreviewed candidate acquisition, CI, mutation runs, process-kill/kill-table tests, and a “TOP” designation before all comparison evidence and the operator decision exist. Follow ADR-0001: skipped or unavailable tests are `NOT_RUN`, never a pass; no mutation or CI checks are run.
+
+## 2. Entry conditions and dependencies
+
+### 2.1 S2 acceptance dependency

In particular, verify the signed gate/store contracts, retry and lease fencing, STOP behavior, deterministic diff gate, reviewer credential boundary, signer separation, external anchor, and startup reconciliation. Record every unavailable scenario as `NOT_RUN` with its exact environment/dependency.

The sandbox must have a fresh passing probe tied to the run id, default-deny egress, no host path outside the run directory, no container-engine socket, non-root worker identity, and no worker signing key or signer IPC access. Do not simulate this evidence. If the sandbox is unavailable, finish documentation and platform-independent fixture work, and mark sandbox-dependent execution `NOT_RUN`.
+
+### 2.3 Candidate acquisition gate
+
+The candidates are **not yet identified by immutable revision**. Before acquiring any candidate, create an audit record for each one containing:
+
+- exact upstream identity (canonical repository/project and owner);

+- license identifier and the in-scope license text/source reviewed;
+- dependency and install/build inputs, including hash-lock feasibility;

Do not clone, install, update, or execute any candidate while preparing this plan. If audit prerequisites cannot be satisfied, that candidate is `NOT_RUN`; do not substitute a different durable engine silently.
+
+## 3. Vendor-neutral adapter contract
+
+One isolated `StoryWorkerAdapter` translates the stable VST run request into the selected backend and returns typed status/evidence. Backend-specific task state must not become a second VST state authority.
+
+| Operation | Input | Observable result and invariant |
+|---|---|---|
+| `start` | run id, story manifest digest, candidate id/revision, sandbox run id, epoch/fence, budget, allowed paths | One attempt is created with a stable operation/idempotency key. Duplicate identical start returns the same attempt. A conflicting payload under that key is rejected. No start occurs if stopped, unreconciled, over budget, or sandbox probe is stale/failed. |
+| `status` | run id and attempt id | Returns a typed state (`QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `STOPPED`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `BLOCKED`) plus bounded progress/evidence references. It does not turn missing evidence into success. |
+| `stop` | run id, attempt id, reason, authorized actor | Idempotently records STOP and prevents later writes/receipts from the stopped epoch. The adapter returns only after stop state is observable or reports timeout/partial stop as `INCONCLUSIVE`; it does not claim cleanup succeeded without evidence. |
+| `resume` | run id, prior attempt id, current epoch/fence, remaining budget | Creates a new attempt/epoch after VST reconciliation. It binds to the prior receipt chain and current candidate revision. It cannot reuse an earlier epoch receipt, repeat completed side effects, or resume a stopped attempt without an allowed transition. |
+
+All calls are bounded by explicit time/cost budgets and carry `run_id`, `attempt_id`, `candidate_id`, `candidate_revision`, manifest digest, epoch/fence, invocation id, and sandbox run id. Adapter errors are typed and visible; provider/model fallback is prohibited unless separately recorded as an authorized manual override and never represented as an ordinary approval.
+
+## 4. Epics and stories
+

+- AC-3: VST remains the sole owner of phase state, attempt fencing, required receipt set, and final verdict; the worker cannot self-approve.
+- AC-4: An unavailable status, malformed response, or unsupported backend state remains non-approving and diagnosable.

+- AC-7: No worker receives signing keys, signer IPC, push credentials, store write credentials, or unrestricted host paths.
+- AC-8: External egress is denied; only the explicitly permitted sandbox-local loopback canary may succeed.

+### E3 — Shared crash/resume and STOP fixture
+
+**S3.3.1** Implement a deterministic synthetic repository fixture with checkpointed interruption inside the worker loop. The interruption is an application-level injected crash/restart at a named checkpoint; do not use prohibited process-kill or kill-table runs.
+
+**S3.3.2** Exercise STOP, retry, resume, budget, worktree isolation, and evidence-chain transitions on the same initial repository state for all candidates.
+
+Acceptance:
+
+- AC-9: A crash after an edit but before receipt leaves no false PASS; restart reconciles state and resumes only with a new fenced attempt.
+- AC-10: STOP is idempotent; after STOP, writes from the stopped attempt and late receipts cannot change the accepted candidate state.
+- AC-11: A failed attempt remains visible after a later PASS; retry count never exceeds the manifest cap; duplicate operation keys do not repeat effects.
+- AC-12: Budget zero starts no worker; exact-cap work may complete only under the documented boundary; any operation that would exceed budget is blocked and recorded without exceeding the cap.
+- AC-13: Candidate edits are confined to the run worktree and manifest allowlist; worktrees for candidates/attempts are isolated and cleanup/retention outcome is recorded.
+- AC-14: An attempted write outside the allowed paths, including a protected hook/config/manifest path, fails the diff gate and cannot yield APPROVE.
+- AC-15: External egress attempt fails closed; no public-network target is used as a positive probe.

+| S2 E5 / blueprint 13.4: sandbox preflight, default-deny egress and least privilege | AC-5..8, AC-15 | Fresh run-bound probe required; stale/missing probe blocks; worker key/signer/store access denied; blocked external target denied; local loopback canary succeeds; no host path/socket leak | Real sandbox E2E and signed probe inventory | Requires operator-provisioned S2 sandbox; no fake inventory |
+| S2 E6 / blueprint 13.4: diff gate before review and read-only reviewer | AC-7, AC-13, AC-14 | Out-of-scope, traversal, symlink, rename-to-hook, CI/config/lockfile/manifest/install-script changes rejected; reviewer cannot write worktree/store | Diff-gate unit plus sandbox identity integration | Requires verified S2 E6 and actual read-only credential boundary |
+| S2 E7: STOP, idempotency, circuit breaker and startup reconciliation | AC-2, AC-9..11 | Stop/retry/resume transitions; repeated operation key causes no second effect; conflicting payload fails; breaker open prevents start and silent fallback; reconciliation precedes lease | State-machine unit and store/adapter integration | Requires verified S2 E7 contracts; any uncovered transition remains open |
+| Candidate audit requirements in this plan | AC-5..8 | Missing immutable SHA/license/compatibility/security record prevents acquisition; attempt to start an unaudited or mismatched revision is rejected | Static audit plus adapter start contract test | Candidate acquisition remains prohibited until separately authorized after audit |
+| Same-fixture comparison and no “TOP” before evidence | AC-1, AC-5, AC-9..15 | For each candidate, preserve identical fixture seed, checkpoints, budget, scope, and environment; compare outcome/evidence completeness; missing candidate result is `NOT_RUN`; no ranking label until all required rows are reviewed | Deterministic comparison record and independent review | Temporal revision/license/compatibility currently UNKNOWN; candidate set not acquired |
+
+### Scenario denominator
+
+For **each** of the three candidates, record these outcomes on the same fixture. An unavailable candidate or environment is a named `NOT_RUN`, not removed from the denominator:
+
+1. Clean start, status progression, completion, and signed gate outcome.
+2. Application-level crash at each declared checkpoint, restart, reconciliation, and resume.
+3. STOP before start, during execution, after edit/before receipt, duplicate STOP, and late write/receipt.
+4. Retry after failure, retry-cap boundary, duplicate operation key, and key reuse with changed payload.
+5. Budget at zero, exactly at cap, and one unit over cap.
+6. Allowed worktree edit; outside-scope write; protected hook/config/manifest/install-script change; rename into a blocked path; symlink change.
+7. Worker attempt to read signer/key/store/push credentials or write outside the scoped worktree.
+8. Blocked external egress and permitted sandbox-local loopback canary.
+9. Fresh versus stale/missing sandbox probe and exact candidate revision mismatch.
+10. Evidence chain integrity: missing receipt, stale epoch receipt, invalid signature, modified artifact, and prior failed attempt retained after a later pass.
+
+Each result records candidate id + commit SHA, fixture version/seed, sandbox probe/run id, manifest hash, attempt/epoch, exact command or adapter request, expected and observed result, receipt references, test ID, test command, interpreter, HEAD, dirty note, and whether it ran or is `NOT_RUN` with exact cause.
+
+## 6. Candidate comparison and decision rule
+
+The comparison table has one row per scenario and candidate, including `NOT_RUN` rows. Compare recovery correctness, STOP behavior, retry/budget enforcement, worktree confinement, unauthorized access attempts, egress, evidence completeness, restart determinism, and operator-visible failure modes. Do not combine missing evidence with success and do not score candidates on speed alone.
+
+No candidate receives a “TOP” label until:
+
+1. all candidates have immutable identity/revision and completed license/compatibility/security audits;
+2. each required scenario is either runtime-proven or explicitly `NOT_RUN` with its dependency;
+3. independent reviewers reconcile the comparison and open findings;
+4. the operator records a decision on the chosen worker and accepted residual gaps.
+
+The durable engine is Temporal for this plan, provisionally. If the pin, license or compatibility audit fails, report the exact blocker; do not silently choose a replacement. The operator owns candidate acquisition authorization and final worker choice; implementation, functional-test and E2E roles execute only after S3 is accepted and its entry gates are met.
+
+## 7. Definition of Ready
+
+- S2 exact-head acceptance evidence has been reviewed and reconciled; code presence alone is insufficient.
+- Operator has provisioned the dedicated sandbox and a fresh probe passes on the intended environment.
+- Candidate identity, immutable commit, license, compatibility, dependency and security audit records exist for BMad Loop, the hand-written loop implementation, and Temporal. Candidate acquisition has explicit authorization; no unpinned upstream is introduced.
+- One synthetic story and deterministic crash/resume fixture are specified, including checkpoints, inputs, expected state transitions, idempotency keys, and allowed paths.
+- Adapter contract, S2 state/gate integration points, test ownership, budget semantics, STOP table and evidence format are reviewed.
+- Test scenarios map to every S3 AC and have valid and invalid fixtures. Test agents confirm the focused command set without running it before coding is complete.
+
+## 8. Definition of Done
+
+- One story adapter provides vendor-neutral `start/status/stop/resume`; VST remains the sole state and acceptance authority.
+- The same fixture and scenario denominator has been run for the three candidates, or every unavailable row is explicitly `NOT_RUN` with exact cause.
+- Crash/resume, STOP, retries, budget zero/exact/over, worktree confinement, unauthorized writes, and egress outcomes satisfy AC-9..15; no weak/partial run is described as a pass.
+- Candidate immutable identity, commit, license, compatibility and security audit are linked to all run evidence.
+- Diff gate and reviewer isolation reject unauthorized writes and access; sandbox probe is fresh and tied to each run.
+- Complete focused functional tests run after each epic and once again on the exact final committed head by the authorized test agents. Evidence includes test IDs, exact commands, interpreter, count, environment, HEAD, dirty note, result, and `NOT_RUN` limitations.
+- Relevant specialist reviews have no open valid BLOCKER/MAJOR; final exact-head approval is recorded before push/PR under project process.
+- The comparison and explicit operator decision are recorded. No “TOP” label appears before these gates pass.
+- Change record, decision/lessons logs, backlog, state, document registry and sprint report are updated as required by the project workflow.
+
