+# Sprint S4 plan: reproducible QA automation
+
+Status: **PREPARED; NOT STARTED**. This document defines the next sprint and authorizes no tests, builds, CI, installs, mutations, seeded product-code defects, or external service calls during preparation.
+
+Sources: `docs/sdlc/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION_PROMPT_S2_S5.md` section 1; `docs/ADR_0001_TEST_AUTHORITY_MODELS_CI_NOT_RUN_2026-10-24.md`; `governance/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`; S2 and S3 plans; current `tests/vst/`, `tools/vst/runner.py`, `tools/vst/slice.py`, and `tools/vst/{contracts,gate,store}.py`.
+
+## Goal and scope
+
+Wire reproducible, category-specific native test runs for the repository's functional, integration, Python API, end-to-end, regression, and seeded-failure scenarios, with exact test-ID accounting and machine-readable artifacts; any skipped or uncollected required test makes the result non-approving.
+
+The repository currently has Python tests under `tests/vst/`, using both pytest-style tests and unittest-compatible tests. Existing S2 modules exercise VST contracts, gate, runner, store, lifecycle, and sandbox-probe interfaces. This plan treats the Python module boundary as the API surface: no HTTP or other network service is evidenced in the current repository. If S3 adds a transport API, it must be separately identified and covered; no HTTP API is presumed here.
+
+Out of scope: CI or release pipelines; mutation testing; red/green cycles that alter product code; live service, customer, production, or external API calls; test execution in the planning phase; accepting skips as satisfied coverage; silently replacing an unavailable test category with an unrelated suite. ADR-0001 remains binding: only `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` author and execute required tests.
+
+## Current evidence and constraints
+
+- `tests/vst/` contains the S1 contract, gate, store, runner, process-death, and slice tests, plus the five S2 acceptance modules. The current discovery evidence is source-path inspection only; this plan makes no runtime claim.
+- `tools/vst/slice.py` provides a synthetic, local vertical-slice harness. `tools/vst/runner.py` executes allowlisted local commands and captures bounded command evidence. They are possible integration points, not yet QA category runners.
+- ADR-0001 forbids CI and mutation runs and requires exact-head agent-run evidence. Its permitted synthetic known-defect fixtures may demonstrate a falsifying oracle without mutating product code.
+- A repository-owned QA dependency lock and stable category/test-ID registry do not currently appear in the inspected paths. Their exact formats and dependency resolution are UNKNOWN and must be established in Gate 1.
+- S3 acceptance artifacts and any new S3 test paths do not yet exist. S4's regression denominator must include the accepted S3 tests once their paths and IDs are established.
+
+## Stories and acceptance criteria
+
+### E1 — Category and test-ID contract
+
+**S4.1.1** Define the supported categories (`functional`, `integration`, `api`, `e2e`, `regression`, `seeded-failure`), their test-owner roles, exact source paths/selectors, required test-ID inventory, applicable environment, and category-level denominator.
+
+**AC-1:** Every required test ID resolves to a committed test and exactly one `primary_category` among `functional`, `integration`, `api`, `e2e`, or `seeded-failure`; duplicate, missing, unknown, or unassigned IDs are rejected before a run can produce an accepting result. `regression` is an aggregate run manifest, not a primary category: it references the union of the accepted functional, integration, API, and E2E test IDs while preserving each ID's single primary category and source-commit provenance.
+
+**AC-2:** Each category has a real native invocation. `api` covers the documented Python API of `tools.vst`; a network API is marked unsupported unless the product adds one and records its route contract.
+
+**AC-3:** The category registry is bound to its content hash and candidate HEAD; stale registry or candidate HEAD cannot produce current evidence.
+
+### E2 — Reproducible environment and native runner
+
+**S4.2.1** Establish a repository-owned, hash-pinned QA dependency input compatible with the required pinned interpreter `C:\Python314\python.exe`, and record relevant OS/runtime/tool versions for each category.
+
+**S4.2.2** Implement one bounded runner entry point that launches pytest's native discovery/execution for the requested category, preserving existing unittest discovery. It records argv, exit code, duration, stdout/stderr references, environment identity, expected and collected IDs, and output artifact digests.
+
+**AC-4:** Running the same committed category manifest with the same interpreter and dependency lock yields the same selected test-ID set; artifact timestamps may differ but are excluded from normalized content hashes.
+
+**AC-5:** A missing interpreter, dependency, category selector, artifact, or test ID produces a typed non-approving result with a cause; no fallback interpreter or empty-success result is allowed.
+
+**AC-6:** The runner does not install or download dependencies during a test run. Dependency installation, if needed, is an explicit environment-preparation step from the exact lock and isolated target.
+
+### E3 — Functional and Python API lanes
+
+**S4.3.1** Define and run functional test subsets for contract validation and verdict behavior using native pytest selection.
+
+**S4.3.2** Define and run Python API contract scenarios over public entry points in `tools/vst/contracts.py`, `gate.py`, `store.py`, `runner.py`, and `supervisor.py`, with local temporary state only.
+
+**AC-7:** Each lane exercises valid and invalid inputs, stale HEAD/evidence and signature failures where applicable; every required ID appears exactly once in the execution record.
+
+**AC-8:** API scope is truthful: direct Python APIs are supported; absent HTTP routes are recorded as `UNSUPPORTED` with repository evidence, and cannot be reported as tested.
+
+### E4 — Integration and end-to-end lanes
+
+**S4.4.1** Define integration selections that cross the real store, signer/runner, gate and local synthetic repository boundaries.
+
+**S4.4.2** Define E2E selections that run the synthetic VST vertical slice and S3 worker adapter through real local boundaries after S3 acceptance exists.
+
+**AC-9:** Integration/E2E use isolated temporary directories and local synthetic repositories/remotes; they make no external network or production writes.
+
+**AC-10:** Missing S3 adapter or sandbox-dependent capability remains `NOT_RUN` or `UNSUPPORTED` with an exact dependency and is never omitted from the denominator.
+
+### E5 — Regression and seeded-failure evidence
+
+**S4.5.1** Define regression as an aggregate manifest containing the explicit union of accepted functional, integration, API and E2E IDs for the current HEAD, with each ID retaining its unique `primary_category` and source-commit provenance. The aggregate does not reassign IDs to a second primary category.
+
+**S4.5.2** Add a bounded synthetic fixture catalog for known failure classes (for example stale HEAD, missing required receipt, invalid signature, out-of-scope diff, skipped required ID, artifact digest mismatch). Each fixture supplies a controlled input record to the unchanged product interface and the expected non-approving outcome; it does not patch, monkeypatch, or rewrite product source.
+
+**AC-11:** Regression reports every required ID and fails on any missing, duplicate, skipped, xfailed, unexpected, or uncollected ID.
+
+**AC-12:** Each seeded-failure fixture is itself a test with a committed fixture ID, input hash, expected rejection, observed rejection and test ID. No actual failing product test is relabeled as an expected seed; no product code is modified to inject a defect.
+
+**AC-13:** Mutation testing and red/green loops remain `NOT_RUN` under ADR-0001. Seeded fixtures do not claim mutation score or prove every defect class.
+
+### E6 — Evidence envelope and gate compatibility
+
+**S4.6.1** Serialize a machine-readable report for each category with schema version, candidate HEAD, dirty-tree state, category-manifest hash, expected/collected/executed/skipped/xfail/unexpected IDs, interpreter and dependency-lock hash, command/exit status, artifact digests, and typed result.
+
+**AC-14:** `APPROVE` is impossible if required IDs are missing or skipped, if evidence is stale or hash-invalid, or if a category is unsupported or `NOT_RUN`; operator waiver behavior remains governed only by ADR-0001 and the authoritative VST gate.
+
+**AC-15:** Evidence artifacts are reproducible and contain no secrets, user-specific absolute paths, tokens, or unrestricted environment values. Environment variable names may be reported only under the existing privacy contract.
+
+## Requirements-to-test map and denominator
+
+| Requirement | ACs | Required falsifying scenario / oracle | Layer | State/dependency |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Native category selection | AC-1, AC-2 | Unknown category, overlapping ID, unknown ID, missing test path -> runner refuses an accepting report | Runner contract | Planned; category registry is new |
+| Exact test accounting | AC-1, AC-11 | Required ID absent, duplicate ID, collection mismatch, skipped or xfailed required ID -> non-approval | Runner integration | Planned |
+| Reproducible environment | AC-4..6 | Wrong Python, missing locked dependency, changed lock hash, missing artifact -> typed failure; runner performs no install/download | Runner/environment integration | Dependency: establish lock format and pinned tool set in E1/E2 |
+| Functional contracts | AC-7 | Valid and invalid contract/gate inputs, including stale evidence and signature failures -> expected verdict | Functional | S2 tests exist; S3 additions are future inputs |
+| Python API | AC-2, AC-8 | Public API accepts valid request and rejects malformed/stale request; nonexistent HTTP route is explicitly unsupported | API contract | Python API exists; transport API UNKNOWN/absent in current paths |
+| Integration boundaries | AC-9 | Real local store/gate/runner flow with temp state; corrupted signature/chain/receipt fails closed | Integration | S2 modules exist; S3 dependency only for worker adapter |
+| E2E journey | AC-9, AC-10 | Synthetic story run through control plane and adapter; missing sandbox/adapter remains NOT_RUN | E2E | S3 and operator sandbox evidence may be required |
+| Regression denominator | AC-11 | Delete, duplicate, skip or xfail one registered test ID -> non-approving report | Aggregate regression run over primary-category IDs | Depends on all prior category IDs |
+| Seeded failure | AC-12, AC-13 | Each unchanged-product synthetic negative fixture triggers its documented rejection; fixture mismatch cannot pass | Seeded-failure | Fixture catalog is new; no mutation or source patch |
+| Evidence integrity | AC-3, AC-14, AC-15 | Alter report/hash or replay against another HEAD -> gate rejects; reports contain no secret values | Evidence/gate integration | Requires report schema and authoritative gate binding |
+
+**Denominator rule:** At sprint start, freeze a committed registry containing every test ID and one `primary_category`, including `UNSUPPORTED` and `NOT_RUN` rows with reasons. The regression manifest is a separate aggregate reference to the required functional, integration, API, and E2E IDs; it does not create duplicate primary-category assignments. Per-primary-category and regression reports must account for 100% of their applicable registry or aggregate manifest. No percentage or category-level PASS can hide an unaccounted ID. Recompute and review the inventory when tests are added or removed; bind it to the exact source HEAD and registry hash.
+
+## Evidence record
+
+Each run emits an immutable JSON envelope and referenced artifacts containing:
+
+- sprint, category, run id, schema version, exact repository HEAD, branch, dirty flag and changed-path list;
+- category-registry version/hash, expected, collected, executed, skipped, xfailed, failed, unexpected and uncollected test IDs;
+- exact argv, working-directory-relative selector, exit code, start/end/duration, interpreter path/version, OS/runtime identity, pytest version and lockfile hash;
+- output artifact relative paths and SHA-256 digests; normalized summary digest excludes nondeterministic wall-clock fields;
+- per-fixture seeded-failure ID, input digest, expected/observed verdict and linked test ID, where applicable;
+- result: `PASS`, `FAIL`, `NOT_RUN`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `INCONCLUSIVE` or `BLOCKED`, with reason and dependency; no implicit conversion between states.
+
+Exact commands are formed from committed category selectors; proposed interface:
+
+```text
+C:\Python314\python.exe -m tools.qa.run --category <category> --manifest docs/qa/categories.json --output <run-dir>
+```
+
+This command and its module are **new paths**, not currently runnable. The runner delegates to pytest's native CLI and captures collection and runtime output without claiming that collection alone is a test pass. The exact pytest flags and artifact format are resolved during E2 design and then pinned in the committed manifest.
+
+## Definition of Ready
+
+- S2 exact-head acceptance and S3 worker adapter scope are reconciled; all dependent or unavailable capabilities are explicit.
+- Category owners, source paths, selectors, test-ID inventory and denominator are agreed from repository artifacts.
+- Existing pinned interpreter and test dependency inventory are recorded; the lock format is selected based on reproducibility and approved repository constraints.
+- Evidence schema and gate-binding interface are specified; a report cannot be treated as a receipt until the authoritative gate validates it.
+- Functional and E2E test agents own the required test map; only those roles will author or execute required QA tests.
+- New expected-failure fixtures use controlled synthetic input records, have a stable version/hash and invoke unchanged product code.
+
+## Definition of Done
+
+1. All six categories have an implemented native runner or a truthful `UNSUPPORTED` row backed by repository evidence; API means Python API unless a real transport API is added.
+2. Functional, integration, Python API, E2E, regression and seeded-failure tests run from committed category manifests using the pinned interpreter and lock, with reproducible artifacts linked from exact-head evidence.
+3. Complete per-epic test sets run after each epic and once again on the exact final committed head by `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner`; exact commands, test IDs, environment, counts, HEAD, dirty note and outputs are retained.
+4. Every expected test ID is accounted for. Any skipped, xfailed, missing, duplicate, unexpected or uncollected required ID blocks ordinary approval and cannot satisfy DoD.
+5. Seeded fixtures reject their named negative inputs through unmodified product contracts; no mutation-testing result or red/green product-source loop is claimed.
+6. `NOT_RUN`, `UNSUPPORTED`, `INCONCLUSIVE` and `BLOCKED` remain explicit and non-approving absent the signed, scoped waiver defined by ADR-0001.
+7. Relevant specialist reviews reach evidence-based consensus on the exact head, all valid BLOCKER/MAJOR findings are resolved and affected tests rerun, then GPT-PM approves that exact head before push/one PR.
+8. Change records, decision/lessons logs, backlog, state, registry and bilingual S4 sprint report are updated under the repository workflow.
+
+## Ownership and proposed backlog
+
+The operator is accountable task owner under the delegated continuation; Codex coordinates implementation. Canonical technical service owners for the QA runner, lock maintenance, and test-category ownership are not identified in current project records (`core/BACKLOG.md` and team roster do not assign them); these remain `UNKNOWN`, not invented. `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` are accountable roles for required test authorship/execution, not named people. `implementation-engineer` executes production-code changes.

+| Proposed item | Scope | Accountable / executor | Dependency |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| S4-A / VST-032 | Category manifest, test-ID registry and denominator | Operator accountable; implementation-engineer executes; technical service owner UNKNOWN | S3 story list and repository test inventory |
+| S4-B / VST-033 | Pinned test environment and bounded native runner | Operator accountable; implementation-engineer executes; lock maintenance owner UNKNOWN | S4-A, pinned Python |

+| S4-D / VST-035 | E2E and regression selectors | Operator accountable; test-agent roles author/run; technical owner UNKNOWN | S3 acceptance and S4-A/B |
+| S4-E / VST-036 | Synthetic seeded-failure fixture catalog | Operator accountable; test-agent roles author/run; fixture service owner UNKNOWN | S4-A, ADR-0001 constraints |
+| S4-F / VST-037 | Evidence envelope, hashes and no-skip gate integration | Operator accountable; implementation-engineer executes; technical gate owner UNKNOWN | S4-B through E; current VST gate contract |
+
+Identifiers VST-032–037 are proposals only and must be reconciled with the canonical backlog when S4 formally starts.

+## Ordered work and safe stopping points

+1. Reconcile the S3 accepted adapter interfaces and enumerate the S4 denominator; stop safely after E1 if an interface or test ID remains unavailable, with unknowns recorded rather than guessed.
+2. Implement and commit environment lock, runner and evidence schema; verify each new seam with its own focused local contract proof after all S4 coding is complete.

+# Sprint S5 plan: bounded AEVE evidence gate
+
+Status: **PREPARED / NOT STARTED**. This is a VST-side plan. It does not access, acquire, or execute the separate AEVE repository and does not claim the analyzer is available in this checkout.
+
+Sources: continuation scope and exit rule in `docs/sdlc/AUTONOMOUS_CONTINUATION_PROMPT_S2_S5.md` section 1; AEVE bounded-evidence role and unsupported-capability caveat in `docs/UNIFIED_ENGINEERING_ORGANIZATION_MASTER_BLUEPRINT_2026-10-23.md` sections 1, 8, 10, 11, 13.1 and 13.2; existing VST receipt contract in `tools/vst/contracts.py`; gate behavior in `tools/vst/gate.py`; S2 authority and exact-head boundaries in `docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`; and `docs/ADR_0001_TEST_AUTHORITY_MODELS_CI_NOT_RUN_2026-10-24.md`. This plan follows the later S2–S5 continuation rather than stale blueprint roadmap labels.
+
+## 1. Goal and constraints
+
+Produce a bounded static-analysis evidence record for one exact VST candidate head, independently authenticate its origin, and have the VST gate reject stale, forged, unsupported-as-supported, incomplete, or out-of-scope evidence. The evidence must identify exactly which rules and acceptance IDs were examined and which were unsupported.
+
+S5 is complete only when the analyzer's supported/unsupported status is truthful and the stale-head negative case fails closed. An analyzer finding no issues on a subset is not a full review or security approval.
+
+Constraints already recorded in this repository:
+
+- VST is the decision authority; AEVE is a bounded, optional source of deterministic evidence, not a general programming or runtime authority (`docs/DESIGN_BASELINE_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`, decision summary).
+- Required tests are authored and run only by `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner`; test execution follows all sprint coding (`ADR-0001`, continuation prompt section 2).
+- CI, mutation, and seeded red/green execution are not authorized by ADR-0001. S5 uses reviewable synthetic positive/negative fixtures and assertion review.
+- The analyzer must not execute the candidate, call a provider, write to the worktree, use network access, mutate VST state, or approve its own output.
+- V1 and v2 receipt bytes and hashes remain immutable. The existing v2 signed body must not gain optional provenance fields after the fact.
+- The exact AEVE source revision, license, supported rule inventory, transport, and runnable integration are **UNKNOWN / NOT_VERIFIED in this repository**. Do not fill these gaps by reading a sibling checkout or by treating blueprint summaries as reproduced evidence.
+
+## 2. Existing interfaces and proposed design
+
+### Existing VST surface
+
+- `tools/vst/contracts.py`: `StaticAnalysis` has `coverage`, `covered_rules`, `unsupported_rules`, and `covered_acceptance`; v2 adds fields only to `TestRun` and `IndependentReview` today. Its `derive_result` returns `PASS` only for `coverage == FULL`, no unsupported rules, and a non-empty covered-rule list; otherwise it returns `INCONCLUSIVE` (see `_validate_static_analysis`, `_derive_static_analysis`, and `RECEIPT_V2_TYPE_FIELDS`).
+- `tools/vst/gate.py`: `evaluate(...)` is the pure, default-deny decision boundary. For a current-epoch slot it verifies receipt validity/signature, chain, manifest binding, candidate head, required rule coverage, and acceptance coverage; stale deciding receipts do not satisfy the slot. The current public API has no AEVE-specific analyzer/profile trust key or source-bundle digest contract.
+- `tools/vst/slice.py`: the existing synthetic fixture can exercise signed receipts, stale heads, unsupported coverage, and `GateDecision` outcomes without using a real project or external service.
+- `tools/vst/schemas/README.md`: the human-readable schema must document any accepted v3 fields and remain consistent with validators and gate behavior.
+
+### Proposed minimum design (decision for S5 implementation)
+
+Retain `StaticAnalysis` as the VST evidence type and introduce an explicit v3 manifest/receipt contract for bounded analyzer provenance; do not add optional fields to the v2 signed body or introduce a second phase-state machine/general-purpose agent protocol. V3 must be opt-in through the manifest contract version, and its schema and signature domain must be distinct from v1/v2. The extension should include, at minimum:
+
+```text
+analyzer_id, analyzer_version, analyzer_sha256,
+profile_id, profile_sha256,
+source_tree_sha256,
+analysis_scope, report_sha256
+```
+
+`analysis_scope` is an exact list of repository-relative included paths (no globs at receipt-validation time); the input to the analyzer is a read-only snapshot whose source tree digest is computed by the trusted VST runner. A separately trusted analyzer identity signs the canonical evidence payload through an explicit domain label. VST verifies the signer against a trust configuration and keeps the analyzer trust root pairwise distinct from worker, supervisor, operator, event, reviewer, and runner-signer roots. No signing key is provided to analyzer code.
+
+The exact trust handoff (direct analyzer signature versus runner-captured output plus independent supervisor/analyzer attestation) must be settled against S2's committed signer/socket boundaries before implementation. Keep the payload contract above stable whichever transport is selected. It is not yet proven that the existing AEVE process can authenticate without adding a new key/service; that remains an implementation discovery, not a reason to infer a pass. V1/v2 fixtures must continue to validate and their canonical bodies/hashes must remain byte-for-byte unchanged; an S5 manifest requiring the new provenance contract must use v3 and cannot silently accept a v2 receipt as equivalent.
+
+The manifest separates `required_rule_ids` from the analyzer's optional rule inventory and lists required acceptance IDs. Under blueprint section 13.3, a rule is mandatory for this receipt only when its stable rule ID is linked to committed seeded-defect evidence that demonstrates the rule's rejecting behavior; other analyzer rules remain optional and do not become S5 acceptance obligations merely because the analyzer can report them. The required ID-to-fixture mapping must be frozen in a committed catalog before S5 implementation; S4's seeded-failure catalog is a prerequisite. For each required rule, the receipt must assign exactly one status: `SUPPORTED_AND_CHECKED` or `UNSUPPORTED`; no missing or duplicate required-rule status is permitted. `covered_rules` remains the set actually checked; `unsupported_rules` is the exact unsupported set. `FULL` is permitted only if every required rule is checked and no required rule is unsupported. `PARTIAL` or `NOT_COVERED` is non-approving for a required full-coverage slot. Optional rules may be reported as checked or unsupported but cannot expand the mandatory denominator. A finding is typed with stable rule ID, severity enum, evidence reference/digest, and path/line provenance. An empty finding list means only “no findings among the rules actually covered.”
+
+### Data flow
+
+1. The supervisor obtains an immutable, read-only candidate snapshot and computes its exact Git HEAD and deterministic source-tree digest over the manifest scope.
+2. The VST runner launches the bounded analyzer with the pinned analyzer/profile identities, read-only input, output directory, resource limits, and no network/credential access.
+3. The analyzer returns a closed-shape report of checked/unsupported rules and findings. It cannot choose the source digest or current HEAD; the runner binds both from its own snapshot.
+4. The trusted signer authenticates the canonical request/evidence payload under the S5 domain. The analyzer never receives signing keys or signer IPC.
+5. VST validates the receipt, provenance hashes, rule partition, signature, manifest/head/epoch and required acceptance mapping. It stores the append-only receipt, and `gate.evaluate` decides. Any identity or hash mismatch, missing rule, stale head, untrusted profile, report tampering, unsupported required rule, timeout, or malformed response is non-approval.
+
+Dependency direction: analyzer adapter -> immutable report value; runner -> adapter and source snapshot; signer -> canonical request; VST contracts/gate -> receipt and decision. Analyzer code must not import or write the VST store, and the gate must not call the analyzer or trust analyzer-supplied current-head values.
+
+## 3. Failure modes and safe outcomes
+
+| Condition | Required outcome |
+|---|---|
+| Exact analyzer or profile SHA absent/untrusted | Refuse launch or produce `BLOCKED`; no analyzer PASS |
+| Rule not implemented by analyzer | Put the rule in `unsupported_rules`; force PARTIAL/NOT_COVERED and non-approval if required |
+| Analyzer claims a rule was checked but emits no check evidence for it | Reject malformed evidence |
+| Empty findings on partial coverage | Preserve partial status; never infer “clean” or full coverage |
+| Source-tree digest, report digest, signature, manifest, scope, candidate HEAD, or epoch mismatch | Hard non-approval; stale exact-head evidence cannot satisfy slot |
+| Analyzer timeout, crash, resource cap, invalid output, or unavailable tool | Record `INCONCLUSIVE`, `BLOCKED`, or `NOT_RUN` with exact cause; no success fallback |
+| Analyzer attempts write, network, subprocess execution, secret access, or path escape | Refuse/terminate within enforced boundary; record the observable violation; never count as clean analysis |
+| Concurrent candidate changes after snapshot | Analyze immutable snapshot; candidate HEAD binding mismatch prevents acceptance |
+| New code commit after evidence | Evidence is stale; rerun affected analysis for the new exact head |
+
+No hard reason is waived. Any allowed non-execution waiver must follow ADR-0001, name the operator record, and cannot turn unsupported coverage into a normal APPROVE.
+
+## 4. Epics and acceptance criteria
+
+### E1 — Versioned bounded evidence contract
+
+**S5.1.1** Add a v3 manifest/receipt contract for exact analyzer provenance fields and closed enums for rule status, severity, and finding reference. Preserve v1 and v2 validators, signed bodies, and hashes unchanged.
+
+**AC-1:** V3 rejects missing, extra, malformed, duplicate, or contradictory provenance fields. Golden v1 and v2 fixtures continue to validate with unchanged canonical hashes and signatures; v2 cannot be upgraded by adding optional provenance fields.
+
+**AC-2:** Every manifest-required rule has exactly one checked or unsupported status; the sets are disjoint and their union equals the declared analysis rule set.
+
+### E2 — Authenticated independent analyzer provenance
+
+**S5.2.1** Resolve the actual trust flow using only S2 runner/signer contracts; keep analyzer executable outside the candidate worktree and do not expose signer credentials.
+
+**AC-3:** The evidence signature verifies only under the explicitly trusted analyzer authority and domain label; worker, supervisor, operator, event, reviewer and runner-signer keys are rejected for the analyzer receipt.
+
+**AC-4:** Analyzer identity, version, executable digest, profile digest, source-tree digest, report digest, manifest, run ID, candidate head, epoch, and scope are bound to the signed payload.
+
+### E3 — Bounded execution and immutable source snapshot
+
+**S5.3.1** Define an adapter that accepts only a read-only snapshot, explicit in-scope paths/rules, and CPU/memory/time/output limits. Network, candidate execution, VST writes and host path access are denied.
+
+**AC-5:** Positive bounded fixture yields a report whose hashes recompute from the exact fixture and whose analyzer cannot modify the source snapshot.
+
+**AC-6:** Path traversal, symlinks/renames outside allowed scope, oversized input/output, timeout, unexpected subprocess request, and network attempt are refused or non-approving with observable cause.
+
+### E4 — Coverage truth and findings
+
+**S5.4.1** Map analyzer-supported rule IDs to manifest rules; preserve unsupported rules explicitly; bind each finding to rule ID, severity and immutable evidence reference.
+
+**AC-7:** Full coverage is emitted only when every required rule was actually checked and no rule is unsupported. A seeded synthetic “known issue” fixture yields its expected finding; a clean fixture yields no finding only for the checked rules.
+
+**AC-8:** An unsupported required rule, omitted rule, duplicate rule, malformed finding, or incomplete evidence never yields PASS or full acceptance coverage.
+
+### E5 — Authoritative gate and exact-head binding
+
+**S5.5.1** Require the signed analyzer receipt as a manifest-declared VST evidence slot. Gate coverage derives from manifest-required rules/acceptance, not analyzer claims alone.
+
+**AC-9:** A valid exact-head, fully covered receipt can satisfy only its declared static-analysis acceptance IDs; it cannot satisfy functional tests or independent review.
+
+**AC-10:** Any receipt from another head, manifest, scope, profile hash, source-tree hash, report hash, run ID, or epoch is rejected or leaves the slot unmet; stale-head test explicitly yields non-approval.
+
+**AC-11:** Missing, extra, forged, replayed, partial, unsupported, `NOT_RUN`, or `INCONCLUSIVE` evidence cannot produce ordinary APPROVE.
+
+### E6 — Operational and evidence record
+
+**S5.6.1** Retain deterministic evidence artifacts and update the schema guide, backlog, state, change records, decision/lessons logs, registry, and bilingual sprint report.
+
+**AC-12:** Evidence records exact HEAD, clean/dirty note, analyzer/profile/source/report digests, manifest/scope, required/checked/unsupported rule sets, findings, command, limits, environment, signature verification, test IDs/counts, and exact unavailable cases.
+
+**AC-13:** Every unsupported analyzer capability is labeled `UNSUPPORTED`; absent integration or platform proof is `NOT_RUN`; neither is described as success.
+
+## 5. Requirements-to-test map and denominator
+
+Only `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` author and run required tests. Author all focused tests after the S5 code is complete; execute per epic and once on the final committed head. The primary coordinator checks coverage against this map.
+
+| Requirement | AC | Falsifying scenario / oracle | Layer | Dependency |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Strict, versioned receipt, immutable v1/v2 | 1-2 | Missing/extra fields, bool for int, duplicate/conflicting rule statuses; golden v1/v2 canonical hashes unchanged; v2 manifest cannot claim v3 provenance | Contract unit | S2 gate APIs stable |
+| Independent analyzer trust | 3-4 | Correct signature accepted; each other trust root, unknown key, replayed request and altered payload rejected | Gate integration | S2 signer boundary verified; analyzer trust provisioning resolved |
+| Bounded execution | 5-6 | Read-only fixture; verify source bytes unchanged; forbidden path, symlink, size/time/output bound, subprocess and egress cases fail closed | E2E at runner boundary | Actual analyzer adapter/runtime identity is available and audited |
+| Truthful support coverage | 7-8 | Full, partial and not-covered matrices; unsupported required rule, omitted/duplicate status, no-findings on partial remain non-approving | Functional + gate integration | Actual pinned capability catalog or explicit all-unsupported fixture |
+| Exact-head gate binding | 9-11 | Exact head passes required static slot only; stale head, changed source/profile/report digest, wrong scope, epoch replay, missing/partial receipt fail | Gate integration | Gate accepts v3 static receipt provenance and records current HEAD |
+| Reproducible evidence | 12-13 | Recompute all hashes from saved synthetic artifacts; evidence loader rejects changed bytes or stale HEAD; `NOT_RUN` fixture stays non-pass | Functional and evidence integration | Stable evidence format and artifact retention location |
+
+### Scenario denominator
+
+For each declared S5 rule, include one supported positive or explicit unsupported case. For every run, include:
+
+1. Exact-head clean synthetic snapshot, one supported rule with findings, and one supported rule with no findings.
+2. Unsupported rule, unsupported required rule, partial coverage, and not-covered profile.
+3. Missing, duplicate, overlapping, unknown, and contradictory rule statuses.
+4. Valid analyzer/profile/source/report digest; each digest altered independently; wrong scope and path traversal.
+5. Valid independent authority and one rejection case per worker, supervisor, operator, event, reviewer, and runner-signer authority.
+6. Exact candidate head accepted and three-head fixture with evidence from each earlier head rejected for current head.
+7. Manifest, run ID, epoch, nonce, profile and analyzer revision mismatches; replayed and malformed signature requests.
+8. Timeout, output cap, input-size cap, subprocess, attempted write, network, missing executable and analyzer crash.
+9. Missing receipt, `NOT_RUN`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, malformed finding and unsupported status preserve non-approval.
+10. Reproducibility: repeat same immutable fixture and compare deterministic report bytes/digest; compare changed source/profile to changed digest and stale/invalid result.
+
+Use a deterministic synthetic fixture and never inject a seeded defect into production code. Do not execute mutation or red/green fault injection: ADR-0001 prohibits those methods. Test assertions may use fixed “known issue” fixture inputs whose expected rule finding is independently reviewed.
+
+## 6. Evidence contract
+
+One evidence record per analyzer run must include:
+
+- repository and exact full Git HEAD; `git status` dirty note; manifest digest and candidate/run/epoch IDs;
+- analyzer ID, immutable version/revision, executable digest; profile ID/digest; policy/config digest;
+- exact included source paths and deterministic source-tree digest; excluded paths and reason;
+- required, checked, unsupported rule IDs; coverage enum; acceptance IDs covered and mapping source;
+- findings with stable ID/rule ID/severity and evidence artifact path + SHA-256;
+- exact executable/adapter command and argv, runtime identity, platform/interpreter, and enforced resource/network/write boundaries;
+- report bytes digest, signer authority/key ID (never secret material), signature result, and gate decision/reasons;
+- exact test command, test IDs, count and outcome, skipped/xfail IDs; unavailable proof recorded as `NOT_RUN` with cause and owner.
+
+All digest algorithms and canonicalization must be versioned. Paths are repository-relative, normalized, unique and traversal-free. Evidence artifacts contain no secrets, private URLs, personal absolute paths, or customer data.
+
+## 7. Definition of Ready
+
+- S2 is merged and its signer, sandbox, store and gate exact-head evidence has been reconciled; any S2 operator-only sandbox dependency is resolved for sandbox-required S5 scenarios.
+- S5 scope, required analyzer rules, supported/unsupported semantics, manifest mapping and exact-head policy are accepted in repository docs.
+- Actual AEVE integration source identity/revision/license/security and available adapter interface are evidenced through an authorized in-scope source; until then integration is `NOT_RUN` and no sibling checkout is accessed.
+- Analyzer trust authority, key provisioning and signed payload/domain contract are reviewed; signer key material is not given to analyzer code.
+- Synthetic fixtures, resource limits, failure boundaries and evidence retention path are specified.
+- Functional and E2E test agents confirm the test map before implementation; they do not run tests until all S5 coding is complete.
+
+## 8. Definition of Done
+
+- Bounded static analyzer integration is pinned and cannot write, execute candidate code, reach network, or access signing/VST secrets.
+- Analyzer and profile provenance, source snapshot, report, manifest, scope, candidate HEAD and epoch are independently hashed and signed.
+- Coverage is truthful: every required rule is checked or explicitly unsupported; unsupported coverage never passes as full.
+- VST gate consumes exact-head signed evidence, gives no acceptance credit outside its manifest mapping, and rejects stale HEAD, forged authority, altered artifacts, partial required coverage, replay and missing evidence.
+- Functional/E2E agents run complete focused per-epic sets and the final committed-head suite; exact IDs, interpreter, environment, counts, command, HEAD and `NOT_RUN` reasons are retained. Skips do not satisfy DoD.
+- Relevant specialists report no open valid BLOCKER/MAJOR; GPT-PM approves the exact final head before one push/PR for S5, then merge is verified against `origin/main`.
+- Change record per commit, decision/lessons logs, state, backlog, document registry, schema guide and bilingual S5 report are current.
+

+
+Operator is the accountable owner of the delegated S5 sprint; Codex coordinates implementation. `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` own required test authorship/execution. No named AEVE technical service owner or adapter maintainer is established by this repository; that specific ownership gap remains UNKNOWN. Do not label a reviewer role as a person or technical service.

+# Virtual Scrum Team worker sandbox specification
+
+Status: implementation contract for S2. A sandbox is not accepted until the
+operator provisioned it and the signed, run-bound pre-flight inventory passes.
+The repository code does not provision or weaken the host boundary.
+
+## Isolation boundary
+
+Use a dedicated WSL distribution or a dedicated virtual machine for each
+trusted execution environment. In WSL, disable Windows drive automount and
+Windows/Linux interoperability in `/etc/wsl.conf`; restart the distribution
+after changing either setting. The worker must not see `/mnt/c`, other Windows
+drive mounts, host home directories, host credential stores, Docker/Podman or
+container-engine sockets, or any host path outside the per-run workspace.
+Prefer a VM when the WSL host cannot enforce these conditions.
+
+Run the worker as a non-root, unprivileged account distinct from the runner,
+signer, supervisor, and reviewer accounts. The worker account receives only
+the run directory and per-run scoped credentials needed for the task. Those
+credentials are created for one run and removed during cleanup. They must
+never include receipt-signing keys or signer credentials. The signing key is
+owned by the signer identity and mode 0600. The Unix signer socket lives in a
+signer-owned directory that grants traversal only to the runner group (mode
+0710); the socket is group-owned by the runner group and mode 0660. The worker
+account is not a member of the runner group and the runner drops supplementary
+groups when launching it. The signer authenticates runner UID using kernel
+peer credentials and rejects all other identities.
+
+Review runs under a separate read-only identity. Its credential must have no
+write access to the worker worktree or control-plane store. The runner verifies
+that the mounted review tree is read-only before launching review. A failure
+to prove the effective OS permissions blocks the review.
+
+## Network policy
+
+Egress is default-deny at the sandbox network boundary. The external egress
+allowlist is empty by default; adding an endpoint requires a separately
+recorded task-specific policy. DNS and indirect routes are also denied unless
+explicitly allowed. The local pre-flight loopback canary binds an ephemeral
+127.0.0.1 port inside the sandbox and is not a public-network exception. An
+operator-root-signed, run/spec/nonce-bound network-policy attestation identifies
+the environment, SHA-256 digests of the enforced policy and private evidence,
+an empty external allowlist, no container socket, and no unapproved host paths.
+The supervisor verifies this attestation independently. A connection attempt
+to one reserved documentation address is only a limited smoke probe; failure
+does not prove default-deny egress and success fails pre-flight.
+
+## Resource and filesystem limits
+
+Each run has an operator-configured CPU quota, memory ceiling, process count
+limit, disk quota, and wall-clock deadline. The values are recorded in the
+run configuration before launch; absence of any limit blocks the worker.
+Commands use the run directory as their working directory, a minimal
+allowlisted environment, no inherited stdin, bounded output capture, and
+process-tree termination. No host path beyond that run directory may be
+mounted or passed to the worker. Job Object nesting on Windows must be
+verified on the target host; unsupported nesting is a refusal, not a
+best-effort success.
+
+## Required pre-flight evidence
+
+Before each worker run, the standard-library-only probe records the mount
+table and an explicit `windows_drive_mounts` list. It classifies a mount as a
+Windows drive only when the mount source is a drive root (`C:` or `C:\\`) and
+the filesystem is `drvfs` directly or WSL's `9p` with `aname=drvfs`; unrelated
+mount targets such as `/mnt/wslg` do not count as Windows-drive automount. It
+also records Windows interop state,
+user and group identity, container socket paths,
+blocked-target smoke-probe result, sandbox-local loopback result, and
+environment variable names. It binds the inventory to the run ID, a fresh
+nonce, and this file's SHA-256 digest. The trusted runner signs the inventory;
+the operator separately signs the network-policy attestation with a distinct
+operator-only key. The operator key is never copied to the runner, worker, or
+analyzer. All six trust roots (worker, supervisor, operator, event, reviewer,
+runner-signer) remain pairwise distinct. Socket discovery spans known engine
+endpoints, numeric per-user runtime directories, and `/proc/net/unix`; inability
+to enumerate a required source fails closed.
+The supervisor may start a worker only when the signature verifies, the probe
+is fresh and bound to the same run and spec digest, and every check passes.
+An enabled automount or interop setting, present container socket, root UID,
+reachable external target, failed loopback canary, missing inventory field,
+or stale run binding blocks launch.
+
+The probe can observe configured conditions; it does not prove that a host
+firewall or hypervisor is correctly configured. Provisioning and enforcement
+of the OS/network/resource boundary are operator-verified acceptance items.
+Record the exact distribution/VM identity and policy evidence with the run.
+
+## External event anchor coordination
+
+The external event anchor and its `.coord.lock` sidecar must both be outside
+the worker mount. Every store process that can write events or make an
+authoritative gate decision must use the same coordinator lock path. The lock
+is held across the SQLite write transaction and all external checkpoint
+appends; an authoritative read holds it from before opening the database
+snapshot through comparison with the external anchor. This prevents a reader
+from interpreting a concurrent valid checkpoint advance as tampering and
+prevents concurrent store writers from appending out of order.
+
+After a crash, startup may advance the external anchor across more than one
+event only when the full database event HMAC chain verifies and the latest
+external checkpoint exactly matches the event at its recorded count. The
+store then compare-and-appends each missing checkpoint in order before
+permitting a lease or gate decision. It never creates a missing anchor for a
+non-empty database, never accepts an anchor ahead of the database, and never
+repairs a fork, malformed event chain, invalid checkpoint, or mismatching
+prefix. Any such condition stays write-locked for operator recovery.

+# 0043 S2 external-anchor concurrency and recovery
+
+## What
+
+- Added a cross-process coordinator lock beside the external anchor and hold it across anchored SQLite transactions plus checkpoint synchronization, and across anchored reads plus checkpoint comparison.
+- Changed synchronization and startup recovery to verify the complete event HMAC chain, confirm that the stored checkpoint is the exact event prefix, then compare-and-append each missing checkpoint in order. Multi-event committed suffixes can recover after a crash.
+- Require the external checkpoint log to start at the signed genesis checkpoint.
+- Updated the S2 E3 contract and sandbox spec with serialization and suffix-recovery behavior.
+- Corrected the `Store` module docstring's schema version from 3 to 4 to match `SCHEMA_VERSION`.
+
+## Why
+
+The database reviewer reported that normal transactions can append multiple events but startup recovered only exactly one event ahead. It also found that independent store processes could commit before synchronizing, allowing one writer to try anchoring directly across a gap. Separately, gate and anchor reads could compare an older SQLite snapshot to a newer valid external checkpoint and permanently integrity-lock the store. I verified those paths in `store.py` and `lifecycle.py` on baseline code HEAD `d779d55ea0cbb5f391a1f028cbab0345cab7e155`.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- `tools/vst/lifecycle.py`: sidecar lock file `.coord.lock`, reentrant within the current thread/path and OS-locked across processes; anchor checkpoint history must begin at count zero/genesis.
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: `_tx`/`_read_tx` coordination, serialized startup reconciliation, verified event-prefix history, ordered suffix synchronization/recovery, gate and event-anchor comparison under the same lock.
+- `docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`: E3 denominator includes multi-event transactions, concurrent writers, and read/write snapshot overlap.
+- `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md`: lock location and fail-closed recovery contract.
+- No database schema migration was added; event and receipt bytes remain unchanged.
+
+## Decisions
+
+- All store processes sharing an external anchor must use the same sidecar coordinator lock. The lock file resides next to the external anchor and must remain outside the worker mount.
+- Recovery may append more than one event only after verifying the complete current DB HMAC chain and proving the latest signed checkpoint matches the exact chain prefix at its recorded count. Each checkpoint is then compare-and-appended sequentially.
+- A missing anchor for a non-empty DB, anchor ahead of DB, invalid/forked chain, malformed checkpoint history, mismatching prefix, or append failure remains fail-closed. The store never reconstructs a missing anchor from DB state.
+- Gate, `verify_event_chain`, and `event_anchor` hold the coordinator lock through their DB snapshot and external-anchor comparison, preventing a valid concurrent advance from being classified as tampering.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- This change was implemented against exact baseline `d779d55ea0cbb5f391a1f028cbab0345cab7e155`, after source review of `store.py` and `lifecycle.py`.
+- No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime commands were run by the implementation agent. The test-agent suite at the baseline predates this change and is not evidence for it.
+- Required test-agent scenarios: multi-event suffix recovery after commit-before-sync interruption; malformed/forked/anchor-ahead cases remain locked; two processes sharing an anchor serialize commits/checkpoints; and authoritative read snapshots do not false-lock while a writer advances.
+

+# 0045 S2 socket inventory permission and symlink fail-closed handling
+
+## What
+
+- Removed `Path.exists()` and `os.path.exists()` from container-socket inventory because those APIs can collapse metadata/permission errors into a false absence.
+- Check system socket candidates with `os.lstat`; a missing candidate is absent, while any other metadata error makes inventory incomplete. Present paths, including symlinks, are reported as exposed.
+- Enumerate the canonical `/run/user` root without following symlinks. A root or numeric per-user entry that is a symlink or not a directory makes inventory incomplete. Permission failures while opening or enumerating the root, UID directories, or candidate parents also make it incomplete.
+- Do not follow a per-user `podman` or `containerd` directory symlink. An absent directory is skipped; an inaccessible or symlinked directory fails closed.

+## Why
+
+Review of change 0044 found that `Path.exists()` and `os.path.exists()` can report false on `PermissionError`, allowing an unreadable socket path to look absent. Following an untrusted per-UID symlink could also make the scan claim coverage outside its inventory root. The supervisor relies on the inventory completeness bit, so these cases must make that bit false.

+# 0046 S2 Windows Job Object assignment race
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/runner.py`: strict Windows runs now create the requested command with the documented `CREATE_SUSPENDED` flag, assign the process to its kill-on-close Job Object, then resume its primary thread using documented Toolhelp and thread APIs. If Job Object creation/configuration/assignment or thread discovery/resume fails, the runner terminates the suspended process and returns a refused, capture-incomplete result without executing command code.
+- Non-strict Windows callers retain ordinary process creation and their existing best-effort `taskkill` fallback. POSIX launch behavior is unchanged.
+- The module and helper documentation now describe strict containment and the pinned Python behavior.
+
+## Why
+
+Reliability review found that normal `Popen` creation allowed command code to spawn descendants before Job Object assignment. The strict sandbox must establish containment before any requested command code executes. Inspection of `C:\Python314\Lib\subprocess.py` confirmed that Python 3.14's Windows `Popen._execute_child` calls `_winapi.CreateProcess` with its creation flags, then closes the returned primary-thread handle. The implementation therefore uses the documented creation flag and documented Win32 Toolhelp/OpenThread/ResumeThread APIs; it does not access CPython private handles or fall back to unsuspended execution in strict mode.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- Strict sandbox process-tree containment in `tools/vst/runner.py`.
+- `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, `core/LESSONS_LOG.md`, and generated `governance/DOCUMENT_REGISTRY.md` record the decision and implementation lesson.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Source/API inspection only: pinned Python 3.14 `subprocess.py` confirms the creation-flags flow and closure of the primary thread handle.
+- No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or Windows runtime probes were run under the task restriction. Correct Windows runtime behavior remains NOT_RUN and must be established by the designated test agent on a Windows host.
+
+## Ownership and next action
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator. Executor: implementation-engineer (`gpt-6-luna`).
+- Runtime evidence owner: designated functional/E2E test agent; host provisioning owner is not established in repository records.
+- Next: test agent exercises suspended start, child-spawn containment, assignment failure, and resume failure on Windows; record exact host/runtime evidence or NOT_RUN if unavailable.

+# 0047 S2 durable supervisor control state
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: added a private supervisor control-event writer and verified reader. Control records use reserved typed payloads inside the existing append-only `NOTE` event kind, so the schema version and event CHECK constraint do not change. Generic `record_event` rejects the reserved control marker.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py`: reconstructs provider breaker count/state and lifecycle state from the verified event chain. Persists the threshold/policy, provider outcomes, override, lifecycle intent, confirmed completion, ambiguous callback outcome, and explicit reconciliation. Outcome/action IDs are idempotent; action ID reuse for a different action fails closed. Start, stop, rollback, resume, and manual override callbacks write intent before invocation. Callback errors and non-JSON return values cannot be mistaken for confirmed completion.

+## Why
+
+Reliability review found that the provider breaker was initialized to CLOSED/zero on each Supervisor construction, and lifecycle callback failures left only volatile state. A restart could therefore forget a paused provider or repeat an external effect after an ambiguous callback result.

+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+S2 E7 / VST-016 through VST-019; `tools/vst/store.py`, `tools/vst/supervisor.py`, S2 worker plan, decision and lesson logs. No database migration or schema version change is introduced. +# 0048 S2 atomic lifecycle intent admission
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: added `begin_action`, which verifies the event chain and external checkpoint, derives lifecycle state and unresolved actions from the control NOTE stream, checks the expected predecessor state, and appends lifecycle intent inside the same serialized write transaction.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py`: routes start, stop, rollback, cleanup, and resume intents through the Store atomic admission path. A stale Supervisor cache cannot authorize an action after another instance has advanced or locked lifecycle state.
+- `docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`: adds cross-instance concurrent lifecycle admission to the E7 test denominator and rejection criteria.
+- Decision/lesson logs and document registry record the MAJOR finding and fix.
+
+## Why
+
+Independent Supervisor instances can cache the same lifecycle state. Appending distinct intents in separate transactions without deriving state under the writer lock allowed both instances to invoke their callbacks. The Store now makes admission and intent append one transaction; the next instance sees the first unresolved intent or the resulting durable state and is rejected before its callback.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+S2 E7 / VST-016 to VST-019; `tools/vst/store.py`, `tools/vst/supervisor.py`, S2 worker plan. No migration or schema change.
+
+## Verification state
+
+No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime probes were run. The two-instance concurrent-start regression case is assigned to the E2E test agent. The earlier accidental `git diff --cached --check` is documented only in change record 0047.

+# 0050 S2 Windows external-anchor coordinator hardening
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/lifecycle.py`: public `FileExternalAnchor.compare_and_append()` now acquires the same cross-process sidecar coordinator lock used by Store operations. Windows skips POSIX-style `chmod(0o600)` calls on both anchor and coordinator files. Sidecar open and Windows lock acquisition failures are reported as `AnchorError`.

The previous JSONL byte-lock change did not fix the Windows access failure. Using one sidecar lock for every public CAS is consistent with the established Store serialization boundary and removes the second Windows file-lock/open interaction. Separate review also found that an `msvcrt` lock acquisition `OSError` could escape construction while the SQLite connection remained open.

+# 0065 S2 bounded idempotent operation remediation design
+
+## Goal
+
+Address reliability review findings for S2 S7.2 and S7.3 before changing code: backend calls must not hold SQLite transactions or the shared event-anchor lock while executing, and retries of a manual breaker override must preserve the original signed payload.
+
+## Current behavior and constraint
+
+- `Store.execute_idempotent` currently invokes the effect callback inside `_tx`; push and pull-request callbacks run local Git subprocesses from `Supervisor._simulate`.
+- The existing `supervisor_operations` table already has an append-only record with operation key, payload digest and JSON result. Schema migration is prohibited; use the existing row and represent an unfinished outcome as a typed JSON result.
+- The synthetic Git backend persists operation-key/payload binding in a bare-repository ref, so retrying the same operation key after an interrupted callback is safe and a conflicting payload is rejected.
+- A completed manual override action currently returns its earlier action event without comparing the retry's embedded signed record.
+
+## Options considered
+
+1. Keep callbacks inside the Store transaction and add a timeout. This still holds the global database and anchor locks throughout the timeout and leaves the action record uncommitted while the side effect runs.
+2. Commit a durable pending intent first, run the backend outside the Store transaction with bounded subprocess operations, then commit the result. On timeout/crash, retain `PENDING`; retry only with the same key/payload, relying on the backend's own idempotency binding. **Chosen:** it releases Store locks during backend execution, makes the uncertain state durable and uses the existing schema.
+
+## Design
+
+- Add an external-operation path separate from the existing transaction-callback helper used by internal receipt insertion.
+- In a short transaction, validate the key/payload digest and either return a committed result, create a `PENDING` result plus intent event, or reject conflicting reuse. Then leave the transaction before invoking the external callback.
+- Bound each local Git subprocess with the configured operation timeout. If the callback raises or times out, leave the row pending and surface the failure. A retry with identical key/payload re-invokes the backend using its same idempotency key; the Git ref binding prevents duplicate or conflicting effects. On success, use a second short transaction to write the canonical result and completion event. Never map `PENDING` to success.
+- For a completed `manual_override` action ID, compare canonical bytes of the requested override record with the record embedded in the prior durable action. Reject any mismatch before returning the old completion. Continue validating the signed record against the current breaker episode.
+- Keep V1/V2 receipt bytes, event anchors, gate contracts, and schema version unchanged; no migration, external backend acquisition, network calls, or real remote is introduced.
+
+## Failure modes and rollout
+
+- A process exit or timeout before effect completion leaves `PENDING`; no approval/success is emitted. Same-key retry is allowed and backend-idempotent. Changed key payload is rejected. A persisted completed result is returned without a second callback.
+- A failure after backend effect but before Store completion remains `PENDING`; retry recovers the backend's original result from its idempotency ref and then stores it.
+- Keep current S2 implementation behind the existing API; record `operation_timeout_sec` in the synthetic backend with a conservative finite default. No destructive rollback is needed; a code revert is the rollback path before promotion.
+
+## Verification plan and owners
+
+- `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` own regression cases for pending/complete/retry/conflicting payload, callback outside Store transaction, bounded Git subprocess timeout, crash window, and changed manual-override payload under an already completed action ID.
+- They execute only after implementation is complete. No tests/checks/builds/CI/migrations are run during design or coding.
+- Reliability reviewer finding owner: S2 executor (Codex) under operator accountability. Exact-head post-fix review remains required before final S2 approval.
+
+## Unknowns
+
+- Runtime timeout behavior on supported Git/platform combinations remains to be established by the designated E2E run.
+- If a future non-Git backend lacks durable idempotency under the operation key, it cannot use this external-operation path without its own recovery contract.

+# 0066 S2 bounded idempotent operation recovery
+
+## What changed
+
+- Added `Store.execute_external_idempotent`: append a durable pending operation intent in a short Store transaction, invoke the callback outside the SQLite transaction and external-anchor lock, and persist canonical completion in a later hash-chained event.
+- An interrupted/failed call remains pending; retries must reuse the same operation and payload digest and invoke the local backend with the same idempotency key. Conflicting completed results fail closed.
+- Added finite per-command timeouts for every Git subprocess used by `SyntheticOperationBackend`.
+- Kept receipt creation on the existing atomic in-Store idempotency path.
+- Rejects reuse of a completed manual-override action ID with a different signed record, both in the current Supervisor cache and in durable Store replay.
+- Updated S2 S7.2/S7.3 contract, Known limits and VST-014/VST-017 backlog notes.
+
+## Why
+
+The fresh reliability review found S7.2 backend callbacks were invoked under a Store transaction and cross-process anchor lock, with no subprocess timeout. A hung Git process could indefinitely block unrelated Store work. The same review found a completed manual-override action could be replayed with a different valid signed record, causing the audit callback and breaker history to disagree. Review scope and exact evidence were `source HEAD 280e2d0a613a0b70252c13ce7afe85f22734f7d1`, documentation HEAD `4f8a0ca693a6045f9ede43a4d4f6fdbc9282bb2c`, GPT-6 Luna medium; the reliability finding was MAJOR for S7.2 and MINOR for S7.3.
+
+## Design and compatibility
+
+- Design alternatives and failure handling are documented in change record 0065.
+- The existing append-only operations row and event stream are reused; no SQLite schema migration or receipt contract version change was made.
+- `execute_idempotent` remains available for atomic internal database effects such as receipt insertion. External callers use the new method and must provide a backend that durably honors the operation key.
+- Previously committed operation rows remain readable as completed results.
+- Only the local synthetic Git backend is in this scope; no remote service or external candidate is added.
+
+## Ownership
+

+- Executor: Codex.

+# 0068 S2 E8 source repository backend design
+
+## Goal
+
+Make the synthetic supervisor backend publish a candidate commit from the isolated worker repository to the local bare remote, with bounded Git execution and supervisor-only authority.
+
+## Current behavior and constraints
+
+- `run_lifecycle_scenarios` creates a worker source repository and a separate bare target. Candidate commits exist only in the source.
+- `SyntheticOperationBackend` currently knows only the bare target and attempts `git --git-dir <bare> push <bare> <head>:<ref>`. It cannot transfer an object that exists only in the source repository.
+- The worker has no push/PR credential or path. The supervisor may operate only on the local synthetic bare remote.
+- Git subprocesses remain finitely timed. No real remote, external network, candidate acquisition, or process-kill scenario is included.
+
+## Options
+
+1. Copy candidate objects from source to target with low-level Git plumbing, introducing object-format and ref-atomicity details into the adapter.
+2. Give the trusted backend an explicit `source_repo` and run `git -C <source_repo> push <bare_target> <head>:<ref>`. **Chosen:** Git local transport moves the referenced commit and objects coherently while the worker remains without publish authority.
+
+## Design
+
+- `SyntheticOperationBackend` accepts an explicit source repository and target bare repository. Every target inspection and source push uses the finite configured timeout.
+- Candidate branch and pull-request refs are created by pushing the exact requested head from source to target. Existing idempotency-key/payload binding and target-ref conflict checks remain in place; no force push is added.
+- The E8 harness provides the worker repository at initial construction and after restart. The backend does not copy or check out files.
+- The generic Supervisor backend protocol is unchanged. Store pending/completion behavior from records 0066-0067 remains unchanged; no schema or receipt version change.
+
+## Failure handling and rollout
+
+- Missing source repository or missing head fails through the bounded Git command; the Store retains `PENDING` and the caller gets no success result.
+- Timeout remains retryable only with the identical key and payload. The target's durable idempotency binding and idempotent ref update prevent a second logical effect.
+- A target ref already bound to a different head is rejected; no overwrite is permitted.
+- The change is internal to the synthetic harness. Reverting the code commit restores the prior implementation.
+
+## Verification and ownership
+
+- `e2e-runner` owns focused local bare-remote cases: head exists only in source, timeout then same-key retry, restart completion, and conflicting payload.
+- `functional-test-reviewer` owns focused method/contract regressions where applicable.
+- Both agents execute only after code is complete. No checks run during implementation.
+- Operator is accountable for the delegated sprint; Codex is executor. No named technical service owner is established by canonical sources.
+
+## Unknowns
+
+- Git local-transport timeout behavior across supported platforms remains for the designated E2E agent to establish.

+# 0072 S2 synthetic Git publication security design
+
+## Goal
+
+Prevent a worker-controlled source repository from executing Git hooks or redirecting the trusted supervisor's local publication operation, which could inherit runner identity and reach runner-only signer IPC.
+
+## Current behavior and evidence
+
+- At code head `c0e7e9ce15958b6c6de7811bcaf1020119ba169d`, `SyntheticOperationBackend` invokes `git -C <source_repo> push <bare_target> <head>:<ref>`.
+- A Git push may invoke the source repository's `pre-push` hook. Source hooks or `core.hooksPath` are worker-controlled unless separately protected. The WSL evidence records runner UID 997 as authorized to use signer IPC and worker UID 999 denied; therefore a hook invoked by the runner would cross the intended identity boundary.
+- Security reviewer `security-reviewer` / GPT-6 Luna, medium, classified this S2 S7.2 / VST-017 risk as MAJOR. The current tests do not establish that worker access to `.git` configuration is denied.
+
+## Options
+
+1. Keep `git push` and pass `--no-verify` plus a trusted empty `core.hooksPath`. This blocks `pre-push` hooks but still asks Git to interpret a worker-controlled repository configuration and remote URL.
+2. Export/import Git objects through a worker-controlled Git remote. This can invoke upload-pack configuration or helper behavior from the source repo.
+3. Run bounded local `git pack-objects --stdout --revs` against the exact requested source commit, import the resulting pack into the supervisor-owned bare target with `git index-pack --stdin`, then atomically update the target ref with `git update-ref <ref> <new> <expected-old>`. **Chosen:** it avoids `push`, transport helpers, source hooks and remote URL rewriting. Fast-forward and pull-request conflict behavior are checked explicitly.
+
+## Design
+
+- Source operation: allowlisted command `git -C <source_repo> pack-objects --stdout --revs`, with exactly the requested candidate head on stdin, a finite timeout, bounded/sanitized environment, and no network or credential configuration. No Git command mutates or executes repository hooks in the worker source.
+- Target operation: `git --git-dir <bare_target> index-pack --strict --stdin` imports the pack in the trusted target; then target-side `cat-file` verifies the commit and target-side `merge-base --is-ancestor` enforces fast-forward for branch refs. `update-ref` uses the observed old value (or all-zero sentinel for create-only) to prevent concurrent clobber. Pull-request refs remain create-only for a key and reject a different head.
+- Existing operation-key/payload binding is written in the trusted target before object transfer. The Store's durable pending/completion protocol and same-key retry behavior remain unchanged. A timeout leaves `PENDING`; imported but unreferenced objects are harmless and same-key retry is safe.
+- No SQLite schema, receipt bytes, or key boundary changes. No real remote, network access, source clone or install.
+
+## Failure modes and rollback
+
+- Invalid/missing source head, invalid pack, timeout, non-fast-forward branch update or unexpected existing pull-request head returns no success and leaves the Store operation pending for same-key diagnosis/retry.
+- A crash after pack import but before ref update leaves unreachable objects in the local bare repository; retry imports/reuses objects and attempts the ref update with the same expected-old rules.
+- A source-controlled `pre-push` file is never invoked because no push command is used.
+- Reverting the code commit restores the previous backend; promotion remains blocked until the hook-denial regression passes.
+
+## Verification and ownership
+
+- `e2e-runner` owns a regression with a malicious source `pre-push` hook marker and timeout/restart publication through the pack path. The test agent runs it only after the source change is complete.
+- `security-reviewer` rechecks the exact final code path; `reliability-reviewer` reviews timeout/crash/ref-race behavior.
+- Accountable task owner: operator. Executor: Codex. No named technical service owner is established in the repository.
+
+## Unknowns
+
+- Runtime pack import/ref-update behavior across supported Windows and WSL Git versions remains for E2E evidence. The test will not invoke process-kill or kill-table scenarios.

+# 0073 S2 hook-free Git object transfer
+
+## What changed
+
+- Replaced `git push` from the worker source repository with a bounded source-side `pack-objects --stdout --revs` operation, target-side strict `index-pack --stdin`, target commit verification, and target-side ref compare-and-swap.
+- Source Git receives a minimal environment that disables system/global configuration, interactive prompting, optional locks, lazy promisor fetch and replace objects. No remote URL, transport helper, push command or source hook is used.
+- Branch ref updates preserve fast-forward behavior through an ancestry check; pull-request refs remain create-only; concurrent ref changes are rejected or treated as the identical already-completed head.
+- Updated S2 S7.2 and schema documentation to describe the protected publication path.
+
+## Why
+
+Fresh security review at source HEAD `c0e7e9ce15958b6c6de7811bcaf1020119ba169d` identified that `git -C <worker-source> push` may execute a worker-controlled `pre-push` hook under the trusted runner identity. The WSL evidence records that runner identity as the only identity authorized to reach signer IPC; therefore a worker-controlled hook could cross the signer boundary. Review role/model/effort: `security-reviewer` / GPT-6 Luna / medium. The finding was MAJOR for S2 S7.2 / VST-017; its evidence and design alternatives are in change record 0072.
+
+## Ownership
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator.

+# 0076 S2 bounded Git pack resources
+
+## What changed
+
+- Replaced whole-pack `subprocess.run(..., stdout=PIPE)` buffering with a 64 KiB streaming pipe from source `pack-objects` into target `index-pack`.
+- Added a 64 MiB maximum transferred pack size and a 250,000 object-count ceiling checked from the Git pack header before forwarding its first complete header.
+- Forced trusted Git pack settings on the source command: one packing thread, 16 MiB window memory, a 10-object delta window, 16 MiB delta cache, and a 32 KiB delta-cache item limit. These command-line settings override worker-controlled repository-local configuration for the relevant resource controls.
+- Added a single bounded timeout for both subprocesses, termination and cleanup when the size/time bounds are exceeded, and bounded diagnostic capture.
+- Kept target-side `index-pack --strict`, commit verification, and guarded ref update. The hook-free pack path remains free of source transport helpers and push hooks.
+
+## Why
+
+An independent code review of exact source HEAD `202e0680e8e1b4fb30dcbe9659bf550d06443d90` found that worker-local Git configuration could select unlimited `pack.windowMemory` and automatic thread count, while the trusted process buffered the entire pack in memory. The source command now overrides these settings and streams with byte and object limits.
+
+Git 2.53.0.windows.1 was observed in the local environment with `git --version`. Its `git index-pack -h` output did not advertise a maximum-input-size option, and the current official `git-index-pack` manual does not list one, so the implementation does not rely on that flag. The current official `git-config` manual documents `pack.windowMemory`, `pack.deltaCacheSize`, `pack.deltaCacheLimit`, and `pack.threads`; the selected settings are passed through Git's standard `-c` command-line configuration interface. The implementation requires no newer index-pack option.
+
+## Resource boundary and remaining dependency
+
+The code bounds each transferred pack to 64 MiB and the associated pack index to at most 250,000 entries. This bounds per-import pack and index material, but it does not impose an aggregate quota on a persistent target object directory across many distinct operations, nor does Git expose a portable per-process memory quota for all object traversal allocations. The synthetic target must therefore remain run-scoped and reside on a quota-limited disposable filesystem; exact aggregate disk and process-memory quota enforcement remains `NOT_VERIFIED` and must be included in fresh S2 E2E/security review before this path is treated as production-capable.
+
+## Ownership
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator.
+- Executor: Codex implementation agent.
+- Required test author/executor: `e2e-runner`, after all S2 coding is complete.
+- Required independent review: fresh reliability/security/code review on the exact resulting source HEAD.
+- Technical service owner for aggregate target-storage and process-memory quotas: not identified in canonical project records.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Baseline source HEAD: `202e0680e8e1b4fb30dcbe9659bf550d06443d90`.
+- Local tool evidence: `git --version` reported `git version 2.53.0.windows.1`; `git index-pack -h` did not list a max-input-size option. These were capability inspection commands, not tests.
+- Official references: [git-index-pack documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-index-pack) and [git-config documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config).
+- No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime pack operations were run for this change.
+- E2E pack transfer, local malicious-config resistance, hard timeout/size cleanup, and exact-head specialist review remain `NOT_RUN` pending designated agents. Aggregate target-storage and full process-memory containment remain dependent on a quota-limited per-run environment.
