+# 0077 S2 cumulative synthetic target object-storage cap
+
+## What changed
+
+- Enforced a 512 MiB cumulative byte cap over the complete synthetic bare repository `objects` tree, including loose objects, packs, and indexes.
+- Added a shared OS file lock at `<bare-path>/.vst-object-storage.lock`, outside the counted object tree. POSIX uses `flock`; Windows uses a one-byte `msvcrt` lock. Acquisition has the backend's bounded command timeout, and the kernel releases the lock on process exit.
+- Serialized both target object-write paths (`hash-object -w` for idempotency records and `index-pack` for transferred packs) across separate backend/supervisor processes.
+- Before pack import, reserved the maximum 64 MiB pack plus a conservative index/reverse-index bound (48 bytes per entry plus 4 KiB) derived from 250,000 objects. A request fails closed when the cumulative cap cannot cover that reservation. Idempotency blobs reserve their raw size plus conservative compression/header overhead.
+- Sanitized target Git process environments and pinned `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` to the bare repository's managed `objects` directory. Untrusted alternate-object-directory and other ambient Git environment variables are not inherited.
+- Reject a symlink target object directory or symlink entries in the counted object tree.
+
+## Why
+
+Change 0076 bounded each import but did not bound cumulative storage across distinct operation keys. Repository inspection found `run_lifecycle_scenarios` creates `local-bare.git` beneath its caller-provided `workdir`; the function does not create or clean a per-run temporary root, and no in-repository caller was found that proves `workdir` is always per-run. Focused test helpers create bare repositories beneath pytest `tmp_path`, but that is test-fixture behavior and cannot establish an operational per-run guarantee. Therefore the backend now enforces its own cumulative logical storage cap and serializes every backend object writer.
+
+## Concurrency and boundary
+
+The lock file is located at `<bare-path>/.vst-object-storage.lock`. Advisory locks are cross-process and shared by all backend instances resolving to the same target bare repository. Every object write in `SyntheticOperationBackend` is inside this lock. The target Git environment fixes its object directory and omits alternate object directories, so the byte counter covers the destination that those commands write.
+
+This is a logical file-length quota, not an operating-system filesystem quota. It bounds backend-managed file bytes at 512 MiB when all writers use this backend. A separate process that writes directly into the same bare repository and ignores the advisory lock can bypass the cap. The target must remain supervisor-owned and exclusively writable through this backend; canonical project records do not identify a separate technical service owner for that boundary. Filesystem metadata, journals, and unrelated files outside the Git object directory are also outside this cap.
+
+## Ownership
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator.
+- Executor: Codex implementation agent.
+- Required test author/executor: `e2e-runner`, after S2 coding is complete.
+- Required fresh review: independent reliability/security review on the exact resulting source HEAD.
+- Technical owner for any non-backend writer or filesystem quota service: not identified in canonical project records.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Baseline source HEAD: `4671e2a804aaae6b0d1eb25c093d439850a0fce2`.
+- Code and documentation are implemented; no tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime pack operations were run for this change.
+- E2E must verify cumulative cap refusal, idempotency blob accounting, concurrent independent backend instances, POSIX and Windows lock behavior, timeout/restart recovery, path pinning, and fail-closed behavior for symlinked storage entries.
+- External direct writers and OS filesystem metadata remain outside the code-level cap; do not claim a filesystem quota or production qualification from this implementation.

+# 0081 S2 fail-closed bounded object import
+
+## What changed
+
+- Added a durable one-byte state journal to the shared target lock file: `HEALTHY`, `IN_PROGRESS`, or `POISONED`. The state is written and `fsync`ed under the cross-process lock. The state is set to `IN_PROGRESS` before a target object-writing child starts.
+- Changed the target lock file format from the prior one-byte mutex file to a two-byte file (byte 0 is the OS lock; byte 1 is the durable state). A legacy one-byte lock file is rejected, because prior code did not record whether an un-reaped Git child might remain.
+- After starting source `pack-objects` or target `index-pack`, cleanup attempts to kill active processes and requires successful `wait()`/reap of both. Any timeout or OS error that prevents confirming reaping durably marks the target `POISONED` before the storage lock is released. If writing `POISONED` fails, the previous durable `IN_PROGRESS` byte remains fail-closed.
+- Every backend object writer (`hash-object -w` and `index-pack`) checks the journal while holding the same in-process and OS-level lock. `POISONED` and recovered `IN_PROGRESS` targets reject all future backend writes; no automatic clear/reset path is provided.
+- Rejected source repository alternates (`objects/info/alternates`, `http-alternates`, Git worktree `commondir`, and external `.git` layouts). Source Git commands receive an allowlisted environment with `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` pinned to the intended local object directory.
+- Added a bounded source preflight before packing: Git `count-objects -v` output is capped at 4 KiB per stream and command time is bounded; alternate output is rejected; object count is capped at 250,000; Git-reported source object size and a no-follow filesystem scan are capped at 512 MiB; filesystem entries are capped at 500,000.
+- Copies only local loose objects and pack/index files into a temporary bare snapshot that omits `objects/info` and all source Git configuration. The requested commit must exist in that isolated object store before pack generation. `pack-objects` runs only against the sanitized snapshot with trusted pack resource settings.
+- Added a 64 KiB limit to durable idempotency blobs and bounded the Git command output used to compare a prior record.
+- Updated VST-017 to distinguish implemented controls from runtime evidence and remaining resource/environment limits.
+
+## Why
+
+The independent reliability review of code at `1ef3fee07d5743dc8e42c632e1dc3100601116a7` found that subprocess kill/wait errors were suppressed, after which the target lock could be released while `index-pack` was still writing. A security review also found that repository-local object alternates could make trusted source-side Git resolve worker-selected object IDs from a supervisor-readable object store. Git pack generation had no bounded source database preflight before traversal.
+
+## Safety behavior and residual limits
+
+- A child that cannot be confirmed reaped leaves the shared status `POISONED`; the recorded state cannot be cleared by this backend. If the final poison-state `fsync` fails, the earlier durable `IN_PROGRESS` state is retained; any later backend writer promotes/rejects that state before object writes.
+- A legacy one-byte lock from changes 0077/0078 fails closed. Use of that target remains `NOT_RUN` until a fresh supervisor-owned target is provisioned; this change does not delete or rewrite existing target data.
+- The source object count and byte caps, trusted pack settings, pack byte cap and bounded command time reduce the Git traversal surface. They do **not** prove a hard process-memory ceiling. An enforced OS memory limit (for example a verified cgroup or Windows Job Object limit) remains `NOT_VERIFIED`; the technical service owner is not identified in canonical project records. The operator is accountable for supplying/authorizing the sandbox runtime evidence.
+- Each sanitized source snapshot is capped at 512 MiB but uses temporary disk under the target bare repository. No filesystem quota is enforced by this code; disk metadata and stale snapshot retention after abrupt supervisor loss are outside the logical object-store cap. A quota-limited per-run filesystem is still required before production qualification.
+- The class requires `.git` and its object store to reside inside the supplied source repository root. External worktree common object databases are unsupported and must remain `NOT_RUN` until a separately safe source path is established. Repository inspection found no in-repository production caller or registry that proves the supplied source path is a designated per-run workspace.
+- The cap and poison state govern writers that use this backend and honor the shared advisory lock. An external direct writer that bypasses this lock can alter the bare target; the target must remain supervisor-owned and exclusive to this backend.
+
+## Ownership
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator.
+- Executor: Codex implementation agent.
+- Required test author/executor: `e2e-runner`, after S2 coding is complete.
+- Required independent review: fresh reliability and security review on the exact resulting source HEAD.
+- Technical owner for the OS memory limit, filesystem quota, and any non-backend target writer: not identified in canonical project records.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Review source: `1ef3fee07d5743dc8e42c632e1dc3100601116a7`; implementation baseline: `7833b92` (documentation-only follow-up commits followed the source baseline).
+- No tests, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime object imports were run for this change. During phase-6 coding, `git diff --check -- tools/vst/slice.py core/BACKLOG.md` was inadvertently run; it produced no output, and its exit code was not preserved. It is not test or runtime evidence and is not reported as a pass. No further checks are being run.
+- E2E must cover injected cleanup uncertainty and persistent poison rejection, two independent backend processes contending on one target, state recovery after restart, alternate and worktree rejection, source object count/size overflow, bounded preflight output, source-only candidate transfer from the isolated snapshot, and target storage caps.
+- Live-child termination/overflow cleanup remains `NOT_RUN` under the process-kill restriction. The OS memory ceiling, per-run filesystem quota, external direct-writer exclusion, and operational source-workspace binding remain `NOT_VERIFIED`.

+# 0084 S2 Windows source-object snapshot identity
+
+## What changed
+
+- Replaced the Windows source-file identity check that compared `DirEntry.stat()` with `os.fstat()` fields. The E2E report records that this comparison failed on Windows for all three snapshot-backed publication regressions, before either pack writer started.
+- On Windows, source object files are now opened with `CreateFileW` using `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` and a read-only sharing mode. The code rejects reparse points, directories, negative sizes, and files with more than one hard link. The sharing mode prevents concurrent write or delete opens while the snapshot is copied.
+- The opened handle is identified through `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` (`FileIdInfo`), and its volume serial, 128-bit file ID, size, and link count must remain unchanged after copying. Failure to obtain these Win32 properties fails closed; there is no fallback to the mismatched Python stat fields.
+- POSIX retains its `O_NOFOLLOW` open and compares directory-entry and descriptor device, inode, and size, also rejecting multiple hard links.
+- The existing source-root containment and symlink/junction checks remain. The copied Git object files are still consumed by Git's object reader and `pack-objects`; the requested commit must still resolve in the isolated snapshot before transfer.
+
+## Why
+
+The E2E run documented in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-e2e-bounded-snapshot-ed531.md` used source HEAD `ed531264d0344c67e948e126c420e60f5272226c` on Windows 11 / Python 3.14.3. It reported 77 passed, 14 skipped, and 3 failed. The failed cases were:
+
+- `test_hook_free_publication_transfers_source_only_commit_without_running_pre_push`
+- `test_synthetic_backend_fast_forward_and_conflicting_branch_and_pr_refs`
+- `test_local_git_timeout_leaves_pending_then_restart_retry_completes_same_key`
+
+All three raised `RuntimeError: synthetic source object file changed during snapshot` at `_copy_source_object_file`. The guard compared `st_dev`, `st_ino`, and `st_size` returned by `DirEntry.stat(follow_symlinks=False)` against `os.fstat(fd)`. The report confirms the comparison failed but does not preserve the individual values. These failures were classified as one Windows compatibility defect, not a flake; no repeat was run before this remediation.
+
+## Safety behavior and residual limits
+
+- Windows identity is now taken from the opened file handle, not from Python's directory-entry stat cache. `OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` plus `FileAttributeTagInfo` rejects a path that resolves to a reparse point; `FileStandardInfo.NumberOfLinks == 1` rejects hard-linked source objects. The handle is held with sharing that denies concurrent write/delete access during the copy.
+- POSIX retains no-follow open and path-to-handle identity comparison. Source repository and object-store real-path containment checks remain unchanged.
+- This code does not independently hash every unreachable loose object copied into the snapshot. Git's object traversal validates objects it reads while generating the transfer pack; candidate commit resolution remains required. Runtime proof of these paths is pending the E2E rerun.
+- If the Windows API binding or `GetFileInformationByHandleEx` queries fail, the import stops before packing; it does not weaken identity or link checks. Microsoft documents `FileIdInfo` support starting with Windows 8 / Windows Server 2012; older Windows versions and filesystems that do not provide it fail closed ([`FILE_INFO_BY_HANDLE_CLASS`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/minwinbase/ne-minwinbase-file_info_by_handle_class), [`FILE_ID_INFO`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/ns-winbase-file_id_info)). `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` is used to open the reparse point itself for explicit rejection ([Reparse Points and File Operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/reparse-points-and-file-operations)).
+
+## Ownership
+
+- Accountable task owner: operator by delegated S2 assignment.
+- Executor: Codex implementation agent.
+- Test author/executor: E2E runner, for a fresh Windows run against the resulting source commit.
+- Technical owner of the Windows host/runtime: not established by the inspected project records.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Failing source revision: `ed531264d0344c67e948e126c420e60f5272226c`.
+- The recorded failing E2E command was `C:\Python314\python.exe -m pytest -q tests/vst/test_s2_runner_lifecycle.py tests/vst/test_s2_store_lifecycle.py`; evidence is in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-e2e-bounded-snapshot-ed531.md`.
+- No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime imports were run for this implementation. The prior red result is diagnostic evidence for the defect, not verification of this fix.
+- Required next step: E2E runner executes the focused Windows lifecycle/store run on this exact new source HEAD. Preserve all existing skipped process-kill/overflow cleanup cases as `NOT_RUN`.

+# Change 0162: Reject explicitly invalid S2 preflight nonces
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/preflight.py::collect_inventory` now generates a nonce only when the argument is omitted as `None`.
+- Explicit empty or non-string nonce values now raise `ContractError` before platform probing or inventory collection.
+- `core/BACKLOG.md`, `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, and `core/LESSONS_LOG.md` record the S2 E5/VST-014 scope, reasoning, and pending verification.
+
+## Why
+
+The previous `nonce = nonce or uuid.uuid4().hex` expression silently changed falsey caller input into a fresh value. Run-bound preflight callers that accidentally supplied an empty nonce could therefore obscure a configuration error. The change preserves existing automatic nonce generation for omitted input and preserves valid explicitly supplied nonce values.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- S2 E5/VST-014 run-bound sandbox inventory and preflight nonce binding.
+- No signer format, attestation schema, sandbox policy, or accepted nonce value is changed.
+- Paths: `tools/vst/preflight.py`, `core/BACKLOG.md`, `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, `core/LESSONS_LOG.md`.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Code implemented at HEAD `6ee97cb06b52900c3c2ab2a9b1b415ae117a7932`.
+- The designated functional-test-reviewer verified omitted nonce generation, valid explicit nonce preservation, and empty/non-string rejection: 4 passed, 22 deselected, 0 failed at test HEAD `deed6abe34eeaa8620593442bcdb1413d846f7982`; see record 0165 and `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-preflight-nonce-functional-run.md`.
+
+## Ownership and next step

+# Change 0319 — Fail closed when Windows Job Object cleanup is unconfirmed
+
+## What changed
+
+- Changed `tools/vst/runner.py` so `_JobObject.terminate_and_close()` checks the Win32 Boolean return values and exceptions from `TerminateJobObject` and `CloseHandle`. It keeps the handle for the final cleanup retry unless `CloseHandle` succeeds.
+- Routed each Job Object cleanup path through one helper. An unconfirmed cleanup triggers the existing best-effort process-tree fallback and remains sticky as `capture_incomplete`, forcing `EXIT_CAPTURE_INCOMPLETE` even if a later close retry succeeds.
+- Updated `tools/vst/schemas/README.md` to describe strict and compatibility behavior and the fail-closed exit code.
+
+## Why
+
+Three independent exact-head S2 reviews found that the Windows runner ignored both API results and could sign a successful receipt after process-tree cleanup failed. The Job Object contract requires terminating associated processes, and its kill-on-close behavior depends on successfully closing the final handle. Microsoft documents nonzero as success and zero as failure for both APIs: [TerminateJobObject](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-terminatejobobject) and [CloseHandle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/handleapi/nf-handleapi-closehandle). The runner must not treat an unconfirmed cleanup as success.
+
+## Evidence and verification
+
+- Baseline before source edits: canonical checkout `D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`, HEAD `08cb561d0c3187c2c023349ba9dd519fcf9339f3`; `tools/vst/runner.py` had no pre-existing diff. The preserved untracked `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-functional-test-run.md` remained untouched.
+- `silent-failure-hunter` (GPT-6 Luna, low effort), `reliability-reviewer` (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort), and `security-reviewer` (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort) independently reported the same reachable MAJOR in `runner.py`; `architect` (GPT-6 Luna, medium effort) separately identified that existing S2 tests do not cover later S3 changes to `tools/vst/store.py` and `tools/vst/slice.py`. These reviews were read-only and ran no tests/checks/builds.
+- No tests, builds, or runtime scenarios were run for this change. Required test authorship/execution remains with the designated test agents.
+- Shortcoming: the implementation agent ran `git diff --check -- tools/vst/runner.py` contrary to its instruction. It reported no output, but did not preserve an exit code; treat this as non-evidence. No tests or builds were run by that agent.
+
+## Remaining acceptance and owners
+
+- Functional/E2E regression coverage of Win32 false/exception returns and exact-head S2 behavior is still required. Operator is accountable for S2; Codex coordinates; `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` own required test authorship/execution.
+- Current S2 runtime evidence remains tied to source HEAD `dc95915018b80f498d5cf775363712fb915fe04e`. The later shared `store.py` and `slice.py` changes still need applicable exact-head test evidence before the S2 gate.
+- Platform-dependent Job Object nesting, prohibited process-kill scenarios, full POSIX containment, and E8 crash/resume remain `NOT_RUN`; resource limits and external-writer exclusion remain `NOT_VERIFIED` as listed in `docs/sdlc/STATE.md`.
+
+Change: 0319
+Executor: Codex

+# Change 0453: design least-privilege POSIX cross-UID cleanup
+
+## What changed
+
+- Added the implementation design for POSIX worker descendant cleanup when runner and worker have different UIDs.
+- Compared a broad runner `CAP_KILL`, a systemd-delegated per-command cgroup, and a privileged root helper; selected scoped cgroup-v2 cleanup.
+
+## Why
+
+The user-authorized VST-013 E4.1 cross-UID test failed at source/test HEAD `161dcc7`: runner UID 997 timed out worker UID 999, but the worker descendant continued writing after cleanup. The current service profile exposes only `CAP_SETUID` and `CAP_SETGID`, so the runner cannot signal a differently owned process. Increasing capabilities would exceed the least-privilege boundary.

+# Change 0454: contain distinct-UID POSIX workers in a delegated cgroup
+
+## What changed
+
+- Added a unique cgroup-v2 child scope under the runner's delegated systemd subtree for distinct-UID POSIX commands.
+- Added a fixed-environment exec gate. The parent sends the worker allowlist environment as pipe data, attaches the gate to its scope, and only then releases the command.
+- Fail closed if delegation/control files, attachment, or confirmed cleanup are unavailable. Cleanup kills the cgroup, waits for `populated 0`, removes it, and retries an unconfirmed result once in finalization.
+- Kept Windows Job Object and same-UID POSIX compatibility paths unchanged; the all-descendant acceptance guarantee is limited to distinct-UID POSIX workers.
+- Added focused fake-boundary coverage and updated the S2 design, sandbox contract, backlog, decision log, lessons, and state.
+
+## Why
+
+The authorized cross-UID timeout selector at source/test HEAD `161dcc7838b2bd05f01f485dab38a37cba9d82b2` failed: the worker UID 999 descendant continued writing after runner UID 997's process-group cleanup. A broad `CAP_KILL` would let the runner signal processes outside the worker tree; a custom privileged helper would add a new root trust boundary. The existing systemd-delegated cgroup-v2 boundary permits a per-command kill scope without either expansion.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- `tools/vst/runner.py`: distinct-UID POSIX launch, gating, scope kill and cleanup.
+- `tests/vst/test_s2_runner_lifecycle.py`: fail-closed and gate-ordering tests mapped to S2 E4.1 / VST-013.
+- `docs/S2_POSIX_WORKER_CGROUP_DESIGN.md`, `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md`: launch and deployment contract.
+- `core/BACKLOG.md`, `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, `core/LESSONS_LOG.md`, `core/STATE.md` and generated `governance/DOCUMENT_REGISTRY.md`.
+
+## Decisions and review
+
+- Rejected broad `CAP_KILL` and a custom privileged root helper; selected a runner-owned per-command delegated cgroup.
+- `architect` reviewed the design. It found the initial gate could inherit loader variables before cgroup attachment and that the same-UID fallback exceeded the stated guarantee. The design now requires a sanitized environment before the first `setpriv` exec, sends worker environment only over a separate FD, and scopes the guarantee to distinct-UID POSIX. A second review confirmed these issues closed.
+- Reviewer: `architect`; model GPT-6 Luna; effort medium; read-only design review. This is not the post-test source review.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Test author: `functional-test-reviewer`.
+- Pre-commit focused command: `python -m pytest -q tests/vst/test_s2_runner_lifecycle.py -k 'distinct_uid_worker_refuses or distinct_uid_cgroup_gate or distinct_uid_attach_failure'`.
+- Result: 5 passed, 85 deselected; one pytest-asyncio deprecation warning; exit 0. The first run found a reversed pipe-end assignment; Codex corrected it and the focused rerun passed. This run used an uncommitted working tree based at HEAD `47cdc4804d881e62cacacb1fba1006d23791529b`; it is provisional, not exact-commit acceptance evidence.
+- Exact-commit functional rerun and actual Ubuntu-24.04 WSL UID 997/999 delegated-cgroup E2E are pending. No test is upgraded to PASS from these mock-based selectors.
+- No CI/build/migration, broad process-kill capability, persistent service deployment, or S2 closure is claimed.
+
+## Ordered next steps
+
+1. Codex: commit this source/test/design change with its generated registry entry.
+2. `functional-test-reviewer`: rerun the focused selectors at the exact commit.
+3. `e2e-runner`: run only `test_posix_worker_timeout_kills_descendant_across_uid_boundary` under the existing bounded Ubuntu-24.04 unit with `Delegate=yes`; capture cgroup path, identities, capabilities, exit and cleanup.
+4. Codex: fix any valid defect, update evidence and rerun the impacted exact-head selectors.
+5. After E4.1/E4.2 are complete, continue the remaining S2 acceptance in sprint order; keep E5-E8 system and operator-only attestations distinct.

+## Attribution

+# Change 0464: Fence stale S2 POSIX command scopes across runner restarts
+
+## What changed
+
+- Add a private cross-process `flock` in `/run/vst-runner/cgroup-admission.lock` around distinct-UID POSIX worker admission and execution.
+- Before admission, reconcile only strict `vst-command-<pid>-<uuid>` child cgroups under the current runner's delegated cgroup. Kill and remove a stale scope only after bounded confirmation that `cgroup.events` reports `populated 0`.
+- Return a non-approving capture-incomplete result if the runtime directory/lock is unsafe or unavailable, stale-scope inspection fails, or cleanup cannot be confirmed. Include lock wait and reconciliation in the existing absolute command deadline.
+- Update the S2 POSIX cgroup design and schema README with the runtime-directory, stable delegated-subtree, and rollout contracts.
+
+## Why
+
+Full architecture and reliability reviews of the seven-file S2 delta at source/test HEAD `4c1692d61ee04e945fc0ccdd44db71869ccd5468` independently found that the cleanup latch and admission mutex existed only in process memory. If a runner exited while a child cgroup remained populated, a replacement process could lose that latch and launch a second worker. The repository had no evidence that an external service boundary fenced this restart path.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- `tools/vst/runner.py`
+- `tools/vst/schemas/README.md`
+- `docs/S2_POSIX_WORKER_CGROUP_DESIGN.md`
+- `tests/vst/test_s2_runner_lifecycle.py` (focused restart/lock acceptance; test owner: functional-test-reviewer)
+- `core/BACKLOG.md`, `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, `core/LESSONS_LOG.md`, `core/STATE.md`, `docs/sdlc/STATE.md`
+
+The lock directory must be provisioned as a real `/run/vst-runner` directory owned by the runner identity and not group/world writable. All lock-aware runner processes must use one stable delegated subtree. Pre-lock runner instances must be stopped before rollout; the code cannot fence a separate old service subtree it cannot see.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Source and focused test implementation are in the working tree; exact code-head test evidence is pending.
+- The designated `functional-test-reviewer` ran 11 focused selectors on dirty repository HEAD `6b0f32948c7b2b804123ba5e1b67271197ef97a9`: `C:\Python314\python.exe -m pytest -q` followed by the seven lock/stale-scope selectors, `test_distinct_uid_worker_refuses_launch_when_delegated_cgroup_is_unavailable`, `test_distinct_uid_launch_preserves_expired_absolute_deadline_at_admission`, and `test_distinct_uid_cgroup_cleanup_failure_is_non_approving`. Final result: 11 passed, one existing pytest_asyncio deprecation warning, 1.63 s. The first attempt had three test-fixture `NameError` failures because the test module lacked `time`; the test role added the import and reran.
+- After tightening runtime-directory validation to require owner-only mode, the reviewer reran four lock selectors (the runtime-directory parameterization contributes three node IDs): 6 passed, one deprecation warning, 1.62 s. +# Change 0471: Implement the S2 persistent manifest runner boundary
+
+## What changed
+
+- Added `tools/vst/runner_service.py`, a bounded Unix-socket service that accepts only signed
+  manifest execution grants, verifies its fixed service generation and dispatcher peer, fetches
+  the exact manifest from Supervisor, and calls the existing manifest runner.
+- Added `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py`, a root-owned authenticated RPC boundary that pins
+  dispatcher, runner, and signer peers by UID/GID, systemd cgroup and kernel peer pidfd; it
+  exposes only the operations assigned to each peer and keeps Store credentials inside the root
+  process.
+- Added `tools/vst/execution_grant.py` and Supervisor issuance/verification for one-use,
+  Ed25519-signed grants with a 30-second claim window and expiry covering the signed, bounded run
+  deadline plus completion slack. Grants bind task, TestRun slot, attempt, story epoch, manifest,
+  consumed run preflight, worker identity, resolved model/provenance, request, invocation, audience,
+  and current service generation. Key material is read through fixed root-controlled paths and
+  passed to OpenSSL by file path; private bytes are not placed in argv or environment.
+- Added Store schema v5 append-only runner execution claims/events. Admission rechecks owner,
+  epoch, manifest, lease, receipt slot, preflight and budget in one transaction before recording
+  `PENDING`. The fixed runner daemon then atomically reserves the exact grant as
+  `EXECUTION_RESERVED`, rechecking current generation, story epoch/owner, lease, deadline and
+  budget immediately before the first command launch. Completion requires this reserved state,
+  stores the exact validated receipt, and appends it to the ordinary receipt table/hash chain in
+  the same transaction. Exact-grant status queries resolve uncertain claim RPC replies only
+  within the original active service generation; they never reclaim work. A new generation turns
+  predecessor `PENDING` and `EXECUTION_RESERVED` claims into terminal `INDETERMINATE` events,
+  and never replays them. A lost reservation reply is ambiguous and cannot authorize a launch.
+  If claim/reservation status is unavailable or shows an already reserved/otherwise ambiguous
+  outcome, the runner sends a bounded refusal when possible and exits nonzero. Existing
+  `Restart=on-failure` creates a new generation whose startup recovery terminalizes the
+  predecessor claim. A reserve failure whose exact status still shows `PENDING` also fail-stops;
+  this source path does not retry reservation in the same generation. By contrast, a claim
+  failure followed by exact-shape `NOT_FOUND` for the same active generation is a normal refusal:
+  no durable claim exists to recover, so it does not restart the service. `NOT_FOUND` after claim
+  admission at the reserve boundary remains fatal.
+  Any later run, signing, receipt, or completion exception after reservation confirmation but
+  before the Supervisor confirms durable `COMPLETE` sends a bounded refusal and exits nonzero
+  before the service can admit another request; exact durable `COMPLETE` replay remains safe, and
+  ordinary pre-reservation refusals remain nonfatal.
+- Added a source-only execution reconciliation boundary using the existing append-only schema-v5
+  runner events. Any task with a nonterminal claim is blocked at `acquire_lease`, grant-basis
+  issuance, and claim admission. A recovered `INDETERMINATE` claim whose predecessor was exactly
+  `PENDING` is proven pre-spawn because launch reservation precedes every child; ordinary lease,
+  retry, epoch, and budget checks still apply. `EXECUTION_RESERVED` and other may-have-started
+  claims remain blocked until a distinct signed resolution. Only `INDETERMINATE` can transition to `RECONCILED`; the signed
+  record binds the full canonical grant digest and grant/request/invocation/task/slot/attempt/epoch/
+  run/service-generation identity, unique resolution ID, evidence digest, actor/key ID, predecessor
+  state, and a closed outcome (`NO_EXECUTION_PROVEN`, `EFFECTS_RESOLVED`, `EFFECTS_UNRESOLVED`,
+  or `RECONCILIATION_REJECTED`) plus its corresponding fixed operator attestation under
+  `vst-runner-execution-resolution-v1` HMAC domain separation;
+  `key_id` is the SHA-256 fingerprint of the configured operator HMAC key. Only the first two
+  permit successor admission; `NO_EXECUTION_PROVEN` is valid only for predecessor `PENDING`. The
+  operator HMAC attests that the evidence digest supports the stated outcome; evidence bytes are external and
+  Store does not independently fetch or validate them. No actual operator-signed resolution is
+  present. The in-process Supervisor/Store API is implemented, but no operator RPC, coordinator
+  caller, or production dispatch path is added or claimed.
+- Updated `tools/vst/runner.py` to require the grant-backed `ExecutionAuthority` for manifest
+  execution and the fixed UID/GID worker helper rather than a `subprocess.Popen(user=...)` path.
+- Added `tools/vst/runner_fence.py`, a root-only hash-chain manager fence that binds systemd
+  `InvocationID`, `ControlGroup`, cgroup and lock inodes, and only removes verified empty command
+  scopes. It fails closed on unknown/populated scopes and never kills predecessor work.
+- Added fixed Supervisor, signer and runner systemd unit templates plus
+  `tools/vst/systemd/README.md`. Added `tools/qa/install_wsl_runtime.ps1` to stream a bounded,
+  exact-HEAD Git archive from the canonical checkout over WSL stdin without a drive mount or
+  second checkout, including `docs/SANDBOX_SPEC.md` needed by runtime preflight. The Linux
+  bootstrap verifies the bundle digest and allowlisted paths and extracts under a unique
+  root-private per-attempt path. Before either installer mutates a fixed destination, it checks
+  existing runtime files/units; exact prior artifacts are accepted only with matching HEAD and
+  archive digest, while mismatched state is preserved and refused. A fresh transfer ID makes a
+  failed extraction retryable without removing old staging state. Installers do not enable or
+  start services. The worker helper clears ambient and effective/permitted/inheritable capability
+  sets, reads them back, and refuses launch if any capability remains.
+- Reconciled `docs/S2_POSIX_WORKER_CGROUP_DESIGN.md`, the implementation/design evidence, and
+  `core/BACKLOG.md` with the source state, runtime-directory mode `0710`, and the remaining gates.
+- Current-turn implementation follow-up fixed the runner config contract: `daemon_gid` is now
+  required, type-checked, and pinned with the other fixed worker-boundary IDs before helper
+  verification. Added `dispatch_authorized_manifest_run` as a library integration function; it
+  requests a grant over authenticated Supervisor IPC and forwards only that grant to the runner
+  socket. It is not a runnable production dispatcher, and no trusted coordinator caller identity
+  or request source is currently established. The source alone therefore does not close dispatcher
+  deployment acceptance.
+- Reconciled the systemd runner stop timeout with its 1800-second maximum grant deadline and
+  bounded post-run signer/Git work: grants allow a 30-second claim window plus 1800 seconds of
+  execution and 90 seconds of completion slack; graceful stop allows 1900 seconds while keeping
+  `SendSIGKILL=no`; failure to exit still cannot be recorded as a clean stop.
+- Bounded signer IPC client/server reads to 10 seconds and complete 4-KiB-or-smaller JSON
+  responses; stream responses are accumulated through EOF rather than assuming one `recv()` is
+  complete. Disconnected-client writes no longer terminate the signer accept loop.
+- Required completed Store startup reconciliation and verified event-chain integrity before
+  idempotently consuming the service preflight record, so an integrity-locked Store cannot be
+  mutated during Supervisor startup.
+- Corrected all execution-grant budget checks to pass the task ID expected by the Store helper,
+  rather than a SQLite row object; grant basis, claim, signer revalidation, and completion now use
+  the same typed input.
+- Resolved the correlated GPT-PM architecture MODIFY for claim ambiguity (request
+  `7f9f9a30-4f93-4df9-9b5f-6f354eac58c1`, reply
+  `bec8fd4b-c921-43bf-a697-63922b9d7970`) by adding the append-only
+  `EXECUTION_RESERVED` transition, an exact-grant status query and a single compare-and-set
+  reservation operation available only to the fixed runner service peer. The claim window gates

+# Change 0472: Correct S2 runner gate and reconciliation authority
+
+Date: 2026-10-28  
+Sprint: S2  
+Branch: `s4-canonical-continuation`  
+Base HEAD: `2da827be982d3f2d6f2adf152668af6ff8007f21`  
+State: source and focused tests implemented; fresh specialist review and exact-head GPT-PM approval pending.
+
+## Why
+
+Fresh database and silent-failure reviews found three defects in the persistent runner path. Gate evaluation could use an older passing receipt while a later execution claim remained unresolved. One `AUTHORITY_CHANGED_BEFORE_COMPLETION` event did not record its actual `EXECUTION_RESERVED` predecessor, so the signed reconciliation did not fully bind the state being resolved. Finally, an exception thrown by the post-reservation daemon-boundary callback could escape before the execution authority marked the reservation confirmed, allowing the service to treat the failure as an ordinary refusal instead of fail-stopping that generation.
+
+## Changes
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: `evaluate_gate()` now checks the append-only runner-claim lifecycle in the same SQLite read snapshot as the receipt chain. Unresolved states fail closed even when an earlier receipt is `PASS`; only a complete claim, a justified predecessor-generation pre-spawn `PENDING`, or a valid signed safe reconciliation can proceed to ordinary gate evaluation.
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: authority-changed completion records `predecessor_state=EXECUTION_RESERVED`. The reconciliation verifier enforces the closed predecessor/outcome matrix: `NO_EXECUTION_PROVEN` only for `PENDING`, `EFFECTS_RESOLVED` only for `EXECUTION_RESERVED`, and non-continuing outcomes only for a recognized predecessor state. The signed record and event must match that exact state.
+- `tools/vst/execution_grant.py`: after the exact durable `EXECUTION_RESERVED` response is validated, reservation confirmation is recorded before the post-reservation boundary callback. Any exception from that callback now enters the existing reserved-but-not-complete fail-stop behavior.
+- No scheduler, CLI, spool, new assignment authority, IPC operation, database migration, or runtime installation was added.
+
+## Verification
+
+The assigned `functional-test-reviewer` added direct regressions and ran four approved groups against the working source/test diff based on base HEAD `2da827be...`:

+- E2 runner authority: 38 passed.

+- Total: 138 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. One installed `pytest_asyncio` deprecation warning was emitted per group.
+
+Exact commands, SHA-256 fingerprints, acceptance mapping, and run limitations are recorded in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-final-gate-authority-regressions-20261028.md`. The test run used in-memory Store instances and fake authority callbacks. It does not prove live service framing, daemon/systemd generation restart, Windows/WSL containment, or production coordinator integration. The full suite, restricted selectors, checks, build, CI, migrations, provisioning, and runtime were not run.

+- Verify helper file type, owner, runner group, setuid mode, link count, bytes,
+  and embedded build identity when loading configuration and immediately
+  before each child spawn. Capture the verified inode identity when the service
+  starts; refuse a changed helper and never fall back to the legacy path.
+- Publish a newly built helper only to an absent versioned path by a
+  no-replace hard link from private staging. Treat an existing artifact as
+  idempotent only when its complete metadata, digest, and build identity match;
+  do not change metadata or bytes of existing helpers.
+- Pin both `core.autocrlf=false` and `core.eol=lf` for the exact-HEAD WSL source
+  archive so POSIX shell sources retain their committed line endings.
+- Update sandbox, schema, and systemd deployment contracts. Document that the
+  installer does not generate privileged Runner configuration; deployment must
+  provision the root-owned config from the audited helper build record.
+
+## Why
+
+The dedicated WSL environment already contains a root-owned setuid helper from
+an older build. The fixed-path installer correctly refused to overwrite that
+different privileged binary. The first scoped archive correction also proved
+insufficient: `core.autocrlf=false` alone still produced CRLF shell members.
+Versioned paths preserve the old executable and allow a future exact build to
+be installed without replacement; the two Git settings preserve LF bytes.
+
+## Affected contracts and paths
+
+- `tools/vst/runner.py`
+- `tools/vst/runner_service.py`

+The Runner configuration producer is not present in this repository. Its

+
+## Current evidence and affected contracts
+
+- Source/design proposal: `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-coordinator-architecture-proposal-20261028.md`.
+- Current baseline when prepared: repository HEAD `70f8953c69276fa9cbc00f2695dde2ca5aded1cc`.
+- Existing code contains a root Supervisor, Store task/lease checks, signed one-use grants,
+  persistent runner, service templates, and `dispatch_authorized_manifest_run`; the latter is a
+  library function and not a runnable production caller (`tools/vst/systemd/README.md`).

+## Proposed design boundary
+
+The proposed coordinator is local-only and forwards bounded requests to the existing root
+Supervisor. It creates no tasks, assignments, leases, independent queue, or spool. The Store remains
+the only durable task/lease authority, and the Supervisor remains the only grant issuer. The
+coordinator is authenticated through a fixed Unix peer identity and service cgroup, cannot accept
+caller-selected commands, executable paths, UIDs, or Store paths, and has no network or fallback
+execution path. Missing or stale root configuration/helper/runtime artifacts/fresh E5 causes
+refusal. Fresh signatures cannot claim unobserved host or firewall properties.

+# Change 0510 — Build the constrained S2 Store-backed pub/sub coordinator
+
+## Why
+
+The operator confirmed the production coordinator and authenticated assignment caller do not exist
+and directed Codex to create the bounded path. GPT-PM's correlated decision accepted source
+implementation only under the constraints in
+`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-pubsub-architecture-adjudication-20261028.md`. Store-backed pub/sub avoids
+introducing a general broker or assignment authority while letting the coordinator forward an
+exact already-authorized intent.
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: schema-v6 closed event kind; gated v3–v5 event-table upgrade; atomic
+  `DISPATCH_INTENT_ACCEPTED` write and idempotency record; validated replay lookup; generation- and
+  audience-bound HMAC cursor; grant basis checks the exact owner and derived lease ID.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py`: narrow owner intent admission, filtered replay/subscription, current
+  authority revalidation, and root-config-derived model provenance for exact grant forwarding.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py`: role-limited owner submit, dispatcher subscription, and
+  dispatcher grant-forward operations; root-owned principal mapping; strict response contracts.
+- `tools/vst/dispatcher_service.py` and `tools/vst/systemd/vst-dispatcher.service`: fail-stop
+  at-least-once subscriber that forwards one accepted intent through the existing runner boundary;
+  cursor advances only after a structurally valid complete receipt.
+- `tools/vst/runner_service.py`: authorized-grant forwarding contract, bounded timeout, and receipt
+  binding to the dispatched grant.
+- `tools/qa/install_wsl_runtime.ps1` and `tools/qa/install_wsl_runner_runtime.sh`: include the
+  dispatcher module/unit in the immutable runtime artifact.
+- `tools/vst/schemas/README.md`, `tools/vst/systemd/README.md`, the proposal, decision log, backlog,
+  state, and this evidence record: document accepted source scope and the still-open gates.
+
+## Decisions and invariants
+
+- Transport is the existing hash-chained Store event log plus Supervisor-filtered AF_UNIX delivery.
+  There is no Redis/NATS/Kafka/RabbitMQ, separate queue/spool, task listing, work selection, task or
+  lease creation, grant signing in the dispatcher, or automatic retry.
+- Principal comes from the authenticated peer and root-owned mapping, never request JSON. Store
+  compares it with the live task owner and binds the event to the exact live lease, slot, attempt,
+  epoch, run, manifest, generation, and request digest.
+- Transient Store busy, integrity, and unknown errors stop delivery without advancing the cursor;
+  only enumerated stale/revoked authority states are skipped.
+- Schema migration is opt-in (`allow_schema_upgrade=false` by default). The schema-v6 migration has
+  not been applied and requires independent database review plus separate authorization.
+- `S2-DISPATCH-M01` remains MAJOR/OPEN because no production owner caller is integrated and no
+  runtime acceptance has occurred. The latest GPT-PM decision does not authorize key provisioning,
+  migration application, service activation, real dispatch, push/PR/merge, or deployment. Root
+  configuration and fresh signed E5 remain absent/unproven. S3 remains unstarted.
+
+## Review and verification
+
+- Code-reviewer, GPT-6 Luna, medium effort: first found a MAJOR where Store errors were all treated
+  as stale and could advance the replay cursor; the implementation was corrected to propagate
+  transient, integrity, and unknown failures. The reviewer rechecked the branch and found no further
+  actionable BLOCKER/MAJOR.
+- Database-reviewer, GPT-6 Luna, medium effort: no actionable BLOCKER/MAJOR found. MINOR observation:
+  grant lookup verifies/scans the append-only history and may cost more as the event log grows; no
+  workload evidence is available.

+  belong to `functional-test-reviewer` and `e2e-runner` after source coding is frozen.
+- No database migration, WSL mutation, key/config provisioning, service start/enable, runtime
+  dispatch, or E5 run was performed.

+# Change 0516: verify signed S2 dispatch instructions at the Supervisor boundary
+
+## Change summary
+
+Implemented the GPT-PM-adjudicated signed instruction path for the S2 dispatch-owner client. The
+client accepts only an exact versioned Ed25519 envelope, verifies it locally, and forwards the full
+envelope. The authenticated root RPC derives the principal from kernel peer mapping and verifies
+the signature again; `Supervisor` repeats verification before Store authority checks. `Store`
+persists the full signed envelope and key ID in the hash-chained dispatch event and binds them to
+the durable idempotency digest. Delivery and grant issuance revalidate signature, expiry, key
+purpose/principal and current Store authority. No unsigned fallback is accepted.
+
+The change does not create a signer or private key, root configuration, account, assignment source,
+scheduler, queue, or migration. It does not install a runtime, activate services, dispatch work,
+produce E5 evidence, or close S2/M01.
+
+## Why
+
+The first owner-client implementation accepted a public caller-constructible task-shaped object.
+An authenticated process and a current Store owner/lease prove peer identity and assignment state,
+but not that the exact dispatch request was authorized. A focused code review found a MAJOR. The
+temporary fail-closed client removed the unsafe RPC path.
+
+GPT-PM selected a purpose-specific signed instruction without creating a second assignment
+authority, with a binding requirement that the root Supervisor independently verify it. The Store
+remains the sole task/assignment/lease authority. The signer may authorize only one exact request
+for already-assigned work.
+
+## Affected contracts and files
+
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_instruction.py` defines the exact envelope, canonical UTC expiry,
+  Ed25519-only algorithm, domain-separated canonical bytes, key purpose/principal mapping, and
+  fail-closed verifier.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_client.py` verifies and forwards the complete envelope without
+  constructing or changing request identity.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py` accepts only the envelope, uses kernel-authenticated peer
+  principal, verifies it at the RPC boundary, and requires a root-configured public-key registry.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py` repeats verification before Store admission, and rechecks provenance
+  before delivery and grant issuance, including expiry and revocation state.
+- `tools/vst/store.py` binds the envelope and key ID into the event and idempotency digest and
+  cross-checks their exact correspondence to the event request fields.
+- `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-owner-instruction-provenance-adjudication-20261029.md` preserves the
+  correlated architecture decision; `s2-dispatch-owner-client-design-20261028.md` reconciles the
+  superseded unsigned proposal with the signed contract.
+- `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-dispatch-owner-client-review-20261028.md` records the initial MAJOR and
+  focused re-review of the temporary fail-closed stub.
+- `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-root-runtime-provisioning-plan-20261028.md` records a non-secret,
+  unprovisioned identity map and the current read-only WSL inventory.
+- `core/STATE.md`, `core/BACKLOG.md`, `core/DECISION_LOG.md`, and `core/LESSONS_LOG.md` record the
+  current S2 state, ownership, GPT-PM decisions, corrected symlink-mode interpretation, and the
+  owner-client provenance lesson.
+
+## Key decisions
+
+GPT-PM source request `7c64c79c-452c-454f-9c55-3143a0fe2976` returned `MODIFY — OPTION A WITH
+SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION`, correlated reply `4c5606a1-6026-56e3-914b-61c89a7e45a9`, job
+`65d31f0e-ba68-411a-8d9a-aeaa5d6c1f0d`, user turn `820712a7-3927-4abd-b115-8755623ac987`. The
+signed fields bind `version`, `algorithm`, `purpose`, `request_id`, `task_id`, `slot`, `attempt`,
+`epoch`, `run_id`, `key_id`, and `expires_at`. The issuer supplies the request ID; the client does
+not derive a substitute. Root Supervisor independently verifies the pinned purpose-specific
+public key's principal and signature before Store admission. The exact signed envelope is included
+in event and idempotency data.
+
+No unsigned compatibility fallback is permitted. The current event-history validator rejects a
+legacy unsigned dispatch event, causing Store startup/history verification to fail closed rather
+than allowing it to reach a grant. Compatibility with any pre-existing such Store has not been
+proven; no automatic conversion or migration was performed.

+The trusted issuer and public key are not present in current evidence. The production path remains
+unusable until an independently authorized issuer and root-pinned public key are provided through
+the proper custody path. Do not create/reuse a signing key or claim M01 acceptance.

+# Change 0518: fence S2 dispatch-owner admission after uncertain completion
+
+## Why
+
+GPT-PM identified that `Restart=no` does not disable a separate active systemd socket unit. After a
+Supervisor call whose durable result is unknown, the socket could start the relay again and admit a
+later instruction before the first request had been reconciled. The exact correlated review and
+required lifecycle design are recorded in
+`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-admission-fence-adjudication-20261029.md`.
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_client.py` now distinguishes a local signed-envelope refusal from any
+  unconfirmed result after the transport call starts. Transport errors, explicit error replies,
+  malformed responses and response-binding failures become `DispatchOutcomeUnknown`; no exception
+  is interpreted as proof that a durable intent was not accepted.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_service.py` requires a single bounded canonical frame followed by EOF
+  (client write-half-close), refuses trailing bytes before Supervisor RPC, returns
+  `reconciliation_required` for unknown results when possible, and exits with status 75 without
+  accepting another connection.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_latch.py` is a root-only systemd `ExecStopPost` helper. On every service
+  termination it atomically persists a root-owned admission latch under `/etc/vst-runner`, then
+  requests that systemd stop the socket unit. It records bounded systemd termination metadata and
+  logs latch/socket-stop outcomes. The unprivileged relay never writes this file.
+- Both dispatch-owner systemd units use `ConditionPathExists=!` for the latch, and service config
+  loading independently refuses while the latch exists. The service unit invokes the root helper
+  with the documented `+` command prefix. The runtime allowlist includes the helper.
+- The service contract, deployment README, non-secret provisioning plan, project state/backlog,
+  decision log and lessons log now specify service/socket lifecycle, failure classes, queued
+  connection behavior, exact Store reconciliation and explicit reopening.
+
+## Contracts and decisions
+
+The local owner relay remains a signed-instruction ingress only. Pub/Sub and the existing Store and
+Supervisor remain the sole assignment/delivery authorities. Local framing, canonical-JSON,
+signature, expiry, principal and trust-registry failures happen before Supervisor RPC and do not
+fence admission. Once a verified envelope crosses that RPC boundary, an unconfirmed result is
+non-approving and stops the relay. There is no automatic retry or latch clearing.
+
+Before independently authorized recovery, inspect the exact signed request ID in the verified
+`DISPATCH_INTENT_ACCEPTED` event and matching `supervisor_operations` idempotency result; compare the
+complete envelope, principal, generation and digest; and inspect subscription/grant state. Store
+commits the event and idempotency result transactionally. Do not replay a present event. Absence is
+not inferred from an RPC error; any retry or replacement requires fresh root/Store checks and a
+separately authorized recovery. Stop and verify the socket is inactive before clearing the latch;
+then explicitly reopen it after reconciliation.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Tests, checks, builds and systemd validation: `NOT_RUN` in this change.
+- Runtime provisioning, `/etc` writes, root helper invocation, service/socket activation, migration,
+  real dispatch, key operation, E5, push, PR and merge: not performed.
+- `functional-test-reviewer` updated focused test sources for the new EOF and fail-stop contract;
+  they remain unexecuted pending the e2e-runner phase.
+- Source is uncommitted pending coding freeze, designated test author/executor, specialist review,
+  fixes and exact-head GPT-PM code/plan gates.
+
+## Acceptance and ownership
+
+This change resolves the draft for `S2-PROV-M03`; it does not close the finding. Required synthetic
+coverage includes an ambiguous Supervisor completion followed by another connection, no RPC for a
+trailing frame or non-half-closed request, persistent root latch behavior, startup refusal with a
+latch, and explicit reconciliation/reopen ordering. Codex owns source and evidence; the
+functional-test-reviewer/e2e-runner own mapped test authoring/execution after source freeze; GPT-PM
+owns focused architecture adjudication; the operator owns any separately authorized privileged
+recovery or production provisioning. `S2-DISPATCH-M01` remains MAJOR/OPEN, S2 remains NOT APPROVED,
+and S3 remains unstarted.

diff --git a/docs/changes/0522-correct-s2-dispatch-latch-stop-order.md b/docs/changes/0522-correct-s2-dispatch-latch-stop-order.md

+# Change 0522: stop S2 dispatch socket before latch storage access
+
+## Why
+
+Independent code and reliability reviews of the 0518 admission fence found a fail-open path. The
+root `ExecStopPost` helper first inspected and wrote `/etc`, then requested an asynchronous socket
+stop. A filesystem stall could let systemd kill the hook while the listener remained active, and a
+latch write failure did not prove that socket shutdown had completed. An active `.socket` can
+activate the relay even when its service uses `Restart=no`.
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_latch.py` now synchronously stops
+  `vst-dispatch-owner.socket` and confirms `ActiveState=inactive` before any `/etc` filesystem
+  access. Failed commands, timeouts and uncertain states retry with a bounded timeout per
+  `systemctl` call and capped exponential backoff. The hook logs each unresolved state and does not
+  proceed while socket shutdown is uncertain.
+- `tools/vst/systemd/vst-dispatch-owner.service` sets `TimeoutStopSec=infinity`, so systemd does
+  not kill `ExecStopPost` while it is holding the admission barrier or persisting the latch. This
+  deliberately trades availability for fail-closed behavior: an unavailable system manager or
+  unhealthy `/etc` can hold service shutdown indefinitely and requires operator-visible recovery.
+- Latch persistence follows confirmed socket shutdown. If the persistent write fails, the listener
+  is inactive at that point and the helper reports failure; without the latch, a later explicit
+  socket start is not guarded. Cross-reboot safety is not established in that case; healthy durable
+  root-controlled `/etc` remains a hard requirement before any later start or reboot. No `/etc`
+  write, root helper invocation, systemd activation or runtime
+  provisioning occurred in this change.
+- `tests/vst/test_s2_dispatch_owner_latch.py` was updated by `functional-test-reviewer` to cover
+  stop-before-storage ordering, inactive-state confirmation, retry after failure/active state,
+  per-command timeout, the absence of `--no-block`, persistence failure after shutdown, and the
+  unit timeout contract. The designated test executor has not run these tests yet.
+- The service contract, admission-fence adjudication, root runtime plan, systemd README and project
+  state/backlog now record the corrected order, indefinite-stop trade-off and storage limitation.
+
+## Failure matrix
+
+| Failure step | Resulting state | Recovery owner/action | Evidence |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Stop command fails, times out, or socket remains active/unknown | Hook stays in `ExecStopPost`; no `/etc` access; no acceptance of successful shutdown | Codex keeps the code fail-closed; operator restores systemd availability; hook retries | Synthetic retry/confirmation test; installed-systemd behavior remains `NOT_RUN` |
+| Parent `stat`, latch open/write, or `fsync` stalls after socket is inactive | Listener is confirmed stopped; systemd does not kill the hook due to `TimeoutStopSec=infinity`; service shutdown may remain pending | Operator repairs durable root-controlled storage; then verifies persistent fence before restart | Test asserts ordering and unit timeout; filesystem-stall runtime scenario `NOT_RUN` |
+| Latch persistence errors after socket stop | Socket is inactive at confirmation; helper exits visibly, but no latch guards a later explicit start and cross-reboot safety is unproven | Operator must restore `/etc` and ensure the durable fence exists before any later start/reboot; no automatic reopening | Synthetic persistence-failure test; root filesystem behavior `NOT_RUN` |
+| Latch persists successfully | Both service/socket startup conditions and loader reject admission; no automatic retry/reopen | Operator reconciles exact Store request ID and idempotency record before separately authorized recovery | Existing mapped latch/source tests; runtime unit activation `NOT_RUN` |
+
+## Verification and acceptance
+
+- Source/tests were not run by the primary agent. `e2e-runner` owns the next focused run after this
+  coding change is committed.
+- Previous 105/105 synthetic results apply to `cec0dbf3249b5734bdae52f644ac790e07d869f8`, before
+  this correction; they do not validate this change.
+- Systemd unit validation, WSL `/etc` writes, root helper invocation, service/socket activation,
+  real dispatch, migration, account/group creation, keys, E5, push, PR and merge are `NOT_RUN` or
+  prohibited. S2 remains `NOT APPROVED`; S3 remains unstarted.
+- Code and reliability reviewers own fresh focused re-review after the new test run; GPT-PM owns
+  focused M03 re-adjudication and the later exact-head gate. Codex owns this implementation and
+  evidence; the operator owns any future privileged runtime recovery.

+# Change 0525: make S2 dispatch outcome acknowledgement Store-authoritative
+
+## Why
+
+GPT-PM accepted the revised M03 architecture for implementation. The existing root systemd latch
+was written after the service stopped, leaving a crash window before durable latch creation. This
+change closes new-request admission in the Store transaction that accepts an intent, then permits
+admission to resume only after an authenticated relay-forwarding acknowledgement is durably
+recorded. It introduces no scheduler, assignment authority, table migration, or runtime operation.
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py` sets `PRAGMA synchronous=FULL`, reads the setting back, commits the pending
+  outcome control note with the accepted event and idempotency result, reconstructs the complete
+  ordered dispatch event/operation/pending/ack history at startup and before admission or ack, and
+  keeps legacy accepted events unresolved. It exposes an idempotent, tuple-bound acknowledgement.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py` delegates acknowledgement to Store.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py` exposes `ack_dispatch_intent` only for the authenticated
+  `dispatch_owner` role and includes it in that role's exact operation allowlist.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_client.py` binds acknowledgement to the canonical Supervisor result.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_service.py` acknowledges only after local response `sendall()` succeeds;
+  forwarding or acknowledgement failure keeps admission pending and stops the relay. The ack means
+  relay-forwarded, not caller-received.
+- Updated the S2 design note, dispatch-owner service contract, and VST schema documentation to
+  match the implementation and preserve the boundary between source behavior and unverified runtime.
+- Regenerated `governance/DOCUMENT_REGISTRY.md`.
+
+## Verification and acceptance
+
+- GPT-PM design acceptance: request `b992acde-35f0-4f18-91a2-0522c3d4e5f6`, reply
+  `8109099c-53f6-45db-be51-13a0d1e36acf`; this is design authorization, not implementation approval.
+- No tests or runtime dispatch have been run against this change. The earlier 107/107 result at
+  `34bd7dc1b085789341b29937655af52e07f2ddbd` verifies the latch-only version and is not evidence
+  for this Store barrier.
+- Required next evidence: focused functional tests authored by `functional-test-reviewer`, executed
+  by `e2e-runner` after the test source is frozen, fresh code/reliability/security reviews, and
+  GPT-PM exact-head adjudication. M03 remains OPEN until those gates close.

+# Change 0531: reject cross-request S2 barrier history interleavings
+
+## Why
+
+Fresh code review at exact HEAD `80b01c55c700d029e357297f1af920e3b3033683` found that the
+validator checked each request's own `PENDING → ACK` order but did not require that request A be
+acknowledged before a later request B is accepted. A contradictory, hash-valid history could
+therefore be classified as fully acknowledged even if B was accepted while A remained pending.
+
+## What changed
+
+- Dispatch outcome reconstruction now verifies global event ordering: every accepted intent after
+  the first must appear after the preceding intent's acknowledgement. Legacy histories with no
+  protocol controls remain `LEGACY_UNRESOLVED`; a mixture of legacy and new controls is integrity
+  failure.
+- Regenerated `governance/DOCUMENT_REGISTRY.md`.
+
+## Verification and acceptance
+
+- The prior focused run at `80b01c55c700d029e357297f1af920e3b3033683` passed 118/118 but did not
+  cover cross-request interleaving. Exact command and environment are in the e2e-runner record for
+  that head; this source correction remains untested.
+- `code-reviewer` identified the finding as MAJOR. `reliability-reviewer` independently found that
+  a pending result becomes permanently stuck if the Runner generation changes; a signed dispatch
+  reconciliation path is not present. That recovery contract is pending GPT-PM adjudication; no
+  bypass has been implemented.
+- `functional-test-reviewer` owns a regression test for the interleaved history. `e2e-runner` must
+  execute it after test source is frozen and this correction is committed.
+- `security-reviewer` found no actionable issue in peer authorization/result binding at the reviewed
+  head. This does not close the MAJOR findings above.

+# Change 0534: implement S2 M03 cross-generation outcome recovery
+
+## Why
+
+After a crash leaves an accepted dispatch result pending, a new Runner generation can make normal
+same-generation idempotency unable to return the original result. The pending barrier then blocks
+new owner submissions. GPT-PM adjudicated request
+`f67c5dd7-5279-42b1-9dc4-94ed4b72b5a1` as MODIFY: exact historical replay is within accepted M03
+scope, provided it is a separate authenticated read-only path and never becomes new admission.
+
+## What changed
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py`: added a consistent-snapshot read-only lookup that verifies the full event
+  chain and anchor plus accepted event, operation result, and ordered pending/ack protocol. It
+  returns a result only for an exact authenticated-principal and complete-envelope match, preserves
+  the original event sequence and service generation, and refuses legacy-unresolved history.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py` and `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py`: added
+  `replay_dispatch_outcome`, restricted to the authenticated `dispatch_owner` role. It has no
+  current-generation, lease, preflight, grant, or Runner side effects. The role operation allowlist
+  includes only submit, historical replay, and acknowledgement.
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_owner_client.py`: current-valid requests continue through normal admission.
+  After an ambiguous admission response, the client reads verified history without repeating
+  admission. When current signature/expiry/key verification fails, it may only use historical
+  lookup; a miss is refused. Exact response principal and envelope bindings are validated before
+  local forwarding/ACK.
+- Updated the S2 schema and owner-service contract, recorded GPT-PM's adjudication, and reconciled
+  project state.
+
+## Decision and boundaries
+
+GPT-PM reply `5cd963a6-2a9a-4ae7-96c6-f3955df216ea` requires current key expiry/revocation not to
+erase a previously accepted fact, while current authorization remains mandatory for new admission.
+An absent or mismatched result never falls through to admission. Legacy, incomplete, corrupt, or
+contradictory Store history remains closed. A compromise incident that casts doubt on a historical
+acceptance requires separate security reconciliation; replay does not make a new trust decision.
+The Store outcome barrier remains separate from Runner claim/reservation recovery.
+
+## Verification state
+
+- Baseline repository HEAD before these source/docs edits: `1bd00cbacac099f34717e9c68fc720a467f6d519`.
+- Mapped focused functional tests at exact follow-up HEAD
+  `c855ca4f2888d7288b006973950e4c6d28023b63`: **130 passed, 0 failed**; exact commands, hashes,
+  and limits are in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-cross-generation-outcome-recovery-test-run-20261029.md`.
+  Fresh code, security, reliability and database reviews found no valid BLOCKER/MAJOR. GPT-PM
+  request `d16dbf96-54f8-4c96-8fa7-2b24445f85d9` returned ACCEPT — SOURCE/TEST SCOPE and closed
+  `S2-PROV-M03-R01`; see
+  `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-cross-generation-outcome-recovery-exact-source-review-20261029.md`.
+- No production identity, root configuration, key, service, runtime/E5, real dispatch, prohibited
+  selector, push, PR, or merge was performed by this change.
+- `S2-PROV-M03-R01` is closed for source/test scope. Overall S2 remains NOT APPROVED;
+  `S2-DISPATCH-M01`, runtime/E5, production configuration, prohibited selectors, and the final
+  exact-head S2 gate remain open. S3 remains unstarted.

+# Change 0540: add explicit S2 runtime artifact staging
+
+## Purpose
+
+Separate immutable artifact installation from selector and fixed-name unit selection so the
+reviewed bootstrap transition can inspect exact staged bytes before any path is switched.
+
+## Changes
+
+- Added opt-in PowerShell `-StageOnly`, passed to the WSL bootstrap as an explicit mode and to the
+  runtime installer as `--stage-only`. The default installer invocation keeps its existing
+  selector/unit validation and installation path.
+- Stage-only performs the source-bundle, OS/WSL configuration, mount and immutable destination
+  checks, then retains the exact versioned runtime tree and worker helper. It skips fixed selector
+  and unit checks/writes and reports `selected=false`, `systemd_units_installed=0`.
+- Stage-only requires absent `/etc/vst-runner`, `/run/vst-supervisor` and `/run/vst-runner`;
+  exactly inactive or not-found S2 units; no matching systemd jobs (parsed as `JOB UNIT TYPE
+  STATE`); and empty inspectable cgroups. Unknown unit states, malformed job rows, or failure to
+  enumerate any required state refuse staging. The WSL installer independently repeats these
+  preconditions so direct invocation cannot bypass the host handoff checks.
+- Added no transition, config, Store, key, identity, service-start or cleanup operation. Existing
+  immutable destination collision remains fail-closed. The separate reviewed bootstrap selector
+  transition is still required.
+
+## Paths and contract
+
+`tools/qa/install_wsl_runtime.ps1` and `tools/qa/install_wsl_runner_runtime.sh`. Stage output
+retains `/opt/vst-runtime-<full-head>` and the versioned worker helper for a later exact-fingerprint
+transition. This interface does not claim that the versioned artifacts are selected or accepted.
+
+## Verification and status
+
+No tests, checks, build, WSL provisioning or service operation were run. This change is uncommitted.
+It implements the phase-6 runtime staging slice only; the bootstrap selector/unit transition and
+manifest validator remain outstanding. Later test roles must verify default-mode compatibility,
+stage-only no-selection, collisions and exact immutable artifact verification after all S2 coding
+is complete.

+# Change 0541: prepare exact S2 bootstrap runtime selection
+
+## Purpose and provenance
+
+Implement the reviewed phase-6 runtime-only design in canonical checkout
+`D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`; no per-sprint worktree is used. AF sprint
+`39b7cc253f5d` tracks existing S2. The source/stage plan review and the post-stage selector
+manifest are distinct. The selector manifest digest supplied to `apply` must come from the
+external exact-manifest review; computing that digest here is not approval.
+
+## Changed paths and behavior
+
+- `tools/vst/runtime_bundle.py` defines a closed canonical non-secret manifest contract and a
+  candidate builder from the staged exact runtime. It binds source/archive/spec revisions, old
+  runtime and selector, complete new runtime tree, helper source/binary/path/identity, six old/new
+  unit fingerprints, and fixed parent metadata. Duplicate, unknown, missing, noncanonical and
+  mismatched fields fail closed.
+- `tools/vst/bootstrap_runtime.py` provides the root-only prepare/apply/recover entry point and
+  `tools/qa/select_wsl_bootstrap_runtime.py` is the canonical-repository wrapper. The immutable
+  runtime package contains the implementation under `tools/vst`, allowing a fixed full-versioned
+  module path at execution.
+- Apply requires the externally supplied exact manifest SHA-256, absent config/runtime socket
+  paths, all six units inactive with no jobs or populated service cgroups, unchanged root-owned
+  parents, exact old selector/unit/runtime and staged new artifact fingerprints. It does not open
+  Store, install config, create keys, enable/start/reload services or issue tasks.
+- Every selector/unit replacement is one same-directory atomic operation, not a collective
+  transaction. A root-only write-ahead journal syncs intent before each rename and completion
+  after filesystem sync. Recovery checks the whole set against old/new states before any write;
+  unknown third-party bytes refuse the whole recovery. Restored prior file snapshots and displaced
+  new files are retained; an absent prior unit is restored by moving the new file to a retained
+  quarantine, not deleting it. Configured-host upgrades are not supported.
+
+## Review and verification state
+
+This source is not yet independently reviewed or test-verified. Per workspace test ownership, the
+functional-test-reviewer/e2e-runner author and execute mapped tests only after all S2 coding is

+real staging or selection.

+# Change 0543: add bounded S2 machine source contracts
+
+## Scope and decision basis
+
+Sprint: S2. Implementation is limited to pure validation of proposed, externally signed
+delegation/assignment records and collection/hash/evaluation of read-only host observations.
+The current human E5 v1 contract remains authoritative. This source change adds no signing
+service, private-key creation/provisioning, Supervisor dispatch path, E5 PASS, config installation
+or runtime activation.
+
+GPT-PM returned MODIFY for request `a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55`, correlated reply
+`0b0b8a4d-0816-4146-ba21-71857b5de49d`. Its exact response is in
+`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-machine-authority-adjudication-20261029.md`. The two MAJOR findings remain
+open until the corrected contract and source receive focused review and GPT-PM verification.
+Security review authorized pure schema/signature-verification helpers and read-only observation
+completeness only. The proposed external assignment record and trust purpose do not exist in the
+current repository and must not be described as existing authority.
+
+## Source changes
+
+- `tools/vst/machine_authorization.py` defines closed candidate schemas for the delegation policy,
+  external signed assignment authorization, and root-configured trust registry. The policy pins
+  a distinct operator key ID; the assignment carries both operator authorization key ID and the
+  intended delegated issuer key ID/purpose; both operator and machine keys carry revocation IDs.
+  It rejects
+  unknown/missing keys, malformed identifiers/digests/signatures, invalid times, mismatched
+  purpose/key/policy bindings, and revocation. Verification uses the existing bounded OpenSSL
+  public-key helper. Assignment matching compares one caller-supplied authenticated read-only
+  Store snapshot; the module performs no Store I/O, task enumeration, mutation or signing.
+- `tools/vst/machine_observations.py` defines bounded read-only WSL command/proc collection and a
+  fixed Windows PowerShell snapshot attempt. It preserves raw observations and errors, hashes
+  canonical records, and returns only `OBSERVATIONS_COMPLETE` or `UNKNOWN`. The Windows effective
+  rule normalizer is intentionally unsupported, so a Windows snapshot remains UNKNOWN. No result
+  is an E5 PASS, policy verdict, trusted collector signature, or Supervisor input.
+
+The assignment verification helper accepts exactly one caller-supplied Store snapshot and
+compares the signed fields with it. It does not itself authenticate how the caller obtained that
+snapshot; no production caller is wired. The policy verifier also requires the root trust config
+to pin the machine key to the digest of the complete canonical signed policy. The E5 observation
+bundle currently emits unsigned source receipts and fixed same-time metadata; its evaluator always
+returns `UNKNOWN` because no pinned collector trust or complete policy normalizer exists.
+
+## Verification state and limitations
+
+No tests/checks, collection, build, key operation, provisioning, migration, or activation was
+performed for this change. The modules have not been independently reviewed. Their schemas are
+candidate source contracts; no matching authority keys/configs exist. The assignment helper trusts
+that its caller obtained the supplied Store snapshot through the authenticated Supervisor read
+boundary. That integration is not implemented here. Windows normalized effective-firewall and
+WSL/Hyper-V evidence is unsupported; both machine findings and S2 remain open. Changes are
+uncommitted.

+# Change 0545: keep assignment revocation independent from policy revocation
+
+## Scope and reason
+
+Sprint: S2. Correct the candidate assignment verifier in
+`tools/vst/machine_authorization.py` after phase-7 test feedback found that the field-binding
+loop compared the assignment record's own `revocation_id` with the signed delegation policy's
+different `revocation_id`. The two records have independent revocation identities; equality is
+not part of the assignment contract and caused valid, independently revocable assignments to be
+rejected before signature and current-Store-snapshot verification.
+
+## Change
+
+Removed `revocation_id` from the policy-to-assignment equality bindings. The verifier continues
+to reject an assignment when its own `revocation_id` occurs in the configured revocation list.
+The signed policy continues to be checked by `verify_policy`, which independently checks the
+policy revocation identifier and the delegated machine principal's revocation identifier. The
+assignment verifier also independently rejects a revoked delegated issuer principal. No schema,
+signature, project binding, issuer key binding, policy digest, or Store snapshot comparison was
+weakened.
+
+## Verification and limits
+
+This is a source-only correction prompted by phase-7 test-agent feedback. No tests/checks were run
+by this implementation agent. The test owner is to rerun the focused assignment authorization
+case and its revoked-assignment/policy controls. The module remains a candidate validator, not a
+production caller or authority source; caller-provided Store snapshot authentication is outside
+this function. No signing service, private-key handling, Store I/O/mutation, E5 PASS, runtime
+activation, provisioning, or production dispatch was added.
+
+The earlier candidate-contract record is
+`docs/changes/0543-s2-machine-source-contracts.md`; this file records the later correction and
+must be committed with the corresponding source change.
