+# Change 0547: make bootstrap journal preparation and recovery retryable
+
+## Scope and starting state
+
+Baseline for the owned source files: initial `git status --short` returned no entries for
+`tools/vst/bootstrap_runtime.py`, `tools/vst/runtime_bundle.py`, and this change-record path;
+these files are the ongoing local S2 implementation. This focused correction changes only
+`tools/vst/bootstrap_runtime.py` and adds this record. No protected evidence or other checkout
+was accessed.
+
+## Failure windows corrected
+
+Journal preparation now occurs in a unique root-owned mode-0700 `.preparing-<manifest>-<nonce>`
+directory. It durably writes the exact manifest and `preparing` state before copying any unit
+snapshots. Only after all snapshots, the ready journal state, each file and the directory are
+synced does `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` publish the directory under its final transaction ID.
+The selector and unit files remain untouched until publication succeeds. The ordinary apply scan
+validates and retains unpublished preparation directories but does not treat them as armed
+transactions, so an I/O failure during the first manifest/state/snapshot write cannot trap future
+apply or recovery attempts. Retries use a new nonce and never remove or overwrite a partial
+preparation. Final journal name collisions refuse safely.
+
+When restoring a previous regular unit, recovery now writes the selected new bytes to a fresh,
+exclusive random retained path, verifies its digest, and syncs the retained directory before
+restoring the previous bytes. A failed short write leaves its partial copy retained; the next
+attempt chooses a different no-replace name. If failure occurs after a complete retained copy but
+before replacement, retry may retain another copy, then safely finish. No partial copy is treated
+as valid, and no file is deleted. Existing full-set old/new preflight remains before any recovery
+write. A previously absent unit is still restored by atomic rename into the retained quarantine.
+
+## Verification status and handoff
+
+No tests, checks, compilation, provisioning or runtime command were run. The functional/E2E role
+is adding deterministic ordinary-I/O exception cases after source coding freezes; no process-kill
+or power-loss selector was authorized. Hand off these two correction points for fresh focused
+review; test owners then verify partial preparation retry, failed partial retention retry,
+durability ordering, no fixed-path mutation before journal publication, and whole-set recovery
+preflight. The runtime selector remains source-only and does not open Store, activate services or
+close S2.

+# Change 0548: Read-only S2 authenticated assignment basis
+
+## State
+
+Implemented in this coding pass; no tests, checks, or runtime acceptance were run. The source is
+fail-closed until a separately reviewed authenticated assignment writer, root-owned policy, and
+dedicated delegated_issuer peer are installed. Existing deployment configurations keep their
+previous schema and do not enable the feature.
+
+## Why
+
+The read-only issuer needs provenance stronger than a legacy owner string or lease row. It must
+bind one exact authenticated assignment operation to the append-only Store history and then
+recheck current Store authority without creating a nested SQLite transaction.
+
+## Changed contracts and paths
+
+- Added tools/vst/assignment_basis.py with closed validators for root policy, handoff, request,
+  and response; the module has no signing key, persistence, or assignment writer.
+- Refactored Store.execution_grant_basis() to delegate its existing validation and result
+  calculation to _execution_grant_basis_locked(). Its public signature and preflight checks stay
+  unchanged.
+- Added Store.authenticated_assignment_basis(). It reads the operation row, exact supervisor
+  NOTE event, complete keyed event chain, configured external anchor, supervisor record/event
+  correspondence, consumed probe, and live task/owner/lease basis under one read snapshot. It
+  refuses absent or legacy operation names and checks the canonical handoff result and its digest.
+- Added Supervisor.assignment_basis(), which uses only constructor-supplied root policy and the
+  configured active-generation provider. Callers cannot select a task, owner, policy, lease, or
+  generation.
+- Added the optional delegated_issuer RPC role, with exactly assignment_basis. It is enabled
+  only when the fixed root policy path and its exact SHA-256 pin are both present in the root
+  service configuration and the peer identity matches that policy. Existing peer allowlists and
+  the default deployment schema are unchanged.
+
+## Decisions and limits
+
+- The authenticated assignment mutation endpoint, role, producer, keys, signing, provisioning,
+  database migration, and E5 integration were not added.
+- A valid row cannot be produced by this change. The reader therefore refuses all legacy records
+  and reports no basis until a separate writer creates the exact operation and linked event.
+- The current policy contract carries a revocation_id but does not define a separate revocation
+  registry. Each request reloads the fixed root-controlled policy and requires it to equal the
+  startup config's exact digest pin. Removal, unreadability, or any replacement fails closed.
+  Per-assignment revocation is not supported; revoking one assignment requires replacing the
+  whole pinned policy.
+- The handoff contains the exact bootstrap request. The reader validates its manifest with the
+  repository TaskManifest validator, checks the task/story/slot against the root allowlist,
+  recomputes the domain-separated operation key, and recomputes the Store payload digest from the
+  request, kernel-mapped bootstrap peer, and policy digest.
+- Change 0549 adds the handoff's required service generation and checks both it and the current
+  Supervisor run ID inside the Store snapshot. Older handoffs are not upgraded.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Tests and checks: NOT_RUN; explicitly deferred until coding is complete and the designated
+  functional-test reviewer takes ownership.
+- Runtime acceptance: NOT_RUN; the authenticated writer and root-owned deployment policy are
+  absent from this bounded change.
+- No commit was created.

+# Change 0549: Fence S2 assignment handoffs to the active run and generation
+
+## State
+
+Implemented as a bounded source correction. Tests and checks remain NOT_RUN; the designated
+functional-test reviewer owns adapting the red source fixture and validating the stale-run and
+stale-generation cases.
+
+## Why
+
+The assignment-basis response reports the currently observed service generation. Without a
+generation recorded in the durable handoff, an old assignment/probe could be observed again by a
+new service generation and appear current. The Supervisor's trusted run identity must also match
+the run bound into the handoff.
+
+## Change
+
+- Added required service_generation to the exact authenticated handoff schema and validate it as
+  a canonical identifier. No legacy handoff shape is upgraded.
+- Supervisor.assignment_basis() now requires its configured run identity and passes both that
+  identity and the currently resolved service generation to the Store.
+- Store.authenticated_assignment_basis() compares the handoff run ID and recorded generation to
+  those trusted current values inside the same read transaction that verifies the handoff, event
+  chain, external anchor, consumed probe, live lease, and owner epoch.
+- A mismatch fails closed; the response can no longer stamp a previous-generation handoff with the
+  current generation.
+
+## Verification
+
+- Tests/checks: NOT_RUN; code is handed to the designated functional-test reviewer.
+- Runtime acceptance: NOT_RUN.
+- No assignment mutation, key, migration, or commit was added.

+
+## State

+Source implemented and disabled by default. No tests, build, provisioning, or
+activation were performed in the coding pass. The implementer later reported one accidental

+mapped rollback, replay, eligibility, stale-state, and budget regressions after the source batch
+freezes; no test files were edited here.
+
+## Contract
+
+- The authenticated Supervisor RPC operation is bootstrap_assignment. Its only caller role is
+  assignment_bootstrap, with exactly that operation. Kernel peer UID/GID, pidfd, and cgroup checks
+  are inherited from the existing root Supervisor RPC boundary.
+- Root policy is the only source for the allowed story/task/project/phase, canonical manifest
+  digest and TestRun slot, owner principal, runner identity, owner/lease TTLs, policy digest, and
+  maximum handoff lifetime. The configured runner_id maps directly to the Store lease worker_id
+  and the handoff runner_id. The caller cannot supply those trusted fields.
+- The exact bootstrap request contains schema, request_id, story_id, task_id, task_manifest,
+  slot, attempt, and run_id. It must be a canonical valid TaskManifest, an exact root-policy tuple,
+  and attempt 1. Extra or missing request fields fail closed.
+- The operation key is SHA-256 over the domain-separated canonical tuple of policy digest,
+  task_id, story_id, task-manifest digest, and request_id. The idempotency payload is the canonical
+  request, kernel-mapped bootstrap peer, and policy digest. Exact replay returns the exact stored
+  result; conflicting operation or payload refuses.
+- One Store.execute_idempotent transaction creates a previously absent story and task, seeds the
+  exact manifest cost budget, advances the new story from epoch 1 to epoch 2, claims attempt 1 and
+  one free Store slot, writes the handoff, then writes the immutable operation row and linked
+  supervisor event. A pre-commit verifier rechecks event/table integrity, policy digest, current
+  generation, consumed probe, owner, lease, and handoff on the same transaction connection. Any
+  failed check rolls back the entire transaction.
+- Fresh eligibility requires no story/task row, relevant event history, lease, receipt, budget row,
+  terminal marker, prior handoff, or noninitial attempt. It does not adopt, resume, retry, renew,
+  or switch an assignment. Public Store methods retain their own transaction boundaries and the
+  legacy acquire_lease commit-before-raise behavior.

+# Change 0553: Pure S2 root-bound dispatch issuance contract
+
+## State
+
+Bounded pure source preparation implemented under GPT-PM decision
+`8b6b69f3-9b39-491b-a948-03c497870b5d`, correlated reply
+`b1728c67-3bc2-4db5-9fbf-6b359a73ad82`. A follow-up reducer finding was fixed in this pass:
+completion can no longer be accepted on envelope shape and digest alone. This does not implement
+a signer, Store journal, Supervisor callsite, key/config producer, or runtime activation. Tests,
+checks, build, runtime, review, PM exact-head verification, and commit were not performed in this
+coding pass.
+
+## Contract and changed paths
+
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_issuance.py` adds detached validators for canonical duplicate-free JSON,
+  the exact assignment policy and handoff shapes, explicit `DELEGATED_V1` key binding, stable
+  deterministic issuance identities, and a frozen unsigned dispatch-instruction v1 intent.
+- Request IDs use the approved
+  `VST_S2_ROOT_DISPATCH_REQUEST_ID_V1\0` domain and the first 128 bits of SHA-256 over the
+  canonical full validated handoff. Operation keys use the separate
+  `VST_S2_ROOT_DISPATCH_ISSUANCE_OPERATION_V1\0` domain over the stable assignment operation ID;
+  the full digest is retained. The frozen payload digest binds the full handoff, policy,
+  unsigned v1 fields, current authority tuple, and signer identity.
+- Freezing requires the explicit finite issuer maximum TTL and minimum safety slack from the
+  approved root configuration. It persists both inputs and the preparation time, then verifies
+  that expiry exactly equals the minimum TTL/handoff/policy/current-authority bound and retains
+  the configured slack. No numeric TTL or slack is invented by this module.
+- The pure event reducer accepts only intent → signing-started → completion or unknown ordering.
+  A started operation without durable completion reduces to `UNKNOWN`; malformed bindings,
+  duplicate/misordered events, changed payloads, and altered completion envelopes reduce to
+  `CONFLICT`. `PENDING` and `UNKNOWN` never report signing authority. A Store transaction must
+  separately claim a signing-started marker before any later implementation can invoke a signer.
+- A durable completion is accepted only when `reduce_issuance_state(...,
+  completion_verifier=callback)` receives an injected callable. Its exact interface is
+  `callback(frozen_signer_binding, signing_bytes, signature_bytes) -> bool`: the binding is a
+  copy of the frozen `{key_id, key_class, purpose, public_key_fingerprint}`, `signing_bytes` are
+  produced by the unchanged v1 `dispatch_instruction_signing_bytes` contract (the
+  `VST_S2_DISPATCH_INSTRUCTION_V1\0` domain followed by canonical unsigned-envelope bytes), and
+  `signature_bytes` are the decoded Ed25519 signature. The reducer first checks exact unsigned
+  equality against the frozen intent and the envelope key ID against the frozen signer; it accepts
+  only the literal result `True`. The callback must verify Ed25519 and establish that its
+  root-pinned public key has the frozen fingerprint and key identity. A missing verifier, false or
+  non-literal-true result, or verifier exception yields `CONFLICT`. This callback contract does not
+  provide key access or signing authority; the pure module reads no key and stores no verifier.
+- The signing-started event now passes closed-schema validation before either `UNKNOWN` or
+  completion can return, so unexpected extra fields consistently produce `CONFLICT`.
+- Current revocation and expiry are an overlay (`REVOKED_EXPIRED`) and do not rewrite historical
+  state. The reducer never infers signing authority from records and always returns
+  `may_sign: false`. Existing v1 wire fields, signing domain, and signature encoding validation
+  were not changed.
+
+## Verification and remaining acceptance
+
+- Source and interface were compared against `tools/vst/dispatch_instruction.py`:
+  `verify_dispatch_instruction(value, trust_registry, *, expected_principal, openssl_path,
+  now=None)` validates envelope shape, then uses `dispatch_instruction_signing_bytes` and the
+  root-configured trust entry to verify the unchanged v1 signature domain. The pure callback
+  adapter is not wired to that runtime verifier in this change. Independent review remains
+  required for exact source.

+  pure validation.

+  coordination pass after the explicit source and record paths were staged.

+# Change 0554: Root issuer verification and transaction contract
+
+Sprint: 39b7cc253f5d
+
+## Why and behavior
+
+Actual database and security reviewers identified two MAJOR design omissions in the root-bound v1 issuer proposal: accepting a structurally valid completion without cryptographic verification, and separating delegated provenance checks from the snapshot/commit which grants authority. The proposal now requires a trusted verifier bound to exact signing bytes, signer fingerprint and immutable journal identity. External cryptographic processes and key reads stay outside SQL; the Store binds a root-owned verification context to exact bytes inside the current transaction. The pure callback contract was committed separately in change0553.
+
+Admission, delivery observation, grant persistence/replay and durable runner claim/reservation use a shared connection-taking current-authority predicate and locked grant-basis helper. Delivery is explicitly a snapshot hint; it cannot preserve authority after revocation. Delegate-origin work cannot fall through to legacy because the feature is disabled or provenance is missing. No new wire version, scheduler, daemon, table or migration is proposed.

+# S2 headless Windows observation runtime
+
+## Change
+
+The bounded subprocess adapter now creates Windows children with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. The Windows
+observation collector runs with a fixed `C:\Windows\System32` working directory and a deliberately
+small environment containing only Windows runtime roots, an empty `PATH`, and a profile-specific
+`PSModulePath` pinned to the fixed system module directory (`...WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\Modules`
+for Windows PowerShell 5 or `...PowerShell\7\Modules` for PowerShell 7). It does not inherit
+ambient environment variables or user module-path settings. Windows process identity remains the
+current process identity. Non-Windows subprocess behavior retains its prior `/` working directory
+and `LC_ALL=C`, empty-`PATH` environment.
+
+`collect_windows_observations()` accepts the explicit `windows-powershell-5` profile by default,
+or the opt-in `powershell-7` profile at the fixed `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe` path.
+It does not silently switch profiles. The fixed command remains `-NoLogo`, `-NoProfile`,
+`-NonInteractive`, and `-ExecutionPolicy Restricted` with the embedded read-only script. The
+script addresses WSL through `C:\Windows\System32\wsl.exe`, so the intentionally empty `PATH`
+does not make executable lookup depend on ambient state. The chosen profile is preserved in
+`raw_command_outputs.collector_profile`, including when the process yields no output.
+
+## Contract and limits
+
+The existing per-command timeout and output caps are unchanged. Missing executables, host startup
+errors, timeouts, and output failures remain `UNKNOWN` or `UNSUPPORTED` collection evidence. The
+normalizer still reports `UNKNOWN`; `collection_complete` remains false and this collector cannot
+produce an E5 attestation, policy verdict, production authority, or `PASS`. The broader Windows
+rule/filter query has not been expanded or normalized. PowerShell 7 is a distinct, explicitly
+selected diagnostic profile, not an equivalent or fallback replacement for Windows PowerShell 5.
+
+## Provenance and verification
+
+The pre-edit checkout was clean for the two assigned paths at source HEAD
+`0cef101ee70be03b0436d82fad459916a79ee65b`. The in-scope observation record is
+[`s2-machine-observations-20261029.md`](../sdlc/evidence/s2-machine-observations-20261029.md): it
+records the Windows PowerShell 5.1 startup error `8009001d`, zero output, and a separate successful
+limited PowerShell 7 profile query; the wider PowerShell 7 query exceeded its 60-second bound.
+Those are recorded observations, not reproduced by this change. No collector invocation, runtime
+command, test, check, build, CI action, activation, or key/config access was performed for this
+change. Runtime behavior remains unverified pending the separately assigned test/evidence phase.
+
+The PowerShell7 module path includes its fixed installation modules and the fixed Windows
+system module root, so Windows-only NetSecurity cmdlets remain discoverable without inheriting
+user module directories. This root integration correction was made before source freeze; actual
+module loading and output remain unverified until the permitted test/evidence phase.

+# Change 0557: S2 integrated root dispatch issuer source
+
+## Scope and authorization
+
+This source change follows the bounded I01 GO recorded in `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-i01-integrated-source-adjudication-20261029.md` (request `c7a8e23e-91f5-489c-a096-c813d84c3b12`, correlated reply `7c3e4eb6-3300-5c5b-ba5c-85aaa10d0487`). It adds a default-off root dispatch signing path using the existing v1 instruction bytes and existing SQLite operation/event journal. It does not provision keys, enable production signing, or claim S2 acceptance.
+
+## Source changes
+
+- `tools/vst/store.py` adds specialized reservation, signer-start, completion, UNKNOWN, and read-verification operations for `VST_S2_ROOT_DISPATCH_ISSUE_V1`. The existing generic external idempotency operation is not used. Startup validates the issuance journal structure, event order, row binding, immutable intent and envelope shape; startup deliberately does not infer cryptographic completion.
+- `tools/vst/root_dispatch_issuer.py` freezes the assignment handoff, policy, signer fingerprint, unsigned v1 envelope, TTL and safety slack before the signer. It calls OpenSSL outside Store transactions, verifies the result with the pinned public key, then asks Store to persist the verified completion. A failure after the started marker is recorded as UNKNOWN where possible.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor.py` adds an operation-ID-only root API. It obtains the current root policy and service generation and reads the exact Store-backed authenticated handoff before invoking the signer.
+- `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py` adds an optional issuer configuration (disabled when absent) and an authenticated `delegated_issuer` RPC restricted to one assignment operation ID. Key files use fixed root paths and existing root-file permission checks.
+
+## Decisions and compatibility
+
+The dispatch instruction v1 wire format and trust-registry entry shape are unchanged. Existing configuration without `root_dispatch_issuer` remains disabled. No schema, migration, table, daemon, scheduler, or event-chain trigger change was introduced.
+
+## Source-condition disposition
+
+- **SRC-01, grant provenance:** delegated acceptance stores the issuance operation key and exact envelope digest. Dispatch-grant operation payloads bind those values and retain the exact signed execution-grant result. Runner claim and reservation join the supplied grant bytes to that operation and its accepted dispatch/issuance; task tuple matching alone is insufficient.
+- **SRC-02, atomic admission/replay:** new delegated acceptance and exact delegated idempotent replay run the same locked current owner, lease, manifest, probe, receipt-gap and budget predicates. Historical outcome replay remains observational.
+- **SRC-03, verified journal:** issuance has its own event family, strict order/multiplicity/field/row checks, separate from generic internal and external operation families. Event chain and external anchor are checked. Startup checks structure only; COMPLETED is returned only after a root-owned verifier validates the exact v1 signing bytes against the pinned key fingerprint outside SQL. A sealed in-process context binds that verification to the same durable envelope at use.
+- **SRC-04, snapshots/current authority:** admission, delivery validation, grant create/replay, runner claim and runner reservation repeat current Store predicates on the same connection used for the relevant read/write boundary. Root policy and generation providers are re-read at authorization boundaries. Issuance reserve, STARTED and completion writes also recheck the current handoff, policy, generation, probe, owner, lease, manifest, receipt gap and budget.
+- **SRC-05, crash-safe signer:** all fields and expiry are frozen before reservation. Only the transaction that appends the unique STARTED marker may enter OpenSSL. A failure after STARTED records UNKNOWN where possible; no retry signs that identity again. Existing operation replay reads the persisted frozen intent and never computes a new expiry.
+
+No tests, checks, builds, runtime commands, private-key operations, or key provisioning were run. Functional/E2E evidence and independent DB/security review remain `NOT_RUN`/pending for the post-coding phase. The issuer stays default-off; this source change does not activate runtime signing or close S2 Phase 8.
+
+## Provenance
+
+At the initial assigned baseline, `git rev-parse HEAD` returned `0cef101ee70be03b0436d82fad459916a79ee65b`; the assigned source and detail files had no scoped pre-existing diff. Parent-session commits advanced the shared HEAD to `4314957986c56ad0a0babb5994390bb67993a4c3` during implementation; this continuation preserved those commits and continued only the assigned source paths. At final source handoff the shared HEAD was observed at `b5862d517d6c6589a85b8750dd4313ab95238bfd`; the provenance of that concurrent HEAD movement is not attributed here. The initial implementation checkpoint was partial; this updated record reflects the later integrated source work.

+`AuthenticatedSupervisorAPI._dispatch()` at `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py:205` currently
+routes only the declared operations. Its role allowlist at line 776 has no assignment-basis or
+authenticated assignment-bootstrap role. The peer identity comes from kernel credentials and
+cgroup inspection in the same module; a caller-supplied principal is not authentication.
+`Store.acquire_epoch()` accepts a plain owner string. Its value and an event-chain MAC alone do
+not prove an authorized caller established the assignment. The current code has no
+assignment-bootstrap operation or authenticated provenance result. Legacy ownership/lease rows
+therefore cannot by themselves authorize delegated signing.
+
+## Bounded design
+
+Use two separate Supervisor roles, neither enabled by default:
+
+1. `assignment_bootstrap` is the only role allowed to create the exact bounded S2 assignment
+   transition under a concrete, operator-authorized delegation policy. Kernel UID/GID, pidfd and
+   cgroup are mapped to this role in root-owned peer configuration. The Supervisor fixes the
+   actor from that mapping; the request cannot name its own principal, policy digest, owner or
+   epoch. The entrypoint accepts one task/story tuple present in the pinned S2 manifest and only
+   the fixed operations `open_story`, `register_task`, `acquire_epoch`, and `acquire_lease`;
+   implementation must use existing Store invariants and bind the resulting task, current epoch,
+   lease, runner, run and consumed probe. It cannot enumerate tasks or create arbitrary scope.
+   This mutation endpoint is only specified here; implementation and enablement require a fresh
+   independent security/code review under the PM decision.
+2. `delegated_issuer` is read-only. It can call only `assignment_basis`; it receives no direct
+   Store handle and cannot list tasks, create assignments/leases, mutate the Store, or invoke
+   dispatch submission. Its principal and generation are derived from trusted configuration.
+
+The proposed root-owned policy `VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_DELEGATION_POLICY_V1` has exactly these fields:
+`schema`, `policy_id`, `repository`, `sprint_id`, `source_head`, `manifest_sha256`,
+`owner_principal`, `allowed_assignments`, `bootstrap_peer`, `issuer_peer`,
+`allowed_bootstrap_operations`, `maximum_handoff_ttl_seconds`, `valid_from_utc`,
+`expires_at_utc`, and `revocation_id`. `owner_principal` is exactly `Codex`.
+`allowed_assignments` is a nonempty duplicate-free array of exact objects
+`{story_id, task_id, task_manifest_sha256, test_run_slots}`; each slot list is nonempty,
+duplicate-free, and matches only `TestRun` slots in that exact task manifest.
+`bootstrap_peer` and `issuer_peer` each have exactly `{role, uid, gid, cgroup}` with distinct
+positive integer UID/GID pairs; roles are respectively `assignment_bootstrap` and
+`delegated_issuer`. `allowed_bootstrap_operations` is exactly the four-operation array above.
+The TTL is a positive integer bounded by the configured upper limit 300 seconds; validity times
+are canonical UTC and expiry exceeds validity. IDs/digests use the repository's fixed patterns.
+Unknown fields, booleans for integer values, duplicate assignments, duplicate roles, peer
+collisions or any out-of-policy task/slot refuse. Bind `policy_sha256` to the canonical policy
+bytes without a digest/signature self-field. The candidate is authorized by the operator only
+when that exact digest and corresponding root-owned config are approved for installation; merely
+writing the file or enabling AF does not make it approved.
+
+A proposed policy or the framework's generic GO is not an installed authorization. No peer or
+policy config for these new roles is currently evidenced. The current v1 instruction verifier
+and human E5 contract remain unchanged. This design does not implement signing, provision
+keys/configuration, enable either peer, issue work, or close the separate machine-E5 finding.
+
+## Durable handoff record
+
+Implementation clarification: the exact handoff also contains `bootstrap_request`, whose exact
+schema is the bootstrap request defined below (including its full canonical task manifest).
+The operation ID is SHA-256 over `b"VST_S2_AUTHENTICATED_ASSIGNMENT_V1\0"` followed by canonical
+JSON of exactly `{policy_sha256, task_id, story_id, task_manifest_sha256, request_id}`.
+The journal's `payload_sha256` is independently recomputed from canonical JSON of exactly
+`{request: bootstrap_request, bootstrap_peer: policy.bootstrap_peer, policy_sha256}`. The reader
+validates request-to-handoff identity and task manifest digest; it does not trust a matching event
+and row digest without recomputing the actual payload. This prepares verification only, not a
+writer endpoint or an authenticated historical record.
+
+Freshness correction from the focused negative test: the exact handoff also includes
+`service_generation`, fixed by the authenticated upstream operation, not the issuer request.
+The Store reader requires trusted `expected_run_id` and `active_service_generation` and compares
+both to the handoff inside the same read transaction. Supervisor must supply its configured
+current run ID; absence disables the path. A still-live consumed probe from another Supervisor
+run or a handoff from a prior service generation cannot be relabelled as current authority.
+Old records missing this field are refused; no compatibility fallback is authorized.
+
+The authenticated bootstrap operation writes one completed row through the existing
+`supervisor_operations` table and `Store.execute_idempotent()` transaction, then records the
+existing append-only `SUPERVISOR_OPERATION` NOTE event. No table or migration is added. Operation
+name is exactly `VST_S2_AUTHENTICATED_ASSIGNMENT_V1`; operation key is a lowercase SHA-256 over a
+fixed domain label and the canonical tuple of the root-derived policy digest, task ID, story ID,
+manifest digest and bootstrap request ID. The canonical idempotency payload includes the exact
+request and kernel-derived bootstrap peer mapping. Same key/same payload returns the immutable
+stored result. Same key/different payload or unresolved result refuses; it never reassigns or
+renews a lease.
+
+The mutation request has exactly `schema` (`VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_BOOTSTRAP_REQUEST_V1`),
+`request_id` (32 lowercase hex), `story_id`, `task_id`, `task_manifest`, `slot`, `attempt`, and
+`run_id`. The handler rejects a story/task/manifest/slot outside the exact root policy. It does
+not accept actor, owner, peer, policy, source head, epoch, lease ID, worker ID, expiry, or event
+actor from the caller. It derives owner `Codex`, current epoch, lease, worker ID, manifest digest,
+run/probe identity and service generation from the trusted peer, verified policy, and Store.
+Idempotency identity is domain-separated from the canonical request and policy digest. The fixed
+request cannot perform task enumeration or select a task outside its named allowlist.
+
+The completed result has exactly these fields and no others:
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": "VST_S2_AUTHENTICATED_ASSIGNMENT_V1",
+  "assignment_operation_id": "64 lowercase hex operation key",
+  "policy_id": "root configured identifier",
+  "policy_sha256": "64 lowercase hex",
+  "repository": "Virtual_scrum_team",
+  "sprint_id": "39b7cc253f5d",
+  "source_head": "40 lowercase hex",
+  "manifest_sha256": "64 lowercase hex",
+  "bootstrap_peer": {
+    "role": "assignment_bootstrap",
+    "uid": 980,
+    "gid": 982,
+    "cgroup": "/system.slice/vst-assignment-bootstrap.service"
+  },
+  "assignment_principal": "Codex",
+  "task_id": "Store task identifier",
+  "story_id": "Store story identifier",
+  "task_manifest_sha256": "64 lowercase hex",
+  "slot": "one manifest TestRun slot",
+  "attempt": 1,
+  "epoch": 1,
+  "lease_id": 1,
+  "runner_id": "configured runner principal",
+  "run_id": "preflight run identifier",
+  "probe_sha256": "64 lowercase hex",
+  "issued_at_utc": "canonical YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ",
+  "expires_at_utc": "canonical YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ",
+  "handoff_sha256": "64 lowercase hex"
+}
+```
+
+The numeric identities and cgroup above are illustrative schema values, not observed or reserved
+production IDs. Schema validation rejects placeholders, booleans in integer fields, malformed
+digests/IDs/times, unknown/missing fields, expired handoffs, and values outside the loaded
+root-owned policy. `handoff_sha256` hashes the canonical result with that field omitted. The
+Store operation row's `operation` must equal the fixed name; its `payload_sha256` and canonical
+result must match the exact bootstrap request and this schema. The linked NOTE event must match
+operation key, operation name, payload digest and result digest. Existing
+`Store._verify_supervisor_records()` validates operation/event correlation. Verification also
+requires the complete Store chain and configured external anchor, if used, to verify.
+
+The new bootstrap handler derives `bootstrap_peer` and policy fields only from the authenticated
+Supervisor peer plus loaded root-owned policy, never from JSON supplied by its caller. It
+derives `assignment_principal=Codex` from that policy. An event actor string alone does not prove
+the peer; the verified handoff result must bind the kernel-derived role, UID, GID and cgroup.
+Rows from older operation names or without this exact result are legacy and are rejected for
+issuer use.
+
+## Read-only `assignment_basis` request and response
+
+Request has exactly `schema` (`VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_BASIS_REQUEST_V1`) and
+`assignment_operation_id` (64 lowercase hex). It has no task, owner, policy, generation,
+manifest or lease selector. Supervisor matches the request to one exact operation row, linked
+verified NOTE event, policy and authenticated bootstrap result. Zero, multiple, malformed,
+revoked, expired or noncanonical records refuse.
+
+Response has exactly `schema` (`VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_BASIS_RESPONSE_V1`),
+`assignment_operation_id`, `handoff_sha256`, `policy_id`, `policy_sha256`,
+`repository`, `sprint_id`, `source_head`, `manifest_sha256`, `task_id`, `story_id`,
+`task_manifest_sha256`, `slot`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `lease_id`, `runner_id`,
+`principal`, `run_id`, `probe_sha256`, `authority_expires_at_utc` and
+`service_generation`. Every value is derived from the verified handoff, fixed policy and
+current Store snapshot. Principal is the root-configured issuer audience `Codex`; the issuer's
+own kernel identity is independently fixed by its `delegated_issuer` peer entry. The request
+cannot choose either value.
+
+Store implements this as one read-only transaction. Refactor
+`execution_grant_basis()` into a locked internal helper that accepts the current SQLite
+connection; do not nest `BEGIN` transactions. Within that same `_read_tx()`, verify the event
+chain, external anchor and supervisor-operation/event correspondence on that connection, load the
+exact operation row/result, validate the handoff schema and policy binding, and call the locked
+basis helper with `expected_owner="Codex"` and the handoff's exact `expected_lease_id`.
+Cross-check every basis field against the handoff; derive current service generation from the
+root Supervisor provider and cap authority expiry by the current owner/lease expiry and handoff
+expiry. The response is an observation in time, not a lease reservation or a promise of future
+authority. Existing admission and Runner rechecks stay in force.
+
+No direct Store access is added to the issuer. The allowlist adds an optional role with exactly
+`assignment_basis`; existing dispatch_owner/dispatcher/runnerd/signer operation sets are
+unchanged. Existing configs do not enable it by default. Root-owned config load is strict and
+must reject duplicated roles, identity collisions, unexpected UID/GID/cgroup/policy bindings,
+unknown operations and missing policy. No DB migration, new table, task enumeration or E5 change
+is part of this read-only API.
+
+Whole-policy revocation is fail-closed: the trusted Supervisor provider reopens the fixed
+root-owned policy on every query and verifies its validity and exact configured digest pin.
+Removing it, losing safe access, changing its bytes or allowing it to expire disables the API.
+A cached policy alone is insufficient; a configured feature without a trusted provider refuses.
+The provider is installed by trusted root service setup, never supplied by the RPC caller.
+Individual assignment revocation is not implemented; revoke the whole policy if needed until
+that narrower mechanism is separately designed. A `revocation_id` string by itself is not
+evidence of checking a revocation source.
+
+## Implementation order and focused tests
+
+1. Implement pure exact handoff/request/response validators and the read-only locked Store helper.
+   Keep the external per-task signed-record module detached; it is not the selected production
+   source and must not be wired to the Supervisor.
+2. Add a fail-closed `assignment_basis` Supervisor method and RPC for a separately configured
+   issuer peer. It accepts only the opaque operation key and uses the root-derived policy/peer.
+   Do not add assignment mutation in this change.
+3. After independent source/security review of the authenticated upstream contract, implement
+   the separate bounded bootstrap mutation entrypoint as its own reviewed change. It must write
+   the exact handoff result and linked Store event atomically through existing operation APIs.
+   Legacy events remain ineligible.
+4. Designated functional-test-reviewer authors and runs tests after coding: valid same-transaction
+   basis and no DB mutation; bad operation/event/result/payload hash or actor identity; legacy
+   row; unknown/duplicate/expired/revoked assignment; wrong principal, task, slot, attempt, epoch,
+   lease, run, policy or manifest; stale generation/authority; external-anchor failure; duplicate
+   read-only requests; and confirmation that existing Supervisor roles still cannot call the new
+   operation. E2E runtime/provisioning is separate and not proven by synthetic RPC tests.
+
+Codex owns source and evidence. GPT-PM owns independent review and adjudication of
+S2-MACHINE-ISSUER-M01. The operator owns explicit authorization of the exact production
+delegation policy and any reserved production action. The external per-task operator signature
+is retired from the proposed contract under this decision; the authenticated assignment writer
+and final trusted production policy remain to be reviewed and authorized. S2-MACHINE-E5-M01,
+current E5 v1, production dispatch, overall S2 closure and exact-head approval are unchanged.
+
+## Fresh-only bootstrap transaction correction (design only; disabled)
+
+This section narrows step 3 above. It is a proposed source contract, not implementation,
+authorization, or evidence that a new endpoint is allowed. The earlier four-operation wording
+must not be read as permission to compose the four public Store methods. Before any writer code,
+security and database reviewers must approve this transaction boundary and GPT-PM must issue a
+source GO. The production policy still needs the separately required exact authorization.
+
+### Eligibility is one new assignment, not adoption or recovery
+
+The only eligible transition is creation of one exact assignment pinned by the root-owned policy:
+`story_id`, `task_id`, project and phase, canonical manifest digest and contents, and one declared
+`TestRun` slot. The request identifies that policy tuple; it cannot widen it. The manifest's
+`cost_cap` and `retry_cap` are fixed by its pinned digest, and `register_task` seeds the task budget
+row from `cost_cap` (`tools/vst/store.py:1937-1972`). This design does not add a caller-selectable
+budget override.
+
+Eligibility is checked inside the write transaction against the same SQLite connection: the
+operation key is new; the story and task IDs have no rows; the task has no lease, receipt, terminal
+marker, or prior attempt; the requested slot is in both the pinned assignment and manifest and is
+typed `TestRun`; attempt is exactly 1; Store reconciliation and event-chain verification are
+healthy; and trusted Supervisor state supplies the current run, consumed probe, and service
+generation. Any existing story/task/lease/receipt, noninitial attempt, expired assignment, prior
+generation, legacy ownership, or existing operation is ineligible. In particular, this does not
+adopt an unowned legacy story, refresh an expired lease/assignment, continue a new generation,
+retry work, or act as a scheduler. A duplicate completed operation is handled only by the
+idempotency rule below; it does not re-enter eligibility or reacquire anything.
+
+### Minimum trusted policy inputs and identities
+
+Extend the strict, closed root policy schema only with fields needed to make this one transition
+deterministic: for the exact allowed assignment, `project_id` and `phase`; and at policy scope,
+`owner_principal`, `worker_id`/`runner_id` (one configured identity with a specified mapping, not
+two caller aliases), `owner_ttl_seconds`, and `lease_ttl_seconds`. Keep the assignment's exact
+task/story/manifest digest/TestRun-slot allowlist. Reject unknown or missing keys, duplicate
+assignment tuples, invalid types, nonfinite/nonpositive TTLs, and TTLs above a documented local
+maximum. `owner_ttl_seconds` is passed to the existing epoch transition; `lease_ttl_seconds` to
+lease creation. The budget cap remains the pinned manifest `cost_cap`; attempt budget is fixed at
+1 and retry policy at the pinned manifest. Do not accept principal, worker/runner identity, owner,
+epoch/generation, expiry, either TTL, budget values, run, probe, or policy digest from the RPC
+caller. A request may carry only the fixed operation/request identifier and the exact assignment
+tuple selectors needed to locate the one policy entry, plus its canonical manifest if required by
+the existing RPC contract; compare every value to root policy before writing.
+
+The kernel-authenticated peer (UID/GID/cgroup and process identity as already established by the
+Supervisor transport) selects the single optional `assignment_bootstrap` role. That role alone
+may invoke `bootstrap_assignment`; it is not a new authority class, scheduler, generic Store API,
+or substitute for `delegated_issuer`. The trusted Supervisor derives the source principal and
+current run/probe/service-generation values and checks them again in the Store callback immediately
+before commit. The handoff records the fixed `owner_principal`, `runner_id`, epoch and lease
+identifiers/expiry, assignment tuple, manifest digest, run, probe and service generation. The
+response and stored handoff must contain the same committed values. A caller-supplied event actor
+string is never identity evidence. This change provides no signing key, key distribution, policy
+provisioning, service activation, or E5/runtime authority.
+
+### One transaction; preserve existing public APIs
+
+The current public `open_story` (`store.py:1633-1648`), `acquire_epoch`
+(`1654-1665`), `register_task` (`1937-1972`), and `acquire_lease` (`2192-2300`) each own a
+`self._tx()` transaction. Calling those public methods from an idempotent callback would nest
+transactions and is prohibited. Implementation may extract connection-taking private locked
+primitives from their existing bodies, preserving validation, events, return values, and public
+wrappers. `_acquire_epoch_locked(conn, ...)` already exists (`1668-1717`); reuse it. Do not create
+a second transaction abstraction or make a public method conditionally accept a connection.
+
+One `Store.execute_idempotent` invocation owns the sole transaction. Its callback receives `conn`
+(`store.py:3633-3663`) and invokes only connection-taking primitives. It creates the new story,
+registers the pinned task and initial budget, acquires epoch 2 from the just-created epoch-1 story,
+creates the attempt-1 lease and slot claim, and writes the complete handoff row/result. The
+operation record and linked `SUPERVISOR_OPERATION` NOTE event are already written by
+`execute_idempotent` on that same connection. Consequently, story/task/budget/epoch/lease/slot,
+handoff/result, operation journal and event either commit together or roll back together. Do not
+commit intermediate rows or perform network, signing, runtime launch, or other external effects
+inside the callback.
+
+The fresh preconditions are deliberately sufficient to make `acquire_lease`'s historical
+commit-before-raise branches unreachable: there is no previous lease or failed attempt, so retry
+exhaustion cannot hold; the budget row is just seeded with `spent = 0` and cap equal to the pinned
+manifest `cost_cap`, so `spent > cap` and an existing budget marker cannot hold; and attempt 1 is
+the only valid first attempt. Prove these predicates under the transaction before invoking the
+lease primitive. If that proof fails, refuse and roll back. Do not remove, reorder, or change the
+legacy public `acquire_lease` behavior that commits a signed retry/budget marker and raises after
+commit (`2192-2300`); the new path must avoid those branches, not weaken their semantics. Extracted
+locked helpers must not catch such errors and turn them into success.
+
+### Idempotency, reconciliation and fail-closed errors
+
+Use one domain-separated operation name and stable operation key derived from the authenticated
+bootstrap request identity. `execute_idempotent` already hashes the canonical payload, returns the
+stored JSON result for the same operation and payload, and refuses a key reused with different
+operation or payload (`store.py:3633-3659`). For a duplicate exact completed request, return that
+exact committed result without calling the callback, refreshing TTLs, incrementing epoch, or
+reacquiring a slot. Conflicting payloads refuse. If the journal/anchor cannot establish whether a
+first commit completed, use the existing operation reconciliation contract and return
+`INCONCLUSIVE`/failure closed; never generate a new key, synthesize a result, or start a second
+assignment. Any malformed/missing handoff or event, stale generation/run/probe, changed policy,
+failed integrity check, or mismatch between committed result and handoff fails closed. The
+read-only `assignment_basis` remains the independent way to verify the resulting committed
+provenance; it is not itself a writer approval.
+
+### Eligibility and failure matrix for the later implementation
+
+| Case | Required result |
+|---|---|
+| Exact root policy tuple; absent story/task/history; attempt 1; live trusted run/probe/generation; healthy Store | One atomic initial assignment and a read-back-verifiable handoff |
+| Same operation key and byte-equivalent canonical payload after commit | Return the exact stored result; no row/event/lease/TTL change |
+| Same operation key with different operation or payload | Duplicate conflict; no write |
+| Existing story or task, lease, receipt, terminal marker, or noninitial attempt | Refuse as ineligible; no adoption or refresh |
+| Unknown policy tuple, wrong manifest digest/content, undeclared/non-`TestRun` slot, or caller attempts trusted-field override | Refuse before mutation |
+| Wrong peer role/UID/GID/cgroup, absent policy, policy digest drift/expiry, or invalid TTL/config | Refuse before mutation |
+| Run/probe/generation changes before the transaction's final trusted-state check | Roll back all assignment writes |
+| No Store slot, stale row/fence, unexpected validation/SQL/event failure | Roll back all rows and operation event |
+| Retry/budget marker condition is encountered despite fresh proof | Treat as invariant violation; transaction rolls back; preserve public legacy semantics |
+| Commit/anchor outcome cannot be reconciled, or stored handoff/result/event disagree | Inconclusive/fail closed; never infer success or retry under a new key |
+
+The later focused test plan belongs to the designated `functional-test-reviewer` and
+`e2e-runner`, after implementation is complete: (1) one valid single-transaction bootstrap and
+read-only basis verification; (2) same-key/same-payload exact-result replay with unchanged row
+counts and TTL; (3) conflicting payload; (4) each existing-row/history exclusion; (5) peer,
+policy, manifest, slot, attempt, TTL and caller-override rejection; (6) Store slot exhaustion and
+injected failure at each write boundary proving complete rollback; (7) trusted run/probe/generation
+change before commit; (8) simulated retry/budget invariant violation with rollback and a separate
+regression proving the public `acquire_lease` still commits its legacy marker before raising; and
+(9) uncertain anchor/commit reconciliation and mismatched handoff/event/result. These are planned,
+not run. No endpoint is approved by this design; only fresh independent security/database review
+and GPT-PM source GO can authorize a code batch.

+# S2 delegated machine issuer and E5 trust design
+
+Sprint: Agentic_Framework `39b7cc253f5d`, mapped to the active project sprint S2.
+Status: candidate source design; it has not passed independent review or GPT-PM verification, and neither machine signer is active.
+Decision source: GPT-PM correlated architecture ruling, request `a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55`, reply `0b0b8a4d-0816-4146-ba21-71857b5de49d`; full record: `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-machine-authority-adjudication-20261029.md`.
+
+**Active assignment-provenance design:** the later GPT-PM ruling `MODIFY — ALTERNATIVE ACCEPTED
+IN PRINCIPLE` (request `4b2e7e61-c0bd-407d-9b2c-b9078da5f7d9`) retires the candidate external
+per-task operator-signed record. Use `docs/sdlc/S2_AUTHENTICATED_ASSIGNMENT_BASIS_DESIGN.md` for
+the selected Store-backed provenance and bounded read-only `assignment_basis` API. The older
+external-record schema and its disconnected validator below are retained as candidate-history;
+they are not an active Supervisor contract. The upstream writer and production issuer remain
+unimplemented and must not be claimed as accepted.
+
+**Root dispatch issuer supersession (bounded):** for the dispatch-issuance choice and crash-state
+contract only, the later GPT-PM ruling `MODIFY` (request
+`8b6b69f3-9b39-491b-a948-03c497870b5d`, reply
+`b1728c67-3bc2-4db5-9fbf-6b359a73ad82`) prefers the existing root Supervisor and unchanged
+signed v1 instruction format. Use
+[`S2_ROOT_BOUND_DISPATCH_ISSUER_DESIGN.md`](S2_ROOT_BOUND_DISPATCH_ISSUER_DESIGN.md) for the
+corrected append-only crash-consistent issuance protocol and explicit delegated-key enforcement.
+This supersedes the separate issuer daemon/v2 dispatch-format proposal below only. It does not
+supersede the selected authenticated assignment-basis design, authorize private-key signing,
+provisioning or activation, close `S2-MACHINE-ISSUER-I01`, or change the existing human E5
+contract. The daemon/v2 material below is retained as historical candidate context, not the active
+dispatch design.
+
+## Decision and boundary
+
+This candidate proposes two separately versioned, purpose-bound machine contracts: one for issuance of an already-authorized S2 assignment and one for collecting E5 host-policy observations. The operator remains the sole human delegation authority. The repository has no established operator assignment-delegation signing purpose or trust configuration for this contract. A policy could become effective only after a new, purpose-separated operator authority key and root-owned trust configuration are explicitly provisioned and the operator signs its canonical bytes. Codex may author the candidate and compute its digest, but may not sign it, claim the operator approved it, or provision a key. The signed delegation states machine identity, exact role, scope, policy digest, validity, and revocation identity.
+
+The issuer receives one immutable authorization record and returns one instruction for that record. It cannot enumerate tasks, accept a task ID as proof of authorization, create or change a Store assignment/lease, or choose among work. The root Supervisor still verifies the signed instruction and performs all existing Store admission checks. The two keys and trust purposes are distinct. E5 v1 remains authoritative until an explicitly approved new policy version is installed and selected; there is no implicit fallback.
+
+This candidate proposes remediation for the two architectural findings in the GPT-PM ruling; both findings remain MAJOR/OPEN pending independent review and GPT-PM verification. GPT-PM's reply labels the gate “MODIFY” and separately scopes its ruling to design only; it authorizes bounded source design, deterministic read-only collectors and synthetic verifiers only. It does not approve privileged signer implementation, key creation, provisioning, activation, production dispatch, replacement of the current human E5 contract, or S2 closure. The reply reports no live-host inspection, key creation, test execution or runtime evidence.
+
+## Existing contracts to preserve
+
+- `tools/vst/dispatch_instruction.py:13-19,25-64` defines an exact v1 envelope and signing domain. It binds request ID, task, slot, attempt, epoch, run, key purpose and expiry, but has no assignment-provenance field. Lines 67-95 verify the key's configured principal/purpose, expiry and Ed25519 signature.
+- `tools/vst/preflight.py:133-208` collects POSIX/WSL inventory and binds run ID, nonce and sandbox-spec digest. Lines 182 and 203 explicitly limit external-egress evidence to one reserved-target smoke test. Lines 220-230 sign the existing network-policy attestation with the operator key; lines 265-281 require that operator signature.
+- `tools/vst/store.py:1102-1210` validates a v1 instruction and transactionally checks request idempotency, task manifest/slot, live owner epoch, current lease, consumed preflight, eligible attempt and receipt absence before recording `DISPATCH_INTENT_ACCEPTED`. The stored result binds the lease and manifest digest. This is admission after instruction receipt; it does not, by itself, authenticate the issuer's upstream choice.
+- Store's event chain and supervisor operation journal are existing durable boundaries, but no signed operator assignment-authorization record or corresponding trust purpose exists today. This candidate therefore defines a new immutable external authorization signed with a new purpose-separated operator authority key. The root Supervisor verifies that record against a read-only current Store assignment snapshot and stores the issued envelope in its existing durable journal. It must not query/list tasks or receive a Store handle capable of assignment/lease mutation.
+- The preflight functions and v1 verifier remain unchanged while the new version is developed and reviewed. The Supervisor selects a format and trust purpose explicitly.
+
+## Trust objects
+
+All JSON objects below use the repository's canonical JSON encoding, reject duplicate/unknown/missing fields, validate exact types and digest formats, and are signed over a fixed domain label plus canonical bytes without the signature field. No object contains private-key bytes.
+
+### Operator delegation policy
+
+Use a new exact schema, `VST_S2_MACHINE_DELEGATION_POLICY_V1`. Its signature purpose is `VST_S2_MACHINE_DELEGATION_POLICY_V1`, trusted only through a new root-owned config path `/etc/vst-runner/machine-delegation-trust.json`. Candidate trust-config schema is `VST_S2_MACHINE_DELEGATION_TRUST_CONFIG_V1`: exact fields `schema`, `operator_authorities`, `machine_principals`, `revocations`. Each operator authority has exactly `key_id`, `purpose`, `public_key_path`, `revocation_id`; purpose is `VST_S2_MACHINE_DELEGATION_POLICY_V1` or `VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_AUTHORIZATION_V1` and uses a distinct key ID/key. Each machine entry has exactly `principal`, `key_id`, `purpose`, `public_key_path`, `policy_sha256`, `not_before`, `expires_at`, `revocation_id`. Revocations are exact `revocation_id`, `revoked_at`, `reason_code` records. Key revocation is represented by the registry entry's explicit `revocation_id`; no caller-selected revocation lookup is trusted. The verifier rejects duplicate IDs, unknown fields, duplicate keys, paths not root-owned and non-regular, symlinked or group/world-writable files, wrong purpose/key-ID combinations, expired or revoked keys. No such signing purpose/config is currently present; this is a candidate path and contract only.
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": "VST_S2_MACHINE_DELEGATION_POLICY_V1",
+  "policy_id": "stable-policy-id",
+  "operator_key_id": "new-policy-authority-key-id",
+  "project": "Virtual_scrum_team",
+  "repository": "https://github.com/xLZDx/Virtual_scrum_team",
+  "sprint_id": "39b7cc253f5d",
+  "role": "dispatch-issuer",
+  "machine_principal": "root-configured-principal",
+  "machine_key_id": "purpose-specific-key-id",
+  "key_purpose": "VST_S2_DELEGATED_DISPATCH_ISSUER_V1",
+  "source_head": "40-lowercase-hex",
+  "manifest_sha256": "64-lowercase-hex",
+  "allowed_authorization_type": "[REDACTED]",
+  "not_before": "canonical UTC",
+  "expires_at": "canonical UTC",
+  "revocation_id": "stable-revocation-id",
+  "signature": "operator signature"
+}
+```
+
+The E5 policy uses the same common fields but has role `network-observer`, a different machine key purpose, and an exact `role_config` with `collector_artifacts`, `evaluator_sha256`, `policy_revision_sha256`, `required_observation_schema`, `environment_id`, and `freshness_seconds`. Each collector artifact entry has exactly `source_id`, `path`, `source_head`, `sha256`, `os_id`, `os_build_constraint`, and `privilege_boundary`. This candidate currently allows only observation-completeness evaluation, not a production network policy verdict. A policy for one role cannot authorize the other. The trust config pins each operator public key by key ID and one of the exact operator purposes above, and maps each machine key ID to one principal and one purpose; revocation/expiry are checked on every verification. Runtime trust/config paths remain root-owned. No permissive default, wildcard repository, caller-selected key, automatic key generation or acceptance of unsigned candidate policy is allowed.
+
+The policy's signed `manifest_sha256` freezes the non-secret sprint scope. The manifest identifies exact allowed story/requirement work and source artifacts. It does not make any task assigned. Assignment still has to exist independently in the authenticated assignment record below.
+
+### Immutable external assignment authorization
+
+Schema clarification for bounded validator implementation: add `authorization_key_id` to the
+exact assignment field set below for the new operator signing key. `issuer_key_id` remains the
+intended delegated machine issuer and must match the policy; it is not the operator key.
+Policy `operator_key_id` selects only the purpose-pinned operator delegation key. Each trust key
+has an explicit revocation ID; verification checks that ID and each record's revocation ID
+against the configured revocation records. For the observation role,
+`freshness_seconds` is an exact integer in 1..3600 (booleans rejected). These clarifications grant
+no production authority; the validator change record specifies the executable exact schema.
+
+The exact `VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_AUTHORIZATION_V1` field set is `schema`, `authorization_id`, `project`, `repository`, `sprint_id`, `manifest_sha256`, `task_id`, `story_id`, `principal`, `slot`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `lease_id`, `run_id`, `request_id`, `policy_id`, `policy_sha256`, `authorization_key_id`, `issuer_key_id`, `issuer_key_purpose`, `issued_at`, `expires_at`, `revocation_id`, and `signature`. The signature purpose is the new `VST_S2_ASSIGNMENT_AUTHORIZATION_V1`, using the new operator authority public key pinned by `/etc/vst-runner/machine-delegation-trust.json`. This purpose, key, configuration and record do not currently exist. The immutable signed record is external to the Store; do not claim that it is an existing Store event. The root Supervisor would verify it and cross-check every assignment field against a read-only snapshot of the current Store owner/lease state before allowing issue-once signing; this is a proposed integration, not an existing callsite.
+
+- authorization ID and digest, project, repository, sprint, manifest digest and task/story identity;
+- principal `Codex`, slot, attempt, epoch, lease identity, run ID, request ID and bounded expiry;
+- the operator authorization identity, policy ID/digest, issuer key purpose, issue-once idempotency key and revocation reference.
+
+The authorization must name exactly one project/repository/sprint/manifest/task/story/slot/attempt/epoch/lease/run/request and Codex principal, with canonical issue and expiry times. The Supervisor obtains the record by its authorization ID, verifies its operator signature under the new purpose and checks it against the current Store snapshot, including current assignment to Codex, live owner epoch, matching live lease, manifest digest, eligible attempt, run-bound consumed probe and absence of an existing receipt. The Store snapshot alone is not the authorization; the signed external record supplies the independent exact-work authorization. The machine caller cannot enumerate records or supply an alternate tuple. Missing, multiple, mutable, stale, expired, revoked, wrong-principal, unassigned, mismatched or unresolved records fail closed. This does not add a scheduler or assignment database.
+
+The signed external authorization record is included inside the new signed envelope, so downstream verifiers can validate the same authority rather than relying on an assumed lookup.
+
+### Dispatch instruction v2
+
+Create `VST_S2_DISPATCH_INSTRUCTION_V2` in a new explicit validator/domain. Keep v1 bytes and validation unchanged. V2 contains the complete v1 tuple plus:
+
+- `policy_id`, `policy_sha256`, `assignment_authorization` and its `authorization_sha256`;
+- `source_head`, `manifest_sha256`, `lease_id`, `principal`, `issue_id`, `issued_at`, and fixed expiry inherited from the authorization;
+- issuer `key_id`, exact purpose `VST_S2_DELEGATED_DISPATCH_ISSUER_V1`, algorithm, version and signature.
+
+The issuer derives every envelope field from the verified immutable snapshot. It never accepts a free-form task/slot/attempt/epoch/run/expiry or client-provided policy digest. The request is authenticated over the fixed AF_UNIX endpoint with kernel peer credentials and the approved UID/GID/cgroup mapping. The request contains only the authorization ID and idempotency identity.
+
+Use the existing append-only Store/Supervisor operation journal for issue-once durability: operation key is a domain-separated hash of policy digest and assignment-authorization digest. The operation payload digest covers the exact canonical authorization snapshot and caller identity. First call stores the completed canonical envelope bytes and signature in one transaction; an identical retry returns those same bytes. A changed payload under the same key, uncertain commit, missing signature record or conflicting prior event returns an unresolved error and does not sign again. Persisted envelope expiry and request ID are therefore stable across retries. Use deterministic Ed25519 signing on identical canonical bytes. Do not use “retry” to mint a new request ID or extend expiry.
+
+The root Supervisor's v2 path verifies the operator assignment signature and delegation policy signature, both key purpose/revocation/expiry checks, machine signature, exact source/manifest/policy bindings and current Store admission. It then executes the existing transaction and checks in `Store.accept_dispatch_intent`. V1 and v2 use separate explicit selectors. An invalid or unknown version is rejected; v1 is never silently reinterpreted as delegated machine authorization.
+
+### E5 observation-only candidate
+
+The authorized source scope supports only an observation collector. It must emit `VST_S2_MACHINE_NETWORK_OBSERVATION_BUNDLE_V1` and must never emit PASS or sign `VST_S2_DELEGATED_MACHINE_NETWORK_POLICY_ATTESTATION_V1`. Full E5 remains UNKNOWN until GPT-PM accepts an exact policy revision, complete source coverage and evaluator predicates. Any later machine attestation uses a new trust purpose `VST_S2_DELEGATED_MACHINE_NETWORK_POLICY_ATTESTATION_V1`, different from both the new delegation authority and dispatch issuer; its key/config are not provisioned.
+
+Candidate source schemas are exact and reject unknown/missing fields. They are schema proposals, not deployed or trusted records:
+
+`VST_S2_MACHINE_NETWORK_OBSERVATION_BUNDLE_V1` contains exactly `schema`, `run_id`, `nonce`, `source_head`, `sandbox_spec_sha256`, `started_at_utc`, `finished_at_utc`, `sources`, `raw_observations`, and `bundle_sha256`. There is no `policy_revision_sha256` or E5 verdict in this observation-only bundle. Each source receipt contains exactly `schema` (= `VST_S2_MACHINE_OBSERVATION_RECEIPT_V1`), `source_id`, `collector_path`, `collector_head`, `collector_sha256`, `os_id`, `os_build`, `principal`, `privilege_boundary`, `observation_schema`, `collected_at_utc`, `raw_sha256`, and `signature`. Receipt signature purpose is `VST_S2_MACHINE_OBSERVATION_RECEIPT_V1`; collector public keys and trust config are not present, so current source collection may emit unsigned receipts only and cannot claim an authenticated measurement. Source IDs are exactly `windows-host` and `wsl-guest`; both are required. Digests are lowercase 64-hex; timestamps canonical UTC; nonce is 32 lowercase hex. Bundle hash is SHA-256 over canonical bundle bytes without `bundle_sha256`.
+
+Windows raw observation object exact fields: `os_id`, `os_build`, `firewall_profiles`, `effective_firewall_rules`, `wsl_hyperv_firewall_profiles`, `effective_wsl_hyperv_firewall_rules`, `wsl_distributions`, `wsl_network_configuration`, `host_endpoints`, `host_path_exposures`, `collection_complete`, `errors`, `raw_command_outputs`. Each Windows profile has `name` (Domain/Private/Public), `enabled`, `default_inbound_action`, `default_outbound_action`, `policy_source`. Each normalized effective rule has `rule_id`, `enabled`, `direction`, `action`, `protocol`, `local_addresses`, `remote_addresses`, `local_ports`, `remote_ports`, `profiles`, `policy_source`; preserve the complete effective set, not just enabled/block rules. WSL/Hyper-V policy has the same profile and rule shapes plus `environment_id` and complete-source markers. WSL distribution entries include exact name/version/state/network mode. Endpoint entries include address, protocol, port, owning process identity and exposure/interface. Error arrays retain command, exit status and parse/completeness error; no omitted rule may be treated as blocked. If the active Windows build/network mode does not expose a complete effective WSL/Hyper-V policy, collection status is UNSUPPORTED.
+
+WSL raw observation object exact fields: `os_id`, `os_build`, `kernel_release`, `nft_ruleset_raw`, `ipv4_routes_raw`, `ipv6_routes_raw`, `ipv4_rules_raw`, `ipv6_rules_raw`, `namespaces_raw`, `interfaces_raw`, `mounts_raw`, `windows_drive_mounts`, `wsl_interop_present`, `wsl_interop_enabled`, `container_socket_paths`, `container_socket_inventory_complete`, `listeners_raw`, `uid`, `gid`, `collection_complete`, `errors`. These raw string fields retain full command/proc output. Hash the canonical raw object before evaluation. The existing `preflight.py` reserved-target egress smoke probe can be recorded as a probe observation only; it cannot stand in for Windows effective firewall, WSL/Hyper-V firewall, nftables or routing tables or prove comprehensive egress blocking.
+
+Windows host collection and WSL collection are separate named source artifacts with pinned path, source HEAD, digest, OS/build and privilege identity. They run read-only. A missing source, permission error, truncated output, unparsed rule, unsupported OS/build/network mode, unmatched firewall/WSL endpoint, incomplete inventory or inconsistent host/guest observation yields UNKNOWN. Do not coerce UNKNOWN to false/true or PASS.
+
+A later deterministic completeness evaluator is a separate pinned artifact and accepts only the exact observation bundle schema. Its result schema is `VST_S2_MACHINE_NETWORK_EVALUATION_V1`: `schema`, `bundle_sha256`, `evaluator_sha256`, `status` (only `OBSERVATIONS_COMPLETE`, `UNKNOWN`, `INCOMPLETE`, or `UNSUPPORTED`; never PASS), `predicates`, `missing_sources`, `unmatched_rules`, and `result_sha256`. Each predicate has `id`, `status` and evidence references `source_id` plus `raw_field_path`. Deterministic predicates are limited to: both exact source IDs present once; source and observation schemas recognized; required fields present with exact types; raw hashes match canonical contents; collector metadata matches pinned source identity when trust config later exists; all required commands completed; firewall profiles and all effective rules captured; nftables ruleset and v4/v6 routes/rules captured; namespace/interface/mount/interop/socket/listener scans complete; Windows WSL distribution/network records correlate with the WSL guest; timestamps ordered and within configured freshness bound; run/nonce/spec/source bindings match. Any missing, unknown, unsupported, incomplete, unmatched or contradictory input returns UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE/UNSUPPORTED. `OBSERVATIONS_COMPLETE` means only that collection met this schema; it is not a policy result, proof of blocked egress, or E5 PASS. No production E5 policy predicate set is approved. A later attestor, only after separate design approval, would verify authenticated source receipts, recompute hashes/evaluation, check freshness and nonce replay, and sign exactly the accepted policy result; it may not populate observations, choose an evaluator, or assert a favorable boolean.
+
+No Supervisor path accepts this observation bundle as E5. A future machine-attestation verifier may be added only when a separately reviewed policy fixes the complete required source and predicate set. It must explicitly select the new record version, verify source identities, raw/evaluator hashes, freshness, run/nonce/source/spec/policy bindings, policy validity/revocation and every required observation. Unknown or contradictory input fails closed; it cannot fall back to operator-E5 v1 or accept a machine key in the operator-key slot. Until the contract is reviewed and activated, current human E5 v1 remains mandatory.
+
+### Threat boundary
+
+This design detects caller forgery, stale/replayed records, substituted artifacts, incomplete collection and untrusted worker input. It does not claim that two UIDs or two processes on one WSL host are independent from a compromised Windows administrator, WSL root, kernel or hypervisor. Such an actor can alter collectors, files or observations before signing. The current authorized scope supports source contracts and read-only host measurements; it does not provide hardware-backed remote attestation. Production claims must state this platform limit. If the accepted policy requires resistance to a compromised host administrator, the design is insufficient and no machine E5 may be accepted.
+
+## Source work allowed now
+
+1. Add pure schema/canonicalization/digest validators for the candidate delegation policy, new-purpose external assignment authorization, v2 dispatch envelope and observation bundle/evaluation. Add verification helpers against caller-supplied public-key fixtures; do not create/provision authority keys or treat fixtures as production trust.
+2. Add Supervisor comparison of one externally signed authorization to one read-only current Store assignment snapshot. Do not invent a signed Store event/table that currently does not exist. No production issue endpoint until the new operator authority purpose/config is reviewed and provisioned separately.
+3. Add read-only Windows and WSL observation collectors with the exact source fields above. Their result is an observation bundle only. Keep the current POSIX probe API and human E5 verifier unchanged.
+4. Add deterministic completeness and consistency evaluation that returns only OBSERVATIONS_COMPLETE, UNKNOWN, INCOMPLETE or UNSUPPORTED. It must not return FAIL/PASS as an E5 policy verdict until an exact egress/policy predicate set and its sources are separately accepted. The current one-target egress smoke result never produces comprehensive E5 PASS.
+5. Do not add an attestor or Supervisor machine-E5 acceptance path yet. Do not change service units, create configs/keys/users, write to WSL, initialize/migrate Store, activate services, dispatch work or claim production authority.
+
+## Negative-test matrix for the later test phase
+
+Tests are planned only; the designated functional-test reviewer/e2e runner author and execute them after all S2 coding is complete.
+
+| Boundary | Negative case | Required outcome |
+|---|---|---|
+| Delegation | unsigned, bad signature, wrong operator key purpose, wildcard scope, wrong sprint/repository/manifest, expired or revoked policy | reject before issuer work |
+| Assignment | arbitrary task ID; no authorization ID; task outside signed manifest; assignment for another principal; altered tuple; task merely eligible but not assigned | reject, with no envelope or Store mutation |
+| Caller | wrong UID/GID/cgroup, non-PID1 peer where PID1 is required, inherited/invalid peer descriptor, alternate socket/path | reject before authorization lookup |
+| Freshness | expired authorization, stale epoch/lease, changed generation, replayed nonce/request, stale source/spec/policy digest | reject and preserve prior durable state |
+| Idempotency | same request replay; same operation key with changed payload; uncertain Store commit; corrupted issuance journal | identical bytes for a known committed retry; otherwise unresolved/fail closed, never mint new authority |
+| V2 binding | modify task/slot/attempt/epoch/run/lease/principal/manifest/authorization digest; v1/v2 downgrade, purpose mismatch or unknown version | signature/provenance failure, no fallback |
+| E5 collector | missing source, permission error, partial firewall/mount/socket inventory, malformed output, unsupported OS/build, conflicting Windows/WSL facts | UNKNOWN/INCOMPLETE/UNSUPPORTED; no attestation |
+| E5 integrity | changed raw evidence, evaluator output, collector or evaluator digest; substituted collector receipt | reject |
+| E5 freshness | wrong run, nonce, source/spec/policy digest; expired record; replayed nonce; revoked delegation | reject |
+| E5 authority | source attempts to produce E5 PASS, evaluator inputs self-asserted, operator key supplied as machine key or vice versa | UNKNOWN/reject; no attestation, human and machine formats stay distinct |
+| Platform limit | source input attempts to represent Windows administrator, WSL root, kernel or hypervisor compromise as independently measured | result must state UNSUPPORTED, not PASS |
+
+## Ordered implementation and review
+
+1. Independent architecture/security review assesses this candidate and both MAJOR findings together; GPT-PM then verifies the exact revised design. Findings stay OPEN until that occurs.
+2. Implement only pure validators, signed-external-authorization comparison against Store snapshot, and read-only observation collectors that cannot report E5 PASS.
+3. Finish all S2 coding before the functional-test reviewer and e2e runner author/run the mapped negative tests and permitted source tests.
+4. Obtain focused security/architecture review, remediate valid BLOCKER/MAJOR findings, and repeat only direct regressions.
+5. Only after separate review and explicit provisioning of new purpose-specific operator authority/trust configuration can policy signing be considered. Machine E5 remains unavailable until its complete policy predicates and independent source trust are reviewed. Exact-head approval and mapped runtime evidence remain required for S2; restricted process-kill/crash/mutation/policy selectors remain NOT_RUN.

Existing production service/config/credentials, root signing key, authenticated systemd/PID 1 issuer identity, current run-bound human E5 signature, activation and owner-to-Runner dispatch remain HOLD. A fixture or observation cannot satisfy these.

+# S2 original epic coverage reconciliation
+
+Sprint tracking ID: `39b7cc253f5d`  
+Reconciliation snapshot: canonical checkout HEAD `6a6d7886746379e2b68218bd8d4fba01edf0bf56`  
+Scope: planning and evidence mapping only. No tests, collection, checks, source changes, runtime provisioning, or activation were performed for this artifact.
+
+## How to read this reconciliation
+
+The original S2 plan defines eight epics, E1–E8, and two deferred S2 items, D1–D2. The later `S2-1` through `S2-5` stories consolidate requirements and add transport, bundle, provenance, and gate work; they do **not** replace or reduce the E1–E8 and D1–D2 acceptance denominator. A pass for a later story is not automatically evidence for an original epic.
+
+The original plan defines semantic denominators (the complete listed cases for each epic), not one stable pytest-ID count. The historical inventory of 209 collected IDs, 189 passed across Windows/WSL, and 20 `NOT_RUN` belongs only to the six modules and source/test HEAD recorded in `s2-safe-functional-exact-4c1692d-20261027.md`. It is not the current denominator: modules and acceptance scope grew afterward. Later runs use different overlapping components and revisions, so their counts must not be added into a project-wide total. S4's 53 policy selectors are not S2 selectors and are excluded from this matrix.
+
+`PASS` below means only the named test behavior passed at the cited source/test revision. It does not imply current-head acceptance, a provisioned system, real authorization, or production-runtime evidence. `NOT_RUN` is not a failure and cannot be promoted to pass; skipped tests remain unverified.
+
