++    lock_path = remote / ".vst-object-storage.lock"
++    lock_path.write_bytes(b"\0" + state)
++    real_run = slice_module.subprocess.run
++    real_popen = slice_module.subprocess.Popen
++    commands = []
++    writers = []
++
++    def capture_run(command, *args, **kwargs):
++        commands.append(list(command))
++        return real_run(command, *args, **kwargs)
++
++    def reject_writer(command, *args, **kwargs):
++        if "pack-objects" in command or "index-pack" in command:
++            writers.append(list(command))
++            raise AssertionError("object writer started on poisoned target")
++        return real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)
++
++    monkeypatch.setattr(slice_module.subprocess, "run", capture_run)
++    monkeypatch.setattr(slice_module.subprocess, "Popen", reject_writer)
++    with pytest.raises(StoreError, match="synthetic target.*poisoned|interrupted object write"):
++        backend.push({"branch": "blocked", "head": head}, operation_key="poison-refusal")
++    assert not any("hash-object" in command for command in commands)
++    assert writers == []
++    assert lock_path.read_bytes()[1:2] == b"P"

++def test_cumulative_target_storage_cap_rejects_before_pack_process_starts(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
++    from tools.vst import slice as slice_module
++
++    remote, repo, backend = _synthetic_git_source(tmp_path, filename="cap.txt")
++    head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=str(repo))
++    payload = {"branch": "capped", "head": head}
++    # Persist the operation binding first so publication reaches the pack preflight.
++    backend._bind_operation("push", "cap-operation", payload)
++    current_bytes = backend._target_object_storage_bytes()
++    backend._MAX_PACK_BYTES = 64
++    backend._MAX_PACK_INDEX_BYTES = 64
++    backend._MAX_TARGET_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES = current_bytes + 127
++    real_popen = slice_module.subprocess.Popen
++    pack_processes = []
++
++    def forbid_pack_process(command, *args, **kwargs):
++        if "pack-objects" in command or "index-pack" in command:
++            pack_processes.append(list(command))
++            raise AssertionError("pack process started despite cumulative-storage preflight rejection")
++        return real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)
++
++    monkeypatch.setattr(slice_module.subprocess, "Popen", forbid_pack_process)
++    with pytest.raises(StoreError, match="synthetic target object storage cap would be exceeded"):
++        backend.push(payload, operation_key="cap-operation")
++    assert pack_processes == []
++    assert backend._target_object_storage_bytes() == current_bytes
++    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
++        backend.ref_head("refs/heads/capped")

++def test_target_storage_lock_times_out_on_another_process_then_releases_normally(tmp_path):
++    from tools.vst.slice import SyntheticOperationBackend
++
++    remote = tmp_path / "storage-lock.git"
++    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "--bare", str(remote)], check=True, capture_output=True)
++    backend = SyntheticOperationBackend(
++        str(remote), source_repo=str(remote), command_timeout_sec=1,
++    )
++    lock_path = remote / ".vst-object-storage.lock"
++    with backend._target_storage_lock():
++        pass
++
++    child_code = r'''import os, sys
++path = sys.argv[1]
++stream = open(path, "a+b")
++if os.fstat(stream.fileno()).st_size == 0:
++    stream.write(b"\0")
++    stream.flush()
++stream.seek(0)
++if os.name == "nt":
++    import msvcrt
++    msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_LOCK, 1)
++else:
++    import fcntl
++    fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
++print("LOCKED", flush=True)
++sys.stdin.readline()
++stream.seek(0)
++if os.name == "nt":
++    msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
++else:
++    fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
++stream.close()
++'''
++    child = subprocess.Popen(
++        [sys.executable, "-c", child_code, str(lock_path)],
++        stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
++        text=True,
++    )
++    try:
++        assert child.stdout.readline().strip() == "LOCKED"
++        with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="timed out waiting for synthetic target storage lock"):
++            with backend._target_storage_lock():
++                pass
++    finally:
++        if child.stdin is not None and not child.stdin.closed:
++            child.stdin.write("release\n")
++            child.stdin.flush()
++            child.stdin.close()
++        assert child.wait(timeout=10) == 0, "lock-holder child did not release and exit normally"
++

++def test_local_git_timeout_leaves_pending_then_restart_retry_completes_same_key(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
++    from tools.vst import slice as slice_module
++
++    remote, repo, backend = _synthetic_git_source(tmp_path, filename="timeout.txt")
++    head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=str(repo))
++
++    db = tmp_path / "timeout-operation.db"
++    store = Store(str(db), event_key=EVENT)
++    supervisor = Supervisor(store, operation_backend=backend)
++    real_popen = slice_module.subprocess.Popen
++    injected = {"done": False}
++    observed_timeout = []
++
++    def timeout_once(command, *args, **kwargs):
++        if not injected["done"] and command[0] == "git" and "pack-objects" in command:
++            injected["done"] = True
++            observed_timeout.append(backend.command_timeout_sec)
++            raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(command, backend.command_timeout_sec)

++    try:
++        with pytest.raises(TimeoutError, match="Git source pack import exceeded its time limit"):
++            supervisor.simulate_push("timeout-retry-key", payload)
++        assert injected["done"] and observed_timeout == [10]
++        row = store._conn.execute(
++            "SELECT operation, payload_sha256, result FROM supervisor_operations WHERE operation_key = ?",
++            ("timeout-retry-key",),
++        ).fetchone()
++        assert row["operation"] == "push"
++        assert json.loads(row["result"]) == {"_vst_state": "PENDING"}
++        intent_count = store._conn.execute(
++            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND actor = 'supervisor'",
++            ("timeout-retry-key",),
++        ).fetchone()[0]
++        assert intent_count >= 2  # durable intent and UNKNOWN timeout outcome
++        store.close()
++
++        restarted_store = Store(str(db), event_key=EVENT)
++        restarted = Supervisor(restarted_store, operation_backend=backend)
++        result = restarted.simulate_push("timeout-retry-key", payload)
++        assert result == {
++            "operation_key": "timeout-retry-key",
++            "ref": "refs/heads/timeout-candidate",
++            "head": head,
++        }
++        assert git("--git-dir", str(remote), "rev-parse", "refs/heads/timeout-candidate") == head
++        completed = restarted.simulate_push("timeout-retry-key", payload)
++        assert completed == result
++        assert backend.push(payload, operation_key="timeout-retry-key") == result
++        with pytest.raises(StoreError, match="remote idempotency key reused with different payload"):
++            backend.push(
++                {"branch": "conflicting-candidate", "head": head},
++                operation_key="timeout-retry-key",
++            )
++        assert restarted_store._conn.execute(
++            "SELECT result FROM supervisor_operations WHERE operation_key = ?",
++            ("timeout-retry-key",),
++        ).fetchone()[0] == json.dumps({"_vst_state": "PENDING"}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
++        completion_count = restarted_store._conn.execute(
++            "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND payload LIKE '%SUPERVISOR_EXTERNAL_OPERATION_COMPLETED%'",
++            ("timeout-retry-key",),
++        ).fetchone()[0]
++        assert completion_count == 1
++        completion_payload = json.loads(restarted_store._conn.execute(
++            "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND payload LIKE '%SUPERVISOR_EXTERNAL_OPERATION_COMPLETED%'",
++            ("timeout-retry-key",),
++        ).fetchone()[0])
++        assert completion_payload["result"] == result
++        restarted_store.close()
++    finally:
++        if store._conn is not None:
++            store.close()

++class _RequestConnection:
++    """In-process protocol peer; this does not model or claim OS identity isolation."""
++
++    def __init__(self, payload: bytes, uid: int = 4242):
++        self.chunks = [payload, b""]
++        self.uid = uid
++        self.response = b""
++
++    def getsockopt(self, _level, _option, _size):
++        return struct.pack("3i", 101, self.uid, 4242)
++
++    def recv(self, _size):
++        return self.chunks.pop(0) if self.chunks else b""
++
++    def sendall(self, response: bytes):
++        self.response = response
++
++
++def _signer_protocol_request(request_id="request-1", candidate_head="a" * 40):
++    parser_id, parser_version, parser_sha = next(iter(contracts.TRUSTED_PARSER_CATALOG))
++    argv = ["python", "-c", "print('PASS t1')"]
++    return {
++        "request_id": request_id,
++        "task_id": "task-1",
++        "slot": "tests",
++        "attempt": 1,
++        "epoch": 1,
++        "manifest_sha256": "b" * 64,
++        "candidate_head": candidate_head,
++        "commands": [{"argv": argv, "exit_code": 0}],
++        "parser_results": [{
++            "argv": argv, "parser_id": parser_id, "parser_version": parser_version,
++            "parser_sha256": parser_sha,
++            "parser_result": {"executed_test_ids": ["t1"], "skipped_test_ids": [], "xfail_test_ids": []},
++        }],
++        "artifact_digests": {},
++    }
++
++
++def _handle_signer_protocol(monkeypatch, server, request):
++    import tools.vst.signer as signer_module
++
++    monkeypatch.setattr(signer_module.socket, "SO_PEERCRED", 1, raising=False)
++    connection = _RequestConnection(json.dumps(request).encode("utf-8"))
++    server._handle(connection)
++    return json.loads(connection.response)
++
++
++def test_signing_request_exact_schema_and_replay_protocol_without_os_claim(monkeypatch):
++    server = object.__new__(AuthenticatedSigner)
++    server.runner_uid = 4242
++    server.key = SIGNER_KEY
++    server._ledger = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
++    server._ledger.execute("CREATE TABLE requests (request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, payload BLOB NOT NULL, signature TEXT NOT NULL)")
++    server._lock = threading.Lock()
++    request = _signer_protocol_request()
++    assert set(validate_signing_request(request)) == {
++        "request_id", "task_id", "slot", "attempt", "epoch", "manifest_sha256",
++        "candidate_head", "commands", "parser_results", "artifact_digests",
++    }
++    first = _handle_signer_protocol(monkeypatch, server, request)
++    replay = _handle_signer_protocol(monkeypatch, server, request)
++    assert set(first) == {"signature"} and first == replay
++    assert verify({**request, "signature": first["signature"]}, SIGNER_KEY, SIGNING_REQUEST_LABEL)
++    assert server._ledger.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM requests").fetchone()[0] == 1
++    changed = {**request, "candidate_head": "c" * 40}
++    rejected = _handle_signer_protocol(monkeypatch, server, changed)
++    assert rejected.get("error") == "invalid_request"
++    assert "different payload" in rejected.get("detail", "")
++    assert server._ledger.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM requests").fetchone()[0] == 1
++    malformed = {**request, "unexpected": True, "request_id": "bad-request"}
++    assert _handle_signer_protocol(monkeypatch, server, malformed).get("error") == "invalid_request"
++    server._ledger.close()
++

++def _job_object_setup_failure_api(close_outcomes):
++    events = []
++    close_calls = []
++
++    class FakeKernel32:
++        @staticmethod
++        def CreateJobObjectW(_attributes, _name):
++            events.append("create_job")
++            return 700
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def SetInformationJobObject(*_args):
++            events.append("configure_job")
++            return False
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def CloseHandle(handle):
++            close_calls.append(handle)
++            events.append(f"close_job_{len(close_calls)}")
++            outcome = close_outcomes[len(close_calls) - 1]
++            if isinstance(outcome, BaseException):
++                raise outcome
++            return outcome
++

++def _install_mock_windows_run(monkeypatch, *, failure=None):
++    events = []
++    command_callbacks = []
++    jobs = []
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "os", SimpleNamespace(name="nt"))
++
++    def popen(argv, **kwargs):
++        flags = kwargs.get("creationflags", 0)
++        suspended = bool(flags & runner._CREATE_SUSPENDED)
++        events.append("create_suspended" if suspended else "create_running")
++        child = _MockChild(4242, events)
++        if not suspended:
++            events.append("command_callback")
++            command_callbacks.append(argv)
++        return child
++
++    class MockJob:
++        def __init__(self):
++            self.closed = False
++
++        def terminate_and_close(self):
++            if not self.closed:
++                self.closed = True
++                events.append("job_cleanup")
++                return True
++            return True
++
++    class Pointer:
++        def __init__(self, value):
++            self.value = (1 << 64) - 1 if value == -1 else value
++
++    class ThreadEntry:
++        def __init__(self):
++            self.dwSize = 0
++            self.th32OwnerProcessID = 0
++            self.th32ThreadID = 0
++
++    class FakeKernel32:
++        @staticmethod
++        def CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(flags, process_id):
++            events.append("thread_snapshot")
++            return 900
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def Thread32First(snapshot, entry):
++            events.append("thread_discovery")
++            if failure == "thread_discovery":
++                return False
++            entry.th32OwnerProcessID = 4242
++            entry.th32ThreadID = 77
++            return True
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def Thread32Next(snapshot, entry):
++            return False
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def OpenThread(access, inherit, thread_id):
++            events.append("open_primary_thread")
++            return 901
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def ResumeThread(thread):
++            events.append("resume_primary_thread")
++            return 0 if failure == "resume" else 1
++
++        @staticmethod
++        def CloseHandle(handle):
++            events.append("close_win32_handle")
++            return True
++
++    api = SimpleNamespace(
++        ctypes=SimpleNamespace(c_void_p=Pointer, sizeof=lambda value: 1, byref=lambda value: value),
++        k32=FakeKernel32,
++        ThreadEntry32=ThreadEntry,
++    )
++    resume_real = runner._resume_suspended_primary_thread
++
++    def attach_job(child):
++        events.append("assign_job" if failure != "assignment" else "assign_job_failed")
++        if failure == "assignment":
++            return None
++        job = MockJob()
++        jobs.append(job)
++        return job
++
++    def resume_primary_thread(pid):
++        resumed = resume_real(pid)
++        if resumed:
++            events.append("command_callback")
++            command_callbacks.append(["synthetic-command"])
++        return resumed
++
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.subprocess, "Popen", popen)
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_JobObject", SimpleNamespace(attach=attach_job))
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_win_api", lambda: api)
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_resume_suspended_primary_thread", resume_primary_thread)
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_kill_tree", lambda child: events.append("process_cleanup"))
++    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "_taskkill_tree", lambda pid: events.append("legacy_tree_cleanup"))
++    return events, command_callbacks, jobs
++

++def test_strict_windows_launch_suspends_assigns_job_then_resumes_before_command(monkeypatch):

++def test_socket_inventory_discovers_runtime_socket_under_non_1000_uid(monkeypatch):
++    user_paths = {"/run/user/1000", "/run/user/1001"}
++    directories = {"/run/user", *user_paths}
++    socket_path = "/run/user/1001/docker.sock"
++
++    class Entry:
++        def __init__(self, name):
++            self.name = name
++            self.path = f"/run/user/{name}"
++
++        def is_symlink(self):
++            return False
++
++        def is_dir(self, *, follow_symlinks):
++            return self.path in user_paths
++
++    class PathEnumerator:
++        def __init__(self, values):
++            self.values = values
++
++        def __enter__(self):
++            return self.values
++
++        def __exit__(self, *exc):
++            return False
++
++    class FakePath:
++        def __init__(self, value):
++            self.value = value
++
++        def read_text(self, *args, **kwargs):
++            return "Num RefCount Protocol Flags Type St Inode Path\n"
++
++    def lstat(path):
++        if path in directories or path == socket_path:
++            return object()
++        raise FileNotFoundError(path)
++
++    fake_path = SimpleNamespace(
++        islink=lambda path: False,
++        isdir=lambda path: path in directories,
++        join=lambda *parts: "/".join(parts),
++        dirname=lambda path: path.rsplit("/", 1)[0],
++    )
++    fake_os = SimpleNamespace(
++        lstat=lstat,
++        scandir=lambda path: PathEnumerator([Entry("1000"), Entry("1001")]),
++        path=fake_path,
++    )
++    monkeypatch.setattr(preflight, "os", fake_os)
++    monkeypatch.setattr(preflight, "Path", FakePath)
++
++    sockets, complete = preflight._container_socket_inventory()
++    assert complete is True
++    assert sockets == [socket_path]

++def test_coordinator_unlock_oserror_is_typed_and_releases_path_mutex(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
++    anchor = FileExternalAnchor(str(tmp_path / "unlock-failure" / "anchor.jsonl"), EVENT)
++    failed_once = False
++
++    def fail_first_unlock(real_lock, unlock_mode):
++        def injected(fd, mode, *extra):
++            nonlocal failed_once
++            if mode == unlock_mode and not failed_once:
++                failed_once = True
++                raise OSError("injected coordinator unlock failure")
++            return real_lock(fd, mode, *extra)
++        return injected
++
++    if os.name == "nt":
++        import msvcrt
++        monkeypatch.setattr(
++            msvcrt, "locking",
++            fail_first_unlock(msvcrt.locking, msvcrt.LK_UNLCK),
++        )
++    else:
++        import fcntl
++        monkeypatch.setattr(
++            fcntl, "flock",
++            fail_first_unlock(fcntl.flock, fcntl.LOCK_UN),
++        )
++
++    with pytest.raises(AnchorError, match="coordinator unlock failed: injected coordinator unlock failure"):
++        with anchor.transaction_lock():
++            pass
++
++    entered = threading.Event()
++    failures = []
++
++    def acquire_after_failure():
++        try:
++            with anchor.transaction_lock():
++                entered.set()
++        except BaseException as exc:
++            failures.append(exc)
++
++    retry = threading.Thread(target=acquire_after_failure, daemon=True)
++    retry.start()
++    assert entered.wait(timeout=5), "coordinator path mutex remained held after unlock failure"
++    retry.join(timeout=5)
++    assert not retry.is_alive()
++    assert failures == []

++_HEX40 = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{40}\Z")
++_BLOCKED_PARTS = {".git", ".github", ".hooks", "hooks", ".husky"}
++_BLOCKED_NAMES = {"package-lock.json", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "yarn.lock", "poetry.lock", "uv.lock", "pipfile.lock", "requirements.lock"}

++def normalize_path(path: str) -> str:
++    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path or "\0" in path:
++        raise ContractError("diff path must be a non-empty string")
++    value = path.replace("\\", "/")
++    if value.startswith("/") or re.match(r"^[A-Za-z]:", value):
++        raise ContractError("diff path must be repository-relative")
++    parts = value.split("/")
++    if any(p in ("", ".", "..") for p in parts):
++        raise ContractError("diff path contains traversal or empty components")
++    return "/".join(parts)
++
++
++def is_blocked_path(path: str) -> bool:
++    lower = path.lower()
++    parts = set(lower.split("/"))
++    name = lower.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
++    return bool(
++        parts & _BLOCKED_PARTS
++        or lower.startswith(_BLOCKED_PREFIXES)
++        or name in _BLOCKED_NAMES
++        or name.endswith(_BLOCKED_SUFFIXES)
++        or name in {"dockerfile", "install.sh", "install.ps1", "setup.py", "setup.cfg", "pyproject.toml"}
++        or name.startswith("dockerfile.")
++    )
++
++
++def check_diff(
++    *, manifest_sha256: str, base_head: str, candidate_head: str,
++    changed_paths: Iterable[str], allowed_paths: Iterable[str], diff_bytes: bytes,
++    symlink_paths: Iterable[str] = (), rename_pairs: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),
++) -> dict:
++    """Return reproducible PASS/FAIL evidence; every path failure is a FAIL."""
++    if not isinstance(manifest_sha256, str) or not _HEX64.fullmatch(manifest_sha256):
++        raise ContractError("manifest_sha256 must be lowercase SHA-256")
++    if not isinstance(base_head, str) or not _HEX40.fullmatch(base_head):
++        raise ContractError("base_head must be a lowercase git object id")
++    if not isinstance(candidate_head, str) or not _HEX40.fullmatch(candidate_head):
++        raise ContractError("candidate_head must be a lowercase git object id")
++    if not isinstance(diff_bytes, bytes):
++        raise ContractError("diff_bytes must be bytes")
++    try:
++        changed = sorted({normalize_path(path) for path in changed_paths})
++        allowed = {normalize_path(path) for path in allowed_paths}
++        symlinks = {normalize_path(path) for path in symlink_paths}
++        renames = [(normalize_path(a), normalize_path(b)) for a, b in rename_pairs]
++    except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
++        raise ContractError(f"invalid diff path evidence: {exc}") from exc
++    reason = "PASS"
++    if symlinks:
++        reason = "SYMLINK_CHANGE"
++    elif any(src in allowed and is_blocked_path(dst) for src, dst in renames):
++        reason = "RENAME_INTO_BLOCKED_PATH"
++    elif any(is_blocked_path(path) and path not in allowed for path in changed):
++        reason = "BLOCKED_PATH_CLASS"
++    elif any(path not in allowed for path in changed):
++        reason = "OUT_OF_SCOPE_PATH"
++    return {
++        "manifest_sha256": manifest_sha256,
++        "candidate_head": candidate_head,
++        "diff_sha256": hashlib.sha256(diff_bytes).hexdigest(),
++        "changed_paths": changed,
++        "verdict": "PASS" if reason == "PASS" else "FAIL",
++        "reason": reason,
++    }
++
++
++def sign_diff_evidence(evidence: dict, runner_key: bytes) -> dict:

++    if not isinstance(evidence, dict) or set(evidence) != fields:
++        raise ContractError("diff evidence fields do not match contract")
++    signed = dict(evidence)
++    signed["signature"] = sign(evidence, runner_key, DIFF_GATE_LABEL)
++    return signed

++"""External event anchoring and lifecycle transition contracts (stdlib only)."""
++
++from __future__ import annotations
++
++import hashlib
++import hmac
++import json
++import os
++import threading
++from contextlib import contextmanager
++from typing import Any, Protocol
++
++from .contracts import canonical_bytes
++from .signing import MIN_KEY_BYTES
++
++CHECKPOINT_LABEL = b"vst-external-checkpoint-v1\0"
++_GENESIS_HEAD = "0" * 64
++_anchor_lock = threading.Lock()
++_anchor_path_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
++_anchor_path_locks: dict[str, Any] = {}
++_anchor_path_lock_state = threading.local()
++
++
++class AnchorError(Exception):
++    """An unavailable, invalid, or conflicting external checkpoint."""
++
++
++class ExternalAnchor(Protocol):
++    def read_latest(self) -> dict | None: ...
++    def compare_and_append(self, expected: dict | None, checkpoint: dict) -> dict: ...
++
++
++def signed_checkpoint(count: int, head: str, event_key: bytes) -> dict:
++    body = {"count": count, "head": head}
++    mac = hmac.new(event_key, CHECKPOINT_LABEL + canonical_bytes(body), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
++    return {**body, "signature": mac}
++
++
++def verify_checkpoint(checkpoint: dict, event_key: bytes) -> bool:
++    if not isinstance(checkpoint, dict) or set(checkpoint) != {"count", "head", "signature"}:
++        return False
++    count, head, signature = checkpoint["count"], checkpoint["head"], checkpoint["signature"]
++    if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int) or count < 0:
++        return False
++    if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 64 or not isinstance(signature, str):
++        return False
++    expected = signed_checkpoint(count, head, event_key)["signature"]
++    return hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected)
++
++
++class FileExternalAnchor:
++    """Append-only JSONL anchor file; configure its path outside the worker mount."""
++
++    def __init__(self, path: str, event_key: bytes):
++        if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
++            raise ValueError("anchor path must be a non-empty string")
++        if not isinstance(event_key, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(event_key) < MIN_KEY_BYTES:
++            raise ValueError("event_key must be bytes of length >= 32")
++        self.path = os.path.abspath(path)
++        self._key = bytes(event_key)
++
++    @contextmanager
++    def transaction_lock(self):
++        """Serialize a store transaction and its external-anchor sync across processes.
++
++        Callers hold this lock across the SQLite commit and all checkpoint appends,
++        or across an authoritative read and its external-anchor comparison. A
++        separate lock file avoids recursively locking the JSONL file used by CAS.
++        Nested use by the same thread and path is reentrant.
++        """
++        lock_path = os.path.realpath(self.path) + ".coord.lock"
++        states = getattr(_anchor_path_lock_state, "states", None)
++        if states is None:
++            states = {}
++            _anchor_path_lock_state.states = states
++        state = states.get(lock_path)
++        if state is not None:
++            state["depth"] += 1
++            try:
++                yield
++            finally:
++                state["depth"] -= 1
++            return
++
++        with _anchor_path_locks_guard:
++            path_lock = _anchor_path_locks.setdefault(lock_path, threading.RLock())
++        path_lock.acquire()
++        stream = None
++        unlock = None
++        primary_error = None
++        try:
++            try:
++                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lock_path), exist_ok=True)
++                stream = open(lock_path, "a+b")
++                if os.name != "nt":
++                    os.chmod(lock_path, 0o600)
++                stream.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
++                if stream.tell() == 0:
++                    stream.write(b"\0")
++                    stream.flush()
++                if os.name == "nt":
++                    import msvcrt
++
++                    stream.seek(0)
++                    msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_LOCK, 1)
++                    unlock = lambda: msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
++                else:
++                    import fcntl
++
++                    fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
++                    unlock = lambda: fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
++            except OSError as exc:
++                raise AnchorError(f"external anchor coordinator setup failed: {exc}") from exc
++            state = {
++                "depth": 1,
++                "stream": stream,
++                "unlock": unlock,
++                "path_lock": path_lock,
++            }
++            states[lock_path] = state
++            yield
++        except BaseException as exc:
++            primary_error = exc
++            raise
++        finally:
++            states.pop(lock_path, None)
++            teardown_error = None
++            try:
++                if unlock is not None:
++                    unlock()
++            except OSError as exc:
++                teardown_error = AnchorError(
++                    f"external anchor coordinator unlock failed: {exc}"
++                )
++            finally:
++                try:
++                    if stream is not None and not stream.closed:
++                        stream.close()
++                except OSError as exc:
++                    if teardown_error is None:
++                        teardown_error = AnchorError(
++                            f"external anchor coordinator close failed: {exc}"
++                        )
++                finally:
++                    path_lock.release()
++            if teardown_error is not None and primary_error is None:
++                raise teardown_error
++
++    def read_latest(self) -> dict | None:
++        try:
++            with open(self.path, "rb") as stream:
++                lines = stream.read().splitlines()
++        except FileNotFoundError:
++            return None
++        except OSError as exc:
++            raise AnchorError(f"external anchor unavailable: {exc}") from exc
++        latest = None
++        for index, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
++            try:
++                item = json.loads(line)
++            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
++                raise AnchorError(f"malformed external checkpoint at line {index}") from exc
++            if not verify_checkpoint(item, self._key):
++                raise AnchorError(f"invalid external checkpoint at line {index}")
++            if latest is None and (item["count"] != 0 or item["head"] != _GENESIS_HEAD):
++                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint history must begin at genesis")
++            if latest is not None and item["count"] != latest["count"] + 1:
++                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint count is not strictly consecutive")
++            latest = item
++        return latest
++
++    def compare_and_append(self, expected: dict | None, checkpoint: dict) -> dict:
++        if not verify_checkpoint(checkpoint, self._key):
++            raise AnchorError("refusing unsigned or invalid checkpoint")
++        # The sidecar lock coordinates both Store transactions and standalone
++        # CAS calls. Locking this JSONL file separately with msvcrt is fragile
++        # across Windows append handles and is unnecessary under that lock.
++        with self.transaction_lock(), _anchor_lock:
++            latest = self.read_latest()
++            if latest == checkpoint:
++                return latest
++            if latest != expected:
++                if latest is not None and latest["count"] == checkpoint["count"]:
++                    raise AnchorError("same checkpoint count has a different head")
++                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint compare-and-append conflict")
++            wanted_count = 0 if expected is None else expected["count"] + 1
++            if checkpoint["count"] != wanted_count:
++                raise AnchorError("checkpoint is not the immediate successor")
++            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.path), exist_ok=True)
++            try:
++                with open(self.path, "a+b") as stream:

++def _loopback_canary() -> bool:
++    server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)

++    its Toolhelp thread snapshot identifies the primary thread without using
++    CPython's private Popen handles or undocumented Windows APIs. The pinned
++    Python 3.14 subprocess implementation closes the CreateProcess thread

++def require_distinct_worker_identity(worker_uid: int) -> None:
++    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(os, "geteuid"):

++def require_worker_cannot_access_signer(socket_path: str, *, worker_uid: int, worker_gid: int) -> None:
++    """Require parent/socket mode bits to exclude the worker principal."""
++    if os.name != "posix":
++        raise ContractError("signer IPC ACL verification is unavailable")
++    socket_file = Path(socket_path)
++    parent = socket_file.parent
++    try:
++        parent_st = parent.stat()
++        socket_st = socket_file.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
++    except OSError as exc:
++        raise ContractError(f"signer IPC is unavailable: {exc}") from exc
++    if not stat.S_ISSOCK(socket_st.st_mode):
++        raise ContractError("signer IPC endpoint is not a Unix socket")
++    if parent_st.st_mode & stat.S_IWOTH or socket_st.st_mode & (stat.S_IROTH | stat.S_IWOTH):
++        raise ContractError("signer IPC grants access to other identities")
++    if worker_uid in (parent_st.st_uid, socket_st.st_uid):
++        raise ContractError("worker identity owns signer IPC path")
++    if worker_gid in (parent_st.st_gid, socket_st.st_gid):
++        raise ContractError("worker primary group can access signer IPC")
++

++def require_runner_can_access_signer(socket_path: str) -> None:
++    if os.name != "posix":
++        raise ContractError("signer IPC access verification is unavailable")
++    socket_file = Path(socket_path)
++    try:
++        parent_st = socket_file.parent.stat()
++        socket_st = socket_file.stat(follow_symlinks=False)
++    except OSError as exc:
++        raise ContractError(f"signer IPC is unavailable: {exc}") from exc
++    groups = set(os.getgroups()) | {os.getegid()}
++    if not stat.S_ISSOCK(socket_st.st_mode):
++        raise ContractError("signer IPC endpoint is not a Unix socket")
++    parent_access = (
++        os.geteuid() == parent_st.st_uid and parent_st.st_mode & stat.S_IXUSR
++    ) or (parent_st.st_gid in groups and parent_st.st_mode & stat.S_IXGRP)
++    if not parent_access:
++        raise ContractError("runner cannot traverse signer socket directory")
++    socket_access = (
++        os.geteuid() == socket_st.st_uid and socket_st.st_mode & stat.S_IWUSR
++    ) or (socket_st.st_gid in groups and socket_st.st_mode & stat.S_IWGRP)
++    if not socket_access:
++        raise ContractError("runner cannot connect to signer socket")

++def require_private_key(path: str, *, owner_uid: int | None = None) -> None:
++    st = os.stat(path, follow_symlinks=False)
++    if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
++        raise ContractError("key must be a regular non-symlink file")
++    if os.name != "posix":
++        raise ContractError("key ACL verification is unavailable; refusing to start")
++    expected_owner = os.geteuid() if owner_uid is None else owner_uid
++    if st.st_uid != expected_owner or stat.S_IMODE(st.st_mode) != 0o600:
++        raise ContractError("key must be owned by trusted identity and have mode 0600")

++def require_read_only_tree(path: str, *, worker_uid: int | None = None) -> None:
++    """Check the credential's effective write bit on every tree entry."""
++    root = Path(path)
++    if os.name != "posix":
++        raise ContractError("read-only reviewer ACL verification is unavailable")
++    if os.geteuid() == 0:
++        raise ContractError("reviewer must not run as root")
++    if worker_uid is not None and (not isinstance(worker_uid, int) or worker_uid == os.geteuid()):
++        raise ContractError("reviewer identity must differ from worker identity")
++    if not root.exists():
++        raise ContractError("read-only resource does not exist")
++    if stat.S_ISLNK(root.lstat().st_mode):
++        raise ContractError("read-only resource root must not be a symlink")
++    entries = [root] if not root.is_dir() else None
++    if entries is not None:
++        parents = [(root.parent, [], [root.name])]
++    else:
++        parents = os.walk(root, followlinks=False)
++    for parent, dirs, files in parents:
++        for name in ([root.name] if entries is not None else [".", *dirs, *files]):
++            item = root if entries is not None else (Path(parent) if name == "." else Path(parent) / name)
++            st = item.lstat()
++            if stat.S_ISLNK(st.st_mode):
++                raise ContractError(f"review tree contains symlink: {item}")
++            if st.st_uid == os.geteuid() and st.st_mode & stat.S_IWUSR:
++                raise ContractError(f"review identity can write tree entry: {item}")
++            try:
++                writable = os.access(item, os.W_OK, effective_ids=True)
++            except (NotImplementedError, TypeError):
++                writable = os.access(item, os.W_OK)
++            if writable:
++                raise ContractError(f"review identity can write tree entry: {item}")
++
++
++def require_read_only_reviewer(worktree: str, store_path: str, *, worker_uid: int) -> None:
++    """Prove reviewer identity differs from worker and cannot mutate either resource."""
++    require_read_only_tree(worktree, worker_uid=worker_uid)
++    require_read_only_tree(store_path, worker_uid=worker_uid)

++
++The service is intentionally POSIX Unix-domain-socket only. It authenticates
++the connecting process with SO_PEERCRED and fails closed on platforms without

++def _key_is_private(path: str) -> bytes:
++    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW"):
++        raise ContractError("signing key ACL verification requires POSIX O_NOFOLLOW")
++    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
++    try:
++        st = os.fstat(fd)
++        if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
++            raise ContractError("signing key must be a regular non-symlink file")
++        if st.st_uid != os.geteuid() or st.st_mode & 0o077:
++            raise ContractError("signing key must be owned by signer and mode 0600")
++        chunks = bytearray()
++        while True:
++            part = os.read(fd, 65536)
++            if not part:
++                break
++            chunks.extend(part)
++        key = bytes(chunks)
++    finally:
++        os.close(fd)
++    if len(key) < MIN_KEY_BYTES:
++        raise ContractError("signing key is too short")
++    return key

++    def _run_bounded_git(
++        self, command: list[str], *, env: dict[str, str],
++        output_limit: int | None = None,
++    ) -> tuple[bytes, bytes, int]:
++        """Run trusted Git plumbing with fixed-size output capture and timeout."""
++        output_limit = self._MAX_PREFLIGHT_OUTPUT_BYTES if output_limit is None else output_limit
++        process = subprocess.Popen(
++            command, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
++            stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env, bufsize=0,
++        )
++        outputs = {"stdout": bytearray(), "stderr": bytearray()}
++        overflow = {"stdout": False, "stderr": False}
++
++        def drain(name: str, stream) -> None:
++            while True:
++                chunk = stream.read(4096)
++                if not chunk:
++                    return
++                remaining = output_limit - len(outputs[name])
++                if remaining > 0:
++                    outputs[name].extend(chunk[:remaining])
++                if len(chunk) > remaining:
++                    overflow[name] = True
++
++        readers = [
++            threading.Thread(target=drain, args=(name, stream), daemon=True)
++            for name, stream in (("stdout", process.stdout), ("stderr", process.stderr))
++        ]
++        for reader in readers:
++            reader.start()
++        try:
++            returncode = process.wait(timeout=self.command_timeout_sec)
++        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
++            try:
++                process.kill()
++            except OSError:
++                pass
++            try:
++                process.wait(timeout=1)
++            except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError) as reap_error:
++                raise TimeoutError("bounded Git preflight process could not be reaped") from reap_error
++            raise TimeoutError("bounded Git preflight command exceeded its time limit") from exc
++        finally:
++            for reader in readers:
++                reader.join(timeout=1)
++            for stream in (process.stdout, process.stderr):
++                if stream is not None:
++                    stream.close()
++        if any(overflow.values()):
++            raise RuntimeError("bounded Git command output exceeded its limit")
++        if any(reader.is_alive() for reader in readers):
++            raise RuntimeError("bounded Git preflight output reader did not finish")
++        return bytes(outputs["stdout"]), bytes(outputs["stderr"]), returncode

++                        raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                    chunk = source.read(min(64 * 1024, remaining))
++                    if not chunk:
++                        raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object file truncated during snapshot")
++                    target.write(chunk)
++                    copied[0] += len(chunk)
++                    if copied[0] > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                        raise RuntimeError("synthetic source snapshot exceeds the 512 MiB limit")
++                    remaining -= len(chunk)
++                if source.read(1):
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object file grew during snapshot")
++            if os.name == "nt":
++                final_identity = self._windows_source_object_file_identity(fd)
++            else:
++                final_stat = os.fstat(fd)
++                final_identity = (
++                    final_stat.st_dev, final_stat.st_ino, final_stat.st_size, final_stat.st_nlink,
++                )
++            if final_identity != initial_identity or self._is_link_or_junction(source_path):
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object file changed during snapshot")
++        finally:

++    @staticmethod
++    def _open_windows_source_object_file(path: str) -> int:
++        """Open a source object without following reparse points or allowing replacement."""
++        import ctypes
++        from ctypes import wintypes
++        import msvcrt
++
++        class FileAttributeTagInfo(ctypes.Structure):
++            _fields_ = [("FileAttributes", wintypes.DWORD), ("ReparseTag", wintypes.DWORD)]
++
++        class FileStandardInfo(ctypes.Structure):
++            _fields_ = [
++                ("AllocationSize", ctypes.c_longlong), ("EndOfFile", ctypes.c_longlong),
++                ("NumberOfLinks", wintypes.DWORD), ("DeletePending", wintypes.BOOLEAN),
++                ("Directory", wintypes.BOOLEAN),
++            ]
++
++        kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
++        create_file = kernel32.CreateFileW
++        create_file.argtypes = [
++            wintypes.LPCWSTR, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.LPVOID,
++            wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.HANDLE,
++        ]
++        create_file.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
++        get_info = kernel32.GetFileInformationByHandleEx
++        get_info.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_int, wintypes.LPVOID, wintypes.DWORD]
++        get_info.restype = wintypes.BOOL
++        close_handle = kernel32.CloseHandle
++        close_handle.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
++        close_handle.restype = wintypes.BOOL
++
++        generic_read = 0x80000000
++        share_read = 0x00000001
++        open_existing = 3
++        open_reparse_point = 0x00200000
++        handle = create_file(
++            path, generic_read, share_read, None, open_existing, open_reparse_point, None,
++        )
++        invalid_handle = ctypes.c_void_p(-1).value
++        if not handle or handle == invalid_handle:
++            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
++        try:
++            attributes = FileAttributeTagInfo()
++            standard = FileStandardInfo()
++            if not get_info(handle, 9, ctypes.byref(attributes), ctypes.sizeof(attributes)):
++                raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
++            if not get_info(handle, 1, ctypes.byref(standard), ctypes.sizeof(standard)):
++                raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
++            if attributes.FileAttributes & 0x400 or standard.Directory:
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object entry is a reparse point or directory")
++            if standard.NumberOfLinks != 1:
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object file has an external hard-link alias")
++            if standard.EndOfFile < 0:
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object file has an invalid size")
++            fd = msvcrt.open_osfhandle(handle, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_BINARY)
++            handle = None
++            return fd
++        finally:
++            if handle is not None:
++                close_handle(handle)

++    @staticmethod
++    def _windows_source_object_file_identity(fd: int) -> tuple[int, int, int, bytes]:
++        """Return volume/file ID, size and link count from the opened Windows handle."""
++        import ctypes
++        from ctypes import wintypes
++        import msvcrt
++
++        class FileStandardInfo(ctypes.Structure):
++            _fields_ = [
++                ("AllocationSize", ctypes.c_longlong), ("EndOfFile", ctypes.c_longlong),
++                ("NumberOfLinks", wintypes.DWORD), ("DeletePending", wintypes.BOOLEAN),
++                ("Directory", wintypes.BOOLEAN),
++            ]
++
++        class FileId128(ctypes.Structure):
++            _fields_ = [("Identifier", ctypes.c_ubyte * 16)]
++
++        class FileIdInfo(ctypes.Structure):
++            _fields_ = [("VolumeSerialNumber", ctypes.c_ulonglong), ("FileId", FileId128)]
++
++        kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
++        get_info = kernel32.GetFileInformationByHandleEx
++        get_info.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.c_int, wintypes.LPVOID, wintypes.DWORD]
++        get_info.restype = wintypes.BOOL
++        handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)
++        standard = FileStandardInfo()
++        identity = FileIdInfo()
++        if not get_info(handle, 1, ctypes.byref(standard), ctypes.sizeof(standard)):
++            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
++        if not get_info(handle, 18, ctypes.byref(identity), ctypes.sizeof(identity)):
++            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
++        return (
++            identity.VolumeSerialNumber,
++            standard.EndOfFile,
++            standard.NumberOfLinks,
++            bytes(identity.FileId.Identifier),
++        )

++    def _copy_source_object_store(self, source_objects: str, snapshot_objects: str) -> int:
++        copied = [0]
++        entry_count = [0]
++        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.command_timeout_sec
++
++        def count_entry() -> None:
++            entry_count[0] += 1
++            if entry_count[0] > self._MAX_SOURCE_STORE_ENTRIES:
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source snapshot exceeds the entry-count limit")
++
++        with os.scandir(source_objects) as source_entries:
++            for entry in source_entries:
++                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                    raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                count_entry()
++                name = entry.name
++                if self._is_link_or_junction(entry.path):
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object store contains a symlink")
++                if name == "info":
++                    continue
++                if name == "pack" and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
++                    with os.scandir(entry.path) as pack_entries:
++                        for pack_entry in pack_entries:
++                            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                                raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                            count_entry()
++                            if self._is_link_or_junction(pack_entry.path):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack directory contains a symlink")
++                            pack_name = pack_entry.name
++                            suffix = ".pack" if pack_name.endswith(".pack") else ".idx" if pack_name.endswith(".idx") else None
++                            if suffix is None:
++                                continue
++                            object_hash = pack_name[5:-len(suffix)] if pack_name.startswith("pack-") else ""
++                            if len(object_hash) not in {40, 64} or not self._is_lower_hex(object_hash):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack file has an invalid name")
++                            if not pack_entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack entry is not a regular file")
++                            self._copy_source_object_file(
++                                pack_entry, os.path.join(snapshot_objects, "pack", pack_name), copied, deadline,
++                            )
++                elif entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) and len(name) == 2 and self._is_lower_hex(name):
++                    with os.scandir(entry.path) as loose_entries:
++                        for loose_entry in loose_entries:
++                            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                                raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                            count_entry()
++                            if self._is_link_or_junction(loose_entry.path):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source loose-object directory contains a symlink")
++                            if len(loose_entry.name) not in {38, 62} or not self._is_lower_hex(loose_entry.name):
++                                continue
++                            if not loose_entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source loose object is not a regular file")
++                            self._copy_source_object_file(
++                                loose_entry,
++                                os.path.join(snapshot_objects, name, loose_entry.name), copied, deadline,
++                            )
++                else:
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object store has an unsupported root entry")
++                if copied[0] > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source snapshot exceeds the 512 MiB limit")
++        return copied[0]

++    @contextmanager
++    def _source_object_snapshot(self, head: str):
++        """Copy only local object files into an isolated Git object database."""
++        _, source_git_dir, source_objects = self._source_repository_paths()
++        self._source_object_storage_bytes(source_objects)
++        source_count, source_size_bytes = self._source_object_counts(source_git_dir, source_objects)
++        if source_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT:
++            raise RuntimeError("synthetic source repository exceeds the 250,000 object limit")
++        if source_size_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++            raise RuntimeError("Git count-objects reports a source ODB larger than 512 MiB")
++        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".vst-source-snapshot-", dir=self.bare_path) as temp_root:
++            template = os.path.join(temp_root, "empty-template")
++            snapshot_git_dir = os.path.join(temp_root, "source.git")
++            os.makedirs(template)

++                ["git", "init", "--bare", f"--template={template}", snapshot_git_dir],
++                env=self._git_env(),

++            if init_returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(init_error.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            snapshot_objects = os.path.join(snapshot_git_dir, "objects")

++            snapshot_count, snapshot_size_bytes = self._source_object_counts(snapshot_git_dir, snapshot_objects)
++            if snapshot_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT or snapshot_size_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                raise RuntimeError("sanitized source object snapshot exceeds its preflight limits")
++            if snapshot_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES or snapshot_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT:
++                raise RuntimeError("sanitized source object snapshot exceeds its preflight limits")
++            snapshot_env = self._git_env(snapshot_objects)
++            _, diagnostic, returncode = self._run_bounded_git(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", snapshot_git_dir, "cat-file", "-e", f"{head}^{{commit}}"],
++                env=snapshot_env,

++                raise RuntimeError(
++                    "candidate commit is not present in the isolated local source object store: "
++                    + diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace")

++            yield snapshot_git_dir, snapshot_env

++    def _import_head(self, head: str) -> None:
++        with self._target_storage_lock() as lease:
++            self._reserve_target_object_storage(
++                self._MAX_PACK_BYTES + self._MAX_PACK_INDEX_BYTES,
++            )
++            self._write_storage_state(lease, "IN_PROGRESS")
++            try:
++                self._import_head_locked(head, lease)
++            except BaseException:
++                if not lease.get("cleanup_uncertain"):
++                    try:
++                        self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++                    except OSError:
++                        # The durable IN_PROGRESS slot remains fail-closed.
++                        pass
++                raise
++            else:
++                self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++            if self._target_object_storage_bytes() > self._MAX_TARGET_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                raise StoreError(
++                    "synthetic target object storage cap was exceeded during pack import",
++                    kind="budget",
++                )
++
++    def _import_head_locked(self, head: str, lease: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
++        with self._source_object_snapshot(head) as (source_git_dir, source_env):
++            self._transfer_snapshot_head_locked(head, source_git_dir, source_env, lease)
++
++    def _transfer_snapshot_head_locked(
++        self, head: str, source_git_dir: str, source_env: dict[str, str],
++        lease: dict[str, Any],
++    ) -> None:
++        source_command = [
++            "git", "-c", "pack.threads=1", "-c", "pack.windowMemory=16m",
++            "-c", "pack.window=10", "-c", "pack.deltaCacheSize=16777216",
++            "-c", "pack.deltaCacheLimit=32768", "--git-dir", source_git_dir,
++            "pack-objects", "--stdout", "--revs",
++        ]
++        target_command = [
++            "git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "index-pack", "--strict", "--stdin",
++        ]
++        source = target = None
++        source_diagnostic = bytearray()
++        target_diagnostic = bytearray()
++        expired = threading.Event()
++        finished = threading.Event()
++
++        def drain(stream, output: bytearray) -> None:
++            while True:
++                chunk = stream.read(4096)
++                if not chunk:
++                    return
++                remaining = self._MAX_GIT_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES - len(output)
++                if remaining > 0:
++                    output.extend(chunk[:remaining])
++
++        def kill_after_timeout() -> None:
++            if finished.is_set():
++                return
++            expired.set()
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
++                    try:
++                        process.kill()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++
++        timer = threading.Timer(self.command_timeout_sec, kill_after_timeout)
++        source_stderr_thread = target_stderr_thread = None
++        cleanup_uncertain = False
++        try:
++            source = subprocess.Popen(
++                source_command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
++                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=source_env, bufsize=0,
++            )
++            target = subprocess.Popen(
++                target_command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
++                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=self._target_git_env(), bufsize=0,
++            )
++            source_stderr_thread = threading.Thread(
++                target=drain, args=(source.stderr, source_diagnostic), daemon=True,
++            )
++            target_stderr_thread = threading.Thread(
++                target=drain, args=(target.stderr, target_diagnostic), daemon=True,
++            )
++            source_stderr_thread.start()
++            target_stderr_thread.start()
++            timer_start = time.monotonic()
++            timer.start()
++            source.stdin.write((head + "\n").encode("ascii"))
++            source.stdin.close()
++
++            total_bytes = 0
++            pack_header = bytearray()
++            while True:
++                chunk = source.stdout.read(64 * 1024)
++                if not chunk:
++                    break
++                total_bytes += len(chunk)
++                if total_bytes > self._MAX_PACK_BYTES:
++                    raise RuntimeError("Git source object pack exceeds the 64 MiB limit")
++                if len(pack_header) < 12:
++                    pack_header.extend(chunk[:12 - len(pack_header)])
++                    if len(pack_header) == 12:
++                        if pack_header[:4] != b"PACK":
++                            raise RuntimeError("Git source did not produce a valid pack header")
++                        object_count = int.from_bytes(pack_header[8:12], "big")
++                        if object_count > self._MAX_PACK_OBJECTS:
++                            raise RuntimeError("Git source object pack exceeds the object-count limit")
++                target.stdin.write(chunk)
++            if expired.is_set():
++                raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit")
++            if total_bytes == 0 or len(pack_header) < 12:
++                raise RuntimeError("Git source repository produced an empty or truncated object pack")
++            target.stdin.close()
++            deadline = timer_start + self.command_timeout_sec
++            source.wait(timeout=max(0.001, deadline - time.monotonic()))
++            target.wait(timeout=max(0.001, deadline - time.monotonic()))
++            if expired.is_set():
++                raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit")
++            if source.returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(source_diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            if target.returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(target_diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
++            raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit") from exc
++        finally:
++            finished.set()
++            timer.cancel()
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
++                    try:
++                        process.kill()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None:
++                    try:
++                        process.wait(timeout=1)
++                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
++                        try:
++                            process.kill()
++                        except OSError:
++                            pass
++                        try:
++                            process.wait(timeout=1)
++                        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
++                            cleanup_uncertain = True
++                    except OSError:
++                        cleanup_uncertain = True
++                    if process.returncode is None:
++                        cleanup_uncertain = True
++            for worker in (source_stderr_thread, target_stderr_thread):
++                if worker is not None:
++                    worker.join(timeout=1)
++            for stream in (
++                source.stdin if source else None, source.stdout if source else None,
++                source.stderr if source else None, target.stdin if target else None,
++                target.stderr if target else None,
++            ):
++                if stream is not None:
++                    try:
++                        stream.close()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++            if cleanup_uncertain:
++                lease["cleanup_uncertain"] = True
++                try:
++                    self._write_storage_state(lease, "POISONED")
++                except OSError as poison_error:
++                    # The previously fsynced IN_PROGRESS slot remains valid and
++                    # blocks future writers even if this final marker write fails.
++                    raise RuntimeError(
++                        "Git child cleanup is unconfirmed; target remains IN_PROGRESS"
++                    ) from poison_error
++                raise RuntimeError("Git child cleanup is unconfirmed; target is poisoned")
++        self._git("cat-file", "-e", f"{head}^{{commit}}")

++    def _is_ancestor(self, ancestor: str, descendant: str) -> bool:
++        completed = subprocess.run(
++            ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ancestor, descendant],
++            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
++            check=False, timeout=self.command_timeout_sec,
++        )
++        if completed.returncode == 0:
++            return True
++        if completed.returncode == 1:
++            return False
++        raise RuntimeError(completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))

++    def _update_ref(self, ref: str, head: str, expected: str | None) -> None:
++        old_value = expected or ("0" * 40)
++        try:
++            self._git("update-ref", ref, head, old_value)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            try:
++                if self.ref_head(ref) == head:
++                    return
++            except RuntimeError:
++                pass
++            raise StoreError("bare target ref changed during synthetic publication", kind="duplicate")
++
++    def ref_head(self, ref: str) -> str:
++        return self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++
++    def _bind_operation(self, kind: str, operation_key: str, payload: dict) -> None:
++        with self._target_storage_lock() as lease:
++            self._bind_operation_locked(kind, operation_key, payload, lease)
++
++    def _bind_operation_locked(
++        self, kind: str, operation_key: str, payload: dict, lease: dict[str, Any],
++    ) -> None:
++        key_hash = hashlib.sha256(f"{kind}\0{operation_key}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
++        ref = f"refs/vst/idempotency/{key_hash}"
++        record = canonical_bytes({"kind": kind, "payload": payload})
++        try:
++            existing_oid = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            existing_oid = None
++        if existing_oid is not None:
++            existing, diagnostic, returncode = self._run_bounded_git(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "cat-file", "blob", existing_oid],
++                env=self._target_git_env(), output_limit=self._MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_RECORD_BYTES,
++            )
++            if returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            if existing != record:
++                raise StoreError("remote idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++            return
++        if len(record) > self._MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_RECORD_BYTES:
++            raise StoreError("synthetic idempotency record exceeds the 64 KiB limit", kind="budget")
++        self._reserve_target_object_storage(len(record) + (len(record) // 100) + 256)
++        self._write_storage_state(lease, "IN_PROGRESS")
++        try:
++            new_oid = self._git("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", input_bytes=record)
++        except BaseException:
++            try:
++                self._write_storage_state(lease, "POISONED")
++            except OSError:
++                pass
++            raise
++        self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++        try:
++            self._git("update-ref", ref, new_oid, "0" * 40)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            # Another supervisor process may have won the create-only ref race.
++            raced_oid = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++            raced = subprocess.run(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "cat-file", "blob", raced_oid],
++                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
++                check=True, timeout=self.command_timeout_sec,
++            ).stdout
++            if raced != record:
++                raise StoreError("remote idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++
++    def push(self, payload: dict, *, operation_key: str) -> dict:
++        branch, head = payload["branch"], payload["head"]
++        if not isinstance(branch, str) or not branch.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
++            raise ValueError("invalid synthetic branch")
++        if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 40 or any(ch not in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in head):
++            raise ValueError("candidate head must be a 40-character git id")
++        self._bind_operation("push", operation_key, payload)
++        ref = f"refs/heads/{branch}"
++        try:
++            current = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            current = None
++        if current != head:
++            self._import_head(head)
++            if current is not None and not self._is_ancestor(current, head):
++                raise StoreError("synthetic branch update is not a fast-forward", kind="duplicate")
++            self._update_ref(ref, head, current)
++        return {"operation_key": operation_key, "ref": ref, "head": head}
++
++    def open_pull_request(self, payload: dict, *, operation_key: str) -> dict:
++        head = payload["head"]
++        if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 40 or any(ch not in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in head):
++            raise ValueError("pull-request head must be a 40-character git id")
++        self._bind_operation("pull_request", operation_key, payload)
++        pr_key = hashlib.sha256(operation_key.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
++        ref = f"refs/pull-requests/{pr_key}/head"
++        try:
++            current = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            current = None
++        if current is not None and current != head:
++            raise StoreError("pull-request key already points at a different head", kind="duplicate")
++        if current is None:
++            self._import_head(head)
++            self._update_ref(ref, head, None)
++        return {"operation_key": operation_key, "ref": ref, "head": head}

++class HandWrittenWorker:
++    """Minimal synthetic worker with scoped edits and no remote/push API."""
++
++    def __init__(self, repository: str, allowed_paths: tuple[str, ...] = ("src/synthetic.py",)):
++        self.repository = os.path.realpath(repository)
++        self.allowed_paths = frozenset(allowed_paths)

++    def _run(
++        self, action: str, path: str, content: str = "", timeout_sec: float | None = None,
++    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
++        worker_code = r'''import os, subprocess, sys
++repo, action, rel, content, timeout_text = sys.argv[1:6]
++timeout = float(timeout_text) if timeout_text else None
++if rel.startswith(("/", "\\")) or ".." in rel.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
++    raise SystemExit(30)
++root = os.path.realpath(repo)

++    def lookup_idempotent_operation(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,

++        operation: str | None = None,
++        payload: Any = None,

++                (operation_key,),

++                raise StoreError("idempotency key reused for a different operation", kind="duplicate")
++            if expected_digest is not None and row["payload_sha256"] != expected_digest:
++                raise StoreError("idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++            try:

++            completed = None
++            inconclusive = False
++            error_types: list[str] = []
++            rows = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND actor = 'supervisor' AND kind = 'NOTE' ORDER BY seq",
++                (operation_key,),

++                    if completed is not None and canonical_bytes(completed) != canonical_bytes(result):
++                        raise StoreError("external operation has conflicting completion records", kind="integrity")

++                "state": "INCONCLUSIVE" if inconclusive else "PENDING",

++    def charge_idempotent(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,
++        task_id: str,
++        amount: int,
++        *,
++        supervisor_key: bytes,
++        runner_id: str = SUPERVISOR_RUNNER_ID,
++        expected_cap: int | None = None,
++        expected_spent: int | None = None,
++    ) -> int:
++        """Charge budget once for an exact key/payload, preserving cap markers.
++
++        A repeated identical request returns its original remaining balance. A
++        reused key with different task, amount, or runner is rejected. An
++        over-cap first attempt atomically records the existing signed budget
++        markers and a durable blocked result; replay raises the same budget
++        error without charging or appending another marker.
++        """

++            _need_int(expected_cap, "expected_cap", 0, MAX_BUDGET)
++        if expected_spent is not None:
++            _need_int(expected_spent, "expected_spent", 0, MAX_BUDGET)
++        payload = {
++            "task_id": task_id, "amount": amount, "runner_id": runner_id,
++            "expected_cap": expected_cap, "expected_spent": expected_spent,
++        }
++
++        def charge(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
++            task = self._task_row(conn, task_id)
++            row = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT cap, spent FROM budget WHERE task_id = ?", (task_id,)
++            ).fetchone()
++            if row is None:
++                raise StoreError(f"no budget set for task {task_id!r}", kind="budget")
++            if ((expected_cap is not None and row["cap"] != expected_cap)
++                    or (expected_spent is not None and row["spent"] != expected_spent)):
++                raise StoreError(
++                    "caller budget snapshot differs from the authoritative ledger",
++                    kind="budget_snapshot",
++                )

++    def stop_attempt_fenced(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,
++        task_id: str,
++        story_id: str,

++        the result is always INCONCLUSIVE until a separate safe cleanup proof

++            raise StoreError("stop binding must be an object", kind="argument")

++            "expected_epoch": expected_epoch, "expected_owner": expected_owner,
++            "reason": reason, "authorized_actor": authorized_actor,
++            "binding": binding or {},

++        def stop(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
++            story = self._story_row(conn, story_id)
++            task = self._task_row(conn, task_id)
++            if task["story_id"] != story_id:
++                raise StoreError("stop task does not belong to the specified story", kind="story")
++            if int(story["epoch"]) != expected_epoch:
++                raise StoreError("stop request has a stale epoch fence", kind="epoch")
++            if story["owner"] != expected_owner:
++                raise StoreError("stop request does not hold current story ownership", kind="epoch")
++            new_epoch = expected_epoch + 1
++            if new_epoch > MAX_COUNTER:
++                raise StoreError("epoch counter exhausted", kind="epoch")
++            lease = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT lease_id, epoch, status FROM leases WHERE task_id = ? AND attempt = ?",
++                (task_id, attempt),
++            ).fetchone()

++                raise StoreError("stop attempt lease belongs to a different epoch", kind="epoch")
++            conn.execute(
++                "UPDATE stories SET epoch = ?, owner = NULL, owner_expires_at = NULL, state = 'OPEN' "
++                "WHERE story_id = ? AND epoch = ? AND owner = ?",

++            )

++                raise StoreError("stop lost the story epoch compare-and-swap", kind="epoch")

++                conn.execute(
++                    "UPDATE leases SET status = 'FENCED' WHERE lease_id = ? AND status = 'LIVE'",
++                    (lease["lease_id"],),

++                    raise StoreError("stop lost the live lease compare-and-swap", kind="lease")

++                    conn, task_id, "store", "LEASE_FENCED",
++                    {"attempt": attempt, "new_epoch": new_epoch, "reason": "STOP"},
++                )

++                "state": "INCONCLUSIVE",
++                "task_id": task_id,
++                "story_id": story_id,
++                "attempt": attempt,
