++    def _copy_source_object_store(self, source_objects: str, snapshot_objects: str) -> int:
++        copied = [0]
++        entry_count = [0]
++        deadline = time.monotonic() + self.command_timeout_sec
++
++        def count_entry() -> None:
++            entry_count[0] += 1
++            if entry_count[0] > self._MAX_SOURCE_STORE_ENTRIES:
++                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source snapshot exceeds the entry-count limit")
++
++        with os.scandir(source_objects) as source_entries:
++            for entry in source_entries:
++                if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                    raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                count_entry()
++                name = entry.name
++                if self._is_link_or_junction(entry.path):
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object store contains a symlink")
++                if name == "info":
++                    continue
++                if name == "pack" and entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False):
++                    with os.scandir(entry.path) as pack_entries:
++                        for pack_entry in pack_entries:
++                            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                                raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                            count_entry()
++                            if self._is_link_or_junction(pack_entry.path):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack directory contains a symlink")
++                            pack_name = pack_entry.name
++                            suffix = ".pack" if pack_name.endswith(".pack") else ".idx" if pack_name.endswith(".idx") else None
++                            if suffix is None:
++                                continue
++                            object_hash = pack_name[5:-len(suffix)] if pack_name.startswith("pack-") else ""
++                            if len(object_hash) not in {40, 64} or not self._is_lower_hex(object_hash):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack file has an invalid name")
++                            if not pack_entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source pack entry is not a regular file")
++                            self._copy_source_object_file(
++                                pack_entry, os.path.join(snapshot_objects, "pack", pack_name), copied, deadline,
++                            )
++                elif entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) and len(name) == 2 and self._is_lower_hex(name):
++                    with os.scandir(entry.path) as loose_entries:
++                        for loose_entry in loose_entries:
++                            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
++                                raise TimeoutError("synthetic source snapshot copy exceeded its time limit")
++                            count_entry()
++                            if self._is_link_or_junction(loose_entry.path):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source loose-object directory contains a symlink")
++                            if len(loose_entry.name) not in {38, 62} or not self._is_lower_hex(loose_entry.name):
++                                continue
++                            if not loose_entry.is_file(follow_symlinks=False):
++                                raise RuntimeError("synthetic source loose object is not a regular file")
++                            self._copy_source_object_file(
++                                loose_entry,
++                                os.path.join(snapshot_objects, name, loose_entry.name), copied, deadline,
++                            )
++                else:
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source object store has an unsupported root entry")
++                if copied[0] > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                    raise RuntimeError("synthetic source snapshot exceeds the 512 MiB limit")
++        return copied[0]

++    @contextmanager
++    def _source_object_snapshot(self, head: str):
++        """Copy only local object files into an isolated Git object database."""
++        _, source_git_dir, source_objects = self._source_repository_paths()
++        self._source_object_storage_bytes(source_objects)
++        source_count, source_size_bytes = self._source_object_counts(source_git_dir, source_objects)
++        if source_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT:
++            raise RuntimeError("synthetic source repository exceeds the 250,000 object limit")
++        if source_size_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++            raise RuntimeError("Git count-objects reports a source ODB larger than 512 MiB")
++        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".vst-source-snapshot-", dir=self.bare_path) as temp_root:
++            template = os.path.join(temp_root, "empty-template")
++            snapshot_git_dir = os.path.join(temp_root, "source.git")
++            os.makedirs(template)
++            init_output, init_error, init_returncode = self._run_bounded_git(
++                ["git", "init", "--bare", f"--template={template}", snapshot_git_dir],
++                env=self._git_env(),
++            )
++            if init_returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(init_error.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            snapshot_objects = os.path.join(snapshot_git_dir, "objects")
++            self._copy_source_object_store(source_objects, snapshot_objects)
++            snapshot_bytes = self._source_object_storage_bytes(snapshot_objects)
++            snapshot_count, snapshot_size_bytes = self._source_object_counts(snapshot_git_dir, snapshot_objects)
++            if snapshot_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT or snapshot_size_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                raise RuntimeError("sanitized source object snapshot exceeds its preflight limits")
++            if snapshot_bytes > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES or snapshot_count > self._MAX_SOURCE_OBJECT_COUNT:
++                raise RuntimeError("sanitized source object snapshot exceeds its preflight limits")
++            snapshot_env = self._git_env(snapshot_objects)
++            _, diagnostic, returncode = self._run_bounded_git(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", snapshot_git_dir, "cat-file", "-e", f"{head}^{{commit}}"],
++                env=snapshot_env,
++            )
++            if returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(
++                    "candidate commit is not present in the isolated local source object store: "
++                    + diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace")
++                )
++            yield snapshot_git_dir, snapshot_env
++
++    def _import_head(self, head: str) -> None:
++        with self._target_storage_lock() as lease:
++            self._reserve_target_object_storage(
++                self._MAX_PACK_BYTES + self._MAX_PACK_INDEX_BYTES,
++            )
++            self._write_storage_state(lease, "IN_PROGRESS")
++            try:
++                self._import_head_locked(head, lease)
++            except BaseException:
++                if not lease.get("cleanup_uncertain"):
++                    try:
++                        self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++                    except OSError:
++                        # The durable IN_PROGRESS slot remains fail-closed.
++                        pass
++                raise
++            else:
++                self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++            if self._target_object_storage_bytes() > self._MAX_TARGET_OBJECT_STORAGE_BYTES:
++                raise StoreError(
++                    "synthetic target object storage cap was exceeded during pack import",
++                    kind="budget",
++                )
++
++    def _import_head_locked(self, head: str, lease: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
++        with self._source_object_snapshot(head) as (source_git_dir, source_env):
++            self._transfer_snapshot_head_locked(head, source_git_dir, source_env, lease)
++
++    def _transfer_snapshot_head_locked(
++        self, head: str, source_git_dir: str, source_env: dict[str, str],
++        lease: dict[str, Any],
++    ) -> None:
++        source_command = [
++            "git", "-c", "pack.threads=1", "-c", "pack.windowMemory=16m",
++            "-c", "pack.window=10", "-c", "pack.deltaCacheSize=16777216",
++            "-c", "pack.deltaCacheLimit=32768", "--git-dir", source_git_dir,
++            "pack-objects", "--stdout", "--revs",
++        ]
++        target_command = [
++            "git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "index-pack", "--strict", "--stdin",
++        ]
++        source = target = None
++        source_diagnostic = bytearray()
++        target_diagnostic = bytearray()
++        expired = threading.Event()
++        finished = threading.Event()
++
++        def drain(stream, output: bytearray) -> None:
++            while True:
++                chunk = stream.read(4096)
++                if not chunk:
++                    return
++                remaining = self._MAX_GIT_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES - len(output)
++                if remaining > 0:
++                    output.extend(chunk[:remaining])
++
++        def kill_after_timeout() -> None:
++            if finished.is_set():
++                return
++            expired.set()
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
++                    try:
++                        process.kill()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++
++        timer = threading.Timer(self.command_timeout_sec, kill_after_timeout)
++        source_stderr_thread = target_stderr_thread = None
++        cleanup_uncertain = False
++        try:
++            source = subprocess.Popen(
++                source_command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
++                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=source_env, bufsize=0,
++            )
++            target = subprocess.Popen(
++                target_command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
++                stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=self._target_git_env(), bufsize=0,
++            )
++            source_stderr_thread = threading.Thread(
++                target=drain, args=(source.stderr, source_diagnostic), daemon=True,
++            )
++            target_stderr_thread = threading.Thread(
++                target=drain, args=(target.stderr, target_diagnostic), daemon=True,
++            )
++            source_stderr_thread.start()
++            target_stderr_thread.start()
++            timer_start = time.monotonic()
++            timer.start()
++            source.stdin.write((head + "\n").encode("ascii"))
++            source.stdin.close()
++
++            total_bytes = 0
++            pack_header = bytearray()
++            while True:
++                chunk = source.stdout.read(64 * 1024)
++                if not chunk:
++                    break
++                total_bytes += len(chunk)
++                if total_bytes > self._MAX_PACK_BYTES:
++                    raise RuntimeError("Git source object pack exceeds the 64 MiB limit")
++                if len(pack_header) < 12:
++                    pack_header.extend(chunk[:12 - len(pack_header)])
++                    if len(pack_header) == 12:
++                        if pack_header[:4] != b"PACK":
++                            raise RuntimeError("Git source did not produce a valid pack header")
++                        object_count = int.from_bytes(pack_header[8:12], "big")
++                        if object_count > self._MAX_PACK_OBJECTS:
++                            raise RuntimeError("Git source object pack exceeds the object-count limit")
++                target.stdin.write(chunk)
++            if expired.is_set():
++                raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit")
++            if total_bytes == 0 or len(pack_header) < 12:
++                raise RuntimeError("Git source repository produced an empty or truncated object pack")
++            target.stdin.close()
++            deadline = timer_start + self.command_timeout_sec
++            source.wait(timeout=max(0.001, deadline - time.monotonic()))
++            target.wait(timeout=max(0.001, deadline - time.monotonic()))
++            if expired.is_set():
++                raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit")
++            if source.returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(source_diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            if target.returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(target_diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
++            raise TimeoutError("Git source pack import exceeded its time limit") from exc
++        finally:
++            finished.set()
++            timer.cancel()
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
++                    try:
++                        process.kill()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++            for process in (source, target):
++                if process is not None:
++                    try:
++                        process.wait(timeout=1)
++                    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
++                        try:
++                            process.kill()
++                        except OSError:
++                            pass
++                        try:
++                            process.wait(timeout=1)
++                        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
++                            cleanup_uncertain = True
++                    except OSError:
++                        cleanup_uncertain = True
++                    if process.returncode is None:
++                        cleanup_uncertain = True
++            for worker in (source_stderr_thread, target_stderr_thread):
++                if worker is not None:
++                    worker.join(timeout=1)
++            for stream in (
++                source.stdin if source else None, source.stdout if source else None,
++                source.stderr if source else None, target.stdin if target else None,
++                target.stderr if target else None,
++            ):
++                if stream is not None:
++                    try:
++                        stream.close()
++                    except OSError:
++                        pass
++            if cleanup_uncertain:
++                lease["cleanup_uncertain"] = True
++                try:
++                    self._write_storage_state(lease, "POISONED")
++                except OSError as poison_error:
++                    # The previously fsynced IN_PROGRESS slot remains valid and
++                    # blocks future writers even if this final marker write fails.
++                    raise RuntimeError(
++                        "Git child cleanup is unconfirmed; target remains IN_PROGRESS"
++                    ) from poison_error
++                raise RuntimeError("Git child cleanup is unconfirmed; target is poisoned")
++        self._git("cat-file", "-e", f"{head}^{{commit}}")
++
++    def _is_ancestor(self, ancestor: str, descendant: str) -> bool:
++        completed = subprocess.run(
++            ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", ancestor, descendant],
++            stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
++            check=False, timeout=self.command_timeout_sec,
++        )
++        if completed.returncode == 0:
++            return True
++        if completed.returncode == 1:
++            return False
++        raise RuntimeError(completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++
++    def _update_ref(self, ref: str, head: str, expected: str | None) -> None:
++        old_value = expected or ("0" * 40)
++        try:
++            self._git("update-ref", ref, head, old_value)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            try:
++                if self.ref_head(ref) == head:
++                    return
++            except RuntimeError:
++                pass
++            raise StoreError("bare target ref changed during synthetic publication", kind="duplicate")
++
++    def ref_head(self, ref: str) -> str:
++        return self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++
++    def _bind_operation(self, kind: str, operation_key: str, payload: dict) -> None:
++        with self._target_storage_lock() as lease:
++            self._bind_operation_locked(kind, operation_key, payload, lease)
++
++    def _bind_operation_locked(
++        self, kind: str, operation_key: str, payload: dict, lease: dict[str, Any],
++    ) -> None:
++        key_hash = hashlib.sha256(f"{kind}\0{operation_key}".encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
++        ref = f"refs/vst/idempotency/{key_hash}"
++        record = canonical_bytes({"kind": kind, "payload": payload})
++        try:
++            existing_oid = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            existing_oid = None
++        if existing_oid is not None:
++            existing, diagnostic, returncode = self._run_bounded_git(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "cat-file", "blob", existing_oid],
++                env=self._target_git_env(), output_limit=self._MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_RECORD_BYTES,
++            )
++            if returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(diagnostic.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            if existing != record:
++                raise StoreError("remote idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++            return
++        if len(record) > self._MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_RECORD_BYTES:
++            raise StoreError("synthetic idempotency record exceeds the 64 KiB limit", kind="budget")
++        self._reserve_target_object_storage(len(record) + (len(record) // 100) + 256)
++        self._write_storage_state(lease, "IN_PROGRESS")
++        try:
++            new_oid = self._git("hash-object", "-w", "--stdin", input_bytes=record)
++        except BaseException:
++            try:
++                self._write_storage_state(lease, "POISONED")
++            except OSError:
++                pass
++            raise
++        self._write_storage_state(lease, "HEALTHY")
++        try:
++            self._git("update-ref", ref, new_oid, "0" * 40)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            # Another supervisor process may have won the create-only ref race.
++            raced_oid = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++            raced = subprocess.run(
++                ["git", "--git-dir", self.bare_path, "cat-file", "blob", raced_oid],
++                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
++                check=True, timeout=self.command_timeout_sec,
++            ).stdout
++            if raced != record:
++                raise StoreError("remote idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++
++    def push(self, payload: dict, *, operation_key: str) -> dict:
++        branch, head = payload["branch"], payload["head"]
++        if not isinstance(branch, str) or not branch.replace("-", "").replace("_", "").isalnum():
++            raise ValueError("invalid synthetic branch")
++        if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 40 or any(ch not in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in head):
++            raise ValueError("candidate head must be a 40-character git id")
++        self._bind_operation("push", operation_key, payload)
++        ref = f"refs/heads/{branch}"
++        try:
++            current = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            current = None
++        if current != head:
++            self._import_head(head)
++            if current is not None and not self._is_ancestor(current, head):
++                raise StoreError("synthetic branch update is not a fast-forward", kind="duplicate")
++            self._update_ref(ref, head, current)
++        return {"operation_key": operation_key, "ref": ref, "head": head}
++
++    def open_pull_request(self, payload: dict, *, operation_key: str) -> dict:
++        head = payload["head"]
++        if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 40 or any(ch not in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in head):
++            raise ValueError("pull-request head must be a 40-character git id")
++        self._bind_operation("pull_request", operation_key, payload)
++        pr_key = hashlib.sha256(operation_key.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
++        ref = f"refs/pull-requests/{pr_key}/head"
++        try:
++            current = self._git("rev-parse", "--verify", ref)
++        except RuntimeError:
++            current = None
++        if current is not None and current != head:
++            raise StoreError("pull-request key already points at a different head", kind="duplicate")
++        if current is None:
++            self._import_head(head)
++            self._update_ref(ref, head, None)
++        return {"operation_key": operation_key, "ref": ref, "head": head}
++

++class HandWrittenWorker:
++    """Minimal synthetic worker with scoped edits and no remote/push API."""
++
++    def __init__(self, repository: str, allowed_paths: tuple[str, ...] = ("src/synthetic.py",)):
++        self.repository = os.path.realpath(repository)
++        self.allowed_paths = frozenset(allowed_paths)
++
++    def _run(
++        self, action: str, path: str, content: str = "", timeout_sec: float | None = None,
++    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
++        worker_code = r'''import os, subprocess, sys
++repo, action, rel, content, timeout_text = sys.argv[1:6]
++timeout = float(timeout_text) if timeout_text else None
++if rel.startswith(("/", "\\")) or ".." in rel.replace("\\", "/").split("/"):
++    raise SystemExit(30)
++root = os.path.realpath(repo)
++target = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(root, rel))
++if os.path.commonpath((root, target)) != root:
++    raise SystemExit(31)
++if action in ("edit", "crash"):
++    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
++    with open(target, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as stream:
++        stream.write(content if action == "edit" else "# partial synthetic edit\n")
++        stream.flush()
++        os.fsync(stream.fileno())
++    if action == "crash":
++        os._exit(97)
++elif action == "commit":
++    subprocess.run(["git", "add", "--", rel], cwd=root, check=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=timeout)
++    subprocess.run(["git", "commit", "-m", content], cwd=root, check=True, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, timeout=timeout)
++    print(subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "--verify", "HEAD"], cwd=root, text=True, timeout=timeout).strip())
++else:
++    raise SystemExit(32)
++'''
++        return subprocess.run(
++            [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", worker_code, self.repository, action, path, content,
++             "" if timeout_sec is None else str(timeout_sec)],
++            cwd=self.repository, env=build_environment(), stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
++            stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, check=False, timeout=timeout_sec,
++        )
++
++    def edit(self, path: str, content: str, *, timeout_sec: float | None = None) -> None:
++        if path not in self.allowed_paths or path.startswith(("/", "\\")) or ".." in path.split("/"):
++            raise ValueError("worker edit is outside the declared synthetic scope")
++        completed = self._run("edit", path, content, timeout_sec)
++        if completed.returncode:
++            raise RuntimeError(completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++
++    def crash_mid_edit(self, path: str = "src/synthetic.py") -> None:
++        if path not in self.allowed_paths:
++            raise ValueError("worker edit is outside the declared synthetic scope")
++        completed = self._run("crash", path)
++        if completed.returncode != 97:
++            raise RuntimeError(completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++        raise RuntimeError("synthetic worker killed during edit")
++
++    def commit_candidate(
++        self, message: str = "synthetic candidate", *, timeout_sec: float | None = None,
++    ) -> str:
++        heads = []
++        for path in sorted(self.allowed_paths):
++            completed = self._run("commit", path, message, timeout_sec)
++            if completed.returncode:
++                raise RuntimeError(completed.stderr.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
++            heads.append(completed.stdout.decode("ascii").strip())
++        return heads[-1]
++

++    def git(cwd: str, *args: str) -> str:

++    subprocess.run(["git", "init", "--bare", remote], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)

++    subprocess.run(["git", "init", repository], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)

++    def execute_idempotent(
++        self, operation_key: str, operation: str, payload: Any, effect: Callable[[], Any]
++    ) -> Any:
++        """Run an internal Store effect atomically with its idempotency record.
++
++        The callback executes under the SQLite transaction and anchor lock. Do not
++        pass a backend, process, network, or other external side effect here.
++        """
++        _need_str(operation_key, "operation_key")
++        _need_str(operation, "operation")
++        payload_digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(payload)).hexdigest()

++                (operation_key,),
++            ).fetchone()

++                if row["operation"] != operation or row["payload_sha256"] != payload_digest:
++                    raise StoreError("idempotency key reused with different operation or payload", kind="duplicate")

++                encoded = canonical_bytes(result).decode("utf-8")
++            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
++                raise StoreError("supervisor operation result is not canonical JSON", kind="argument") from exc
++            conn.execute(
++                "INSERT INTO supervisor_operations(operation_key, operation, payload_sha256, result) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
++                (operation_key, operation, payload_digest, encoded),
++            )
++            self._record_event_locked(
++                conn, operation_key, "supervisor", "NOTE",
++                {
++                    "event": "SUPERVISOR_OPERATION", "operation": operation,
++                    "payload_sha256": payload_digest,
++                    "result_sha256": hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
++                },
++            )
++            return result

++    def lookup_idempotent_operation(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,
++        *,
++        operation: str | None = None,
++        payload: Any = None,
++        check_payload: bool = False,
++    ) -> dict | None:

++
++        Supplying ``operation`` and setting ``check_payload`` binds the lookup to

++                (operation_key,),

++                return None
++            if operation is not None and row["operation"] != operation:
++                raise StoreError("idempotency key reused for a different operation", kind="duplicate")
++            if expected_digest is not None and row["payload_sha256"] != expected_digest:
++                raise StoreError("idempotency key reused with different payload", kind="duplicate")
++            try:
++                stored_result = json.loads(row["result"])
++            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
++                raise StoreError("stored idempotent operation result is invalid", kind="integrity") from exc

++            if row["result"] != canonical_bytes(pending).decode("utf-8"):

++                    "operation": row["operation"],
++                    "payload_sha256": row["payload_sha256"],
++                    "state": "COMPLETED",

++            completed = None
++            inconclusive = False
++            error_types: list[str] = []
++            rows = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND actor = 'supervisor' AND kind = 'NOTE' ORDER BY seq",
++                (operation_key,),

++                except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
++                    raise StoreError("stored operation event is invalid", kind="integrity") from exc
++                if event.get("operation_key") != operation_key:

++                    if (event.get("operation") != row["operation"]

++                        raise StoreError("external operation uncertainty binding is invalid", kind="integrity")

++                        raise StoreError("external operation result digest is invalid", kind="integrity")
++                    if completed is not None and canonical_bytes(completed) != canonical_bytes(result):
++                        raise StoreError("external operation has conflicting completion records", kind="integrity")
++                    completed = result

++                return {
++                    "operation": row["operation"],

++    def charge_idempotent(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,
++        task_id: str,
++        amount: int,
++        *,
++        supervisor_key: bytes,
++        runner_id: str = SUPERVISOR_RUNNER_ID,
++        expected_cap: int | None = None,
++        expected_spent: int | None = None,
++    ) -> int:
++        """Charge budget once for an exact key/payload, preserving cap markers.
++
++        A repeated identical request returns its original remaining balance. A
++        reused key with different task, amount, or runner is rejected. An
++        over-cap first attempt atomically records the existing signed budget
++        markers and a durable blocked result; replay raises the same budget
++        error without charging or appending another marker.
++        """
++        _need_str(operation_key, "operation_key")
++        _need_str(task_id, "task_id")
++        _need_int(amount, "amount", 0, MAX_BUDGET)
++        sup_key = self._need_supervisor_key(supervisor_key)
++        _need_str(runner_id, "runner_id")
++        if expected_cap is not None:
++            _need_int(expected_cap, "expected_cap", 0, MAX_BUDGET)
++        if expected_spent is not None:
++            _need_int(expected_spent, "expected_spent", 0, MAX_BUDGET)
++        payload = {
++            "task_id": task_id, "amount": amount, "runner_id": runner_id,
++            "expected_cap": expected_cap, "expected_spent": expected_spent,
++        }
++
++        def charge(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
++            task = self._task_row(conn, task_id)
++            row = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT cap, spent FROM budget WHERE task_id = ?", (task_id,)
++            ).fetchone()
++            if row is None:
++                raise StoreError(f"no budget set for task {task_id!r}", kind="budget")
++            if ((expected_cap is not None and row["cap"] != expected_cap)
++                    or (expected_spent is not None and row["spent"] != expected_spent)):
++                raise StoreError(
++                    "caller budget snapshot differs from the authoritative ledger",
++                    kind="budget_snapshot",
++                )
++            if row["spent"] + amount > row["cap"]:
++                self._budget_exceeded_locked(conn, task, sup_key, runner_id, amount)
++                return {"state": "BLOCKED", "remaining": row["cap"] - row["spent"]}
++            conn.execute(
++                "UPDATE budget SET spent = spent + ? WHERE task_id = ?", (amount, task_id)
++            )
++            return {"state": "COMPLETED", "remaining": row["cap"] - row["spent"] - amount}
++
++        result = self.execute_idempotent(
++            operation_key, "budget_charge", payload, charge
++        )
++        if not isinstance(result, dict) or result.get("state") not in {"BLOCKED", "COMPLETED"}:
++            raise StoreError("stored idempotent budget result is invalid", kind="integrity")
++        if result["state"] == "BLOCKED":
++            raise StoreError(f"budget exceeded for task {task_id!r}", kind="budget")
++        remaining = result.get("remaining")
++        if isinstance(remaining, bool) or not isinstance(remaining, int):
++            raise StoreError("stored idempotent budget balance is invalid", kind="integrity")
++        return remaining

++    def stop_attempt_fenced(
++        self,
++        operation_key: str,
++        task_id: str,
++        story_id: str,
++        attempt: int,
++        expected_epoch: int,
++        expected_owner: str,
++        reason: str,
++        authorized_actor: str,
++        binding: dict | None = None,
++    ) -> dict:
++        """Durably STOP an attempt and atomically advance its story fence.
++
++        The old live lease, if present, is fenced in the same transaction as the
++        epoch advance and idempotency record. This prevents old-epoch receipts
++        from being accepted. It does not terminate an operating-system process;
++        the result is always INCONCLUSIVE until a separate safe cleanup proof
++        exists. Replaying an identical stop key/payload returns the prior result
++        without advancing the epoch again. ``authorized_actor`` is recorded as
++        audit identity; this method does not authenticate that identity.
++        """
++        for value, name in (
++            (operation_key, "operation_key"), (task_id, "task_id"),
++            (story_id, "story_id"), (expected_owner, "expected_owner"),
++            (authorized_actor, "authorized_actor"),
++        ):
++            _need_str(value, name)
++        if not isinstance(reason, str) or not reason.strip() or len(reason) > 512:
++            raise StoreError("stop reason must contain 1..512 characters", kind="argument")
++        if not self.reconciliation_complete:
++            raise StoreError("startup reconciliation must complete before STOP", kind="integrity")
++        if binding is not None and not isinstance(binding, dict):
++            raise StoreError("stop binding must be an object", kind="argument")
++        _need_int(attempt, "attempt", 1)
++        _need_int(expected_epoch, "expected_epoch", 1)
++        payload = {
++            "task_id": task_id, "story_id": story_id, "attempt": attempt,
++            "expected_epoch": expected_epoch, "expected_owner": expected_owner,
++            "reason": reason, "authorized_actor": authorized_actor,
++            "binding": binding or {},
++        }
++
++        def stop(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> dict:
++            story = self._story_row(conn, story_id)
++            task = self._task_row(conn, task_id)
++            if task["story_id"] != story_id:
++                raise StoreError("stop task does not belong to the specified story", kind="story")
++            if int(story["epoch"]) != expected_epoch:
++                raise StoreError("stop request has a stale epoch fence", kind="epoch")
++            if story["owner"] != expected_owner:
++                raise StoreError("stop request does not hold current story ownership", kind="epoch")
++            new_epoch = expected_epoch + 1
++            if new_epoch > MAX_COUNTER:
++                raise StoreError("epoch counter exhausted", kind="epoch")
++            lease = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT lease_id, epoch, status FROM leases WHERE task_id = ? AND attempt = ?",
++                (task_id, attempt),
++            ).fetchone()
++            if lease is not None and int(lease["epoch"]) != expected_epoch:
++                raise StoreError("stop attempt lease belongs to a different epoch", kind="epoch")
++            conn.execute(
++                "UPDATE stories SET epoch = ?, owner = NULL, owner_expires_at = NULL, state = 'OPEN' "
++                "WHERE story_id = ? AND epoch = ? AND owner = ?",
++                (new_epoch, story_id, expected_epoch, expected_owner),
++            )
++            if conn.execute("SELECT changes()").fetchone()[0] != 1:
++                raise StoreError("stop lost the story epoch compare-and-swap", kind="epoch")
++            fenced = False
++            if lease is not None and lease["status"] == LEASE_LIVE:
++                conn.execute(

++    def execute_external_idempotent(
++        self, operation_key: str, operation: str, payload: Any, effect: Callable[[], Any]
++    ) -> Any:

++
++        The append-only operation row is the durable intent. Completion is a
++        separate hash-chained event, so a crash leaves an observable pending
++        operation. Retrying the same key/payload is safe only when the backend
++        also durably enforces that idempotency key.

++        _need_str(operation, "operation")

++        completion_event = "SUPERVISOR_EXTERNAL_OPERATION_COMPLETED"
++        pending = {"_vst_state": "PENDING"}
++        no_completion = object()

++        def completion_locked(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> Any:
++            rows = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT payload FROM events WHERE task_id = ? AND actor = 'supervisor' AND kind = 'NOTE' ORDER BY seq",
++                (operation_key,),

++                try:
++                    event = json.loads(row["payload"])
++                except (TypeError, ValueError):

++                if event.get("event") != completion_event:
++                    continue
++                if (event.get("operation") != operation
++                        or event.get("payload_sha256") != payload_digest
++                        or event.get("operation_key") != operation_key):
++                    raise StoreError("external operation completion binding is invalid", kind="integrity")
++                result = event.get("result")
++                encoded = canonical_bytes(result).decode("utf-8")
++                if hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest() != event.get("result_sha256"):
++                    raise StoreError("external operation result digest is invalid", kind="integrity")
++                if completed is not no_completion and canonical_bytes(completed) != canonical_bytes(result):
++                    raise StoreError("external operation produced conflicting completed results", kind="integrity")
++                completed = result
++            return completed
++
++        with self._tx() as conn:
++            row = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT operation, payload_sha256, result FROM supervisor_operations WHERE operation_key = ?",
++                (operation_key,),
++            ).fetchone()
++            if row is not None:
++                if row["operation"] != operation or row["payload_sha256"] != payload_digest:
++                    raise StoreError("idempotency key reused with different operation or payload", kind="duplicate")
++                if row["result"] != canonical_bytes(pending).decode("utf-8"):
++                    # Results committed by the pre-intent implementation remain
++                    # readable and idempotent across the transition.
++                    return json.loads(row["result"])

++                if result is not no_completion:
++                    return result

++                    "INSERT INTO supervisor_operations(operation_key, operation, payload_sha256, result) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",

++                (operation_key,),

++                try:

++                except (TypeError, ValueError):
++                    continue
++                if prior.get("event") == intent_event:
++                    attempts = max(attempts, int(prior.get("attempt", 0)) + 1)
++            self._record_event_locked(
++                conn, operation_key, "supervisor", "NOTE",
++                {"event": intent_event, "operation_key": operation_key,
++                 "operation": operation, "payload_sha256": payload_digest,
++                 "state": "PENDING", "attempt": attempts},
++            )
++
++        try:
++            result = effect()
++            encoded = canonical_bytes(result).decode("utf-8")
++        except BaseException as exc:
++            with self._tx() as conn:
++                self._record_event_locked(
++                    conn, operation_key, "supervisor", "NOTE",
++                    {"event": "SUPERVISOR_EXTERNAL_OPERATION_UNKNOWN",

++                     "payload_sha256": payload_digest, "attempt": attempts,
++                     "error_type": type(exc).__name__},
++                )
++            raise
++
++        result_digest = hashlib.sha256(encoded.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
++        with self._tx() as conn:
++            row = conn.execute(
++                "SELECT operation, payload_sha256 FROM supervisor_operations WHERE operation_key = ?",
++                (operation_key,),
++            ).fetchone()
++            if (row is None or row["operation"] != operation
++                    or row["payload_sha256"] != payload_digest):
++                raise StoreError("external operation intent changed before completion", kind="integrity")
++            prior_result = completion_locked(conn)
++            if prior_result is not no_completion:
++                if canonical_bytes(prior_result) != canonical_bytes(result):
++                    raise StoreError("external operation retry returned a conflicting result", kind="integrity")
++                return prior_result
++            self._record_event_locked(
++                conn, operation_key, "supervisor", "NOTE",
++                {"event": completion_event, "operation_key": operation_key,
++                 "operation": operation, "payload_sha256": payload_digest,

++            raise StoreError("probe nonce must be fresh and non-empty", kind="probe")

++        self._seen_run_ids.add(run_id)
++        self._seen_probe_nonces.add(nonce)

++            self._control_history = self.store.control_events(); self._replay_controls()

++        self.store._append_control_event("CONTROL_PROVIDER_FAILURE", outcome_id or str(uuid.uuid4()), {})
++        self._control_history = self.store.control_events(); self._replay_controls()

++    def manual_override(self, record: dict) -> None:
++        """Resume the paused provider only with a distinct operator record."""
++        if not isinstance(record, dict) or not record or "verdict" not in record:
++            raise StoreError("manual override requires a distinct signed/identified record", kind="provider")
++        try:
++            canonical_bytes(record)
++        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
++            raise StoreError("manual override record must be canonical JSON", kind="provider") from exc
++        required = {
++            "id", "action", "breaker_state", "breaker_episode_id",
++            "breaker_config_id", "verdict", "evidence_sha256", "signature",

++        if set(record) != required or record.get("action") != "manual_override" or record.get("breaker_state") != "PAUSED_PROVIDER":
++            raise StoreError("manual override signature must bind action and paused breaker state", kind="provider")
++        if not isinstance(record.get("verdict"), str) or record.get("verdict").upper() == "APPROVE":
++            raise StoreError("manual override cannot be represented as plain APPROVE", kind="provider")
++        override_id = record.get("id")
++        if not isinstance(override_id, str) or not override_id.strip():
++            raise StoreError("manual override requires a stable record id", kind="provider")
++        if not _valid_sha256(record.get("evidence_sha256")):

++        if not isinstance(self.operator_key, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(self.operator_key) < 32:
++            raise StoreError("trusted operator key is unavailable for manual override", kind="provider")
++        if not verify(record, bytes(self.operator_key), OPERATOR_MANUAL_OVERRIDE_LABEL):
++            raise StoreError("manual override operator signature is invalid", kind="provider")
++        if self.manual_override_recorder is None:
++            raise StoreError("manual override record sink is unavailable", kind="provider")

++            raise StoreError(

++                kind="duplicate",

++        self.store.append_manual_override(record, operator_key=bytes(self.operator_key))
++        self._control_history = self.store.control_events(); self._replay_controls()

++    def stop(self, terminate: Callable[[], None], cleanup: Callable[[], None], *, action_id: str | None = None) -> None:
++        if self.lifecycle_state == "BLOCKED_RECOVERY": raise StoreError("unresolved lifecycle action requires reconciliation", kind="lifecycle")
++        base = action_id or (self.lifecycle_action_id if self.lifecycle_state == "STOPPING" else None) or str(uuid.uuid4())
++        if self.lifecycle_state == "RUNNING":

++            self.lifecycle_state = next_state

++                if self.lifecycle_state != "BLOCKED_RECOVERY":
++                    self.lifecycle_state = previous_state
++                raise
++        elif self.lifecycle_state != "STOPPING":

++        self._perform("stop_cleanup", cleanup, base + ":cleanup", group_id=base)
++        self.lifecycle_state = final_state
++        self.lifecycle_action_id = None

++    def rollback(self, rollback_effect: Callable[[], None], cleanup: Callable[[], None], *, action_id: str | None = None) -> None:
++        if self.lifecycle_state == "BLOCKED_RECOVERY": raise StoreError("unresolved lifecycle action requires reconciliation", kind="lifecycle")
++        base = action_id or (self.lifecycle_action_id if self.lifecycle_state == "ROLLING_BACK" else None) or str(uuid.uuid4())
++        if self.lifecycle_state == "RUNNING":
++            previous_state = self.lifecycle_state
++            next_state, _ = transition(self.lifecycle_state, "ROLLBACK")
++            self.lifecycle_state = next_state
++            try:
++                self._perform("rollback_effect", rollback_effect, base + ":effect", group_id=base)
++            except BaseException:
++                if self.lifecycle_state != "BLOCKED_RECOVERY":
++                    self.lifecycle_state = previous_state
++                raise
++        elif self.lifecycle_state != "ROLLING_BACK":
++            raise StoreError("rollback can continue only from RUNNING or ROLLING_BACK", kind="lifecycle")
++        final_state, _ = transition(self.lifecycle_state, "CLEANUP_COMPLETE")
++        self._perform("rollback_cleanup", cleanup, base + ":cleanup", group_id=base)
++        self.lifecycle_state = final_state
++        self.lifecycle_action_id = None

++    def resume(self, increment_epoch: Callable[[], Any], *, action_id: str | None = None) -> Any:
++        if self.lifecycle_state == "BLOCKED_RECOVERY": raise StoreError("unresolved lifecycle action requires reconciliation", kind="lifecycle")
++        next_state, _ = transition(self.lifecycle_state, "RESUME")
++        epoch = self._perform("resume", increment_epoch, action_id)
++        self.lifecycle_state = next_state
++        return epoch

++    def _simulate(
++        self, kind: str, idempotency_key: str, payload: dict,
++        effect: Callable[[], Any],
++    ) -> Any:
++        if kind not in {"push", "pull_request", "receipt"}:
++            raise StoreError("unsupported supervisor operation", kind="argument")
++        # Bind the operation payload to both caller intent and the repository
++        # object identity; no corresponding method exists on a worker object.
++        binding = {"kind": kind, "payload": payload, "payload_sha256": hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(payload)).hexdigest()}
++        return self.store.execute_external_idempotent(idempotency_key, kind, binding, effect)
++
++    def simulate_push(self, idempotency_key: str, payload: dict) -> Any:

++            lambda: self.backend.push(payload, operation_key=idempotency_key),

+2. Критические интеграционные условия
+
+Следующие требования обязательны для реализации. Их пропуск создаст SOURCE MAJOR.
+
+I01-SRC-01 — Grant provenance binding
+
+Существующий Supervisor.issue_execution_grant() создаёт собственные случайные request_id, grant_id и invocation_id. Поэтому нельзя считать совпадение task/slot/attempt достаточным доказательством происхождения grant.
+
+Реализация обязана:
+
+Связать точные подписанные grant bytes с immutable dispatch_grant operation.
+
+Связать эту операцию с исходным accepted dispatch request и завершённой issuance.
+
+Проверять эту связь при persistence, exact replay, runner claim и reservation.
+
+Отказывать при отсутствии или несоответствии связи.
+
+Существующий wire format execution grant сохраняется.
+
+I01-SRC-02 — Atomic admission and replay
+
+В текущем Store.accept_dispatch_intent() ветка существующей idempotent operation возвращает результат раньше проверок live task/lease.
+
+Для delegated v1 обе ветки — новая acceptance и exact replay — должны соблюдать исправленный контракт. Historical replay может возвращать сохранённый факт, но не создавать новую execution authority.
+
+I01-SRC-03 — Verified journal integration
+
+Текущий _verify_supervisor_records() поддерживает generic internal/external operation families.
+
+Новая issuance family требует самостоятельной полной корреляции row/event и проверки:
+
+Единственности INTENT и STARTED.
+
+Допустимого порядка событий.
+
+Неизменности payload и signer identity.
+
+Единственного действительного completion.
+
+Отсутствия смешивания protocol families.
+
+Целостности event chain и anchor.
+
+Cryptographic verification выполняется вне SQL. В транзакцию допускается только trusted context, связанный с точными immutable bytes и fingerprint.
+
+I01-SRC-04 — Snapshot and current authority
+
+Использовать единую connection-taking predicate и повторять её непосредственно на write boundaries. Результат предшествующего read-only вызова не считается разрешением на grant или execution.
+
+Root policy, revocation, generation и key registry должны проверяться через доверенные root-owned providers. При невозможности установить их актуальность операция отказывается.
+
+I01-SRC-05 — Crash-consistent signing
+
+Нельзя использовать execute_external_idempotent() для этой операции. После committed STARTED допускается максимум один вызов OpenSSL для immutable operation identity.
+
+Потерянный completion означает UNKNOWN, а не повторное подписание.

+# S2 delegated machine authority adjudication — 2026-10-29
+
+Owner: Codex (coordination); GPT-PM (architecture adjudication).
+Request: `a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55`; job: `be44cabb-4181-4458-ade7-a8b8e89b2a5d`; correlated reply: `0b0b8a4d-0816-4146-ba21-71857b5de49d`.
+Transport lifecycle: `uncertain`; result.correlated: `true`. The parked client deadline expired, but the persisted job contains the correlated harvested reply below. This is an architecture decision, not exact-head approval or runtime evidence.
+
+## Exact harvested reply
+
+ChatGPT said:
+
+REQUEST_ID: a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55
+
+S2 — Delegated Machine Issuer & E5 Attestor Architecture Review
+MODIFY — DESIGN ONLY
+MACHINE DELEGATION PERMISSIBLE
+2 MAJOR OPEN
+
+Project: Virtual_scrum_team
+Declared committed source: 9c1be0f
+Scope: Two proposed machine trust roles, their authority and the conditions for replacing human-produced signing artifacts.
+Excluded: Provisioning, key creation, runtime activation, production dispatch and E5 approval.
+
+1. Architecture decision
+
+A purpose-specific delegated-machine issuer and a separate machine policy attestor are acceptable architectural directions. Neither must be represented as another human user.
+
+The sole human operator can delegate bounded, repeatable machine operations. The design must distinguish three different facts:
+
+Delegation: The operator authorizes the machine role to perform a particular class of operation.
+
+Evidence: The machine actually measures or verifies the conditions required by that operation.
+
+Attestation: A specifically authorized cryptographic identity signs the measured evidence.
+
+These are not interchangeable. A signature from a machine key proves that the corresponding key signed a record; it does not independently prove that the measurements are true or that the operator personally approved that run.
+
+My ruling is therefore MODIFY, not REJECT. The proposed roles fit the accepted architecture, but two missing trust-boundary invariants must be resolved before authorizing implementation of either privileged signing service.
+
+Crucially, the current human-attestation contract remains mandatory until a separately accepted contract version explicitly replaces it. Broad autonomous GO does not itself change the meaning of an operator signature.
+

+Both findings concern the proposed architecture. They do not reopen accepted transport, Store history or Runner fencing code.
+
+MAJOR 1 — Machine issuer must not become an assignment authority
+
+Affected boundary: Proposed machine issuer → dispatch_instruction.py → owner relay → authenticated Supervisor → Store.
+
+The existing signed-instruction contract binds the task, slot, attempt, epoch, run ID, request ID, key ID and expiry. It verifies a purpose-specific Ed25519 signature against a trusted public key mapped to a principal. 
+dispatch_instruction.py
+
+That proves the envelope's cryptographic provenance. It does not independently establish that its signer was entitled to select that particular work.
+
+A machine service with unrestricted signing access could generate valid envelopes for arbitrary task identifiers. The current Store would reject work lacking valid ownership or leases, but the machine issuer would still possess a broader instruction-selection capability than the proposed model allows.
+
+Required invariant: The issuer signs only a single, already-authorized, immutable work identity obtained through a trusted and separately bounded request-provenance mechanism. The signer must not be able to turn arbitrary caller-provided task IDs into authorization merely because Store currently considers the work eligible.
+
+The minimum acceptable implementation contract is:
+
+Authenticate the requesting service identity through a fixed UID/GID/cgroup and kernel-authenticated AF_UNIX boundary.
+
+Obtain the exact assignment tuple from a verified Store/Supervisor authority record, with no task enumeration or free-form task selection.
+
+Bind the tuple to the approved project, manifest digest, owner principal Codex, attempt, epoch, lease identity, run ID, policy revision and signing-key purpose.
+
+Restrict the issuer to one exact issuance per unique authorization identity; repeated identical requests return the same signed envelope, not a newly minted request ID or expiry.
+
+Reject changed assignment, stale generation, expired authority, unavailable Store provenance or unresolved signing history.
+
+Keep the private key inaccessible to owner relay, dispatcher, Runner and worker.
+
+Record issuance provenance durably without adding another task/lease/assignment authority.
+
+Preserve independent Supervisor signature verification and all existing Store admission checks.
+
+The existing instruction v1 envelope does not carry every proposed provenance field. The design must specify whether those fields are verified through an immutable external authorization record or require a separately versioned signed-envelope contract. They cannot simply be assumed to be cryptographically bound.
+
+Closure evidence: Exact issuance-source contract, authenticated caller mapping, immutable issuance/idempotency mechanism, complete input-to-envelope mapping and tests proving that a caller cannot request an unauthorized task, change an issued tuple or obtain new authority by retrying.
+
+A machine issuer is acceptable. A general-purpose signing endpoint is not.
+
+MAJOR 2 — Machine E5 attestation must prove measurement provenance
+
+Affected boundary: Host/WSL observations → machine attestor → preflight record → root Supervisor E5 verification.
+
+The current preflight.py implements:
+
+A runner-signed probe inventory.
+
+A separate operator-key-signed network-policy attestation.
+
+Verification against the expected run ID, nonce, sandbox-spec digest and required policy fields.
+
+The network-policy attestation fields currently include environment_id, policy_sha256, evidence_sha256, empty_external_allowlist, no_container_socket and no_unapproved_host_paths. Its verifier requires those three boolean policy claims to be true and validates the operator-key signature. 
+preflight.py
+
+The current external_egress_blocked probe is explicitly a single reserved-target smoke test; the source does not claim that it proves comprehensive egress policy. 
+preflight.py
+ 
+preflight.py
+
+Replacing the human-attestation signer with a machine signer without changing the evidence architecture would preserve the same fundamental limitation: a machine could sign asserted policy booleans without proving the actual Windows host and WSL restrictions.
+
+Required invariant: A machine attestation may be accepted only when the signer is cryptographically bound to fresh, complete observations gathered through explicitly identified, independently trusted measurement sources and a separately approved policy evaluation.
+
+In particular, the machine must not be able to construct its own favorable measurements and then independently certify them as valid.
+

+4. Can the human-produced E5 artifact be replaced?
+
+Yes, by an explicitly approved new contract—no inherent technical requirement forces every future E5 record to be manually signed by a human.

+
+The existing human-attestation verifier remains unchanged until the new version has independently passed source review, security review, synthetic tests and its separate activation gate.
+
+Operator authorization interpretation
+
+The repeated GO and express delegation support Codex designing and implementing a bounded machine-assisted workflow.
+
+They do not establish the exact authority policy for a new machine principal to issue production dispatch instructions or certify host security, particularly when that delegation changes an existing gate's trust model.
+
+For a future production delegation, there must be a concrete operator-authorized policy identifying the machine principal, its specific powers, source of authority, scope, validity and revocation. That record may be prepared by Codex, but it cannot be silently self-approved or presented as a human-signed record.

+This is a specific security-authority boundary, not a request to find another person.

+# S2 signed dispatch-instruction provenance adjudication — 2026-10-29
+
+## Correlation and scope
+
+- GPT-PM request: `7c64c79c-452c-454f-9c55-3143a0fe2976`
+- PM Bridge job: `65d31f0e-ba68-411a-8d9a-aeaa5d6c1f0d`
+- User turn: `820712a7-3927-4abd-b115-8755623ac987`
+- Correlated reply: `4c5606a1-6026-56e3-914b-61c89a7e45a9`
+- Declared source baseline: `0dac9d58a3dd5bf779e1a2908a1ff2929ef5e69f`
+- Verdict: `MODIFY — OPTION A WITH SUPERVISOR VERIFICATION`
+
+The decision authorizes source work only for the trusted dispatch-instruction verifier. It retains
+`S2-DISPATCH-M01` as `MAJOR / OPEN`, full S2 as `NOT APPROVED`, and S3 as blocked. GPT-PM reviewed
+the supplied files and previously established S2 contracts; it did not independently fetch the
+declared Git HEAD, run tests, or modify this repository.
+
+## Binding contract
+
+An explicit signed instruction can establish provenance for one exact dispatch request without
+creating a second assignment authority. The Store remains the sole task, assignment, and lease
+authority. The signer can authorize only an exact request for already-assigned work; it cannot
+create tasks, assignments, leases, or execution grants.
+
+The signed envelope binds the exact fields:
+
+`version`, `algorithm`, `purpose`, `request_id`, `task_id`, `slot`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `run_id`,
+`key_id`, `expires_at`, and `signature`.
+
+The six dispatch identifiers plus key ID and absolute UTC expiry must be included in a canonical,
+domain-separated Ed25519 signature. The issuer supplies a unique 32-character lowercase
+hexadecimal `request_id`; the client must preserve it on replay. No unsigned field may change
+authorization meaning. Principal, UID/GID, worker, command, model, artifact path, Store/config path,
+grant, or lease mutation instructions are prohibited from the envelope.
+
+The root Supervisor must independently verify the exact schema, version, algorithm, signature,
+domain/purpose, pinned key, principal mapping, expiry, key revocation/trust, request identity,
+current Store owner and lease, epoch, attempt, manifest slot, run-bound preflight, budget, and
+service generation before appending `DISPATCH_INTENT_ACCEPTED`. Client verification alone is not
+sufficient. Missing/unavailable trust configuration and malformed signatures fail closed; no
+unsigned compatibility path is allowed. The exact signed envelope and key identity must be bound
+to the hash-chained event and durable idempotency record: identical request ID plus identical
+envelope may resolve to the same outcome; the same ID with different bytes is refused.
+
+Trust is purpose-separated. The client has no signing authority. The instruction private key
+belongs to an independently authorized issuer; the public verification key belongs in a
+root-controlled Supervisor registry mapping key ID to principal and purpose. It must not be reused
+for E5 attestation, execution grants, Store event integrity, receipts, or reconciliation.
+
+## Authorized and prohibited work
+
+Authorized source work:
+
+- Strict typed signed-envelope parsing and verification.
+- Purpose-specific Ed25519 verification against a pinned public-key registry.
+- Expiry, revocation, principal binding, exact-envelope replay protection, and Supervisor-side
+  verification.
+- Tests with synthetic signing fixtures, explicitly identified as non-production test keys.
+- Keep submission fail-closed until real trusted issuer configuration exists.
+
+Not authorized:
+
+- Creating or reusing an instruction-signing private key or inventing an authorized signer.
+- Account creation, root configuration installation, migration application, runtime installation,
+  service activation, real dispatch, network-policy claims, or E5 operator attestation.
+- Adding a scheduler, task/assignment/lease authority, task enumeration/selection, queue/spool, or
+  grant-signing path.
+
+The decision explicitly requires `M01 MAJOR / OPEN` until implementation, independent source and
+security review, an actually authorized issuer and pinned public key, OS identity/service boundary,
+Store admission, Pub/Sub delivery, one-use grant/Runner integration, replay/revocation/generation
+evidence, authorized runtime acceptance, and the exact-head GPT-PM gate are evidenced. Source
+authorization is not runtime authorization or acceptance.
+
+## Next steps and owners
+
+1. Codex implements the envelope verifier and Supervisor enforcement while preserving the
+   fail-closed default.
+2. `functional-test-reviewer` authors and executes the acceptance cases after source coding is
+   complete; GPT-6 Luna is the required/default model for that test role.
+3. Codex coordinates exact-scope architecture/security review; GPT-PM reviews the exact resulting
+   source and trust-registry contract.
+4. The operator owns any separate decision to establish a real instruction issuer/private key or
+   authorize privileged runtime provisioning. No signer/key exists in current evidence, and no
+   secret is requested in chat.
+
+`S2-DISPATCH-M01` and full S2 remain open until all applicable source, runtime, and gate evidence
+is complete.
