+# S2 persistent runner service design and implementation record
+
+Date: 2026-10-27  
+Repository: `D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`  
+Observed documentation HEAD before this note: `2da827be982d3f2d6f2adf152668af6ff8007f21`  
+Status: source implementation is present in the canonical checkout working tree; it has not been
+tested, provisioned, runtime-proven, or accepted. GPT-PM's correlated decision approved design
+only; implementation still needs exact-diff specialist review and a fresh exact-head GPT-PM gate.
+Correlated design decision: request
+`0ea02a82-72ba-44dc-a431-213d99bf8192`, reply
+`62890e6f-0fc5-432c-8bde-ba46be1fad8b`, job `411b4d13-4c15-400c-85f6-54c8f7db289b`.
+
+## Goal
+
+Close the S2 restart-fence deployment gap by ensuring every real call to
+`run_manifest_commands` runs inside one persistent, stable, delegated systemd service cgroup.
+Replacement processes must inherit the same parent cgroup and shared admission-lock directory,
+then reconcile abandoned command scopes before accepting another run.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Do not weaken the fail-closed POSIX identity and cgroup checks or claim Windows support.
+- Do not create a no-op unit or use a synthetic `systemd-run --wait --collect` unit as evidence.
+- Do not add arbitrary command execution, remote access, shell evaluation, policy-selector
+  execution, process-kill/crash scenarios, or a new test entry point that bypasses manifests.
+- Do not provision accounts, install the units/helper, enable services, migrate the Store, or
+  mutate host state during this source-code pass. Deployment preparation is recorded in
+  `tools/vst/systemd/README.md`.
+- Do not begin S3 work or approve S2 from a design note.
+
+## Current behavior and constraints
+
+- `tools/vst/runner.py::run_manifest_commands` now requires an `ExecutionAuthority`, binds each
+  manifest/run field and bounded execution deadline to one signed grant, claims it durably before
+  the first child, and persists the validated receipt through the Supervisor before returning it.
+  Store completion appends the same receipt to the normal `receipts` table and
+  `RECEIPT_APPENDED` hash chain in the claim-completion transaction; gate reads and retry tips
+  therefore use the ordinary receipt path. This source path remains untested.
+- `_DelegatedCgroup._runner_parent` reads `/proc/self/cgroup`; stale-scope reconciliation can
+  only inspect strict `vst-command-<pid>-<uuid>` children under that current process's parent.
+  The new fixed persistent unit and root lifecycle fence provide the source contract for keeping
+  the same manager-owned parent across process replacement; this behavior remains unverified.
+- `tools/vst/signer.py::AuthenticatedSigner` provides the persistent Unix-socket signer and pins
+  runner peer credentials, pidfd, cgroup, signed grant, active service generation, and current
+  Store `PENDING` claim.
+- `tools/vst/runner_service.py` provides the manifest-only runner entry point;
+  `tools/vst/supervisor_service.py` provides the root-owned authenticated grant/Store boundary.
+  `Supervisor.start_worker` remains the separate callback-based lifecycle coordinator.
+- The current source tree contains the runner, Supervisor and signer service entry points, fixed
+  units, lifecycle fence, and exact-HEAD installers. Existing transient-unit evidence is not
+  restart evidence and does not establish that these new paths work.
+
+## Options and decision criterion
+
+1. **Preferred: add a small foreground runner daemon with a private local Unix socket.** The
+   daemon is the sole production entry point for manifest-bound runs, validates each bounded
+   request, calls the existing `run_manifest_commands` library, and returns a receipt/result.
+   A persistent systemd unit owns its cgroup parent and `/run/vst-runner` lock directory across
+   process replacement. This directly connects the deployment invariant to real work.
+2. **Integrate the library into an identified existing trusted service.** This avoids a new
+   daemon, but no such in-scope service entry point is currently identified in repository
+   evidence. It remains viable if a concrete caller is named and can guarantee the same unit,
+   cgroup, lock, and restart behavior.
+3. **Keep transient invocation and waive persistence.** Rejected for S2 acceptance because the
+   current evidence does not show that replacement invocations share the predecessor's cgroup
+   parent or reconcile its scopes.
+
+The decisive criterion is observable proof that the same stable service boundary owns actual
+manifest-run calls before and after replacement, while preserving the existing worker/signer
+separation and fail-closed recovery.
+
+## Proposed design
+
+### Service boundary
+
+- Add a foreground `python -I -S -m tools.vst.runner_service` entry point. It loads a root-owned,
+  non-writable service configuration from a fixed path, resolves the repository/run root once,
+  validates that configured `vst-worker` UID/GID differs from the runner and signer identities,
+  and refuses unsupported platforms or cgroup v2/delegation profiles before binding its socket.
+- Bind one Unix stream socket under the provisioned `/run/vst-runner` directory, owned by
+  the fixed `vst-runner` daemon identity (`997:988`) and the dedicated dispatcher group with mode `0710`; the group may traverse but
+  cannot list or write the directory. Keep the shared admission lock owned by the daemon with
+  mode `0600`, and the socket mode `0660` for the dispatcher group. The worker must not belong to
+  that group. Authenticate each peer with `SO_PEERCRED`; reject unexpected UID/GID and
+  malformed or oversized messages before dispatch. The candidate worker is never a permitted
+  client and cannot read or write the socket directory.
+- Accept only a versioned, bounded JSON request containing an immutable manifest digest, slot,
+  attempt/epoch, signed run authorization, and relative artifact paths. Do not accept `argv`,
+  parser functions, signing keys, arbitrary environment entries, or caller-supplied
+  cwd/UID/GID/model/runner identity as authority. Derive worker identity, signer socket, working
+  root, environment, and limits from trusted service configuration.
+- The manifest must come from a trusted source and its provenance must be verified before
+  dispatch. Existing `validate_task_manifest` and `manifest_sha256` validate structure/digest,
+  not author authenticity. The proposed execution authorization is a signed, bounded grant
+  verified against a provisioned trust root, binding manifest digest, task, slot, attempt, epoch,
+  run ID, invocation ID, resolved-model provenance, and expiry. Peer UID authentication alone
+  does not authorize arbitrary manifests. The grant includes a unique `grant_id`, `request_id`,
+  and service audience; the caller cannot change any of them without invalidating its signature.
+  **Grant authority and trust root:** the sole issuer is the trusted Supervisor/Store
+  authorization transaction, never the runner daemon, dispatcher, or caller. Before signing,
+  it verifies current task registration, immutable manifest digest, authorized test slot,
+  attempt and epoch, current lease/fence, run-bound preflight, remaining budget, and active
+  service generation. Grants have a 30-second claim window and an expiry covering the signed
+  overall execution deadline (capped at 1,800 seconds) plus 30 seconds of completion slack. Store
+  accepts a new claim only inside the claim window; a PENDING grant remains verifiable through the
+  bounded run deadline. An expired COMPLETE grant may return only its identical stored receipt;
+  it cannot start new work. The canonical, versioned grant uses a distinct signature domain
+  (`VST_EXECUTION_GRANT_V1\0`) and binds the audience, service generation, manifest, task, slot,
+  attempt, epoch, run/invocation/request/grant IDs, resolved-model provenance, and expiry.
+  The grant uses Ed25519 signatures with the root-owned OpenSSL `pkeyutl` provider: only the
+  Supervisor reads the issuer private key, while the runner receives a key-ID-indexed public-key
+  ring. OpenSSL and key paths are absolute, root-owned, and non-writable by group/other; the
+  signature input is a bounded regular temporary file so Ed25519 verification does not depend on
+  an unknown-length stdin stream. Unsupported OpenSSL/Ed25519/key conditions refuse admission.
+  The official OpenSSL interface requires `-rawin` for Ed25519 before OpenSSL 3.5 and describes
+  its one-shot input requirement: https://docs.openssl.org/3.1/man1/openssl-pkeyutl/.
+  Root-provisioned private key custody is restricted to the issuer; the daemon has only a
+  separately provisioned verification trust root. Key IDs, rotation, revocation, and an
+  unknown-key fail-closed rule are part of the signed root-owned trust configuration. STOP,
+  epoch/fence changes, grant revocation, or service-generation replacement invalidate unused
+  grants. The durable Store `PENDING` claim rechecks current authority immediately before
+  dispatch; a grant cannot restore authority revoked by Supervisor/Store. No key is provisioned
+  by this proposal. Operator owns actual host key provisioning; Codex owns the implementation
+  contract and evidence.
+- Resolve the manifest from the configured immutable/read-only registry by its authorized digest,
+  verify the digest against canonical bytes, and dispatch only through `run_manifest_commands`.
+  Restrict each grant to its exact manifest, slot, attempt, epoch and one invocation. The
+  production boundary uses the existing fixed `vst-runner` daemon (997:988), a distinct
+  dispatcher UID/GID, and the fixed `vst-worker` (999:989). This preserves the operator-approved
+  narrow helper contract; do not create an alternate per-sprint checkout or daemon user. Only the daemon
+  identity may write the delegated cgroup and create command scopes; dispatcher and worker
+  identities have neither cgroup write access nor execution authority. Daemon code/config are
+  root-owned and non-writable to those identities; requests cannot choose a library entry point,
+  signer socket, cgroup, worktree, or executable. A fixed service configuration supplies the
+  signer endpoint and execution capability. A static call-site inventory is evidence, not
+  enforcement. `run_manifest_commands` itself requires a verified grant plus an atomically
+  claimed Store `PENDING` authorization and daemon-only execution capability before spawning the
+  first child; direct callers without both are denied before child creation. The signer
+  independently validates pinned daemon identity, pidfd-bound peer, cgroup, service-generation
+  ID, and invocation-specific grant; a generic invalid-request ping is not authorization. Bind
+  `SO_PEERCRED` to Linux `SO_PEERPIDFD`, keep the pidfd open through validation/request handling,
+  require the peer to remain alive, and fail closed when peer-pidfd support is absent. Do not
+  authorize from an unpinned PID followed by `/proc/<pid>` lookup. The systemd unit keeps the
+  daemon in the manager-reported `ControlGroup` and delegates only its descendant subtree; record
+  parent/subtree permissions, identity separation, and all service processes in runtime evidence.
+  Root remains trusted. Key material and Store credentials never enter requests, receipts,
+  candidate environment, or process arguments.
+- Close the production call-path inventory by static search of all import/call sites and by
+  runtime enumeration of every process running under the daemon (`vst-runner`), dispatcher
+  (`vst-dispatcher`), and worker (`vst-worker`) identities, plus every unit that can access the
+  signer socket. The only allowed production caller is the pinned foreground daemon in the
+  configured cgroup; tests may call the library only through explicit test fixtures. Any
+  alternate service, scheduled task, shell path, or direct production call blocks acceptance.
+- Bound request bytes, concurrent requests, per-command/overall deadline, output and response
+  sizes. Serialize distinct-UID admission using the existing cross-process `flock`; startup and
+  every request fail closed if runtime-directory ownership/mode, lock, delegated parent, or stale
+  scope reconciliation cannot be verified. Return structured non-approving errors; never return
+  a successful-looking receipt on partial capture or cleanup failure.
+- Make duplicate request delivery idempotent with a crash-safe ledger: the database has unique
+  constraints on `grant_id`, `invocation_id`, and `request_id`; all three are cryptographically
+  bound in the grant. Atomically insert `PENDING` for all three with the authorization/payload
+  digest before any command can start; reject a grant, invocation, or request already seen,
+  including when replayed with a different request ID; reject same-ID concurrent requests while
+  pending; reject a different payload under the same ID; after
+  `run_manifest_commands` returns and the complete receipt is durably stored, atomically
+  transition to `COMPLETE`. A duplicate `COMPLETE` request returns the exact stored receipt. On
+  restart, any surviving `PENDING` request becomes `INDETERMINATE` and is permanently
+  non-replayable until explicit signed reconciliation; it is never automatically rerun. A crash
+  after signer acceptance but before runner-ledger completion therefore cannot execute the
+  command twice or emit a false receipt. The signer ledger is a separate replay/signature boundary
+  and does not replace the runner's pre-execution `PENDING` claim.
+  The in-repository implementation adds Store schema version 5; the additive migration has not
+  been executed. The root Supervisor now verifies a root-controlled run-bound probe and operator
+  attestation, idempotently records the exact preflight tuple on restart, and refuses startup on
+  changed evidence. The source wires the ledger through authenticated Supervisor IPC and startup
+  recovery, but neither the migration nor recovery path has been run in dedicated WSL.
+
+### Persistent systemd contract and lifecycle fence
+
+- Support exactly one manager-controlled systemd unit and normal in-unit process restart. Do not
+  support parallel unit instances, transient invocations, unit renames, in-process replacement,
+  direct startup, or host reboot without a separately re-authorized bootstrap. Each process
+  generation records unit name, manager `InvocationID`,
+  manager-reported `ControlGroup`, observed cgroup directory device/inode, lock file device/inode,
+  and predecessor fence outcome. `RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=restart` is proposed to retain the
+  private runtime directory across restart; actual behavior must be observed before acceptance.
+- Set an explicit stop/restart policy, proposed as `KillMode=control-group` and
+  `SendSIGKILL=no`, so systemd does not restart the unit while processes remain in its unit cgroup.
+  A root-controlled system-manager lifecycle helper is the sole fence writer: the fixed unit uses
+  `ExecStartPre=+/usr/libexec/vst-runner-fence start` and
+  `ExecStopPost=+/usr/libexec/vst-runner-fence stop`. The `+` command prefix makes both hooks
+  privileged even though the service itself runs as `vst-runner`; the manager runs `ExecStartPre`
+  before `ExecStart`, and `ExecStopPost` after the stop command but before it completes the unit
+  stop/restart transaction. The helper is installed root-owned and cannot be invoked or replaced
+  by the daemon, dispatcher, or worker.
+  On start it obtains unit name, current `InvocationID`, and `ControlGroup` from systemd; validates
+  the durable prior-generation record; then atomically writes a `RUNNING` record for this exact
+  invocation before `ExecStart` can admit work. On stop it obtains the invocation and cgroup
+  identity from the manager, confirms the only remaining process (if any) is the lifecycle helper
+  itself, confirms no command scopes remain, and writes `STOPPED_EMPTY`; any query/check/write
+  failure writes or leaves `UNVERIFIED` and prevents the next start. Records are versioned,
+  root-owned, append-only or atomically replaced via temp-file, fsync, and rename, and bind unit
+  name, predecessor `InvocationID`, manager `ControlGroup`, cgroup device/inode, lock
+  device/inode, generation sequence, and observed cleanup outcome. The next `ExecStartPre` must
+  match the last `RUNNING` generation to its `STOPPED_EMPTY` predecessor record; a missing,
+  duplicate, out-of-order, or mismatched record fails closed. Because systemd also invokes
+  `ExecStopPost` after a failed start, that helper may transition only a matching current
+  `RUNNING` generation; it must never turn a missing/malformed start record or an older
+  `UNVERIFIED` state into `STOPPED_EMPTY`. First install has no inferred clean
+  predecessor: a one-time root provisioning step must inventory existing runner identities and
+  scopes, establish they are absent, create a generation-zero `BOOTSTRAP_EMPTY` record, and then
+  enable the fixed unit. No automated startup may create this baseline from missing state. Startup
+  also refuses on changed lock inode, unexpected unit identity, or unexplained delegation
+  identity change. If parent path and directory identity are preserved, it reconciles only safe
+  empty stale scopes under the shared lock before admission. A changed parent is eligible only
+  after a verified empty predecessor fence; path or inode equality alone is insufficient. This is
+  a manager-mediated predecessor-stop/fence-before-replacement protocol, not an assumption that
+  a unit name or shared lock provides exclusivity.
+- The unit owns lifecycle of worker descendants and must not permit an older pre-lock process or
+  alternate unit to run concurrently. Before rollout, stop and account for every prior runner
+  process; then enable exactly one service instance. Any uncertainty blocks worker admission.
+- Resource limits and restart policy must be bounded and explicit. The service must not restart
+  indefinitely while unresolved cleanup is present; it should start in a refusing state until
+  `reconcile_stale` has completed under the shared lock.
+- This note does not prescribe unverified systemd directive semantics. The exact unit and
+  runtime-directory preservation behavior require primary-documentation review and exact WSL
+  observation before claiming acceptance.
+
+Systemd's cgroup interface describes the unit cgroup as managed by PID 1 while a delegated
+service controls its descendant subtree; it also recommends asking the manager for the unit's
+`ControlGroup` rather than translating unit names locally. See
+https://systemd.io/CONTROL_GROUP_INTERFACE/ and
+https://systemd.io/CGROUP_DELEGATION/. Linux `SO_PEERPIDFD` pins the Unix-socket peer process
+identity rather than exposing only a reusable numeric PID; see the upstream kernel change
+https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/7b26952a91cf65ff1cc867a2382a8964d8c0ee7d. These are
+design references; support in the provisioned WSL kernel is not yet runtime-verified.
+The proposed `KillMode=control-group` and `SendSIGKILL=no` combination is based on systemd's
+documented behavior: the manager targets the unit cgroup and does not restart a control-group or
+mixed service while processes from a prior instance remain there
+(https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.kill.html). The proposal still
+requires exact unit validation and runtime observation before this behavior is counted as S2
+evidence. `RuntimeDirectoryPreserve=restart` preserves the configured runtime directory on
+automatic and manual service restart, but not system reboot; see
+https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html. The fence record must
+therefore fail closed when manager invocation identity or runtime state cannot be reconciled.
+The `+` prefix on `ExecStartPre=`/`ExecStopPost=` is systemd's documented privileged-command
+exception to the unit's `User=` setting; see the same `systemd.exec` reference. Exact directive
+support and the helper's effective credentials still require validation in the provisioned
+system manager.
+systemd documents that `ExecStopPost=` runs after stop and also after start failure, and that
+restart consists of stop followed by start; see
+https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.service.html. The hook contract
+above accounts for those cases and never upgrades absent start evidence to a clean predecessor.
+
+## Failure modes and required behavior
+
+| Failure | Required behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Unsupported OS, missing `SO_PEERCRED`/`SO_PEERPIDFD`, or non-unified/missing delegation | Service refuses startup; no worker command starts. |
+| Wrong peer UID/GID or cgroup, candidate peer, oversized/malformed request | Reject before dispatch; signer refuses direct library calls outside the configured runner service cgroup; record bounded diagnostic without request secrets. |
+| Missing/untrusted config, private runtime directory, signer socket, or lock | Refuse admission and return a non-approving result. |
+| Cgroup parent differs after restart or contains unknown stale scope | A changed parent is eligible only after the manager-mediated predecessor record proves `STOPPED_EMPTY`, current unit/generation/lock identities pass fresh admission checks, and only safe empty scopes require reconciliation; otherwise remain unavailable. Unknown or populated scopes always remain unavailable and are never killed or adopted. |
+| Crash after atomic `PENDING` claim but before durable `COMPLETE` receipt | Restart marks the request `INDETERMINATE`; return no approving receipt and do not replay absent explicit signed reconciliation. |
+| Worker timeout, capture failure, or cleanup not confirmed | Preserve existing non-approving receipt semantics; reconcile under the same stable parent before a later admission. |
+| Two service instances or rolling replacement overlap | Shared lock serializes compliant calls; signer cgroup allowlist plus unit provisioning must prevent an alternate production caller or second parent and refuse if stable-parent identity cannot be established. |
+
+## Rollout and rollback
+
+1. Obtain GPT-PM adjudication of whether this service is required and whether the proposed request,
+   idempotency, and restart boundaries satisfy S2 architecture.
+2. Complete the final source/documentation pass in the canonical checkout only; launch actual
+   specialist reviewers against the exact diff before the functional-test phase.
+3. Run the required focused tests only through the designated functional test reviewer, followed
+   by a bounded e2e-runner runtime run after coding is complete. Record exact source head, service
+   unit hash, UID/GID, cgroup path before/after replacement, lock path/inode, requests, and outcomes.
+4. Provision the unit only after code review and explicit runtime change authorization; preserve
+   previous config and provide a rollback that stops the new unit, prevents parallel old/new
+   runners, restores prior config, and leaves existing scopes available for safe reconciliation.
+5. Do not claim Phase 8 acceptance until GPT-PM reviews exact-head code, required test/runtime
+   evidence, and the other outstanding S2 criteria.
+
+## Test and verification plan
+
+After code completion, the `functional-test-reviewer` authors/runs focused tests for request schema
+and size bounds, peer authentication, manifest-only dispatch, config ownership/mode, duplicate
+request semantics, deadline/output limits, fail-closed startup, and restart reconciliation. The
+`e2e-runner` then proves that an actual `run_manifest_commands` call is served by the persistent
+unit and that a replacement process reports the same delegated parent and lock identity before
+reconciling the controlled safe stale-scope fixture. No crash, process-kill, mutation, or restricted
+policy selector is implied; those retain their current `NOT_RUN` state unless separately authorized.
+

+- User turn: `d82d2124-ec09-4e3b-a321-d767350ed73a`
+- Correlated response: `67045970-e83f-538b-866e-ba97e9d269ec`
+- Verdict: **ACCEPT — WITH BINDING CONSTRAINTS**
+
+This later response supersedes the earlier point-to-point proposal and the pending provenance
+amendment only for the narrow source-implementation scope below. It does not close
+`S2-DISPATCH-M01`, approve runtime or migration application, authorize key creation or service
+activation, or authorize push/PR/merge/deployment.
+
+## Accepted source contract
+
+1. The durable intent is one typed `DISPATCH_INTENT_ACCEPTED` event in the existing hash-chained
+   Store; no external broker, general-purpose bus, user queue/spool, task enumeration, scheduler,
+   or assignment authority is introduced.
+2. A narrowly configured owner peer submits one exact request. Supervisor derives its principal
+   from AF_UNIX kernel credentials, pidfd/process identity, exact cgroup, provisioned UID/GID, and
+   root-owned mapping. Principal is never accepted from the request body.
+3. The event binds request ID, task, TestRun slot, attempt, epoch, run ID, derived lease ID,
+   principal, canonical payload digest, current service generation, and manifest digest.
+4. Store accepts the intent atomically only when the authenticated principal owns the live task
+   epoch and the named lease, manifest slot, consumed preflight, receipt position, and budget are
+   current. The dispatcher receives only Supervisor-filtered intents through AF_UNIX and cannot
+   access Store directly.
+5. The dispatcher forwards only the exact accepted intent using a Supervisor-issued grant. It
+   cannot create tasks or leases, choose work, sign grants, or supply commands, paths, worker
+   identities, Store paths, or model provenance.
+6. Delivery is at-least-once. Same request ID and same payload may replay within the same generation;
+   request-ID reuse with changed payload, owner/lease/epoch/manifest/generation changes, and
+   ambiguous launches fail closed. No automatic retry follows an ambiguous execution.
+7. The event chain and generation-/peer-bound cursor must be verified. Source-level schema/migration
+   code may be prepared, but migration application requires separate independent review and
+   authorization.
+
+## Work and gates
+
+The decision authorizes source implementation and mapped source tests after coding. It does not
+authorize applying the schema-v6 migration, generating or provisioning keys, enabling or starting
+services, dispatching a real task, or claiming E5/S2 acceptance. Required evidence still includes
+owner identity, durable event, delivery/replay, idempotency, revocation/generation fencing, grant
+integration, negative tests, exact-head independent review, and separately authorized runtime
+acceptance. The earlier request `9fcaec9d-c344-4388-b79a-1392fb6f4cb4` remains uncertain and is not
+approval.
+
+## Current evidence boundary
+
+This record preserves the correlated decision and its scope. It does not assert that implementation,
+tests, migration, configuration, service activation, or runtime acceptance have completed. Current
+code and documentation status is tracked in `core/STATE.md`, `core/BACKLOG.md`, and the linked
+change record.

+Unit `s2-restart-lock-a6-r2.service`, invocation ID `34c1baf6c61b46e7985e5d7ffe6c2a03`, ran `/usr/bin/python3 /run/vst-s2-restart-lock-a6/flock-smoke.py`. +```
+
+Harness source:
+
+```python
+import importlib, os, pwd, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile, time, types, uuid
+from pathlib import Path
+from tools.vst.runner import _DelegatedCgroup, _posix_cgroup_process_lock
+
+runtime_dir = Path("/run/vst-runner")
+st = runtime_dir.stat()
+assert st.st_uid == os.geteuid() == pwd.getpwnam("vst-runner").pw_uid
+assert st.st_mode & 0o777 == 0o700, oct(st.st_mode & 0o777)
+print(f"runtime-directory mode={st.st_mode & 0o777:o} owner={st.st_uid}:{st.st_gid}")
+print(f"invocation-id={os.environ.get('INVOCATION_ID','not-set')}")
+with open("/proc/self/cgroup", encoding="ascii") as stream:
+    print("cgroup=" + next(line.strip() for line in stream if line.startswith("0::")))
+
+base = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="vst-flock-smoke-"))
+child = r"""
+import importlib, os, sys, time, types
+from pathlib import Path
+from tools.vst.runner import _posix_cgroup_process_lock
+role, root = sys.argv[1:3]
+if role == "b":
+    real = importlib.import_module("fcntl").flock
+    proxy = types.SimpleNamespace(LOCK_EX=2, LOCK_NB=4)
+    def observed(fd, operation):
+        try:
+            return real(fd, operation)
+        except BlockingIOError:
+            Path(root + ".blocked").touch()
+            raise
+    proxy.flock = observed
+    sys.modules["fcntl"] = proxy
+with _posix_cgroup_process_lock(time.monotonic() + 10):
+    if role == "a":
+        Path(root + ".held").touch()
+        until = time.monotonic() + 10
+        while not Path(root + ".release").exists():
+            if time.monotonic() >= until:
+                raise SystemExit("release event deadline expired")
+            time.sleep(0.005)
+    else:
+        Path(root + ".acquired").touch()
+"""
+def wait_file(path, seconds=5):
+    until = time.monotonic() + seconds
+    while time.monotonic() < until:
+        if path.exists():
+            return
+        time.sleep(0.005)
+    raise RuntimeError(f"condition deadline expired waiting for {path.name}")
+a = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", child, "a", str(base)])
+try:
+    wait_file(Path(str(base) + ".held"))
+    b = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", child, "b", str(base)])
+    wait_file(Path(str(base) + ".blocked"))
+    assert not Path(str(base) + ".acquired").exists(), "second runner process entered held lock"
+    Path(str(base) + ".release").touch()
+    assert a.wait(timeout=10) == 0
+    assert b.wait(timeout=10) == 0
+    assert Path(str(base) + ".acquired").exists()
+finally:
+    if a.poll() is None:
+        a.wait(timeout=10)
+print("actual flock: second runner process waited until first released")
+
+parent = _DelegatedCgroup._runner_parent()
+stale = os.path.join(parent, f"vst-command-{os.getpid()}-{uuid.uuid4().hex}")
+os.mkdir(stale, 0o700)
+with open(os.path.join(stale, "cgroup.events"), encoding="ascii") as stream:
+    events = dict(line.split() for line in stream if line.strip())
+with open(os.path.join(stale, "cgroup.procs"), encoding="ascii") as stream:
+    pids = stream.read().strip()
+assert events.get("populated") == "0" and not pids, (events, pids)
+print(f"stale synthetic scope before reconcile: populated={events['populated']} cgroup.procs=empty path={stale}")
+with _posix_cgroup_process_lock(time.monotonic() + 10):
+    pass
+assert not os.path.exists(stale), "empty stale scope was not removed"
+print("empty stale scope reconciled; no populated cgroup or process was killed")
+shutil.rmtree(base)
+```
+
+```text
+runtime-directory mode=700 owner=997:988
+invocation-id=34c1baf6c61b46e7985e5d7ffe6c2a03
+cgroup=0::/vst.slice/vst-run.slice/s2-restart-lock-a6-r2.service
+actual flock: second runner process waited until first released
+stale synthetic scope before reconcile: populated=0 cgroup.procs=empty path=/sys/fs/cgroup/vst.slice/vst-run.slice/s2-restart-lock-a6-r2.service/vst-command-776-a5152ece9c094491af0b6ea06c7341f4
+empty stale scope reconciled; no populated cgroup or process was killed
+```

+Before reconciliation, the harness read and asserted `cgroup.events populated=0` and empty `cgroup.procs`. It then acquired the same lock helper and confirmed removal. No populated scope existed, no process was killed, and no runner crash was simulated. Unit result: success, runtime 891 ms, CPU 844 ms, memory peak 448 KiB.

+# S2 runner-claim reconciliation adjudication
+
+Date: 2026-10-27  
+Repository: `D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`  
+Declared base HEAD: `2da827be982d3f2d6f2adf152668af6ff8007f21`  
+Request: `e73cabde-5580-4be5-9ad1-63f65521f347`  
+Reply: `9f337b5f-04f6-4610-b453-3926ba4a6bc8`  
+PM Bridge job: `3cbf606b-b4ea-4902-9ad6-f3a05958d807`  
+Correlation: `correlated=true`; request payload hash `62b49ee34d9ae746e73e4177cd5419b06772fc478610f9d82b39777ef9f51ecc`.
+
+## Verdict and core invariant
+
+GPT-PM returned `MODIFY`: `S2-RC-M01` is a valid MAJOR and source correction is required.
+The response considered supplied source context and prior review; it did not independently
+verify the complete working diff or committed exact head.
+
+`INDETERMINATE` terminalizes the original grant, but does not prove that its command had no
+effects and does not authorize attempt+1. After a claim reached `EXECUTION_RESERVED` or may have
+started a command, a successor attempt must remain blocked until a distinct authenticated
+reconciliation establishes a disposition that explicitly permits continuation. Lease expiry and
+a `WORKER_LOST` marker do not substitute for execution reconciliation. Retry authorization is a
+separate action by the existing coordinator under current epoch, budget and policy.
+
+## Finding
+
+`S2-RC-M01 — ambiguous execution does not fence successor attempts` (**MAJOR, source correction
+required**). Store terminalizes predecessor claims as `INDETERMINATE`, while normal lease and
+execution grant admission did not require a distinct effect-resolution record before a later
+attempt. This can permit attempt N+1 despite unresolved effects of attempt N; no duplicate effect
+needs to be reproduced for this to be a valid contract defect.
+
+## Required source boundary
+
+The correction is confined to existing Store/Supervisor reconciliation and admission boundaries:
+
+- A distinct `RECONCILED` event must bind the exact predecessor `grant_id`, `request_id`,
+  `invocation_id`, `task_id`, `slot`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `run_id`, `service_generation`, and
+  grant payload digest.
+- It must include a unique durable `resolution_id`, closed outcome enum, evidence digest,
+  authenticated actor/key identity, and a domain-separated signature over the complete record.
+- Outcomes that leave effects unresolved or reject reconciliation keep the task blocked. At minimum,
+  only evidence-backed `NO_EXECUTION_PROVEN` or `EFFECTS_RESOLVED` can become retry-eligible, with
+  ordinary epoch/budget/policy checks still required.
+- Store admission must enforce the block at lease acquisition, execution-grant basis, and claim,
+  so a prior lease cannot bypass it.
+- A generic `NOTE`, unsigned boolean, `INDETERMINATE` event, expired lease, or `WORKER_LOST`
+  receipt is not reconciliation authority.
+- Recovery remains separate from grant issuance: no implicit global reaper in `issue_grant` and
+  no dispatcher-facing reaper or general reconciliation capability.
+- No new scheduler, CLI, spool, broad dispatcher capability, or second assignment authority.
+
+The existing production coordinator call site remains unidentified and `S2-DISPATCH-M01` remains
+MAJOR/OPEN. Source corrections may proceed within this S2 boundary, but production integration and
+the S2 code gate cannot be declared closed without that real source.
+

+Runner admission and reservation independently recheck execution authority. Those checks remain required.
+
+These mechanisms support using the root Supervisor and Store as the source of current assignment facts instead of introducing an external per-task authorization database.
+
+However, one distinction remains decisive:
+
+A verified Store assignment is not automatically proof that the assignment was created by an authorized actor.
+
+The proposal must close that upstream boundary before the machine issuer can treat a Store assignment as sufficient signing authorization.
+
+2. Focused finding
+
+Finding

+MAJOR
+

+OPEN — outside this review
+
+S2-MACHINE-ISSUER-M01 — Upstream authorization is not yet authenticated
+
+The exact gap is visible in the Store interfaces.
+
+Store.acquire_epoch() accepts an owner string and establishes that owner when no currently live owner exists. Store.acquire_lease() accepts a task, worker, epoch and attempt under its existing Store checks.
+
+These methods enforce state consistency, but their public in-process arguments do not themselves authenticate the actor requesting the mutation.
+
+For example, Store.acquire_epoch() validates that the supplied owner is nonempty and applies the ownership compare-and-swap. It does not verify a kernel-authenticated caller identity. 
+store.py
+
+Consequently, this sequence is not yet sufficient:
+
+Plain text
+Store says owner = Codex
+    ↓
+Machine issuer requests assignment_basis
+    ↓
+Supervisor confirms current owner = Codex
+    ↓
+Machine issuer signs
+
+The missing question is: Who was authorized to establish that Store ownership and lease in the first place?
+
+The HMAC event chain protects recorded history against undetected alteration within its key-custody assumptions. It does not independently authenticate the original assignment decision.
+
+This is the remaining MAJOR invariant—not the absence of a per-task human signature.
+
+3. Required narrow upstream contract
+
+The safe alternative is a fixed, authenticated assignment/bootstrap boundary that uses the existing Store APIs rather than introducing a second authority.
+
+The minimum upstream requirements are:
+
+1. Authenticated assignment principal. A root-configured service identity, pinned by UID/GID, cgroup and kernel peer credentials, may invoke only the specifically authorized existing Store transitions. It must not become a general-purpose Store writer.
+
+2. Fixed delegation scope. A reviewed, operator-authorized policy binds the machine principal to Virtual_scrum_team, the exact repository, approved sprint/manifest scope, allowed owner Codex, permitted transitions, validity and revocation. This authorizes a class of operations, not arbitrary work.
+
+3. Bounded mutation entrypoint. Any required assignment/bootstrap RPC must use exact fields and existing Store compare-and-swap mechanisms. It cannot accept a caller-asserted owner identity as authentication evidence.
+
+4. Durable provenance. The authenticated actor, delegation-policy identity/digest and exact assignment operation must be durably attributable to the resulting Store transition. A plain event actor string is insufficient unless the trusted API derives and fixes it.
+
+5. Fail-closed legacy behavior. Historical assignments created before authenticated provenance was established cannot automatically become eligible for delegated machine issuance. They require independently authorized reconciliation or a fresh, properly authenticated assignment transition.
+
+6. No arbitrary task discovery. The issuer must receive one exact authorized work reference. It cannot enumerate tasks, select the next task or turn an arbitrary requested task ID into proof of assignment.
+
+This does not require a new human participant. The sole operator may authorize a bounded machine bootstrap role through a concrete delegation policy. The machine's authenticated execution then supplies the per-operation provenance.
+
+4. Exact assignment_basis contract
+
+A separate read-only Supervisor RPC is acceptable within this architecture.
+
+A suitable operation name is:
+
+assignment_basis
+
+It must be restricted to the new purpose-specific issuer peer, not added to the generic dispatch_owner, dispatcher, runner or signer roles.
+
+Request
+
+The minimal request should identify an exact, preauthorized assignment handoff, such as an opaque assignment-operation identity whose issuance is rooted in the authenticated upstream transition.
+
+It must not accept a caller-controlled owner principal, service generation, manifest digest or policy as authoritative values.
+
+If the request includes task_id, slot, attempt or epoch for matching, those fields are selectors only. The Supervisor must derive their authoritative counterparts and validate them against the authenticated handoff.
+
+Response
+
+The root Supervisor derives and returns an immutable snapshot containing:
+
+Field
+
+	
+
+Authoritative source
+
+
+
+
+Project/repository/sprint scope
+
+	
+
+Approved root-owned delegation manifest and registered task
+
+
+
+
+task_id, story_id, slot, attempt
+
+	
+
+Authenticated assignment handoff and Store
+
+
+
+
+principal
+
+	
+
+Trusted peer/delegation mapping, expected Codex
+
+
+
+
+epoch, lease_id, worker identity
+
+	
+
+Current Store state
+
+
+
+
+manifest_sha256, timeout and budget eligibility
+
+	
+
+Registered Store manifest/budget
+
+
+
+
+run_id, consumed probe identity
+
+	
+
+Current Supervisor/Store preflight
+
+
+
+
+service_generation
+
+	
+
+Trusted current Runner generation provider
+
+
+
+
+Owner/lease authority expiry
+
+	
+
+Current Store snapshot
+
+
+
+
+Delegation policy ID/digest
+
+	
+
+Root-controlled approved policy
+
+
+
+
+Assignment-operation ID/digest
+
+	
+
+Verified authenticated transition history
+
+The Store must verify these facts within one consistent read snapshot, rather than assembling independently timed responses.
+
+The response is a short-lived statement of observed authority, not a lease reservation or durable promise that the authority will remain valid.
+
+The issuer must verify that sufficient authority remains for issuance. Supervisor/Store must recheck current authority at dispatch acceptance; Runner must continue its existing claim/reservation fencing.
+
+No signed instruction may be issued from a stale, incomplete, ambiguous or unverified assignment basis.
+
+5. Issue-once and v2 instruction rules
+
+The proposed machine issuer remains bounded by the earlier accepted safeguards:
+
+One exact assignment identity produces at most one immutable signed envelope.
+
+The issue-once journal preserves the original request ID, expiry and canonical signed bytes.
+
+A confirmed duplicate returns the exact stored envelope.
+
+An ambiguous signing/journal outcome never authorizes generating a replacement identity.
+
+The private signing key remains unavailable to relay, dispatcher, Runner and worker.
+
+The issuer cannot create tasks, leases or ownership.
+
+The v2 envelope should bind the authenticated assignment-operation digest and root-derived snapshot, along with the immutable deployment-policy scope.
+
+The existing v1 instruction and verifier must remain unchanged during preparation. A new v2 verifier must explicitly enforce the new provenance fields and must not accept a v1 instruction as equivalent machine-delegated authority.
+
+The submitted design currently describes a mandatory externally signed assignment-authorization record. That part may be replaced by the authenticated Store provenance contract, but the design document must be revised consistently: removing only the signature field while retaining references to an external authorization object would leave contradictory trust rules. 
+S2_DELEGATED_MACHINE_TRUST_DESIGN.md
+
+6. Can the external per-task operator signature be retired?
+
+YES — as a proposed design requirement.
+
+The earlier requirement for independently authenticated assignment provenance did not inherently require a per-task operator signature.
+
+The external signed-authorization record was one possible way of establishing provenance. A properly authenticated and durably attributable Store assignment/bootstrap operation can satisfy the same security objective.
+
+This ruling therefore permits Codex to retire the mandatory external per-task signature from the candidate architecture, replacing it with the upstream authenticated assignment provenance mechanism described above.
+
+It does not authorize removing any existing production signature verification. The approved v1 dispatch-instruction verification and current operator E5 requirements remain unchanged.
+
+A concrete operator-authorized delegation policy is still needed to establish which machine principal may create or approve assignments. Broad GO alone is not a substitute for that exact machine-authority policy.
+
+7. Source work permitted now
+BOUNDED READ-ONLY SOURCE GO
+
+Codex may implement and test a strictly read-only assignment_basis path after updating the architecture contract to specify its authenticated handoff and required provenance fields.
+
+The permitted source work includes:
+
+Pure validators for the delegation and assignment-basis schemas.
+
+A read-only Store snapshot function.
+
+A narrowly authenticated Supervisor RPC with fixed issuer-role authorization.
+
+Synthetic tests for exact matching, wrong principal, stale epoch/lease/generation, unknown assignment, missing provenance, expired delegation, integrity failure and read-only behavior.
+
+Documentation replacing mandatory per-task operator authorization with authenticated Store provenance.
+
+The following remain held: production issuer signing code, machine-key provisioning, new privileged assignment mutation endpoints, activation, runtime dispatch and any change to the E5 acceptance verifier.
+
+The upstream mutation/bootstrap contract must receive independent source/security review before such an endpoint is implemented or enabled.
+

+Final disposition — MODIFY
+
+The simplified approach is preferable to requiring a human to sign every task, provided authenticated assignment provenance begins at the Store mutation boundary.
+
+execution_grant_basis() already supplies most of the current-state validation needed for a read-only issuer query. It does not supply authenticated provenance for the original assignment creator.
+
+Required next step: Codex should revise S2_DELEGATED_MACHINE_TRUST_DESIGN.md to replace external per-task authorization with one precise authenticated bootstrap/assignment-operation contract, then implement only the read-only basis API and mapped synthetic tests.
+
+One MAJOR remains open for this alternative: S2-MACHINE-ISSUER-M01.
+
+No operator question is needed for this bounded design/source preparation. No production authority, key creation, privileged provisioning, E5 approval, restricted testing, push, PR, merge or full S2 acceptance is granted.
+
+Evidence limitation: This decision is grounded in the attached Store, Supervisor, Supervisor RPC and candidate design files. It does not verify a deployed assignment source, a live WSL identity, current signed E5, or an exact Git HEAD.

+# S2 Windows ACL and signer boundary — design disposition
+
+Date: 2026-10-27  
+Repository: `D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`  
+Branch: `s4-canonical-continuation`  
+Source/test baseline: `a6ea0dc15b9e02b37f48a85f1fcc76cbe81df5a3`  
+Documentation baseline: `41cfd5e2aad01d77ac5db416dc5aa8c42e66c617`
+
+## Goal
+
+Resolve whether the missing Windows key ACL evidence can be closed with a local helper change,
+without weakening the S2 worker/signing trust boundary or implying Windows signed-worker support
+that the current code does not provide.
+
+## Current contract and evidence
+
+- S2.3 explicitly requires Windows ACL protection and POSIX owner/mode `0600` checks; the runner
+  must refuse to start if the command account can read the signing key (`docs/S2_SANDBOX_WORKER_PLAN_2026-10-24.md`, S2.3).
+- `tools/vst/runner.py::run_manifest_commands` rejects every non-POSIX host before the signed v2
+  execution path. Its worker identity parameters are numeric POSIX UID/GID values.
+- `tools/vst/signer.py::_key_is_private` requires POSIX `O_NOFOLLOW`; `AuthenticatedSigner`
+  requires POSIX Unix sockets and `SO_PEERCRED`.
+- `tools/vst/sandbox.py` therefore fails closed for Windows key and signer IPC checks. These
+  helpers are called after the runner's POSIX-only boundary; the Windows signed-worker path is not
+  implemented.
+- The Windows nested Job Object probe at exact source/test HEAD `a6ea0dc` proved assignment of a
+  normal-exit child to nested jobs only. It did not prove key ACL, signed-worker launch, cleanup,
+  or descendant termination. Its evidence is
+  `s2-windows-nested-job-safe-a6ea0dc-20261027.md`.
+
+Read-only review in this turn:
+
+- `architect` (default GPT-6 Luna, medium) found that a DACL helper alone is disconnected from
+  runner launch and signer authentication because no Windows worker SID/token or signer IPC
+  contract exists.
+- `security-reviewer` (default GPT-6 Luna, medium) independently found that parsing a DACL or
+  checking only the runner account cannot establish worker effective access. Group membership,
+  inherited ACEs, and reparse/open races must be covered by the actual worker token and key-open
+  operation.
+- Neither reviewer edited files or ran tests/checks.
+
+PM Bridge status in this turn:
+
+- The exact S2 review request `d9e174a1-fbdf-4ba7-bcd0-ec1902ed38c4` / job
+  `11cffada-67dd-442f-9649-6ac6b706086d` remains `uncertain`, `sendPhase=sending`, with
+  `userTurnId=null`, `replyId=null`, `correlated=null`, and
+  `CHATGPT_RENDERER_STALLED`. The active sending lineage means it must not be blindly resent.
+- A separate read-only peek job `59419e68-d9d2-4c22-aa9a-b511721c8d87` surfaced a message whose
+  text names that request and says `MODIFY — S2 NOT APPROVED`, but the bridge still reports no
+  correlated reply ID or user turn. It is retained only as uncorrelated context, not a gate result
+  or architecture adjudication. The PM gate remains `S2-PHASE-8: in-progress`.
+
+## Options and recommendation
+
+1. **Add a standalone Windows ACL helper.** Rejected. It would not be called by the signed v2
+   runner, would have no authoritative worker token to evaluate, and would not secure signer IPC.
+   Treating it as acceptance would overstate the boundary.
+2. **Keep the signed v2 worker POSIX-only and seek explicit platform-scope adjudication.**
+   Recommended. Preserve the current fail-closed runner/signer behavior. Keep Windows Job Object
+   evidence as a separately bounded host containment result. GPT-PM must decide whether S2.3's
+   Windows ACL clause can be scoped to a future Windows worker profile or whether this sprint must
+   implement the full Windows boundary. No Windows ACL acceptance is claimed meanwhile.
+3. **Implement a complete Windows signed-worker profile.** Required if Windows worker execution is
+   in S2: define worker/signer SIDs and the actual worker access token; create the worker under
+   that token; check effective file and parent-path access; open the key without following
+   reparse points and bind checks to the opened object; define authenticated signer IPC (for
+   example, a named pipe bound to the caller token); then add focused negative tests and Windows
+   runtime evidence. This is a cross-module trust-boundary change, not a helper-only patch.
+
+## Failure behavior and rollout
+
+Until the platform contract is adjudicated, unsupported Windows signed-worker execution must
+continue to fail closed. Do not turn a missing ACL API into a permissive result, reinterpret the
+Windows Job Object probe as signer isolation, or alter the signed v2 POSIX contract. If GPT-PM
+selects the complete Windows profile, implement the identity/token and signer IPC contract first,
+then integrate ACL checks and tests as one reviewed source change. Rollback leaves Windows signed
+worker launch unavailable; it must not fall back to an unauthenticated signer channel.
+
+## Verification plan and ownership
+
+- GPT-PM owns the architecture/scope adjudication.
+- Codex owns reconciliation of the uncertain PM Bridge lineage, coordination and, if Windows is
+  selected, the identity/token/IPC implementation and
+  evidence records.
+- `functional-test-reviewer` owns focused ACL, token, path-race, and fail-closed tests after source
+  coding is complete; `e2e-runner` owns bounded Windows runtime evidence after that.
+- The operator owns only any external environment authorization genuinely required; no such
+  authorization is requested by this design note.
+- No tests/checks/build/CI/migration were run for this design record.
+
+## Disposition
+
+No source change is justified by the current contract evidence. VST-011's Windows ACL and signer
+isolation acceptance remains `NOT_VERIFIED`; VST-015's Windows read-only credential behavior also
+remains `NOT_VERIFIED`. Existing POSIX evidence remains platform-scoped. The exact-head S2 gate
+cannot be marked approved from this design review.
+
+Executor: Codex. Read-only design reviewers: architect and security-reviewer, GPT-6 Luna / medium.

+# S2 Windows nested Job Object assignment — safe bounded evidence
+
+Date: 2026-10-27. Repository: `D:\Repo\Virtual_scrum_team`.

+## Scope and provenance

+```powershell
+$script = @'
+<in-memory Python body below>
+'@; & 'C:\Python314\python.exe' -c $script; Write-Output "EXIT:$LASTEXITCODE"

+The body creates an outer Job Object without setting limits or `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, assigns the current probe process to it, then launches one stdin-blocked child. It instruments the actual project `runner._JobObject.attach(proc)`, checks child membership in both jobs, releases the child to exit normally, and only then closes both job handles. The exact body was executed as follows:
+
+```python

+from ctypes import wintypes
+from tools.vst import runner
+started = time.monotonic()
+api = runner._win_api()
+if api is None:

+k32 = api.k32
+k32.GetCurrentProcess.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
+k32.GetCurrentProcess.argtypes = []
+k32.IsProcessInJob.restype = wintypes.BOOL
+k32.IsProcessInJob.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE, wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(wintypes.BOOL)]
+outer = k32.CreateJobObjectW(None, None)
+if not outer:
+    err = ctypes.get_last_error()
+    print(json.dumps({"result":"OUTER_CREATE_FAILED","winerror":err}))
+    raise SystemExit(2)
+current = k32.GetCurrentProcess()
+ctypes.set_last_error(0)
+outer_assigned = bool(k32.AssignProcessToJobObject(outer, current))
+outer_error = 0 if outer_assigned else ctypes.get_last_error()
+if not outer_assigned:
+    close_ok = bool(k32.CloseHandle(outer))
+    print(json.dumps({"result":"OUTER_ASSIGN_FAILED","winerror":outer_error,"outer_close_ok":close_ok,"elapsed_sec":round(time.monotonic()-started,3)}))
+    raise SystemExit(2)
+member = wintypes.BOOL()
+if not k32.IsProcessInJob(current, outer, ctypes.byref(member)) or not member.value:
+    close_ok = bool(k32.CloseHandle(outer))
+    print(json.dumps({"result":"OUTER_MEMBERSHIP_UNCONFIRMED","outer_close_ok":close_ok,"elapsed_sec":round(time.monotonic()-started,3)}))
+    raise SystemExit(2)
+child_code = "import sys; print('READY',flush=True); data=sys.stdin.buffer.read(1); print('RELEASED',flush=True); sys.exit(0 if data == b'x' else 1)"
+proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", child_code], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW)
+child_in_outer = wintypes.BOOL()
+child_query_ok = bool(k32.IsProcessInJob(int(proc._handle), outer, ctypes.byref(child_in_outer)))
+original_assign = k32.AssignProcessToJobObject
+inner_assign_calls = []

+k32.AssignProcessToJobObject = observed_assign
+try:

+finally:
+    k32.AssignProcessToJobObject = original_assign
+inner_member = None
+if inner is not None:
+    check = wintypes.BOOL()
+    inner_member = bool(k32.IsProcessInJob(int(proc._handle), inner._handle, ctypes.byref(check))) and bool(check.value)
+stdout, stderr = proc.communicate(input=b"x", timeout=5)
+if proc.returncode != 0:
+    print(json.dumps({"result":"CHILD_NONZERO","returncode":proc.returncode,"stdout":stdout.decode(errors="replace"),"stderr":stderr.decode(errors="replace"),"elapsed_sec":round(time.monotonic()-started,3)}))
+    raise SystemExit(3)
+inner_close_ok = None
+if inner is not None:
+    inner_close_ok = bool(k32.CloseHandle(inner._handle))
+    if inner_close_ok:

+# S2 WSL archive line-ending reproduction — exact HEAD `9a5c41d` — 2026-10-28
+
+## Scope and result
+
+This record captures read-only Git archive comparisons at committed HEAD
+`9a5c41de5ce2878558402665eafaa0a80c09d177` and read-only inspection of the existing WSL helper.
+No installer retry, WSL mutation, helper replacement, or commit was performed.
+
+The host installer had been changed to set `core.autocrlf=false`, but that setting alone does not
+prevent CRLF conversion under this repository's `* text=auto` attribute and the host's Windows Git
+configuration. The helper script in the resulting archive still had 149 CRLF sequences and
+`set -eu\r\n` on line 2. Adding `core.eol=lf` produced an LF-only archive member matching the raw
+committed script blob.
+
+## Reproduction
+
+Both comparisons used the committed source at HEAD `9a5c41de5ce2878558402665eafaa0a80c09d177` and
+the same archive path set:

+```text

+With only the setting present in the committed host installer:

+```text

+```
+
+The `install_wsl_worker_helper.sh` member had SHA-256
+`cd3031fab777bf286876087058cc613788499c69d62c5d97632a1fcbbe592bc1`, 7332 bytes, line 2
+`set -eu\r\n`, and 149 CRLF sequences.
+
+With both settings:
+
+```text
+git -c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf --no-replace-objects archive --format=tar 9a5c41de5ce2878558402665eafaa0a80c09d177 -- <paths above>
+```
+
+The full archive SHA-256 was
+`9f613418037e2cc3bf2415c39e18b2a7d10bbf5ad308b9db7635b63c97518181`. Its helper member SHA-256
+was `ef14f99d1eed7b3af6624015c55404ea1927bec2387e53c5cc67fe749a5cf1cc`, matching the raw
+committed blob. The member was LF-only: line 2 `set -eu\n`, zero CRLF and zero bare-CR bytes.
+
+The comparison was performed in memory using Python's `subprocess`, `tarfile`, and `hashlib`; it did
+not write an archive or extracted files. This confirms the additional Git setting repairs line
+endings in the archive comparison; it does not claim that the committed installer has been updated
+to use both settings or that runtime installation succeeded.

+## Scope and method
+
+Read-only inventory of the in-scope `Ubuntu-24.04` WSL2 distribution for the current S2
+coordinator/configuration task. The inspected project revision was `e3464a9f5d50156b4b242270c498fb2cffb3b927`.
+No test, source install, credential read, service start/enable, network-policy change, or E5 probe
+was performed. Secret file contents were not opened or printed.
+
+Commands used from PowerShell (the initial invocation that returned no output and the malformed,
+non-executed shell-quoting attempt are excluded):
+
+```text
+wsl.exe --list --verbose
+wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc 'id; uname -r; test -e /etc/vst-runner/runner-service.json && stat -c "%U:%G %a %n" /etc/vst-runner/runner-service.json || echo RUNNER_CONFIG_ABSENT; test -e /etc/vst-runner/supervisor-service.json && stat -c "%U:%G %a %n" /etc/vst-runner/supervisor-service.json || echo SUPERVISOR_CONFIG_ABSENT; test -e /etc/vst-runner/signer-service.json && stat -c "%U:%G %a %n" /etc/vst-runner/signer-service.json || echo SIGNER_CONFIG_ABSENT; systemctl is-enabled vst-supervisor.service vst-signer.service vst-runner.service 2>&1 || true; systemctl is-active vst-supervisor.service vst-signer.service vst-runner.service 2>&1 || true; find /etc/vst-runner /var/lib/vst-runner -maxdepth 2 -type f -printf "%u:%g %m %p\n" 2>/dev/null'
+wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc 'printf "WSL_CONF_BEGIN\n"; if test -f /etc/wsl.conf; then cat /etc/wsl.conf; else echo WSL_CONF_ABSENT; fi; printf "KEY_METADATA_BEGIN\n"; if test -d /var/lib/vst/keys; then find /var/lib/vst/keys -maxdepth 1 -type f -printf "%u:%g %m %s %f\n"; else echo VST_KEY_DIR_ABSENT; fi; printf "OLD_PRIVATE_E5_METADATA_BEGIN\n"; if test -e /var/lib/vst/private-e5-final-inventory-8024493e38ba44df96ee5f127a24b338.json; then stat -c "%U:%G %a %s %n" /var/lib/vst/private-e5-final-inventory-8024493e38ba44df96ee5f127a24b338.json; else echo OLD_PRIVATE_E5_ABSENT; fi; printf "SYSTEMD_UNIT_FILES_BEGIN\n"; find /etc/systemd/system -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "vst-*.service" -printf "%u:%g %m %p\n" 2>/dev/null; printf "END\n'
+wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc 'printf "RUNTIME_MANIFEST_BEGIN\n"; if test -f /opt/vst-runtime/.vst-source-manifest.json; then stat -c "%U:%G %a %s %n" /opt/vst-runtime/.vst-source-manifest.json; cat /opt/vst-runtime/.vst-source-manifest.json; else echo RUNTIME_MANIFEST_ABSENT; fi; printf "HELPER_METADATA_BEGIN\n"; find /usr/local/libexec -maxdepth 1 -type f -name "vst-s4-worker-exec-*" -printf "%u:%g %m %s %f\n" 2>/dev/null; printf "UNITS_HASH_BEGIN\n"; sha256sum /etc/systemd/system/vst-runner.service /etc/systemd/system/vst-supervisor.service /etc/systemd/system/vst-signer.service; printf "STORE_DIRS_BEGIN\n"; find /var/lib/vst -maxdepth 2 -type d -printf "%u:%g %m %p\n" 2>/dev/null; printf END'
+wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- bash -lc 'find /var/lib/vst/keys -mindepth 2 -maxdepth 4 -type f -printf "%u:%g %m %s %p\n" 2>/dev/null'
+Get-FileHash tools/vst/systemd/vst-runner.service,tools/vst/systemd/vst-supervisor.service,tools/vst/systemd/vst-signer.service -Algorithm SHA256
+```

+The second command inspected only metadata for private key files and one prior private E5 inventory;

+# S2 database and object-store review
+
+## Review identity
+
+- Review role: `database-reviewer`.
+- Model and effort: GPT-6 Luna, medium effort.
+- Source code reviewed: `1ef3fee07d5743dc8e42c632e1dc3100601116a7`.
+- Repository head during review: `eab4ea5d6363e3f8efa99533a996a5388ffaa48c`; this later commit adds tests/evidence only, not production source.
+- Review scope: `SyntheticOperationBackend` target object accounting, cumulative storage cap, object-write serialization, lock release behavior, and partial import failures in `tools/vst/slice.py`.
+- Evidence consulted: source code, change records 0076-0077, and [`s2-e2e-hook-free-pack-1ef3fee.md`](evidence/s2-e2e-hook-free-pack-1ef3fee.md).
+- No tests, checks, builds, CI, migrations, or runtime operations were run for this review.
+
+## Finding
+
+### MAJOR — an unreaped Git child can outlive the target storage lock
+
+In `tools/vst/slice.py`, `_import_head_locked` starts `pack-objects` and `index-pack` while `_import_head` holds `_target_storage_lock` (`1232-1242`). The timeout callback suppresses errors from `process.kill()` (`1286-1296`). Its `finally` block repeats that suppression and also suppresses a one-second `process.wait()` timeout (`1355-1371`). If `index-pack` remains alive after either condition, `_import_head_locked` can unwind and `_target_storage_lock` can release its OS lock while the child continues writing into `objects/`.
+
+A second backend instance can then acquire the same lock, scan current object-file lengths, reserve capacity, and begin another object write while the first child is still adding files. The serialized-writer assumption and 512 MiB cumulative cap no longer hold. The same race is possible after a non-timeout exception in the streaming path if cleanup cannot terminate and reap the child.
+
+This failure path is not covered by the current E2E evidence: live child termination and post-start overflow cleanup are explicitly `NOT_RUN` because the test policy prohibits process-kill scenarios. The Windows normal lock behavior and WSL POSIX `flock` contention test prove acquisition, contention, and normal release only; they do not prove lock retention when process cleanup fails.
+
+**Required disposition:** treat the target as poisoned and refuse any later object writes if child exit cannot be confirmed, or use a termination/reap strategy that guarantees every writer has exited before releasing the storage lock. Do not suppress cleanup failures and proceed as if the object store were quiescent. The operator is accountable for the delegated S2 task; Codex is the executor. No separate technical service owner for direct target writers is established in canonical project records.
+
+## Other reviewed invariants
+
+- The target object-byte walk recursively counts file lengths under the managed `objects/` directory and rejects symlinked entries. Target Git processes receive a pinned `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`; the backend does not inherit ambient alternate-object-directory variables.
+- Both backend object writers—`hash-object -w` for idempotency blobs and `index-pack` for candidate packs—run while holding the same per-target OS lock and in-process lock. The reservation is made before launching the pack processes. Cross-process lock contention/release is covered on Windows and POSIX by the E2E record.
+- The 512 MiB cap is a backend-managed logical file-length limit. It does not constrain a direct external writer that ignores the advisory lock, filesystem metadata, or files outside `objects/`. The change record explicitly requires a supervisor-owned target and identifies that limitation; no separate disk-quota claim is made.
+- A failed or partial `index-pack` may leave target files. Under the current single-writer assumption, later scans account for those files and subsequent reservations fail closed when insufficient capacity remains. This accounting conclusion is conditional on resolving the unreaped-child finding above.
+- The pack and object-count reservations are conservative by inspection, but no runtime test exercised a maximum-sized pack/index or post-import overflow because the cleanup path would invoke process termination. Keep that scenario `NOT_RUN`.
+
+## Conclusion
+
+The cumulative object-store cap and cross-process serialization are sound for normal backend-managed writes, as covered by the available Windows/WSL lock evidence. One MAJOR remains: cleanup does not prove child exit before releasing the lock, so an orphaned `index-pack` could invalidate both properties. No other database finding is raised in this review.

+# S2 focused functional and runtime test plan
+
+Sprint: `39b7cc253f5d` — active project sprint S2  
+Status: planning only; S2 coding is still in progress. No tests were authored or executed for this plan.
+
+## Purpose and evidence boundary
+
+This plan maps future tests to the accepted S2 stories and numbered acceptance criteria in `docs/sdlc/backlog.md`. It covers the accepted Store-authorized path: `DispatchOwnerService` → authenticated Supervisor/Store admission → Store-filtered Pub/Sub → `StoreBackedDispatcher` → Runner. Store remains the only assignment and lease authority. It does not add another coordinator, scheduler, or assignment authority.
+
+The recorded source/test evidence is bounded:
+
+| Story | Recorded evidence | What it establishes | What it does not establish |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| S2-1, `S2-PROV-M03-R01` | GPT-PM source/test acceptance at `c855ca4`; the linked M03 run record reports 130 passed, 0 failed in Ubuntu 24.04 WSL with Python 3.12.3/pytest 7.4.4. | Source/test behavior for cross-generation historical-result recovery at that revision. | Installed runtime, systemd identity, kernel credentials, current-head equivalence, production issuer/E5, or full S2 acceptance. |
+| S2-2 | GPT-PM transport decision `b0f60d46-42b7-486a-b2f0-5d2253780f55`; `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-dispatch-owner-transport-wsl-run-20261029.md` records 34 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed at HEAD `20fda2c`. | One local AF_UNIX socketpair request/half-close/EOF/response/ACK path through the real `DispatchOwnerService._handle()` method. | Live systemd socket activation, actual PID 1 credentials, kernel peer credentials, pidfd, socket filesystem metadata, provisioned identities/configuration, Store, Runner, or production owner-to-Runner behavior. Those properties were mocked or absent. |
+
+These historical results are not rerun or promoted to current-head proof by this plan. Source/test acceptance of S2-1 and S2-2 is distinct from S2 runtime acceptance. Current disposition remains S2-3 open, S2-4 blocked by `S2-DISPATCH-M01` (MAJOR/OPEN), and S2-5 pending; S2 is NOT APPROVED and S3 remains unstarted (`docs/sdlc/backlog.md`, `docs/sdlc/requirements.md`).
+
+## Execution order and ownership
+
+1. Codex completes accepted S2 source coding, including the immutable bundle/schema validation and inactive-only exact-revision transition described in `docs/sdlc/design.md`. The runtime transition code is not complete, so test authorship and execution must wait.
+2. After coding is complete, `functional-test-reviewer` authors the focused source-level tests in this matrix. `e2e-runner` owns permitted runtime selectors and reports exact command, source HEAD, environment, and result. Neither role may convert a prohibited or unavailable scenario into a pass.
+3. Run source-level cases first. Proceed to permitted runtime qualification only after the exact non-secret bundle has been reviewed by GPT-PM under the recorded conditional scope, required configuration/identities exist, and the Store has been read-only classified. Store disposition `UNKNOWN` blocks initialization; only a separately gated fresh schema-v6 Store may be initialized. Existing Store migration remains behind its separate gate.
+4. Keep affected services inactive through bundle preparation and artifact transition. The initial transition is only for an unconfigured host: `/etc/vst-runner` and runtime socket directories must be absent; all six affected units/socket must be inactive, with no queued systemd jobs or populated VST cgroups. A configured host is refused; upgrades remain out of scope. Each individual rename is atomic; replacing the selector and multiple units is a recoverable sequence, not a single atomic transaction. Store `UNKNOWN` permits selecting already verified inactive artifacts because selection does not open or mutate Store data; it continues to block Store initialization, migration, activation, and dispatch.
+5. GPT-PM's correlated architecture decision `a3e130f0-9aec-4304-b001-388a45c0be55` (reply `0b0b8a4d-0816-4166-ba21-71857b5de49d`) is `MODIFY — DESIGN ONLY`: bounded delegation contracts, pure validators, and read-only measurement collectors may be designed/implemented. Production signing keys/services, E5 contract replacement, and activation are not authorized. The findings `S2-MACHINE-ISSUER-M01` and `S2-MACHINE-E5-M01` remain open pending design and review. This decision is not runtime evidence. See `docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-machine-authority-adjudication-20261029.md`.
+5. After mapped tests and permitted runtime evidence, relevant specialist reviews, and fixes, GPT-PM reviews the exact final head and correlated evidence. A changed head requires a fresh exact-head decision (S2-5 / REQ-006).
+

Every test must assert externally observable state (Store events/lease, selected link/unit bytes, process/unit activity, or actual Runner outcome), not just helper return values.

+## Explicitly prohibited or unavailable coverage
+
+The following remain `NOT_RUN`, not pass, skip, waiver, or implied coverage:
+
+- Process kill, crash recovery, mutation, E8, and all restricted policy selectors (S2-4 AC-3; REQ-006).
+- Real systemd/PID 1 peer authentication, production credentials/keys, current signed E5, and installed production configuration until their genuine prerequisites and separate authorization exist.
+- Existing Store migration and production service activation/dispatch. Store disposition is currently `UNKNOWN`; do not infer that it is fresh.
+- Any scenario that would create/impersonate an issuer or trust key, fabricate an operator-root signature, overwrite/delete an existing runtime/helper, or create a second assignment authority.
+- GPT-PM permits bounded delegation-contract design, pure validators, and read-only measurement collectors only; production signing keys/services and E5 contract replacement remain unauthorized (`docs/sdlc/evidence/s2-machine-authority-adjudication-20261029.md`).
+
+If a permitted scenario cannot run, record `NOT_RUN` with the exact unavailable prerequisite/error, revision, and owner. Never replace it with a synthetic pass. Test evidence is complete only for the mapped acceptance criterion and exact revision that the test actually exercised.

+const pmBridgeRoot = "D:/Repo/pm-bridge/src";
+const projectId = "vst-attachment-fixture";

+const sha256 = (value) => crypto.createHash("sha256").update(value).digest("hex");

+function git(repo, args, input = undefined) {
+  return execFileSync("git", ["-C", repo, ...args], {
+    input,
+    encoding: "utf8",
+    windowsHide: true,
+  }).trim();
+}
+
+function commitFixture(repo, content, parent, message) {
+  const blob = git(repo, ["hash-object", "-w", "--stdin"], content);
+  const tree = git(repo, ["mktree"], `100644 blob ${blob}\tfixture.txt\n`);
+  const parentLine = parent ? `parent ${parent}\n` : "";
+  const raw = `tree ${tree}\n${parentLine}author Fixture <fixture@example.invalid> 1793232000 +0000\ncommitter Fixture <fixture@example.invalid> 1793232000 +0000\n\n${message}\n`;
+  return git(repo, ["hash-object", "-t", "commit", "-w", "--stdin"], raw);
+}
+
+function createFixtureRepo(root) {
+  const repo = path.join(root, "repo");
+  fs.mkdirSync(repo, { recursive: true });
+  execFileSync("git", ["init", "--quiet", "--initial-branch=main", repo], { windowsHide: true });
+  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(repo, "docs", "sdlc"), { recursive: true });
+  const baseSha = commitFixture(repo, "before\n", null, "fixture base");
+  const headSha = commitFixture(repo, "after\n", baseSha, "fixture head");
+  git(repo, ["update-ref", "refs/heads/base", baseSha]);
+  git(repo, ["update-ref", "refs/heads/main", headSha]);
+  return { repo, baseSha, headSha };
+}
+
+async function readJson(req) {
+  const chunks = [];
+  for await (const chunk of req) chunks.push(chunk);
+  return JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8"));
+}
+
+async function listen(server) {
+  await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
+    server.once("error", reject);
+    server.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve);
+  });
+  return server.address().port;
+}

+        if (!durableJob) {
+          res.writeHead(404, { "content-type": "application/json" });

+          return;
+        }
+        res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" });
+        res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, job: durableJob }));
+        return;
+      }
+      if (req.url !== "/send_and_await") {
+        res.writeHead(404, { "content-type": "application/json" });

+      });

+      const replyId = "reply-fixture-1";

+test("native review.js dump-only mode writes the exact canonical prompt and exits before any transport", (t) => {
+  const tempRoot = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "vst-native-review-dump-e2e-"));
+  t.after(() => fs.rmSync(tempRoot, { recursive: true, force: true }));
+

+  const configDir = path.join(tempRoot, "pm-config");
+  const stateDir = path.join(tempRoot, "pm-state");
+  const runtimeDir = path.join(tempRoot, "pm-runtime");
+  const packetPath = path.join(tempRoot, "scope-packet.md");
+  const dumpPath = path.join(tempRoot, "canonical-prompt.txt");
+  const receiptsPath = path.join(tempRoot, "receipts.jsonl");
+  const registryPath = path.join(configDir, "projects.json");
+  const project = {
+    projectId,
+    displayName: "Synthetic AF attachment review fixture",
+    repoUrl: null,
+    repoRoots: [repo],
+    conversationId: "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333",
+    createdAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+    updatedAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
+  };
+  fs.mkdirSync(configDir, { recursive: true });
+  fs.writeFileSync(registryPath, `${JSON.stringify({ version: 1, projects: [project] }, null, 2)}\n`);
+  const scopeNote = "Synthetic scope packet: prove the native prompt dump path and stop before transport.";
+  fs.writeFileSync(packetPath, `${scopeNote}\n`, "utf8");
+
+  const nativeReview = "D:/Repo/pm-bridge/src/cli/review.js";
+  const command = [
+    nativeReview,
+    "--cwd", repo,
+    "--base", baseSha,
+    "--project", projectId,
+    "--final",
+    "--scope-note-file", packetPath,
+  ];
+  const env = {
+    PATH: process.env.PATH ?? "",
+    SystemRoot: process.env.SystemRoot ?? "",
+    WINDIR: process.env.WINDIR ?? "",
+    TEMP: tempRoot,
+    TMP: tempRoot,
+    USERPROFILE: tempRoot,
+    HOME: tempRoot,
+    PM_BRIDGE_EXECUTION_ROOT: "D:/Repo/pm-bridge",
+    PM_BRIDGE_SOURCE_ROOT: "D:/Repo/pm-bridge",
+    PM_BRIDGE_RUNTIME_ROOT: runtimeDir,
+    PM_BRIDGE_CONFIG_DIR: configDir,
+    PM_BRIDGE_STATE_DIR: stateDir,
+    PM_BRIDGE_GENERATIONS_DIR: path.join(runtimeDir, "generations"),
+    PM_BRIDGE_RECEIPTS_FILE: receiptsPath,
+    PM_BRIDGE_BROWSER_LOCK_PATH: path.join(runtimeDir, "browser.lock"),
+    PM_BRIDGE_DEBUG_DUMP_PROMPT: dumpPath,
+    PM_BRIDGE_DEBUG_DUMP_PROMPT_ONLY: "1",
+    PM_BRIDGE_NO_EXECUTION_AUTHORITY: "1",
+    PM_BRIDGE_BREAK_GLASS_DIRECT: "0",
+  };
+  const processResult = execFileSync(process.execPath, command, {
+    cwd: tempRoot,
+    env,
+    encoding: "utf8",
+    windowsHide: true,
+    timeout: 30000,
+  });
+  const diagnostic = JSON.parse(processResult.trim().split(/\r?\n/).at(-1));
+  assert.equal(diagnostic.diagnostic, true);
+  assert.match(diagnostic.error, /dumped prompt, skipped transport/);
+  assert.equal(diagnostic.ok, false, "dump-only is preflight evidence, not a successful review");
+
+  const actualBytes = fs.readFileSync(dumpPath);
+  const actualHash = sha256(actualBytes);
+  const diff = execFileSync("git", ["-C", repo, "diff", `${baseSha}...${headSha}`, "--", ".", ":(exclude)reports"], {
+    encoding: "utf8",
+    windowsHide: true,
+  });
+  const scopeBlock =
+    `Scope of THIS round -- read before reviewing:\n${scopeNote}\n\n` +
+    "Findings outside that scope are still welcome, but mark them explicitly as out-of-scope " +
+    "and do NOT let them set the VERDICT line: the verdict must answer the scoped question. " +
+    "If the scoped question is genuinely satisfied, say APPROVE even when out-of-scope work " +
+    "remains -- an unrelated open item is not a reason to withhold a verdict on this one.\n\n";
+  const expectedPrompt =
+    `Code review request for project "${projectId}".\n\n` +
+    scopeBlock +
+    "Reply with a VERDICT line first (APPROVE, or BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR findings), then " +
+    "each finding as: severity | claim | evidence | failure scenario | required change.\n\n" +
+    "Apply a devil's-advocate stance throughout: actively look for reasons this change " +
+    "is wrong, unsafe, incomplete, or will break something, rather than defaulting to " +
+    "approval. This does not license inventing problems that aren't real: every " +
+    "objection still needs the same real file/line evidence required above -- if after " +
+    "genuinely trying to find a problem there is none, say so plainly rather than " +
+    "manufacturing a NIT to seem thorough.\n\n" +
+    "Diff:\n```diff\n" + diff + "\n```";
+  const expectedBytes = Buffer.from(expectedPrompt, "utf8");
+  const expectedHash = sha256(expectedBytes);
+  assert.deepEqual(actualBytes, expectedBytes, "native dump must byte-match the independently assembled canonical prompt");
+  assert.equal(actualHash, expectedHash, "dump hash must match the canonical expected prompt hash");
+  assert.ok(actualBytes.includes(Buffer.from(scopeNote, "utf8")));
+  assert.ok(actualBytes.includes(Buffer.from(diff, "utf8")));
