+"""Root-only persistent admission fence for ambiguous dispatch-owner outcomes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import time
+
+LATCH_PATH = "/etc/vst-runner/dispatch-owner-admission-blocked.json"
+SOCKET_UNIT = "vst-dispatch-owner.socket"
+SYSTEMCTL_PATH = "/usr/bin/systemctl"
+SYSTEMCTL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10
+SOCKET_STOP_RETRY_INITIAL_SECONDS = 1
+SOCKET_STOP_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS = 30
+_LOGGER = logging.getLogger("vst.dispatch_owner_latch")
+_ALLOWED_RESULTS = frozenset({
+    "protocol", "timeout", "exit-code", "signal", "core-dump", "watchdog",
+    "exec-condition", "oom-kill", "killed", "start-limit-hit", "resources", "success",
+})
+
+
+def _check_root_parent(path: str) -> str:
+    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
+    current = parent
+    while True:
+        info = os.stat(current, follow_symlinks=False)
+        if (not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0
+                or stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) & 0o022):
+            raise RuntimeError("dispatch-owner admission directory is not root-controlled")
+        if current == "/":
+            break
+        current = os.path.dirname(current)
+    return parent
+
+
+def _write_latch(result: str, exit_code: str, exit_status: str) -> None:
+    parent = _check_root_parent(LATCH_PATH)
+    payload = json.dumps({
+        "exit_code": exit_code[:32],
+        "exit_status": exit_status[:32],
+        "service_result": result,
+        "state": "BLOCKED",
+        "unit": "vst-dispatch-owner.service",
+        "version": 1,
+    }, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode("ascii") + b"\n"
+    flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL
+    if hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW"):
+        flags |= os.O_NOFOLLOW
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(LATCH_PATH, flags, 0o644)
+    except FileExistsError:
+        info = os.stat(LATCH_PATH, follow_symlinks=False)
+        if (not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0
+                or info.st_gid != 0 or stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != 0o644):
+            raise RuntimeError("existing dispatch-owner admission fence is invalid")
+        return
+    try:
+        os.fchown(fd, 0, 0)
+        os.fchmod(fd, 0o644)
+        offset = 0
+        while offset < len(payload):
+            written = os.write(fd, payload[offset:])
+            if written < 1:
+                raise OSError("short write while persisting dispatch-owner admission fence")
+            offset += written
+        os.fsync(fd)
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+    dir_fd = os.open(parent, os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY", 0))
+    try:
+        os.fsync(dir_fd)
+    finally:
+        os.close(dir_fd)
+
+
+def _stop_socket_and_confirm_inactive() -> None:
+    """Keep the service stop hook alive until socket admission is actually closed."""
+    delay = SOCKET_STOP_RETRY_INITIAL_SECONDS
+    while True:
+        try:
+            stopped = subprocess.run(
+                [SYSTEMCTL_PATH, "stop", SOCKET_UNIT],
+                check=False,
+                timeout=SYSTEMCTL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+            )
+            state = subprocess.run(
+                [SYSTEMCTL_PATH, "show", "--property=ActiveState", "--value", SOCKET_UNIT],
+                check=False,
+                timeout=SYSTEMCTL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
+                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                text=True,
+            )
+            active_state = state.stdout.strip() if state.returncode == 0 else "unknown"
+            if stopped.returncode == 0 and active_state == "inactive":
+                _LOGGER.info("dispatch-owner socket is confirmed inactive")
+                return
+            _LOGGER.critical(
+                "dispatch-owner socket stop is not confirmed (stop=%s, state=%s); retrying",
+                stopped.returncode,
+                active_state,
+            )
+        except Exception:
+            _LOGGER.exception("dispatch-owner socket stop could not be confirmed; retrying")
+        time.sleep(delay)
+        delay = min(delay * 2, SOCKET_STOP_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    if os.geteuid() != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError("dispatch-owner admission fence requires root")
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s")
+    result = os.environ.get("SERVICE_RESULT", "")
+    if result not in _ALLOWED_RESULTS:
+        result = "resources"
+    # Close the live admission path before touching /etc: parent stat/open/fsync can block on
+    # unhealthy storage. A confirmed stop protects this boot even if persistence then fails.
+    _stop_socket_and_confirm_inactive()
+    latch_error: Exception | None = None
+    try:
+        _write_latch(
+            result,
+            os.environ.get("EXIT_CODE", "unknown"),
+            os.environ.get("EXIT_STATUS", "unknown"),
+        )
+        _LOGGER.error("dispatch-owner admission fenced after service termination (%s)", result)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        latch_error = exc
+        _LOGGER.exception("dispatch-owner admission latch could not be persisted")
+    if latch_error is not None:
+        raise RuntimeError("dispatch-owner admission could not be durably fenced") from latch_error
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Socket-activated signed-instruction relay for the S2 root Supervisor."""

+from dataclasses import dataclass

+    DISPATCH_INSTRUCTION_PURPOSE, DISPATCH_INSTRUCTION_TRUST_REGISTRY_PATH,
+)

+_LOGGER = logging.getLogger("vst.dispatch_owner")

+def _unique_json_object(pairs: list[tuple[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    result: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    for key, value in pairs:
+        if key in result:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner JSON contains a duplicate field")
+        result[key] = value
+    return result
+
+
+def _read_root_json(path: str, *, expected_mode: int, expected_gid: int,
+                    max_bytes: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not os.path.isabs(path):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted file path is invalid")
+    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
+    while True:
+        try:
+            info = os.stat(parent, follow_symlinks=False)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted-file directory is unavailable") from exc
+        if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0 or info.st_mode & 0o022:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted-file directory is not root-controlled")
+        if parent == "/":
+            break
+        parent = os.path.dirname(parent)
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted file is unavailable") from exc
+    try:
+        info = os.fstat(fd)
+        if (not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0
+                or info.st_gid != expected_gid
+                or stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != expected_mode
+                or info.st_size > max_bytes):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted-file owner, mode, or size is invalid")
+        raw = bytearray()
+        while len(raw) <= max_bytes:
+            chunk = os.read(fd, min(65536, max_bytes + 1 - len(raw)))
+            if not chunk:
+                break
+            raw.extend(chunk)
+        if len(raw) > max_bytes:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted file exceeds its size limit")
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+    try:
+        value = json.loads(raw, object_pairs_hook=_unique_json_object)
+    except (ValueError, TypeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted file is malformed JSON") from exc
+    if not isinstance(value, dict):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner trusted file must be a JSON object")
+    return value
+
+
+def load_dispatch_owner_config(path: str = DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH) -> "DispatchOwnerServiceConfig":
+    if os.path.lexists(DISPATCH_OWNER_ADMISSION_LATCH_PATH):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner admission is blocked pending reconciliation")
+    if os.geteuid() == 0 or os.getgid() < 1:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner service must run under its dedicated unprivileged identity")
+    try:
+        with open("/proc/self/cgroup", encoding="ascii") as stream:
+            rows = [line.rstrip("\n").split(":", 2) for line in stream]
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner service cgroup is unavailable") from exc
+    cgroup = next((row[2] for row in rows if len(row) == 3 and row[:2] == ["0", ""]), None)
+    if cgroup != "/system.slice/vst-dispatch-owner.service":
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner service is outside its fixed systemd cgroup")
+    config = _read_root_json(
+        path, expected_mode=0o640, expected_gid=os.getgid(), max_bytes=65536,
+    )
+    if set(config) != {"principal", "openssl_path"}:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner config fields do not match its fixed schema")
+    if config != {"principal": OWNER_PRINCIPAL, "openssl_path": OPENSSL_PATH}:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner config does not match its fixed trust boundary")
+    registry = _read_root_json(
+        TRUST_REGISTRY_PATH, expected_mode=0o644, expected_gid=0, max_bytes=65536,
+    )
+    _validate_trust_registry(registry)
+    return DispatchOwnerServiceConfig(
+        principal=config["principal"], openssl_path=config["openssl_path"],
+        trust_registry=registry,
+    )
+
+
+def _validate_trust_registry(registry: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+    if not registry:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public trust registry is empty")
+    for key_id, entry in registry.items():
+        if (not isinstance(key_id, str)
+                or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,127}", key_id)
+                or not isinstance(entry, dict)
+                or set(entry) != {"principal", "purpose", "public_key_path"}
+                or entry.get("principal") != OWNER_PRINCIPAL
+                or entry.get("purpose") != DISPATCH_INSTRUCTION_PURPOSE
+                or not isinstance(entry.get("public_key_path"), str)
+                or not os.path.isabs(entry["public_key_path"])):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public trust registry is malformed")
+        _validate_root_public_key(entry["public_key_path"])
+
+
+def _validate_root_public_key(path: str) -> None:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW") or not os.path.isabs(path):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public key path is invalid")
+    parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
+    while True:
+        try:
+            info = os.stat(parent, follow_symlinks=False)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public-key directory is unavailable") from exc
+        if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0 or info.st_mode & 0o022:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public-key directory is not root-controlled")
+        if parent == "/":
+            break
+        parent = os.path.dirname(parent)
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public key is unavailable") from exc
+    try:
+        info = os.fstat(fd)
+        if (not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0 or info.st_gid != 0
+                or stat.S_IMODE(info.st_mode) != 0o644 or info.st_size > 65536):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch instruction public key owner, mode, or size is invalid")
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DispatchOwnerServiceConfig:
+    principal: str
+    openssl_path: str
+    trust_registry: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, str]]
+
+
+class DispatchOwnerService:
+    """Relay signed instructions; task assignment authority remains in Store/Supervisor."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config: DispatchOwnerServiceConfig,
+                 supervisor: Any | None = None) -> None:
+        if config.principal != OWNER_PRINCIPAL or config.openssl_path != OPENSSL_PATH:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner service configuration is not fixed")
+        self.client = DispatchOwnerClient(
+            principal=config.principal,
+            trust_registry=config.trust_registry,
+            openssl_path=config.openssl_path,
+            transport=(supervisor if supervisor is not None else SupervisorClient(
+                SUPERVISOR_SOCKET_PATH, timeout_sec=REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC,
+            )),
+        )
+        self._shutdown = threading.Event()
+        self._outcome_unknown = False
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        self._shutdown.set()
+
+    def serve_forever(self, listener: socket.socket) -> None:
+        if (listener.family != socket.AF_UNIX
+                or listener.getsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_TYPE) != socket.SOCK_STREAM
+                or listener.getsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_ACCEPTCONN) != 1
+                or listener.getsockname() != OWNER_SOCKET_PATH):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner activation socket is not the fixed local listener")
+        listener.settimeout(0.5)
+        while not self._shutdown.is_set():
+            try:
+                conn, _ = listener.accept()
+            except socket.timeout:
+                continue
+            with conn:
+                if self._handle(conn):
+                    self._outcome_unknown = True
+                    self._shutdown.set()
+                    return
+
+    def _handle(self, conn: socket.socket) -> bool:
+        conn.settimeout(REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC)
+        outcome_unknown = False
+        accepted_result: dict | None = None
+        try:
+            header = _recv_exact(conn, _HEADER.size)
+            length = _HEADER.unpack(header)[0]
+            if length < 2 or length > MAX_REQUEST_BYTES:
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner request size is invalid")
+            payload = _recv_exact(conn, length)
+            if conn.recv(1) != b"":
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner connection contains trailing request bytes")
+            request = json.loads(payload, object_pairs_hook=_unique_json_object)
+            if (not isinstance(request, dict) or set(request) != {"instruction"}
+                    or canonical_bytes(request) != payload):
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner request does not match the exact envelope")
+            try:
+                result = self.client.submit(request["instruction"])
+            except DispatchOutcomeUnknown as exc:
+                _LOGGER.error("dispatch-owner Supervisor outcome is unknown (%s)", type(exc).__name__)
+                outcome_unknown = True
+                response = {"ok": False, "error": "reconciliation_required"}
+            else:
+                accepted_result = result
+                response = {"ok": True, "result": result}
+        except Exception as exc:
+            _LOGGER.warning("dispatch-owner request refused (%s)", type(exc).__name__)
+            response = {"ok": False, "error": "refused"}
+        encoded = canonical_bytes(response)
+        if len(encoded) > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
+            encoded = canonical_bytes({"ok": False, "error": "response_too_large"})
+            if accepted_result is not None:
+                outcome_unknown = True
+        try:
+            conn.sendall(_HEADER.pack(len(encoded)) + encoded)
+        except OSError:
+            if accepted_result is not None:
+                outcome_unknown = True
+            return outcome_unknown
+        if accepted_result is not None and not outcome_unknown:
+            try:
+                self.client.acknowledge_forwarded(accepted_result)
+            except DispatchOutcomeUnknown as exc:
+                _LOGGER.error("dispatch-owner outcome acknowledgement is unknown (%s)", type(exc).__name__)
+                outcome_unknown = True
+        return outcome_unknown
+
+
+def _recv_exact(conn: socket.socket, count: int) -> bytes:
+    chunks = bytearray()
+    while len(chunks) < count:
+        part = conn.recv(count - len(chunks))
+        if not part:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner request frame ended early")
+        chunks.extend(part)
+    return bytes(chunks)
+
+
+def _systemd_listener() -> socket.socket:
+    if (os.environ.get("LISTEN_PID") != str(os.getpid())
+            or os.environ.get("LISTEN_FDS") != "1"
+            or os.environ.get("LISTEN_FDNAMES") != "dispatch-owner"):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner requires its exact systemd socket activation descriptor")
+    for key in ("LISTEN_PID", "LISTEN_FDS", "LISTEN_FDNAMES"):
+        os.environ.pop(key, None)
+    try:
+        listener = socket.socket(fileno=3)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner activation descriptor is unavailable") from exc
+    listener.set_inheritable(False)
+    return listener
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX"):
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner requires POSIX Unix sockets")
+    if len(sys.argv) != 1:
+        raise ContractError("dispatch-owner does not accept command-line configuration")
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s")
+    service = DispatchOwnerService(load_dispatch_owner_config())
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda _signum, _frame: service.shutdown())
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda _signum, _frame: service.shutdown())
+    listener = _systemd_listener()
+    try:
+        service.serve_forever(listener)
+    finally:
+        listener.close()
+    if service._outcome_unknown:
+        raise SystemExit(OUTCOME_UNKNOWN_EXIT)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Transport-only client for submitting an already signed dispatch instruction."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import select
+import socket
+import stat
+import struct
+from typing import Any
+
+from .contracts import ContractError, canonical_bytes
+from .dispatch_instruction import validate_dispatch_instruction
+from .dispatch_owner_client import DispatchOutcomeUnknown
+
+OWNER_SOCKET_PATH = "/run/vst-supervisor/dispatch-owner.sock"
+REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC = 10.0
+MAX_REQUEST_BYTES = 64 * 1024
+MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 256 * 1024
+_HEADER = struct.Struct("!I")
+
+
+class DispatchOwnerSocketClient:
+    """Forward one exact signed envelope; never select, sign, or retry work."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *, expected_principal: str, expected_socket_gid: int,
+                 socket_path: str = OWNER_SOCKET_PATH,
+                 timeout_sec: float = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SEC) -> None:
+        if (os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(socket, "AF_UNIX")
+                or not hasattr(socket, "SO_PEERCRED")
+                or getattr(socket, "SO_PEERPIDFD", None) is None):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner transport requires POSIX Unix-socket support")
+        if socket_path != OWNER_SOCKET_PATH:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket path is fixed")
+        if not isinstance(expected_principal, str) or not expected_principal.strip():
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner principal is invalid")
+        if type(expected_socket_gid) is not int or expected_socket_gid < 0:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket group is invalid")
+        if (isinstance(timeout_sec, bool) or not isinstance(timeout_sec, (int, float))
+                or not 0.1 <= timeout_sec <= 30.0):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket timeout is outside its allowed range")
+        self.socket_path = socket_path
+        self.expected_principal = expected_principal
+        self.expected_socket_gid = expected_socket_gid
+        self.timeout_sec = float(timeout_sec)
+
+    def submit_signed_instruction(self, instruction: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        envelope = validate_dispatch_instruction(instruction)
+        request = canonical_bytes({"instruction": envelope})
+        if len(request) > MAX_REQUEST_BYTES:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner request exceeds its size limit")
+        self._validate_socket_path()
+
+        client = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
+        client.settimeout(self.timeout_sec)
+        pidfd: int | None = None
+        try:
+            try:
+                client.connect(self.socket_path)
+                raw_creds = client.getsockopt(
+                    socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_PEERCRED, struct.calcsize("3i"),
+                )
+                if not isinstance(raw_creds, bytes) or len(raw_creds) != struct.calcsize("3i"):
+                    raise ContractError("kernel returned malformed dispatch-owner peer credentials")
+                peer_pid, peer_uid, _peer_gid = struct.unpack("3i", raw_creds)
+                if peer_pid != 1 or peer_uid != 0:
+                    raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket peer is not systemd PID 1")
+                pidfd = self._peer_pidfd(client, peer_pid)
+            except OSError as exc:
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket endpoint is unavailable or unauthenticated") from exc
+            except ContractError:
+                raise
+
+            try:
+                client.sendall(_HEADER.pack(len(request)) + request)
+                client.shutdown(socket.SHUT_WR)
+                response = self._read_response(client)
+            except (OSError, ContractError) as exc:
+                raise DispatchOutcomeUnknown(
+                    "dispatch-owner outcome is unknown; do not retry the submission"
+                ) from exc
+            if not self._peer_is_alive(pidfd):
+                raise DispatchOutcomeUnknown(
+                    "dispatch-owner systemd socket peer exited during submission"
+                )
+        finally:
+            client.close()
+            if pidfd is not None:
+                os.close(pidfd)
+
+        if response == {"ok": False, "error": "refused"}:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner refused the signed instruction")
+        if response == {"ok": False, "error": "reconciliation_required"}:
+            raise DispatchOutcomeUnknown(
+                "dispatch-owner requires reconciliation; do not retry the submission"
+            )
+        if (not isinstance(response, dict) or set(response) != {"ok", "result"}
+                or response["ok"] is not True or not isinstance(response["result"], dict)):
+            raise DispatchOutcomeUnknown("dispatch-owner returned an unrecognized outcome")
+
+        result = response["result"]
+        if (result.get("principal") != self.expected_principal
+                or result.get("instruction") != envelope
+                or result.get("key_id") != envelope["key_id"]
+                or any(result.get(field) != envelope[field] for field in (
+                    "task_id", "slot", "attempt", "epoch", "run_id", "request_id",
+                ))):
+            raise DispatchOutcomeUnknown("dispatch-owner result does not match the submitted envelope")
+        return result
+
+    def _validate_socket_path(self) -> None:
+        try:
+            parent = os.lstat(os.path.dirname(self.socket_path))
+            endpoint = os.lstat(self.socket_path)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket path is unavailable") from exc
+        if (not stat.S_ISDIR(parent.st_mode) or parent.st_uid != 0
+                or parent.st_gid != self.expected_socket_gid
+                or stat.S_IMODE(parent.st_mode) != 0o710):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket directory identity is unauthorized")
+        if (not stat.S_ISSOCK(endpoint.st_mode) or endpoint.st_uid != 0
+                or endpoint.st_gid != self.expected_socket_gid
+                or stat.S_IMODE(endpoint.st_mode) != 0o660):
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner socket inode identity is unauthorized")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _peer_pidfd(client: socket.socket, peer_pid: int) -> int:
+        option = getattr(socket, "SO_PEERPIDFD", None)
+        if option is None:
+            raise ContractError("kernel peer pidfd support is unavailable")
+        raw = client.getsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, option, struct.calcsize("i"))
+        if not isinstance(raw, bytes) or len(raw) != struct.calcsize("i"):
+            raise ContractError("kernel did not return a peer pidfd")
+        pidfd = struct.unpack("i", raw)[0]
+        if pidfd < 0:
+            raise ContractError("kernel returned an invalid peer pidfd")
+        try:
+            os.set_inheritable(pidfd, False)
+            if not DispatchOwnerSocketClient._peer_is_alive(pidfd):
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner systemd socket peer has exited")
+        except Exception:
+            os.close(pidfd)
+            raise
+        return pidfd
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _peer_is_alive(pidfd: int | None) -> bool:
+        if pidfd is None:
+            return False
+        poller = select.poll()
+        poller.register(pidfd, select.POLLIN | select.POLLHUP | select.POLLERR)
+        return not poller.poll(0)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _read_response(client: socket.socket) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        header = DispatchOwnerSocketClient._recv_exact(client, _HEADER.size)
+        length = _HEADER.unpack(header)[0]
+        if length < 2 or length > MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner response size is invalid")
+        payload = DispatchOwnerSocketClient._recv_exact(client, length)
+        if client.recv(1) != b"":
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner response contains trailing bytes")
+        try:
+            response = json.loads(payload)
+        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner response is malformed JSON") from exc
+        if not isinstance(response, dict) or canonical_bytes(response) != payload:
+            raise ContractError("dispatch-owner response is not canonical JSON")
+        return response
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _recv_exact(client: socket.socket, size: int) -> bytes:
+        result = bytearray()
+        while len(result) < size:
+            chunk = client.recv(size - len(result))
+            if not chunk:
+                raise ContractError("dispatch-owner response ended early")
+            result.extend(chunk)
+        return bytes(result)

+"""Fail-closed Store-backed pub/sub adapter for exact VST dispatch intents."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import signal
+import sys
+import threading
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+from .contracts import ContractError
+from .runner_service import (
+    MAX_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SEC, _read_root_controlled_json, dispatch_manifest_run,
+)
+from .supervisor_service import SupervisorClient
+
+DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = "/etc/vst-runner/dispatcher-service.json"
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DispatcherServiceConfig:
+    supervisor_socket: str
+    runner_socket: str
+    idle_poll_sec: float = 0.25
+    rpc_timeout_sec: float = 5.0
+
+
+def load_dispatcher_service_config(
+    path: str = DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH,
+) -> DispatcherServiceConfig:
+    value = _read_root_controlled_json(path, max_bytes=65536)
+    required = {"supervisor_socket", "runner_socket"}
+    optional = {"idle_poll_sec", "rpc_timeout_sec"}
+    if set(value) - required - optional or not required <= set(value):
+        raise ContractError("dispatcher service configuration fields do not match its schema")
+    for field in ("supervisor_socket", "runner_socket"):
+        if not isinstance(value[field], str) or not os.path.isabs(value[field]):
+            raise ContractError(f"dispatcher service {field} must be an absolute path")
+    for field, default, maximum in (
+        ("idle_poll_sec", 0.25, 5.0), ("rpc_timeout_sec", 5.0, 30.0),
+    ):
+        number = value.get(field, default)
+        if (isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, (int, float))
+                or not 0.01 <= number <= maximum):
+            raise ContractError(f"dispatcher service {field} is outside its allowed range")
+    return DispatcherServiceConfig(
+        supervisor_socket=value["supervisor_socket"],
+        runner_socket=value["runner_socket"],
+        idle_poll_sec=float(value.get("idle_poll_sec", 0.25)),
+        rpc_timeout_sec=float(value.get("rpc_timeout_sec", 5.0)),
+    )
+
+
+class StoreBackedDispatcher:
+    """Consume only Supervisor-filtered intents; never enumerate or select tasks."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config: DispatcherServiceConfig):
+        self.config = config
+        self.supervisor = SupervisorClient(
+            config.supervisor_socket, timeout_sec=config.rpc_timeout_sec,
+        )
+        self._shutdown = threading.Event()
+        self._cursor: dict[str, Any] | None = None
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        self._shutdown.set()
+
+    def serve_forever(self) -> None:
+        while not self._shutdown.is_set():
+            delivery = self.supervisor.next_dispatch_intent(self._cursor)
+            intent = delivery["intent"]
+            if intent is None:
+                self._cursor = delivery["cursor_idle"]
+                self._shutdown.wait(self.config.idle_poll_sec)
+                continue
+            request_id = intent.get("request_id")
+            if not isinstance(request_id, str):
+                raise ContractError("Supervisor delivered an intent without a request id")
+            grant = self.supervisor.issue_dispatch_grant(request_id)
+            deadline = grant.get("execution_deadline_sec")
+            if type(deadline) is not int or deadline < 1:
+                raise ContractError("Supervisor returned a grant with an invalid execution deadline")
+            timeout = min(MAX_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SEC, float(deadline + 120))
+            # Cursor advances only after a complete receipt. Any ambiguous RPC or runner outcome
+            # stops this service; restart replays the same event and the one-use grant fences it.
+            dispatch_manifest_run(
+                self.config.runner_socket, grant, timeout_sec=timeout,
+            )
+            self._cursor = delivery["cursor_after"]
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(signal, "SIGTERM"):
+        raise ContractError("VST dispatcher requires POSIX signal and Unix-socket support")
+    config_path = DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH
+    if len(sys.argv) == 2:
+        config_path = sys.argv[1]
+    elif len(sys.argv) > 2:
+        raise ContractError("dispatcher service accepts only one fixed config path")
+    config = load_dispatcher_service_config(config_path)
+    service = StoreBackedDispatcher(config)
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda _signum, _frame: service.shutdown())
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, lambda _signum, _frame: service.shutdown())
+    service.serve_forever()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Signed, one-invocation authority for the persistent runner boundary.
+
+This module validates grant shape and signature only. The caller must still
+recheck current Store authority, claim and reserve the grant before spawning a child;
+signature validity alone never authorizes execution.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import base64
+import hashlib
+import math
+import os
+import re
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import tempfile
+import time
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from .contracts import ContractError, canonical_bytes
+
+EXECUTION_GRANT_LABEL = b"VST_EXECUTION_GRANT_V1\0"
+EXECUTION_GRANT_VERSION = 1
+MAX_EXECUTION_DEADLINE_SEC = 1800
+GRANT_CLAIM_WINDOW_SEC = 30
+GRANT_COMPLETION_SLACK_SEC = 90
+_IDENTIFIER = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,127}$")
+_SHA256 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
+_FIELDS = frozenset({
+    "version", "key_id", "grant_id", "request_id", "audience",
+    "service_generation", "manifest_sha256", "task_id", "slot", "attempt",
+    "epoch", "run_id", "invocation_id", "runner_id", "resolved_model",
+    "model_provenance_sha256", "execution_deadline_sec",
+    "issued_at", "claim_expires_at", "expires_at", "signature",
+})
+_RUN_CONTEXT_FIELDS = frozenset({
+    "manifest_sha256", "task_id", "slot", "attempt", "epoch", "run_id",
+    "invocation_id", "request_id", "runner_id", "resolved_model",
+    "model_provenance_sha256", "execution_deadline_sec", "service_generation",
+})
+
+
+class AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(ContractError):
+    """A claim/reservation may be durable, so this daemon generation must exit."""
+
+
+def _identifier(value: object, field: str) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not _IDENTIFIER.fullmatch(value):
+        raise ContractError(f"execution grant {field}: invalid identifier")
+    return value
+
+
+def validate_execution_grant(value: object) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Validate the canonical grant envelope without trusting its signature."""
+    if not isinstance(value, dict) or set(value) != _FIELDS:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: fields do not match v1 contract")
+    if type(value["version"]) is not int or value["version"] != EXECUTION_GRANT_VERSION:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: unsupported version")
+    for field in (
+        "key_id", "grant_id", "request_id", "audience", "service_generation",
+        "task_id", "slot", "run_id", "invocation_id", "runner_id", "resolved_model",
+    ):
+        _identifier(value[field], field)
+    for field in ("manifest_sha256", "model_provenance_sha256"):
+        if not isinstance(value[field], str) or not _SHA256.fullmatch(value[field]):
+            raise ContractError(f"execution grant {field}: expected lowercase SHA-256")
+    for field in ("attempt", "epoch"):
+        number = value[field]
+        if type(number) is not int or number < 1 or number > 2**63 - 1:
+            raise ContractError(f"execution grant {field}: expected positive bounded integer")
+    for field in ("execution_deadline_sec",):
+        number = value[field]
+        if type(number) is not int or number < 1 or number > MAX_EXECUTION_DEADLINE_SEC:
+            raise ContractError(
+                f"execution grant {field}: expected integer in 1..{MAX_EXECUTION_DEADLINE_SEC}"
+            )
+    for field in ("issued_at", "claim_expires_at", "expires_at"):
+        number = value[field]
+        if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, (int, float)):
+            raise ContractError(f"execution grant {field}: expected finite timestamp")
+        if not math.isfinite(number) or number < 0:
+            raise ContractError(f"execution grant {field}: expected finite timestamp")
+    if not (value["issued_at"] < value["claim_expires_at"] < value["expires_at"]):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: claim and completion expiries are out of order")
+    signature = value["signature"]
+    if not isinstance(signature, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{86}", signature):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: malformed Ed25519 signature")
+    try:
+        decoded = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(signature + "==")
+    except (ValueError, base64.binascii.Error) as exc:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: malformed Ed25519 signature") from exc
+    if len(decoded) != 64 or base64.urlsafe_b64encode(decoded).decode("ascii").rstrip("=") != signature:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: malformed Ed25519 signature")
+    return value
+
+
+def _trusted_root_file(path: str, *, private: bool) -> None:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW") or not os.path.isabs(path):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant keys require absolute POSIX paths without symlinks")
+    parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
+    while True:
+        try:
+            info = os.stat(parent, follow_symlinks=False)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise ContractError("execution grant key directory is unavailable") from exc
+        if (not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0 or info.st_mode & 0o022):
+            raise ContractError("execution grant key directory is not root-controlled")
+        if parent == "/":
+            break
+        parent = os.path.dirname(parent)
+    try:
+        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant key file is unavailable") from exc
+    try:
+        info = os.fstat(fd)
+        if (not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0
+                or (info.st_mode & 0o077 if private else info.st_mode & 0o022)):
+            raise ContractError("execution grant key file permissions are unsafe")
+    finally:
+        os.close(fd)
+
+
+def _trusted_openssl(path: str) -> str:
+    if os.name != "posix" or not os.path.isabs(path):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant OpenSSL path must be absolute on POSIX")
+    path = os.path.realpath(path)
+    try:
+        info = os.stat(path, follow_symlinks=False)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant OpenSSL executable is unavailable") from exc
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_uid != 0 or info.st_mode & 0o022:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant OpenSSL executable is not root-controlled")
+    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
+    while True:
+        try:
+            directory = os.stat(parent, follow_symlinks=False)
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise ContractError("execution grant OpenSSL directory is unavailable") from exc
+        if (not stat.S_ISDIR(directory.st_mode) or directory.st_uid != 0
+                or directory.st_mode & 0o022):
+            raise ContractError("execution grant OpenSSL directory is not root-controlled")
+        if parent == "/":
+            break
+        parent = os.path.dirname(parent)
+    return path
+
+
+def _input_file(data: bytes):
+    stream = tempfile.TemporaryFile(mode="w+b")
+    stream.write(data)
+    stream.flush()
+    stream.seek(0)
+    return stream
+
+
+def _openssl_signature(
+    openssl_path: str, *, key_path: str, payload: bytes,
+    signature: bytes | None = None, private: bool,
+) -> bytes | bool:
+    executable = _trusted_openssl(openssl_path)
+    _trusted_root_file(key_path, private=private)
+    data_file = _input_file(payload)
+    signature_file = None if private else _input_file(signature or b"")
+    try:
+        argv = [executable, "pkeyutl", "-sign" if private else "-verify", "-rawin"]
+        if not private:
+            argv.append("-pubin")
+        argv.extend(["-inkey", key_path])
+        if private:
+            argv.extend(["-in", f"/proc/self/fd/{data_file.fileno()}"])
+        else:
+            assert signature_file is not None
+            argv.extend([
+                "-in", f"/proc/self/fd/{data_file.fileno()}",
+                "-sigfile", f"/proc/self/fd/{signature_file.fileno()}",
+            ])
+        inherited = (data_file.fileno(),) if signature_file is None else (
+            data_file.fileno(), signature_file.fileno(),
+        )
+        try:
+            result = subprocess.run(
+                argv, cwd="/", env={"LC_ALL": "C", "PATH": ""}, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
+                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, close_fds=True,
+                pass_fds=inherited, timeout=5, check=False,
+            )
+        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
+            raise ContractError("execution grant Ed25519 operation is unavailable") from exc
+        if private:
+            if result.returncode != 0 or len(result.stdout) != 64:
+                raise ContractError("execution grant Ed25519 signing failed")
+            return result.stdout
+        return result.returncode == 0
+    finally:
+        data_file.close()
+        if signature_file is not None:
+            signature_file.close()
+
+
+def sign_execution_grant(
+    grant_without_signature: dict[str, Any], *, key_id: str,
+    private_key_path: str, openssl_path: str,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Sign using root-owned Ed25519 issuer key; private bytes never enter argv."""
+    if not isinstance(grant_without_signature, dict) or "signature" in grant_without_signature:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: signing input must omit signature")
+    candidate = {**grant_without_signature, "key_id": _identifier(key_id, "key_id")}
+    candidate["signature"] = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(bytes(64)).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
+    validate_execution_grant(candidate)
+    body = {name: value for name, value in candidate.items() if name != "signature"}
+    signature_bytes = _openssl_signature(
+        openssl_path, key_path=private_key_path,
+        payload=EXECUTION_GRANT_LABEL + canonical_bytes(body), private=True,
+    )
+    assert isinstance(signature_bytes, bytes)
+    signature = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(signature_bytes).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
+    result = {**body, "signature": signature}
+    validate_execution_grant(result)
+    return result
+
+
+def verify_execution_grant(
+    grant: object,
+    trusted_keys: Mapping[str, str],
+    *,
+    audience: str,
+    service_generation: str,
+    openssl_path: str,
+    now: float | None = None,
+    max_clock_skew_sec: float = 5.0,
+    allow_expired: bool = False,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Verify grant signature, audience, generation, and validity interval.
+
+    The key mapping must come from root-controlled trust configuration. Unknown
+    or revoked key IDs fail closed. This check does not replace the Store's
+    immediate pre-dispatch authorization and durable pending claim.
+    """
+    valid = validate_execution_grant(grant)
+    if not isinstance(trusted_keys, Mapping):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant trust: key registry is invalid")
+    key_path = trusted_keys.get(valid["key_id"])
+    if not isinstance(key_path, str):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant trust: unknown or revoked key id")
+    if valid["audience"] != _identifier(audience, "expected audience"):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: audience mismatch")
+    if valid["service_generation"] != _identifier(service_generation, "expected service generation"):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant: service generation mismatch")
+    timestamp = time.time() if now is None else now
+    if isinstance(timestamp, bool) or not isinstance(timestamp, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(timestamp):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant verification time is invalid")
+    if isinstance(max_clock_skew_sec, bool) or not isinstance(max_clock_skew_sec, (int, float)):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant clock skew is invalid")
+    if not math.isfinite(max_clock_skew_sec) or max_clock_skew_sec < 0:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant clock skew is invalid")
+    if type(allow_expired) is not bool:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant expiry policy is invalid")
+    if (valid["issued_at"] > timestamp + max_clock_skew_sec
+            or (not allow_expired and valid["expires_at"] <= timestamp)):
+        raise ContractError("execution grant is not currently valid")
+    body = {name: item for name, item in valid.items() if name != "signature"}
+    signature = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(valid["signature"] + "==")
+    verified = _openssl_signature(
+        openssl_path, key_path=key_path,
+        payload=EXECUTION_GRANT_LABEL + canonical_bytes(body),
+        signature=signature, private=False,
+    )
+    if verified is not True:
+        raise ContractError("execution grant signature is invalid")
+    return dict(valid)
+
+
+class ExecutionAuthority:
+    """One-process admission capability for the manifest runner.
+
+    The trusted service creates this only after verifying the grant against its
+    root-owned key ring. ``claim`` rechecks Store authority and inserts the
+    one-time PENDING claim; ``claim_status`` resolves only that exact grant
+    and generation after an uncertain claim reply; ``reserve`` atomically
+    rechecks authority and commits EXECUTION_RESERVED before launch; ``complete``
+    persists the exact final receipt. These callbacks are supplied by the
+    privileged Supervisor/Store boundary, never by a socket request.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        grant: object,
+        *,
+        daemon_uid: int,
+        service_generation: str,
+        trusted_keys: Mapping[str, str],
+        openssl_path: str,
+        audience: str,
+        daemon_boundary_check: Any,
+        claim: Any,
+        claim_status: Any,
+        terminalize_no_execution: Any,
+        reserve: Any,
+        complete: Any,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.grant = verify_execution_grant(
+            grant, trusted_keys, audience=audience,
+            service_generation=service_generation, openssl_path=openssl_path,
+        )
+        if type(daemon_uid) is not int or daemon_uid < 1:
+            raise ContractError("execution authority daemon UID is invalid")
+        self.daemon_uid = daemon_uid
+        self.service_generation = _identifier(service_generation, "service generation")
+        if self.grant["service_generation"] != self.service_generation:
+            raise ContractError("execution authority generation does not match grant")
+        if (not callable(daemon_boundary_check) or not callable(claim)
+                or not callable(claim_status) or not callable(terminalize_no_execution)
+                or not callable(reserve) or not callable(complete)):
+            raise ContractError("execution authority callbacks are invalid")
+        self._daemon_boundary_check = daemon_boundary_check
+        self._claim = claim
+        self._claim_status = claim_status
+        self._terminalize_no_execution = terminalize_no_execution
+        self._reserve = reserve
+        self._complete = complete
+        self._claimed = False
+        self._reserved = False
+        self._completed = False
+        self._no_execution_confirmed = False
+
+    @property
+    def reservation_confirmed(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether this process received exact confirmation before child launch."""
+        return self._reserved
+
+    @property
+    def completion_confirmed(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the Supervisor confirmed durable COMPLETE for this process."""
+        return self._completed
+
+    @property
+    def no_execution_confirmed(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether the exact claim has a durable terminal pre-spawn disposition."""
+        return self._no_execution_confirmed
+
+    @property
+    def claim_confirmed(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether this process confirmed the exact durable PENDING claim."""
+        return self._claimed
+
+    def authorize_and_claim(self, context: object) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
+        """Enforce exact binding and return a stored receipt for safe COMPLETE replay."""
+        if not isinstance(context, dict) or set(context) != _RUN_CONTEXT_FIELDS:
+            raise ContractError("execution authority context does not match the runner contract")
+        for field in _RUN_CONTEXT_FIELDS - {"attempt", "epoch", "execution_deadline_sec"}:
+            _identifier(context[field], f"context {field}")
+        for field in ("manifest_sha256", "model_provenance_sha256"):
+            if not _SHA256.fullmatch(context[field]):
+                raise ContractError(f"execution authority context {field} is malformed")
+        for field in ("attempt", "epoch"):
+            if type(context[field]) is not int or context[field] < 1:
+                raise ContractError(f"execution authority context {field} is invalid")
+        deadline = context["execution_deadline_sec"]
+        if type(deadline) is not int or not 1 <= deadline <= MAX_EXECUTION_DEADLINE_SEC:
+            raise ContractError("execution authority context deadline is invalid")
+        expected = {
+            "manifest_sha256": "manifest_sha256", "task_id": "task_id",
+            "slot": "slot", "attempt": "attempt", "epoch": "epoch",
+            "run_id": "run_id", "invocation_id": "invocation_id",
+            "request_id": "request_id", "runner_id": "runner_id",
+            "resolved_model": "resolved_model",
+            "model_provenance_sha256": "model_provenance_sha256",
+            "execution_deadline_sec": "execution_deadline_sec",
+            "service_generation": "service_generation",
+        }
+        for context_field, grant_field in expected.items():
+            if context[context_field] != self.grant[grant_field]:
+                raise ContractError(f"execution authority {context_field} does not match grant")
+        if self._claimed:
+            raise ContractError("execution authority has already claimed a run")
+        if os.name != "posix" or os.geteuid() != self.daemon_uid:
+            raise ContractError("manifest execution is restricted to the configured daemon identity")
+        if self._daemon_boundary_check() is not True:
+            raise ContractError("manifest execution is outside the configured daemon boundary")
+        try:
+            result = self._claim(dict(self.grant))
+        except Exception as claim_error:
+            try:
+                status = self._claim_status(dict(self.grant))
+            except Exception as status_error:
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "execution claim outcome is unknown; refusing to launch"
+                ) from status_error
+            if (not isinstance(status, dict)
+                    or status.get("service_generation") != self.service_generation):
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "execution claim status is not bound to this service generation"
+                ) from claim_error
+            if (status.get("state") == "NOT_FOUND"
+                    and set(status) == {"state", "service_generation"}):
+                # Exact current-generation absence proves this grant never
+                # established durable claim state; refuse without recycling
+                # the service generation.
+                raise ContractError("execution claim was not found; refusing to launch") from claim_error
+            if status.get("state") == "PENDING" and set(status) == {"state", "service_generation"}:
+                # The exact one-time claim committed, but its RPC reply was lost.
+                # Only this same still-live generation may advance it to reserve.
+                result = None
+            elif (status.get("state") == "COMPLETE"
+                    and set(status) == {"state", "service_generation", "receipt"}
+                    and isinstance(status["receipt"], dict)):
+                self._claimed = True
+                return dict(status["receipt"])
+            else:
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "execution claim is absent, reserved, or terminal; refusing to reclaim or launch"
+                ) from claim_error
+        if result is not None and not isinstance(result, dict):
+            raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError("execution claim returned an invalid result")
+        self._claimed = True
+        if result is not None:
+            if set(result) != {"state", "receipt"} or result["state"] != "COMPLETE":
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError("execution claim returned an unsupported replay state")
+            if not isinstance(result["receipt"], dict):
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError("stored execution receipt is invalid")
+            return dict(result["receipt"])
+        return None
+
+    def reserve(self) -> None:
+        """Durably reserve the exact grant immediately before its first child launch."""
+        if not self._claimed or self._reserved:
+            raise ContractError("execution reservation requires one unreserved claim")
+        if os.name != "posix" or os.geteuid() != self.daemon_uid:
+            raise ContractError("manifest execution is restricted to the configured daemon identity")
+        if self._daemon_boundary_check() is not True:
+            raise ContractError("manifest execution is outside the configured daemon boundary")
+        try:
+            result = self._reserve(dict(self.grant))
+        except Exception as reserve_error:
+            try:
+                status = self._claim_status(dict(self.grant))
+            except Exception:
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "execution reservation outcome is unknown; refusing to launch"
+                ) from reserve_error
+            if (not isinstance(status, dict)
+                    or status.get("service_generation") != self.service_generation):
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "execution reservation status is not generation-bound"
+                ) from reserve_error
+            # Even if the status proves reservation committed, the lost reserve
+            # reply is ambiguous: this process must not infer ownership or spawn.
+            raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                f"execution reservation was not confirmed (state={status.get('state')}); refusing to launch"
+            ) from reserve_error
+        expected_digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(self.grant)).hexdigest()
+        if (not isinstance(result, dict)
+                or set(result) != {"state", "grant_id", "payload_sha256", "service_generation"}
+                or result.get("state") != "EXECUTION_RESERVED"
+                or result.get("grant_id") != self.grant["grant_id"]
+                or result.get("payload_sha256") != expected_digest
+                or result.get("service_generation") != self.service_generation):
+            raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                "execution reservation response does not match the exact grant"
+            )
+        # The exact response proves that the durable reservation committed.
+        # Any later local boundary failure is therefore an ambiguous reserved
+        # run and must trigger the runner service's generation fail-stop.
+        self._reserved = True
+        if self._daemon_boundary_check() is not True:
+            raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                "runner service generation changed after launch reservation"
+            )
+
+    def terminalize_no_execution(self, reason_code: str) -> None:
+        """Close a claimed run only when this process has not confirmed reservation."""
+        if not self._claimed or self._reserved or self._completed:
+            raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                "pre-spawn terminalization is unavailable after reservation or without a claim"
+            )
+        try:
+            result = self._terminalize_no_execution(dict(self.grant), reason_code)
+        except Exception as terminalize_error:
+            try:
+                status = self._claim_status(dict(self.grant))
+            except Exception as status_error:
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "pre-spawn terminalization outcome is unknown"
+                ) from status_error
+            if (not isinstance(status, dict)
+                    or status.get("service_generation") != self.service_generation
+                    or status.get("state") != "INDETERMINATE"
+                    or status.get("reason_code") != reason_code):
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "pre-spawn terminalization was not confirmed by exact claim status"
+                ) from terminalize_error
+        else:
+            digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes(self.grant)).hexdigest()
+            if (not isinstance(result, dict)
+                    or set(result) != {"state", "grant_id", "payload_sha256", "service_generation"}
+                    or result.get("state") != "NO_EXECUTION"
+                    or result.get("grant_id") != self.grant["grant_id"]
+                    or result.get("payload_sha256") != digest
+                    or result.get("service_generation") != self.service_generation):
+                raise AmbiguousExecutionAuthorityError(
+                    "pre-spawn terminal response does not match the exact claim"
+                )
+        self._no_execution_confirmed = True
+
+    def complete(self, receipt: object) -> None:
+        """Persist exactly one receipt after the runner returned a complete result."""
+        if not self._reserved:
+            raise ContractError("execution cannot complete before its durable launch reservation")
+        if not isinstance(receipt, dict):
+            raise ContractError("execution completion receipt must be an object")
+        self._complete(dict(self.grant), dict(receipt))
+        self._completed = True

+def _reviewer_registry_ok(registry: Any, manifest: dict, operator_key: Any,
+                          reviewer_keys: Any, hard: list[str]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Validate signed registry and return normalized principal -> key id."""
+    if not isinstance(registry, dict) or set(registry) != {"version", "entries", "signature"}:
+        hard.append("reviewer registry missing or has invalid fields")
+        return {}
+    if not isinstance(registry["version"], str) or registry["version"] != manifest["reviewer_registry"]["version"]:
+        hard.append("reviewer registry version does not match manifest")
+        return {}
+    entries = registry["entries"]
+    if not isinstance(entries, list):
+        hard.append("reviewer registry entries must be a list")
+        return {}
+    if not _key_ok(operator_key) or not verify(registry, operator_key, REVIEWER_REGISTRY_LABEL):
+        hard.append("reviewer registry signature invalid")
+        return {}
+    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical_bytes({"version": registry["version"], "entries": entries})).hexdigest()
+    if digest != manifest["reviewer_registry"]["sha256"]:
+        hard.append("reviewer registry digest does not match manifest")
+    result: dict[str, str] = {}
+    key_ids: set[str] = set()
+    for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
+        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"principal", "key_id"}:
+            hard.append(f"reviewer registry entry {i} has invalid fields")
+            continue
+        try:
+            principal = normalize_principal(entry["principal"])
+            key_id = entry["key_id"]
+            if not isinstance(key_id, str) or not key_id.strip():
+                raise ValueError("key_id must be non-empty")
+            if principal in result or key_id in key_ids:
+                hard.append("reviewer registry contains duplicate principal or key id")
+                continue
+            result[principal] = key_id
+            key_ids.add(key_id)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            hard.append(f"reviewer registry entry {i} invalid: {type(exc).__name__}")
+    author = normalize_principal(manifest["author_principal"])
+    if author in result:
+        hard.append("manifest author principal is registered as a reviewer")
+    if not isinstance(reviewer_keys, dict):
+        hard.append("reviewer_keys must map key ids to trusted key bytes")
+    else:
+        for key_id in key_ids:
+            if not _key_ok(reviewer_keys.get(key_id)):
+                hard.append(f"reviewer key {key_id!r} is not trusted")
+    return result
+

+"""External event anchoring and lifecycle transition contracts (stdlib only)."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import hmac
+import json
+import os
+import threading
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Any, Protocol
+
+from .contracts import canonical_bytes
+from .signing import MIN_KEY_BYTES
+
+CHECKPOINT_LABEL = b"vst-external-checkpoint-v1\0"
+_GENESIS_HEAD = "0" * 64
+_anchor_lock = threading.Lock()
+_anchor_path_locks_guard = threading.Lock()
+_anchor_path_locks: dict[str, Any] = {}
+_anchor_path_lock_state = threading.local()
+
+
+class AnchorError(Exception):
+    """An unavailable, invalid, or conflicting external checkpoint."""
+
+
+class ExternalAnchor(Protocol):
+    def read_latest(self) -> dict | None: ...
+    def compare_and_append(self, expected: dict | None, checkpoint: dict) -> dict: ...
+
+
+def signed_checkpoint(count: int, head: str, event_key: bytes) -> dict:
+    body = {"count": count, "head": head}
+    mac = hmac.new(event_key, CHECKPOINT_LABEL + canonical_bytes(body), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
+    return {**body, "signature": mac}
+
+
+def verify_checkpoint(checkpoint: dict, event_key: bytes) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(checkpoint, dict) or set(checkpoint) != {"count", "head", "signature"}:
+        return False
+    count, head, signature = checkpoint["count"], checkpoint["head"], checkpoint["signature"]
+    if isinstance(count, bool) or not isinstance(count, int) or count < 0:
+        return False
+    if not isinstance(head, str) or len(head) != 64 or not isinstance(signature, str):
+        return False
+    expected = signed_checkpoint(count, head, event_key)["signature"]
+    return hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected)
+
+
+class FileExternalAnchor:
+    """Append-only JSONL anchor file; configure its path outside the worker mount."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: str, event_key: bytes):
+        if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
+            raise ValueError("anchor path must be a non-empty string")
+        if not isinstance(event_key, (bytes, bytearray)) or len(event_key) < MIN_KEY_BYTES:
+            raise ValueError("event_key must be bytes of length >= 32")
+        self.path = os.path.abspath(path)
+        self._key = bytes(event_key)
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def transaction_lock(self):
+        """Serialize a store transaction and its external-anchor sync across processes.
+
+        Callers hold this lock across the SQLite commit and all checkpoint appends,
+        or across an authoritative read and its external-anchor comparison. A
+        separate lock file avoids recursively locking the JSONL file used by CAS.
+        Nested use by the same thread and path is reentrant.
+        """
+        lock_path = os.path.realpath(self.path) + ".coord.lock"
+        states = getattr(_anchor_path_lock_state, "states", None)
+        if states is None:
+            states = {}
+            _anchor_path_lock_state.states = states
+        state = states.get(lock_path)
+        if state is not None:
+            state["depth"] += 1
+            try:
+                yield
+            finally:
+                state["depth"] -= 1
+            return
+
+        with _anchor_path_locks_guard:
+            path_lock = _anchor_path_locks.setdefault(lock_path, threading.RLock())
+        path_lock.acquire()
+        stream = None
+        unlock = None
+        primary_error = None
+        try:
+            try:
+                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(lock_path), exist_ok=True)
+                stream = open(lock_path, "a+b")
+                if os.name != "nt":
+                    os.chmod(lock_path, 0o600)
+                stream.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
+                if stream.tell() == 0:
+                    stream.write(b"\0")
+                    stream.flush()
+                if os.name == "nt":
+                    import msvcrt
+
+                    stream.seek(0)
+                    msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_LOCK, 1)
+                    unlock = lambda: msvcrt.locking(stream.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
+                else:
+                    import fcntl
+
+                    fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
+                    unlock = lambda: fcntl.flock(stream.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)
+            except OSError as exc:
+                raise AnchorError(f"external anchor coordinator setup failed: {exc}") from exc
+            state = {
+                "depth": 1,
+                "stream": stream,
+                "unlock": unlock,
+                "path_lock": path_lock,
+            }
+            states[lock_path] = state
+            yield
+        except BaseException as exc:
+            primary_error = exc
+            raise
+        finally:
+            states.pop(lock_path, None)
+            teardown_error = None
+            try:
+                if unlock is not None:
+                    unlock()
+            except OSError as exc:
+                teardown_error = AnchorError(
+                    f"external anchor coordinator unlock failed: {exc}"
+                )
+            finally:
+                try:
+                    if stream is not None and not stream.closed:
+                        stream.close()
+                except OSError as exc:
+                    if teardown_error is None:
+                        teardown_error = AnchorError(
+                            f"external anchor coordinator close failed: {exc}"
+                        )
+                finally:
+                    path_lock.release()
+            if teardown_error is not None and primary_error is None:
+                raise teardown_error
+
+    def read_latest(self) -> dict | None:
+        try:
+            with open(self.path, "rb") as stream:
+                lines = stream.read().splitlines()
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            return None
+        except OSError as exc:
+            raise AnchorError(f"external anchor unavailable: {exc}") from exc
+        latest = None
+        for index, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+            try:
+                item = json.loads(line)
+            except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
+                raise AnchorError(f"malformed external checkpoint at line {index}") from exc
+            if not verify_checkpoint(item, self._key):
+                raise AnchorError(f"invalid external checkpoint at line {index}")
+            if latest is None and (item["count"] != 0 or item["head"] != _GENESIS_HEAD):
+                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint history must begin at genesis")
+            if latest is not None and item["count"] != latest["count"] + 1:
+                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint count is not strictly consecutive")
+            latest = item
+        return latest
+
+    def compare_and_append(self, expected: dict | None, checkpoint: dict) -> dict:
+        if not verify_checkpoint(checkpoint, self._key):
+            raise AnchorError("refusing unsigned or invalid checkpoint")
+        # The sidecar lock coordinates both Store transactions and standalone
+        # CAS calls. Locking this JSONL file separately with msvcrt is fragile
+        # across Windows append handles and is unnecessary under that lock.
+        with self.transaction_lock(), _anchor_lock:
+            latest = self.read_latest()
+            if latest == checkpoint:
+                return latest
+            if latest != expected:
+                if latest is not None and latest["count"] == checkpoint["count"]:
+                    raise AnchorError("same checkpoint count has a different head")
+                raise AnchorError("external checkpoint compare-and-append conflict")
+            wanted_count = 0 if expected is None else expected["count"] + 1
+            if checkpoint["count"] != wanted_count:
+                raise AnchorError("checkpoint is not the immediate successor")
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(self.path), exist_ok=True)
+            try:
+                with open(self.path, "a+b") as stream:
+                    if os.name != "nt":
+                        os.chmod(self.path, 0o600)
+                    latest = self.read_latest()
+                    if latest == checkpoint:
+                        return latest
+                    if latest != expected:
+                        if latest is not None and latest["count"] == checkpoint["count"]:
+                            raise AnchorError("same checkpoint count has a different head")
+                        raise AnchorError("external checkpoint compare-and-append conflict")
+                    stream.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
+                    end = stream.tell()
+                    if end:
+                        stream.seek(end - 1, os.SEEK_SET)
+                        if stream.read(1) != b"\n":
+                            # A crash may leave a complete JSON record without
+                            # its final newline. Separate it durably before the
+                            # next record so recovery never merges two objects.
+                            stream.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
+                            stream.write(b"\n")
+                            stream.flush()
+                            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
+                    stream.write(canonical_bytes(checkpoint) + b"\n")
+                    stream.flush()
+                    os.fsync(stream.fileno())
+            except OSError as exc:
+                raise AnchorError(f"external checkpoint append failed: {exc}") from exc
+            return checkpoint
+
+
+# S7.1: table is data as well as documentation. Unknown pairs are rejected.
+STOP_TRANSITIONS = {
+    ("RUNNING", "STOP"): {
+        "next_state": "STOPPING", "cleanup_action": "terminate process group", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+    ("STOPPING", "CLEANUP_COMPLETE"): {
+        "next_state": "STOPPED", "cleanup_action": "release lease", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+    ("STOPPED", "RESUME"): {
+        "next_state": "READY", "cleanup_action": "increment epoch and require fresh receipt", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+    ("RUNNING", "ROLLBACK"): {
+        "next_state": "ROLLING_BACK", "cleanup_action": "restore scoped worktree snapshot", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+    ("ROLLING_BACK", "CLEANUP_COMPLETE"): {
+        "next_state": "STOPPED", "cleanup_action": "release lease", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+    ("READY", "START"): {
+        "next_state": "RUNNING", "cleanup_action": "start isolated worker", "trigger": "supervisor",
+    },
+}
+
+
+def transition(state: str, event: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    try:
+        row = STOP_TRANSITIONS[(state, event)]
+        if row["trigger"] != "supervisor":
+            raise ValueError("transition trigger is not the supervisor")
+        return row["next_state"], row["cleanup_action"]
+    except KeyError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"unsupported lifecycle transition: {state!r} + {event!r}") from exc
